"Uhh..." A sound of a flustered whimper could be heard behind the book then. Again, Caba felt himself feeling embarrassed by the human’s pure, maiden-like reaction.
The demon cleared his throat and continued with a sheepish grin. "Oh, well...yeah, what I mean is...since His Lordship took you as his bride, I should accept it gladly."
After Caba made his conclusion, the room fell into silence. The human lowered the book finally, cheeks still adorned with blooming red, as he exhaled long.
The two other demons, however, tilted their head and narrowed their eyes. Eruha tapped on the armrest and commented. "Hmm, there’s something icky about this..."
"Are you making excuses, Caba?" Lesta crossed his arms, eyeing the bald demon dubiously.
"I’m not! Can you just stop slandering me?!" Caba barked in frustration at the demon who was supposed to be his friend. But this was not the time for him to pick a fight with the smirking demon. He shifted his gaze toward the human again and sighed. "Anyway, I’m not saying all this for you to forgive me or anything, Young Master," he paused, and looked at the floor. "Just...I hope you understand that I’m just a stupid subordinate of His Lordship."
He had been thinking about what he did during his punishment. And then, when the Lord told them that they shouldn’t approach the Lord’s private quarters yesterday, he realized that he was one of the reasons why. He bit down his sigh and continued in a careful but sincere tone.
"So...I hope what I did won’t discourage you from staying here with His Lordship, Young Master," he bowed his head again, even though he had never bowed to anyone but his Lord. When he lifted his head, the look in his eyes was soft and sincere. "Because in all my years serving him, I’ve never seen him happier than after he met you."
The young human met his gaze with surprised eyes. The long, dark eyelashes fluttered shyly, but rather than getting flustered like before, the man was just fidgeting with pressed lips, as if containing himself from smiling.
That nice atmosphere, however, couldn’t hold out for long.
"Wow, you actually say something sensible for once," Lesta said with a smirk.
Glaring at the smirking demon, Caba held up his hand and put his thumb and index finger together. "Just so you know, I’m thiiiis close to throwing you out of the window..."
Lesta just met the threatening glare with a brief laugh, before he turned his gaze toward the young human. Right, they should hear what the young master thought about this.
Seeing the three demons staring at him, the young human-druid blinked and straightened his back a little bit. "Umm..." he bit his red lower lips for a while, before finally speaking in a firmer voice. "I don’t want you to misunderstand."
The green eyes stared at Caba, who was still on the floor and tilted his bald head in confusion.
"It’s not that I hate you or anything," the human shook his head, the words prompting Caba to sit on his heels, as if listening to a lecture.
Or his Lord’s order.
After a brief pause, the human continued. "But you...or rather, what transpired that night triggered something quite traumatic for me, and because of that, my body reacted by itself..."
The human looked at his hand, which unless he gripped something, was still slightly trembling. He shifted his gaze at Caba after, with slightly downturned brows and saddened eyes. "So, I’m sorry, but...I don’t know when I would stop having that kind of reaction,"
The three demons went silent at that. Caba, especially, felt his guts churn. His mouth opened and closed repeatedly without any sound, until he finally swallowed and spoke dejectedly.
"...I understand," he lowered his head again. "I will do by best so you don’t have to see me or hear my voi—"
"No! That’s not what I mean!" the young human swiftly cut him off. Caba looked up with widened eyes and raised brows, and found the young human shaking his head frantically and started to explain.
"I just want to say that if I happened to flinch at your voice or something, please don’t get offended..."
Again, another silence.
"How..." Caba almost couldn’t find his voice at this point. "How dare I feel offended by you, Young Master..."
"Well...you might? I mean, it’s not nice to have someone getting scared of you for no apparent reason..." the young human paused, staring down again, as if recalling some experience. He looked up after a few seconds and added with a quiet voice. "...right?"
Caba didn’t really know what he was supposed to say to that. At this kind of moment, the one with the most sensible remark usually was Eruha. And as expected, the tall demon spoke to break the silence.
"Hmm," Eruha nodded, his long drop earrings swaying from the motion. "Besides, it’s actually better to face a trauma head-on," he looked at the young human with a praising smile. "Who knows, after a few times hearing your annoying voice, Young Master will get used to it enough."
Caba very much wanted to smack the tall demon, but he held his palm back this time.
"Yes, I think so too," the young human finally smile while nodding in agreement, before looking at Caba with a radiant gaze. "So please don’t feel like you have to avoid me or anything."
Needless to say that Caba was getting more speechless at that. The whole reaction, and the fact that the Lord’s partner actually felt bad for him made his gut twisted in shame over what he did in the past.
"I..." he looked at the floor. He would have prostate again if he didn’t remember that the young human was uncomfortable with that. So he just gripped his knees and tried to make his voice steady. "I understand," he nodded weakly.
"Pfft—are you crying?"
"I’m not!"
Truly, couldn’t these demons let him have his moment in peace?!
"Mm, mm," and in truly Eruha fashion, the tall demon clapped his hand, ignoring the emotional demon with a nonchalant remark. "Now that everything had been cleared up, why don’t we call it a day?"
He started to get up and looked at the other two demons. "Lesta, you go with Caba since he’s coming all the way here to look at you. I’ll take Young Master to His Lordship’s office."
The young human suddenly perked up at his words. "Oh?"
Lesta raised his brow and stared at Eruha for a while, before shrugging. "Hmm, sure," he turned toward the human and bent his waist. "Then, Young Master, let’s meet again."
"Okay," the man nodded with a smile.
Still on the floor, Caba muttered timidly. "C-can I say that too?"
With a light-hearted tone, the young human replied with a bright laugh. "Of course!"
"Then...see you again, Young Master..." the bald demon bowed his head again, face lowered so the other couldn’t see his glazed eyes.
"Yes, see you!"
* * *
"Ahh...our Young Master is even more adorable than what Dhuarta told me," Lesta said while stretching his arms up as they walked out of the library.
"Well..." Caba, who was still in a daze quite a bit, replied slowly. "I would not deny that..."
"Pfft—look at you being all soft now," Lesta laughed. The mad wolf truly looked like a tamed dog right now—which he did not expect, honestly. "Anyway, why are you looking at me in the library? How do you know I was there?"
"Huh? Someone just told me," Caba answered with a shrug.
"Who?"
"An orderly?"
"And that orderly did not tell you that I was with the young master?"
"...no?"
Caba halted his pace and turned around because Lesta suddenly stopped walking. "What?"
"Who...was that person?"
The bald demon felt confused about this sudden interrogation, but he tried to recall as best as he could. "I don’t know his name," he crossed his arms and looked up in concentration. "I think I saw him around you or Eruha sometimes though..." after musing about it for a few seconds, he finally snapped his fingers and looked at Lesta again. "You know, those who liked playing chess with you guys and—what?"
Caba tilted his head at the widened black eyes of the other demon. "Don’t tell me..." Lesta muttered and turned his head toward the direction of the library.
"Huh?"
He couldn’t think about it earlier due to the hectic situation. But now that things had resolved well, he had leeway to contemplate everything.
Like why would someone tell Caba where he was without mentioning the young human, which was the source of interest among the castle staff these days? And it was almost suspicious how no one was in the library, including the librarian.
Everything was a perfect stage for a sudden rendezvous, including any settlement arising from the possible conflict. He remembered Eruha only led the young human to calm down rather than telling Caba to go. He was also bringing them naturally to the private room, and agreed easily that the young master shouldn’t avoid meeting Caba.
Lesta suddenly let out a laugh. Was this the extent you would go to shape the chosen one to be the best partner for His Lordship?
"Damn, Eru..." he started to walk again while laughing and shaking his head, leaving the used Caba in confusion behind.
"...huh??"

chapters.title: Chapter 89: A little taste of adventure in the heart of a demon castle
chapters.content:
Chapter 89: A little taste of adventure in the heart of a demon castle
After putting back the book that I had been unconsciously clutching to all this time back onto the bookshelf, I followed Eruha deeper into the library. I was confused at first, because I thought we’d be going out—but why were we going further in instead?
"Since you’ve handled Caba well, I’m going to reward you, Young Master," Eruha said with a smile as he led me to one of the rooms in the back.
It looked like another room intended for discussion too, but with the typical school library setting; a large table with a dozen chairs around it. The vibe felt more solemn and scholarly, with cabinets containing stacks of blank papers and notebooks, as well as stationaries available in one corner.
"Reward?" I asked with a mix of confusion and expectation. I thought my reward was to see Natha in the middle of his work.
He just winked and told me to follow him, even putting his finger on his lips, signaling me to quiet down. It gave a sense of suspense, even though there was no one in the library in the first place.
So I followed him toward one of the bookshelves, and suddenly hit with an epiphany. I grabbed his sleeve in reflex and asked with a pounding heart. "Is...is this the s-secret passage?"
Damn, I even stuttered.
"Oh, you’re quick, Young Master," he said. And then he told me to get closer, and pointed to a book with a green cover. It looked ordinary, just like any other book. "Here, remember this one," he said to me, and then pointed to the gap above the book. "Put your hand there, Young Master."
Still with a pounding heart, I slip my hand between the green book and the wooden roof of the shelf. I ran my fingers around the hard wood until finally, somewhere toward the back, I felt a little carving.
"Ah,"
"Send a little bit of mana there," Eruha instructed further, which I followed, letting put just a whiff of mana.
Immediately, I felt the carving heat up and I heard a crisp clicking sound from somewhere. I looked at Eruha for confirmation, and the demon nodded with a smile. "Good, pull your hand out now."
I thought the bookshelf would suddenly move afterward, but nothing seemed to happen. What...so the shelf was just where the trigger button was? I pulled out and followed Eruha again, this time toward the utility cabinet I saw earlier. The demon then grabbed the side of the cabinet and swung it aside like a door.
And a door it was, for a wide gap enough for an adult demon to go through was there.
"Oh..."
Eruha looked at me and grinned, before gesturing with his hand inside. Without wasting any more time, I stepped through the frame and entered a dark passageway. With the light from the library room, I could see the stone path and walls before Eruha slipped inside and pulled the cabinet closed again.
There was a few seconds of darkness when I couldn’t see anything, but Eruha swiftly snapped his fingers and conjured up a blue fire to light our way.
The path was just as wide as the double-door cabinet, just enough for two adults walking side by side. With floating fires hovering on our front and back, Eruha led me deeper into the path, as I looked around the place like a kid in an amusement park.
"Will the path be locked automatically after we close the cabinet?"
"Yes," Eruha nodded. "And when you want to use the path to go inside the library instead, just find the same carving on the wall and send your mana like earlier."
Well, I guessed since this was a fantasy setting and all, the secret passages and traps would have to do with magic rather than complicated mechanics.
"Where is this path headed?" I asked after we walked for a while. Since the scenery was the same, it got boring looking around after a while.
"There are two places this path ends up in," Eruha told me. "We’ll reach the crossroad in a bit—ah, there it is."
He sent one of the fires forward, and soon, I could see the intersection. Just as Eruha said, it was a crossroads. One of them was just leading to a niche with what looked like a stone bench. It was probably some kind of resting place. The other two paths should lead to different places; one ahead and one on our left.
"We’ll be going forward this time," Eruha informed me, and then added as I stared at the path on our left with curiosity. "You can find out about this one yourself sometime, Young Master."
...ooh! Exploring secret passages by myself did seem like a nice plan to spend my time here. But for now, I just went straight as Eruha instructed.
We kept walking for a while, which reminded me of the time Natha took me to his private quarters for the first time. Eruha filled the time by starting his lesson on that demon language, asking me what my progress with it so far was. It made me stop wondering when would we arrive at the end of the tunnel.
So I didn’t even realize we had reached the end until I saw the floating fires ahead of us congregating in front of a wall.
"To your left, Young Master," Eruha pointed with his chin, and my eyes darted to find the carving on the wall. It was just a bit under my eye level, so I found it quickly, and brushed my fingers there.
Again, I heard a whirring sound that ended up with a light click, and curiously pushed on the wall in front of me. This time, rather than swung open, it slid to the side, and we were greeted with...another wall?
Eruha chuckled at my confused face, and lightly kicked the bottom of the wall, which was actually a wooden board. It slid to the side just like the stone wall, and opened to the interior of an empty cupboard.
Eruha slipped inside first, and opened the cupboard’s door to make room. After I stepped inside and walked out of the narrow space, he came back to close the stone and wooden wall before joining me on the outside.
The cupboard, as it turned out, was located in the back of a pantry. There were shelves of teas and other drinks, as well as tins of biscuits and cookies, which Eruha casually snatched.
He opened a small tin, enough to be held with one hand, and gave it to me after taking a piece. Raising my brow, I took the tin and looked inside to see nice-looking cookies wafting a scent of butter. It looked like the one the servants gave me as my afternoon tea snack, and I took one in delight, since I hadn’t had anything else after breakfast.
"Where is this?" I asked while munching on the cookies, and he answered by walking to the front side where a couple of startled servants greeted us.
"Easy there, I’m just stealing some biscuits for the Young Master," he said light-heartedly, and I almost choked on the cookies for that.
The servants looked at me and bowed deeply, and as my mouth was filled with cookies, I just nodded awkwardly in acknowledgment. Damn, this tall demon—using me as an alibi! He looked at me with a little smirk and I returned it by munching on another butter cookie aggressively.
He led me out of the pantry to a quiet hall adorned with velvet carpet, and I could hear faint murmurs of activity from around me; from the rooms flanking the corridor. Eruha brought me through the hall and some turns, before entering a room.
It looked like a meeting room, but for now, it was empty. There was another door at the back, where he led me to. As we stand before the door, he suddenly looked at me and whispered. "Let’s be quiet for a bit," he said mysteriously, before opening the door carefully with minimum sound.
And then, I heard it; a deep voice that got me to react instantly. I gripped the half-empty tin in my hand tightly, before scooting closer to the door. Again, Eruha gave me a wink and a deep smile, and pressed his body close to the door, as if he was about to peek inside.
Which I followed.
Closely, and carefully so as to not make a sound, I looked inside the room with a pounding heart.
The room was quite wide, with a seating area bearing eleven chairs, and walls filled with shelves containing scrolls and books. There was minimal decoration adorning the room, keeping the air stern and serious. Still, I could see the furniture was made from the highest quality materials, just like in the private quarters.
The solemnness and the minimalistic approach brought attention to the room’s centerpiece; a large desk with beautiful carving bearing many documents on top of it.
And then, leaning handsomely against the desk with a paper in his hand, was the Lord of the castle.

chapters.title: Chapter 90: The bring-your-lover-to-work day is always embarrassing
chapters.content:
Chapter 90: The bring-your-lover-to-work day is always embarrassing
It was ridiculous.
I had only not seen him for a few hours, but the moment my eyes laid on his figure, my heart skip a beat. I had no idea whether I stopped breathing because I didn’t want to be found out while peeking, or because he was just that gorgeous.
He still wore his black formal wear from this morning, although his cape was neatly hung on the coat rack. What got my lung to cease functioning was the way he rolled his sleeve to his elbow, giving me a full show of his sturdy, veiny arm.
And Gods above—he wore glasses!
Was today my birthday? Why did all my fantasies come to life?
Leaning on the edge of his desk, he looked like a painting. I felt like watching a scene from a movie as he spoke with his staff and gave some orders. They seemed to talk about some mines and a suspicious movement at the border. Not sure, I was just too focused on observing Natha.
I had no idea how long I was there, crouching behind the door and peeking into the room. There were staff coming and going, bringing documents to be signed, putting down proposals, making reports... I watched him walking around the office for who knew how long, oblivious to the time.
"You can go for now," he said to the staff after some time, and then came back to sit on his comfortable-looking chair behind the desk. Seemed like he was about to take a rest?
I wondered when would be the best time to come out. Or would we just go back to the suite? I wasn’t sure if I should disturb him in the middle of his work. I looked up at Eruha to inquire about it, when I heard Natha’s voice again.
"So, are you going to ever come out?" he asked, prompting me to flinch in surprise. "Or was it more fun watching me from behind the door?"
I looked at Eruha and mouthed; ’How does he know?’
"Why wouldn’t he? His Lordship could sense our thought..." the tall demon answered casually with a shrug.
Oh...right! I forgot about it since Natha said he wouldn’t sense mine anymore. But that didn’t mean he couldn’t sense the one that belonged to my chaperone.
"You’re getting comfortable there, sweetheart?" he asked again, and when I looked at him again, I could see his silver eyes trained on me—no longer obatructed by the glasses. A smile played on his face, and I got up in reflex, peeking my head inside first with a sheepish grin.
Natha smiled wider and reached out his hand. "Come," he said briefly, and my body followed it like a command.
Or perhaps it was my heart.
I slipped through the slightly opened door and walked hurriedly across the room as if my feet were impatient. He did chuckle because of it, and when I was close enough, he pulled me by my waist, and the next thing I knew, I was already sitting on one of his thighs.
"W-what are you doing?" I hissed quietly, even though there was no one but Eruha there.
"Why?" Natha gave me an amused smile. "We always do this,"
"No, we’re not!" I replied immediately as I felt my cheeks burn from embarrassment. "...not always," I added quietly.
He laughed then, and as if proving his intention to ignore my fluster, he pulled me even closer that I let out a gasp in surprise. "We should make it a habit then, so you can get used to it,"
My Lord, why are you flirting in the middle of work hours?!
"It’s alright, no one’s here. It’s nearly lunch so I just take an early break," he said with a playful smile, as if replying to my thought.
Gasp! "You said you won’t do it again!" I let out a protest, pursing my lips in annoyance. But Natha just laughed and rubbed on my twisted lips in response.
"I’m not sensing your thought, though?" he tilted his head with a smile. "It’s just written all over your blushing face..."
I’m not blushing?! Or...was I? I pressed my lips to prevent myself from making grunting noises. He pinched my chin lightly with another laugh before looking down, and pointing to my hand with his chin.
"What’s that?"
I followed his gaze with a raised brow, just realizing that I still had the small cookie tin in my hand. "Cookies..." I kept on eating it on the way here, so it already decreased to half now. "Eruha stole it from your pantry," I tattled, prompting the Lord to raise his brow and glance toward the tall demon—who was still here, by the way.
The demon in question cleared his throat before correcting me. "Our pantry," he shrugged with a smile.
Natha scoffed and turned to look at me again. "You like that one?"
"I like all the snacks you’ve been giving me," I took one out, which was shaped like a leaf, and put it in front of his mouth. "Since I could never eat them before."
The sweet ones, the fatty ones, the sour ones, the spicy ones...every flavor was something new to me, and it was exhilarating. Even the strangest flavor still tasted like an adventure, which was miles better than bitter medicines and tasteless meals.
Natha opened his mouth with a smile, and let me hand-feed him the cookie—which I did not expect. I thought he didn’t really like them, since he rarely touch those during our tea time, and only did it as a prank. Was I mistaken?
He closed his eyes and tilted his head, before nodding. "Mm...yeah, I still don’t like it. You can finish all of them, sweetheart."
I laughed at how he swallowed with a frown, and put the remaining cookie in my mouth. So I was right—he did dislike them.
"Well, since I delivered the package, I shall bid my farewell," Eruha said with a chuckle and curtsied elegantly. "Good day, my Lord, Young Master."
"Mm,"
"Oh, thank you, Eruha," I waved my cookie-free hand at him, which he returned with a chuckle before disappearing behind the door. I turned toward Natha again and found that he’d been looking at me with an inquisitive gaze. "What?"
"Seemed like you manage to get close to my vassals," he said with a smile.
But there were also questions reflected in his eyes, so I proceeded to tell him about what happened all this morning, including my conversation with Caba.
At the end of my retelling, he tapped on his chin and looked at me amusedly. "So you even manage to conquer my crazy hound, huh?"
"What, he’s called a hound?" I tilted my head and looked up, musing in confusion. "But...he got no fur?"
Pfft—Natha pressed his head against my side and laughed with a shaking shoulder. "Yeah...he got no...fur, right?" he inhaled deeply after finishing laughing. "Perhaps we should reconsider another nickname for him..."
I giggled at that, and he pulled me even closer to him. My hands, which were already free of the cookie tin, found themselves on his chest, holding on to the sudden jolt. I could see my surprised and flustered face through the reflection in the silver orbs, and my breath hitched for a bit.
"But do you really need to learn the language with them?" he asked in that deep voice that got me confused about whether he was seducing me or threatening me. "I can teach you myself, you know."
Wow...I thought it was only the other demons’ silly conjecture, but Natha did sound reluctant. But I braved myself and told him flatly. "No, I don’t want to."
Natha looked taken aback then. Perhaps he didn’t think I would immediately reject him like that, so he even looked a bit hurt.
"There’s a saying that you shouldn’t ask your lover to teach you something," I explained immediately, so he did not misunderstand. "Because we might end up fighting."
He raised his brow—the surprised and disappointed face turned into confusion. "How?"
"Because...because you might see how pathetic I am, or become disappointed at how slowly I progress. And you might get annoyed, and I’ll get frustrated and annoyed too. And so we’ll end up fighting and...and..." I explained with flailing hands, and Natha blinked repeatedly at my conjured-up scenario. I stopped and dropped my hand to my lap, sighing. "Anyway, that’s about it."
Natha kept his silence for a while, to the point that I felt awkward. Was I...being too weird—
When I was still musing, however, he suddenly snatched my chin and pulled my face closer, and my mind ceased thinking as my lips were being claimed. I gasped against his lips, and he only used the chance to slip between them while pulling my body even closer, until we were practically glued to each other.
I grabbed the cord on his clothes as he caressed my cheek to guide me deeper, but the kiss was too sudden and I depleted my air too soon, so I pulled on his cord and he parted his lips with a deep smile while I panted slightly.
Before I could question his action, he already kissed my cheek and trailed his lips to whisper in my ears. "You called me your lover," he said with palpable glee in his voice.
"Well...aren’t you?" I replied quietly, still with bated breath, and he laughed merrily, pulling me into another kiss.
Oh, I just hoped his staff didn’t suddenly come through the door.

chapters.title: Chapter 91: Fun time in new place begets melancholy
chapters.content:
Chapter 91: Fun time in new place begets melancholy
Thankfully, no one barged into the Lord’s office while I was there and making out with Natha. Perhaps Eruha told them not no disturb us, or perhaps they just didn’t dare to go inside until Natha summoned them.
At any rate, I was spared from further embarrassment, and Natha was pleased enough at my reasoning that he permitted me to have that lessons with Lesta and Eruha.
So it was all good.
When I first arrived here a few days ago, I thought I would have to stay quietly in the private quarters. Since he said it was a trial, I thought I wouldn’t meet with anyone but the servants.
I certainly did not expect to arrive in front of all his vassals, or ended up spending a nice and friendly time with half of them. I especially never thought I’d get to reconcile with the bald one—Caba was it?
Ignoring the time when I cried my heart out above the lake, or when I got a nightmare I did not remember, I could say my time here was turning out to be quite good and productive—especially when I found out about the ’failed product’ which became one of my homework now.
I had been so worried and filled with anxiety before, but not once had I received scorn like I was afraid of. I should have known though, with Natha’s personality, there was no way any of the staff would dare express their concern about me, since it would mean challenging the Lord’s decision.
While I had only explored a tiny part of the big castle, and only met a handful of demons, I could safely say that I didn’t mind staying here.
Not now, though.
However much I wanted to stay with Natha, I still had Jade to worry about back home. And the Lair still had the best environment for my—and my familiar’s—development. I still hadn’t mastered all the elements, which I felt would be important and helpful, should I stay in the Castle for the foreseeable future. There was also the Spear of Judgment that needed to be looked into further, as well as all those ’failed products’ I needed to research.
So, after Natha got back to the private quarters and we finished our dinner, I braced myself and told him I wanted to go back to the tower.
He looked at me keenly, as if trying to see if there was something that made me uncomfortable about my stay here, so I immediately added. "I miss them; Zia and Angwi and everyone...and the little bird is getting restless..."
While I couldn’t see Jade, I could feel the little bird somewhat through our connection. Its distress grew stronger day by day, which made me feel uncomfortable.
"I feel like that guy will fly here if I stay any longer..." I sighed. Jade was still a baby—ahem, a toddler—and it was still hard for the little guy to get separated from me. I should have only stayed here for a night initially, but now it had been days, and I could feel its fear about my condition. "Jade thinks you’re imprisoning me," I told Natha with a laugh.
The Demon Lord chuckled at that, and finally stopped looking at me suspiciously. "Well, I guess you do stay much longer than we planned," he said with a smile, and I could finally let out a quiet breath of relief as he went inside his dressing room to change.
"But you really don’t find it uncomfortable here?" he asked again once he was done changing into his nightrobe, sitting beside me on the couch.
"No, it’s nice here," I shook my head and answered with a smile. "I was so worried before, but everyone has been so nice to me."
I could see the silver eyes curled as Natha smiled pleasantly. He caressed my hair and turned me around before proceeding to braid my hair as usual. "Alright, I’ll send you back tomorrow."
Enjoying the feeling of his hands on my hair, I closed my eyes and hummed in delight. "But if there’s something you find uncomfortable, you have to tell me so I can fix it, alright? Since I’m not sensing your thought, you have to express them out loud for me to know."
"Okay," I nodded slightly since my hair was still in his hands, and he rewarded me with a kiss on my temple.
"Hmm..." as he fastened the cord at the end of the braid, he suddenly made a serious contemplative sound. Before I could turn my head to ask him why, he already leaned forward and circled his hand around my waist. "It’s going to be hard after days of having you by my side," he said while nuzzling my hair. "I’m used to seeing your face first thing in the morning now,"
I bit my lips and leaned back against his chest, letting him pull me closer. "Yeah...me too..." I admitted after struggling with embarrassment for a while.
What if I had another unpleasant or weird dream and he wasn’t there to calm me down? I remembered waking up and trying to sniff the other pillows on the bed, just to find out his scent was no longer there. I took a deep breath and sighed.
Oh, it was such a dilemma. I wanted to always be with him, but I also wanted to be with the others; the friends and familar I had acquired and grew attached to. "Haa...I’m so greedy..."
"You say such silly things sometimes," Natha chuckled at my words. The hand on my waist traveled up to my chin and tilted my head up so I could stare at his face. "You’re the bride of the Lord of Greed. What are you lamenting about being greedy for?"
From here, I could see the glint in his eyes that got my heart to skip a beat. "Didn’t I tell you? You should be more greedy, sweetheart. Greedier than anyone. Let yourself free to desire for something, for anything,"
I could hear the sound of my throat swallowing as Natha lowered his head and deepened his voice. "Be greedy, and let this lover of yours fulfill your desire."
As I looked at the gleaming silver orbs, my heart fluttered with a swirling mess of emotions that even I could not fully decipher.
Was it really alright for me to be that greedy? Even if I wanted him to be mine and mine only? Even if I wanted him to love me completely, not Valmeier?
I took a deep breath and tilted my head to press my lips on his, and my heart fluttered even more when I could feel his lips stretched into a smile. He let me go and I turned around to climb into his lap, arms circling his neck as he grabbed my nape to lead me back to his lips.
During the kiss which turned passionate, I realized sadly that I wouldn’t get this kiss anytime I wanted to anymore after I went back to the tower, and it got me to cling to him even more. I knew this wasn’t exactly our last night, and I’d get to meet him again after a few days, but I still chased his coldness as if I was about to venture into a volcano tomorrow.
When I started to move on my own to savor our kiss, his hand left my nape and traveled down, cold fingers moving across my spine. It got me shivering and gasping with fluttering lashes, which he only used to shove his tongue further.
Within the haziness of pleasure rising from his kiss, I barely noticed when his hands had slipped behind my nightshirt and caressed my skin directly. While my mind didn’t register it, my body did, and my hips squirmed on his lap from the sensation.
Up on my back, and down on my waist, his cold hands were tracing every segment and hunting every imperfection; the small scars left in this body from years of war which I had healed gradually through the druid’s regeneration. It felt ticklish at first, and got me squirming so much within his hold. But after getting used to it, the tickling feeling turn pleasurable, sending heat toward my abdomen. I didn’t realize it, but I was arching my back gradually, impatient for his touch.
My hands were no longer just circling his neck now, but clutching into his back and grasping his hair as shivers ran through my body with his every touch. His cold skin and my heated temperature were playing their game and muddled my brain.
In the end, I couldn’t help but part our lips and moaned slightly, squirming in delight and embarrassment at his incessant yet gentle ministration.
And then, I could feel his fingers tracing my waistline and he parted his lips. With a heavy breath that wasn’t too different from mine, he whispered against my lips as his fingers traveled down and stopped above my clothed entrance.
"Sweetheart, may I touch you here?"

chapters.title: Chapter 92: You know nothing, Me (M)
chapters.content:
Chapter 92: You know nothing, Me (M)
Here? When he said ’here’, did he mean...
Oh my God!
It seemed like I made quite an expression because he immediately leaned forward to kiss my cheek and temple and spoke in a soothing voice. "Ssh—it’s okay if you say no, sweetheart," the hand he placed down there shifted upward, stroking my back in a pacifying action. I wondered if I looked frightened or something, because he was smiling quite anxiously. "It’s alright, I’m just asking. You don’t have to allow it."
He continued to pepper my face with light, soft kisses like he always did when I was having my panic episodes, and I started to relax. It was then that I realized I had been holding my breath. As I felt my hands getting warmed again, I also realized that my heart might have been in a stutter earlier.
How weird. I didn’t think I felt scared, though? Perhaps just...surprised?
Natha no longer had his hands on any of my sensitive places, just holding me and kissing my face, before nuzzling on my neck as if we were just cuddling before, instead of making out passionately.
Oh, my Demon Lord...he was just so so patient, wasn’t he?
"Umm..." I let out a soft murmur, and he swiftly looked at me, as if someone waiting for judgment. "Just...just touch?"
Slowly, I could see the silver eyes widen in surprise. It took a few seconds before he replied in a rather raspy voice. "If you allow me...to put my fingers there too..." He looked keenly at me, caution written on his gorgeous face, before he added in a whisper. "...inside,"
I could hear myself gulping; in nervousness, in arousal, I had no idea which one.
Yes, I was a virgin through and through. This soul, as well as this body, had only been experiencing carnal pleasure not long ago. That being said, it wasn’t like I had no idea about what would eventually happen, where would our intimacy lead to.
And it wasn’t like I’d never...imagined it.
But being able to imagine it didn’t mean my heart and body felt ready. There was still this uncertainty in my heart that whispered about how much I would regret it if we went all the way. But! But...
"No...no more than that?" I asked, quietly, while thinking that it might—it might be okay if we just stopped at fingers.
His hold on me felt tighter suddenly, and I didn’t think I had seen him this messy before; his silver eyes were flickering, and his brows furrowed in an apparent effort to control his emotions. His chest was rising in short breathing, and he spoke in that raspy voice again.
"Yeah," Natha took a deep breath, and when he spoke again, it was back to the nice and smooth voice he usually had. "Yeah, no more than that..."
It was different from the time when I played with his horns. The face he made earlier was more...raw. It was that of a struggle, of a repressed desire, and it made my heart flutter for how much he seemed to hold back. I felt like he might break his restraint for a bit because I was asking to go back to the tower tomorrow. And I understood it, because even though I was the one who asked to go back, I was also reluctant to be apart.
So the thought of being closer, physically, also felt like it would satisfy the longing in our hearts for a bit.
"Okay," I nodded, clutching the fabric of his nightrobe, and breathed slowly. "Okay..."
The kiss I got from that single word was consuming, making my head go blank for a little bit as he plundered my mouth and played with my surprised tongue. I thought he would immediately proceed to strip my pants, but Natha pulled back not long after, looking at me with not just lust, but affection.
"If you don’t like it, tell me," he said, as he stroked my back tenderly. "If you want me to stop anytime, don’t hesitate to say it."
I was too focused on the cold fingers rubbing along my waistline that I didn’t bother to answer, just biting my lips in nervousness and anticipation. But the cold hands grabbed my waist and Natha pulled my attention back with a little bite on my lower lips. "Answer me, sweetheart."
"O-okay..." I stuttered for a bit while nodding at his low warning. I took a deep breath to calm myself and replied again. "I’ll...I’ll tell you..."
It was only then that he smiled a little bit, and continued to kiss me. It was slow and gentle this time, as his fingers moved to pull on the string of my pants. I shivered for a bit from the slightly colder air brushing the skin of my exposed crotch as the loose fabric slid down and Natha pulled down my undergarment.
He broke the kiss slowly and looked at me, the depth of those silver orbs made me feel like a deer caught in a headlight. I froze for a bit because of that—and the cold feeling assaulting my bum. Natha kept his gaze on my face while moving his fingers to my entrance, and I bit my lips to hold the whimper getting out due to a sudden wet feel down there.
Blinking my shock away, I belatedly realized that Natha was conjuring some kind of slick substance with magic and somehow it felt...funny?
"Is it uncomfortable?" he asked while staring at me keenly, and I couldn’t help but giggle. I had no idea if it was a common practice here, to create lube with magic, but I found its practicality to be funny. "Well, at least you seem to be having fun this far."
He started to rub along the rim at my reaction, spreading the cold and wet feeling further, and I shivered more. But the earlier thought also made my lower body feel relaxed and...tingly, so I giggled again.
That giggle, however, turned into a gasp the next second, as the pad of his finger pressed on my rim, which twitched in response. I grabbed his hair in reflex, breathing caught in my throat.
"Take a deep breath," he advised me, and I complied almost instinctively, sucking the air into my lungs and getting my lower back relaxed.
Immediately, I felt the digit pushed inside, and I gasped again. I could feel it met with a slight resistance, and a surge of wet, slimy liquid filled my inside.
"O-oh..." I exhaled harshly as I felt his finger pulled back, before pushing back in, further this time due to the added existence of the magically conjured lube.
"Does it hurt?" he asked with a gentle voice, holding my back with another hand. His finger halted for a bit as he waited for my reply, and I answered with a shake of my head.
"N-no," I managed to speak, feeling my hole twitch in response. I thought it would, but it didn’t. There was a slight pressure as his finger breached my entrance every time, but rather than hurting, it actually felt good.
Or at least I thought so, because my heart rippled and my back shuddered in the same way I felt when he kissed me deeply.
"I can continue?" he asked again, and I nodded almost immediately.
I felt a bit surprised at my own enthusiasm, but I had no leeway to ponder about it since Natha moved his finger again, faster this time. He went deeper with every move, adding another wet and cold liquid from time to time, until I could feel his knuckles against my rim.
"Mmh?" I looked down, and realized that I had started to get hard. I felt my cheeks burn, even though I knew they should be red enough already. "Oh?"
"I’m glad," Natha whispered against my ear, his breath, a little bit heavier than usual, tickling my lobe and making me shudder. "I’ll add another one, yeah?"
He didn’t wait for my reply this time, perhaps the way I grabbed tightly on his shoulder and moaned slightly at his whisper was enough for confirmation. He pulled his finger for a bit, leaving it halfway there, and another cold, wet finger pushed through my entrance.
"Nggh!!"
It stretched, and it felt good. But it also burned, a bit of a stinging sensation accompanied the thrill. My eyes flickered as the second digit lodged slowly inside, feeling so full and it was wonderful, but also weird and worrying. It hurt for a bit, but my mind didn’t seem to mind it. And while my body wriggled at the uncomfortableness of the new sensation, it also remembered the slight pleasure the fingers gave at the entrance, and carved for a similar feeling.
It was confusing, and the confusion scared me more than the fact that there were two long, thick fingers inside me. It translated to my stuttered, short breathing and Natha helped me with his tender kisses again.
"You’re okay?"
Again, he stroked my back gently. But his fingers didn’t stop moving, back and forth again as if digging their way inside me.
"Just...feels weird..." I couldn’t seem to stop squirming, and it made his fingers brush against a place behind my wall that got me gasping loudly—or it was probably a little scream, I wasn’t really sure. "Oh!"
He stopped his movement, and stared at me keenly with a glint of wonder in his silver orbs. His fingers backtracked and started to move in a different way. Rather than digging deeper, they rubbed my flesh as if looking for something.
"Hmm..." he frowned for a bit, fingers moving with more precision, before stopping somewhere. He looked at me, and when my hazy eyes caught the silver orbs, he smiled slightly.
And pressed hard on that spot.
"Oh—God!"
I almost cursed—it was a good thing I didn’t know many cursed words.
But I also almost tore his night robe open with how hard I clutched the fabric. It was like some kind of weird button was switched inside my body, and it lit out the nerves all over my system. My back bent and my head almost slammed to his shoulder, as a new kind of sensation assaulted me.
I heard. I heard about it. I heard about ’that’ place.
But God! I knew nothing.
As I stared at Natha’s face with widened eyes, I saw his smile, the gleam within the silver orbs, and the lick of his lips.
And I knew it was just the beginning.

chapters.title: Chapter 93: In the night when nothing else mattered (M)
chapters.content:
Chapter 93: In the night when nothing else mattered (M)
"Na—Natha!"
Was that my voice, pathetically whimpering in a mix of whine and moan? That high-pitch keen and loud gasping sound that I only imagined existed in porn?
I had no idea. I had no leeway to discern the obcenity of my state as I grasped his hair and panted against his face, as he nuzzled on my cheek with a smile on his exploring lips. He still held me tight, and oh so tenderly on my back, making sure my bent figure and wobbly hips didn’t topple down. But his other hand...oh, that effin’ hand!
His fingers kept on exploring my inside, massaging the walls and digging deeper, as if widening a tunnel. He did it slowly, persistently, making sure it was wet enough for him to move, and halted for a bit every time I whined that it stung.

chapters.title: Chapter 94: Demons are as boisterous as they are dramatic
chapters.content:
Chapter 94: Demons are as boisterous as they are dramatic
"Good morning,"
The first thing that greeted me as I blinked my bleary eyes open was Natha’s dazzling smile. The second thing was the low, gentle whisper of good morning. And the third was a slow, tender, sweet kiss upon my lips.
Indeed. What a good morning it was, even though it was raining outside.
When Natha parted his lips, he only used the few seconds after that to gaze into my confused—but delighted—eyes at this display of tenderness before stroking my cheek and giving me another beautiful smile. As I blinked in a mind-blinding wondrous, he chuckled and went back to kiss me again.
I was confused, but I wasn’t complaining.
I felt like we spent that morning just kissing for a long time, until I felt the coldness of the room and shivered. Natha let my lips go then, and kissed my cheek before wordlessly tucking me back inside the blanket and walking to the steaming tray on the table—like always.
As I waited for him, I wondered about the fact that I had never felt uncomfortable from Natha’s cold temperature, even though I’d shivered and reacted to cold weather. Was it magic? Or was it because it was someone I liked?
Who knew? But I knew that Natha was in a really good mood this morning. And I knew why...probably.
Yeah...my body had been wiped clean and free of any slimy substance, and with good sleep, it almost felt like nothing happened. But this refreshed mind, of course, refused to forget. How could it, when it was also another first for me?
As Natha came back and put the steaming cup in my palm, my gaze fell upon his fingers and I blushed slightly knowing where they were last night.
Where they were and what they had done to me.
"You’re beyond adorable," he chuckled softly and pressed his lips right on my burning cheek.
What was that even mean? I hid my face behind the cup, and he laughed harder, kissing my forehead now, gently, making my heart flutter.
Damn Demon Lord of Greed—I bet he liked stealing and possessing people’s hearts too!
Did it feel that good last night? I mean...it was for me, but I thought he would feel unsatisfied since we didn’t go all the way. And yet, this good mood and the bright expression on his face persisted all morning.
Natha had always been affectionate, but he was even more so today. He didn’t even read his papers during breakfast, and kept his gaze on me all the time, putting food on my plate as usual, telling me to eat slowly, and playing with my hair as I chewed.
I swore the servants even had their eyes widened and their lips parted all morning. Perhaps because they never saw Natha being this bright and smiley. To be fair, he usually only did that in the confine of our bedroom, or if there was no one in the vicinity. As the Lord, Natha always maintained a dignified, cold face. Even when he smiled, he did it subtly.
So it was probably something rare for the others.
It was quite embarrassing, honestly. It was even more embarrassing when he kissed me in front of the door; slow and tender, and long. So long I shifted from melting in his embrace to flustering to gasping for air. And right after I got some air, he went back to kiss me again, to the point that the guards and servants lowered their eyes in fluster.
"N-Natha..." I put my fingers on his lips after I pulled back for another batch of air, panting as if I was just getting back from a hike. If he kissed me again, I felt like I would either collapse from embarrassment or oxygen deprivation.
In turn, he kissed the fingers I put on his lips and rubbed my wrist. "I don’t really want to send you back..."
How unfair! What should I do if you said that with such a forlorn gaze, my Lord?! I pressed my lips as he continued to kiss my fingers and palm, feeling my resolve start to waver.
It might be, if not for the sudden shocked exclaim from the hallway.
"Y-Young Master is g-going back?!"
I almost jumped in startle, and turned my head to see Dhuarta, Lesta, and Caba in the hall in front of the Lord’s door. Dhuarta was the one who shouted with a surprised voice.
"W-when?" she asked.
Still blinking in surprise myself, I answered. "Um...today?"
She gasped, loudly, and clasped her cheek with both hands. "No!"
What...with this reaction? No? I couldn’t get back? What?
"I haven’t finished gathering the snacks I promised you!"
...Oh.
"Umm...you can just give it to me next—"
"My Lord! When will you send Young Master back?" she shifted her gaze toward Natha, who was still holding me. But she just continued to speak without even waiting for a reply. "Don’t send him before I come back, okay?"
Did this demon just order her Lord around? I watched in confusion and amusement as she immediately bolted from the hall without even waiting for a response from either Natha or myself.
And yet, before I had leeway to muse about that, another shocked voice came to my attention. This time, it was quieter, rather sad and anxious too.
"I...is it because of me?" the bald demon wobbled forward like a zombie with a sad face. Because of that, I instinctively flinched and stepped back, even though Natha’s hand was still on my waist.
My reaction, in turn, made Caba even more shocked and saddened. He even went down to his knees with big, glazed eyes. "Are...if you feel uncomfortable, I won’t appear in front of you again, Young Master!" now he even shouted in a freaking hallway. "I...I can leave the Castle too if you—"
"Stop!" I stomped my feet and shouted in flusters. I couldn’t take this anymore! "Why are you people being so dramatic?!"
Whether it was the Lord or his vassals—why were they being like this? It wasn’t like I went to a faraway land? I was sure Natha would pick me up again on the weekend?
I started to open my mouth again, but then paused when I saw their face. Be it Caba or Lesta or the guards and servants who happened to be there, they were all looking at me with a stunned expression. Caba, who was kneeling before was on his butt now, as if someone had pushed him, and Lesta was stepping back in a defensive stance.
And so were the guards, who had their shields upfront.
It got me blinking in confusion. What? Why...was it because I was yelling?
I pressed my lips and felt Natha’s cold hand stroking my head. "It’s okay, they’re just surprised," I looked at him, and he was smiling—somehow rather proudly. "Although maybe less stomping next time. The wind pressure is quite...mm..."
What wind pressure? I tilted my head and looked at Natha inquisitively, but the Demon Lord just smiling charmingly in response, so I swallowed my question and shifted my attention back to the demon on the floor.
Now that I looked at him again, he looked rather pitiful. With that position and his pledge earlier, the ’wolf’ looked rather like a drenched puppy, even though he had no...fur. So I sighed and stepped closer.
"Uhh...I mean...no, it’s not because of you, okay?" I stopped in front of him, who looked at me like he was in a daze. "I just have things to do back in the Lair."
"Re...really?" he replied in a mix of bewilderment and uneasiness, but also relief.
Looking at his expression, this scary-looking demon didn’t look fierce anymore. He looked more and more like a pitiful, overly loyal pet—like the big pitbull my grandpa used to own—and I couldn’t help but rising my hand. Since he was quite big, even in his position, I didn’t need to bend to put my hand on the demon’s head.
"Yeah," I stroked the hairless surface. "So stop being like this, okay?"
Because shouldn’t it be me that flinched and fear him? Why did it become reversed like this?
The bald head nodded obediently while answering. "Y-yes, Young Master."
"Mm," I tapped his head lightly with a smile. "Good, good..."
And then, not a second later, my arm was getting snatched off the demon and my body got pulled back by a cold hand. "You’re touching other people in front of me, now?"
With a gasp, Caba, who was already getting calmer, suddenly slammed—and I really meant slammed, with a loud blasting sound—his head to the floor. "My...my apologies, Your Lordship!" he was back to shouting again. "I was being insolent! Please punish me!"
Goddamnit! Didn’t I tell them to stop being dramatic?!
I groaned and tapped on the hand grabbing my waist. "Natha...Natha!"
The silver eyes, which had been narrowed in a bit of disdain, turned soft as he looked at me. "Mm?"
"Sense my thought," I told him, and then added at his surprised expression. "I’ll allow it for a bit."
The silver eyes blinked for a bit, before turning deeper, and I thought of what I wanted to convey to him; that I’m just curious about his head since I never touched a bald head before.
I didn’t know how much he could read, but it should at least be clear enough with two keywords;
—curiosity, bald head
Pfft—he stifled a laugh suddenly, so I guessed it worked. He even hide his laughing face on my shoulder, shaking for a bit before finally taking hold of himself and excusing the poor vassal on the floor. "Ahem, alright, you can get up now, Caba."
"B-by your command!" the bald demon raised his head in confusion, which only made him look even funnier. I could feel Natha wanting to laugh again and jab his ribs with my elbow.
"Phew," I let out an exasperated breath, but soon had to sigh again. "Stop laughing Lesta."
"I’m...I’m sorry...pfft," like his Lord, Lesta bit his lips to stifle his laugh before making a show of courtesy toward me. "Well, it seems like our lesson need to be postponed, Young Master."
Ah well, at least this one didn’t act so dramatic.

chapters.title: Chapter 95: Pacifying two screaming babies is...not that hard?
chapters.content:
Chapter 95: Pacifying two screaming babies is...not that hard?
"Vaaal!"
*CHIIIIRPPP!!*
What greeted me the moment I set foot inside the tower was two flying objects...err, creatures. The flap of their little wings was enough to create a wind current that blasted the air around me. I would have toppled back if it wasn’t for the sturdy cushion of a Demon Lord behind me.
Jade was one thing, but I didn’t expect Zia to act like this too. With one hand on the fluffy fur, and one hand on the succubus’s shoulder, I patted them gently as their face was buried in my chest.
"So cruel!" Zia lifted her face and barked angrily. "Angwi said you’d only be there for a night! How could you do this to us?!"
*CHIIRP!*
"There’s no message! You didn’t even say goodbye!"
*CHIIRP CHIRP!*
"How could you just leave me like that? Do you know how lonely it is having no one to talk to?!"
*CHIRP!*
Wow...they seemed to become a bit of a buddy-buddy while I was gone. I just let them gush out a series of protests while comfortably leaning on Natha and looking at Angwi, who just shook her head exasperatedly.
But...it felt good though, having someone greet me enthusiastically like this, making me feel like I was coming back home. It felt as good as when Angwi scolded me for coming back late from the forest that one time.
"Okay, okay, I’m sorry," I patted them both as they continued to make noise. "I bring some snacks as a souvenir, though..."
Somehow, that effectively shut them up, as both the purple and green eyes perked up. I took out the big big basket full of snacks that Dhuarta assembled for me, and put it into their outstretched hands.
"Here, help me carry this inside," I told them, and the succubus-elemental bird pair saluted me with sparkling eyes before marching inside with the snacks.
"You’re getting proficient in taming others," Natha commented with a chuckle.
After making sure the two kids already entered the other room, I turned around to stare at the silver eyes, who still looked at me with the same bright affection he gave me all morning.
Oh...I knew I was the one who asked to go back, but now that I had to part with him, it was quite hard too. Harder even, than the time when we only met for the weekend. Perhaps because I had been so used to his presence for days.
"I’ll come in three days, unless the portal finished first," he told me while stroking my hair. "Give me a kiss?" he smiled with a tilted head, acting so charming and innocent.
I narrowed my eyes, feeling like all we did since the morning was just kiss.
But who was I to deny the Demon Lord? So I lifted my heels and gave him a soft peck on the lips, which he returned with a tight embrace. He spent a while burying his face in my hair, taking a deep breath as if inhaling my scent.
Did I...even have a scent?
But then again, Natha also had a scent; the one I always searched on the bed. Thinking that I wouldn’t be able to smell it again in the tower, I also took a chance to sniff at him, inhaling the scent of parchment and sandalwood oil.
He chuckled at my not-so-subtle attempt at sniffing him, and I hit him lightly in response. He replied with a tender kiss on my forehead, before dispersing in a flurry of black feathers again.
Twirling a dark plume between my fingers, I walked toward the two babies in need of appeasing inside.
* * *
"Oh, so you ended up meeting the vassal too, then?" Zia nodded while munching on a beast-shaped biscuit from the pile of snacks.
"Mm," I nodded while caressing Jade’s little head, which had been nuzzling me nonstop with pitiful noises. I took the time to slowly send my mana too, since the little bird had been deprived of food for days. "I didn’t expect it, but I met with five of them."
Zia whistled then. "Conquering half in just a few days, huh?"
"What do you mean conquering?" I threw a package toward her, although the snack just ended up hovering around the succubus like some kind of solar system...a snack system. "I just converse with them for a bit."
"That’s exactly what I meant," Zia wiggled her hand, suddenly acting like a senior in life as if she already forgot how she tackled me with a crying face earlier. "You exchanged friendly conversations; meaning they accepted you. If they don’t, they would just greet you politely as a courtesy."
Hmm...was that how it was?
"But Natha said they are part of the ’friendly’ camp..."
"Meaning they won’t act hostile toward you," Zia explained further. It was fascinating how she could shift from being a teenager to a life consultant—was it because she was, inevitably, an author?
She paused to concentrate on opening a box of sour cotton candy—one of my favorites—before continuing. "Being polite is already enough. But didn’t they ask to meet you again?"
"Well...we also arrange some lessons..."
"See," Zia shrugged. "They didn’t have to, since Lord Cousin didn’t ask for it. That bald...wolf one that you mentioned also comes around on his own, right?"
"Mm..."
"Trust me, Val," Zia waved her fingers and sent a cloud of cotton candy flying toward me. "You have the power to charm others."
I frowned at the hovering cloud in front of my face, before opening my mouth to let it in. While savoring the sweet and sour sensation exploding inside my mouth, I looked at the ceiling while rubbing Jade’s green head absentmindedly. "Is that so?" I muttered quietly.
The power to charm others? What power? Power as the Lord’s bride? Power as the royal druid? They did say demons respect and fear the powerful. I just didn’t think I had that power, however. All I had was status as the Lord’s contracted bride.
But what if the contract was broken? What if I lost the power of priest and druid, again, like how Valmeier lost it a few months ago?
Would they still get charmed? Would they still look at me favorably? Would they still praise me as the Lord’s proud bride?
I...I wasn’t sure.
I knew how it was with people and power. I used to have that power, and enjoyed the way the nurses and doctors took care of me affectionately. Until they deemed I was being abandoned by my family, and they all turned cold and looked at me as a mere job...
*Chiirp!!*
My thought was suddenly interrupted by the little bird, who wasn’t just chirping loudly, but headbutting my cheek. It must have sensed my depressed state and I laughed while scooping the little guy off my cheek before it get bruised.
"I know, I know," I patted the bird again, swallowing my bitter memories. Didn’t I make a promise to myself to let go of such insecurity? "It’s just a short moment of weakness. It won’t happen again," I tried to pacify the anxious bird.
Well, at least I’d try to not think about such a thing anymore.
Jade wasn’t the only one who got anxious though, since I had to face Zia and Angwi’s inquisitive stare next. "What? I’m alright. Things turned out to be better than I expected there, too."
"Hmm..." Zia narrowed her eyes dubiously, but she didn’t pursue it more, thankfully. "Well, you’re right, it’s a good thing anyway."
I nodded in agreement. As far as a trial went, it could be considered a success. I didn’t feel uncomfortable, and I had at least five—no, six if I counted the twins’s older sister, Malta—vassals on my side. It wasn’t like Natha wanted me to attend anything around the Castle too, or faced the citizens.
"But..." Zia folded her legs above the couch and looked at me from behind her knees. "It means...you’ll move there?"
*chirp??*
Jade twitched against my fingers, and suddenly flew toward my face again. I grab it before my cheek got headbutted again, and kept the little guy between my palms. "Don’t worry, I’ll wait until you can follow me."
*chirp!*
Only then that Jade looked cheerful, nuzzling my palm instead of headbutting it. It was easy to see that the little bird was happy, after sulking so much earlier. Even as I gave my mana, Jade was still a bit resentful of being left behind. It was only now that the little bird looked happy.
"What about me?!" Zia slammed her hand on the table, jostling some of the snacks.
I tilted my head with a raised brow. "You want to follow me too?"
"I need someone to talk to!" she pursed her lips and spoke in a desperate voice. I guessed, after months of talking to me, it got hard just spending time with the silent maid.
"You can just live in the Castle too, right?" I tilted my head to the other side.
"Nope, since I’ll be considered a diplomatic guest there, and I don’t like it!"
Right—I often forgot, but she was still the princess of other realms. "Well, you can just use the portal to visit," I shrugged. "Since the mana supply came from the elemental birds, we can use it often."
"Oh? This is the first time I hear about it..." Zia raised her brows, before nodding and mumbling to herself. "Mm, mm, I see...as expected of Lord Cousin, he’s truly meticulous..."
Well, seeing the things he prepared in the Castle for me—from the private quarters to the greenhouse—I could vouch for that meticulousness. Freaking Demon Lord even made a whole media coverage about the kingdom’s filth just so Valmeier’s name could get cleaned. Even building disgustingly expensive portal gates to allow me to traverse my two new homes easily.
Damn, I loved him so much.
"So...what are you going to do now?" Zia cut my worshipping thought.
"Hmm..." to be honest, there were lots of things I needed to do, from evolving Jade to researching pseudo-modern inventions, to checking up on the hero’s movement...
But for now, my priority would be to hasten the moving procedure, which meant...
I looked at Jade, who tilted its head at my gaze. "What do you think about swimming?"

Chapter 96: A fantasy cheat key for someone who never swims in his life is...
"You have to remember the path, Jade," I told the little bird as we followed Doun deeper inside the forest. "I don’t really have a spatial gift, you know."
Jade chirped energetically while hovering beside me. The bird was a bit sulky yesterday, perhaps to express its frustration with my prolonged stay in the Castle. But after I fed it with a lot of mana, and spent the night sleeping beside me on the pillow, Jade was back to being the energetic bird that it was.
And not just energetic, it also became clingy, way more than before.
When the little bird was just born, it stayed with me most of the time, sleeping as close as it could to me. But after evolving once, Jade had this independent streak where it would fly around from time to time or spend time with the older elemental bird instead. It also preferred to sleep on the cushion I prepared above the table below the window—unless Natha came, during which Jade would disdainfully and aggressively peck the Demon Lord once and wordlessly flew away.
But now, the little bird even came with me while I bathe. And while we were walking inside the forest, it stayed hovering around me instead of flying above like the time we frequented that small clearing.
"I think if you ask the trees, they would tell you the way for a bit, Young Master," Doun told me with a smile. "Although you might need to be patient while at it."
Huh? Why? Did they talk in a really loong and slooow way like in the stories?
"They liked to give it in riddles," Doun answered my silent question.
Oh, ouch—I wasn’t good at it. Especially since I had no power of native knowledge. So I looked at Jade and repeated my order sternly, The green orbs looked at me in earnest and the little head swayed up and down, wings flapped quicker as if saying ’leave it to me!’.
Anyway, we went deeper, past the small clearing to the part where the trees were older and higher—so high I couldn’t see the tip clearly. They were big too, with wide leaves that felt like a canopy. The deeper we went, the more it felt as if the world was getting bigger.
"It’s fascinating..." I muttered, feeling not only the trees, but everything around and below with my senses.
Another thing that I started to train was the ability to sense everything even as I did mundane things like walking and staying still. In the book that I read, it said that doing so would help me become more aware of my surrounding. Like how Natha sensed others’ thoughts, I could train to sense nature’s thoughts.
It was of course different from sensing a clear sentience thought, like if I sense Jade’s thought as my familiar. It was more like a collective consciousness, like sensing where the wind wanted to go, or how many fruits a tree wanted to bear.
But with that, I could also sense if there was a disturbance within nature’s course, or if there was something that wasn’t supposed to be there, like intruders. Wouldn’t that be useful for my safety? Not that I was in any danger, but...
"We’re here, Young Master," Doun cut my thought, and I shifted my focus from the fight between a flower and a weed over the soil to the front. There, about a hundred pace from us, I could see the glimmering reflection of sunlight between the fence of trees.
*chirp chirp?*
"Sure," I nodded, and Jade flew away from me for the first time. It should be the little bird’s first time looking at a river too, so I got its excitement.
I mean...I was excited too.
The last time I saw a river was probably during my forgotten childhood, before I was sick. I remembered a bit about going to the countryside—my grandma’s convalescence home, even though it was just her deathbed. There was a river behind the house, if I recalled correctly, and we could see it from the second floor’s balcony.
There was something about this particular memory that tickled my mind, but I couldn’t remember what.
Well, I had no leeway for that too, since soon the full expanse of the river was gracing my vision. And that...that didn’t look like a river.
It was like a road—a road made of water.
It was so wide that I was sure a medium-sized ship would be able to sail there. The river in my imagination—as well as memory—was no more than two or three meters wide. You know, the kind of river where people used to frolic and had a picnic on the side. River that looked like a blue sparkling ribbon, that I could safely enter without any aquatic skill because it would be shallow.
Instead, I got a river people used to do commerce in. Or doing secluded cultivation training.
"It’s huge!" was what came out of my mouth the moment we stepped at the beach—yes, it even had a sandy beach.
"Well, this is the mainstream," Doun explained. "The ones outside the forest are smaller, but that would be outside of the Tower’s territory."
"Oh..."
"Please be careful to not go outside the boundary, Young Master," Doun’s voice turned serious suddenly, and he looked at me with a stern gaze. "The Lord’s protection only worked around the estate."
I blinked at the sudden warning, because it felt like it came out of nowhere. Why would Doun suddenly warn me about going outside when we were literally in the middle of a very vast forest, which was also located in the middle of a mountain?
"Why would I go outside the boundary?" I asked in confusion. Above me, Jade seemed to already finish scouting the place and landed on my head, looking at our interaction with interest.
"Because you are about to train in the water, and you tend to do things excessively,"
The answer only added to my confusion, and I tilted my head the other way. Jade too, tilted its little green head. Looking at my face, Doun took a deep breath and started to explain further. "You know how elementals have their own properties right, Young Master?"
I nodded in response and the demon continued. "Just like how you were ’rooted’ for a long time in the clearing from infusing yourself too much with the wood element, there might be a side effect this time too."
"...what side effect?" I asked carefully, in a quiet voice that was almost like a whisper.
Rather than answering my question immediately, Doun trained his gaze on the river, following its current. "From my grandma’s story, a lot of young druids from the water tribe went missing while having their training alone in the river. Some of them, however, would reappear someday in a completely different part of the region..."
Water tribe...it would be what they called the druid who preferred to mingle with water elementals. As I learned more about druids, I found out there were various tribes with their own specialties. Aside from conforming to their own traits, it was also because aside from those with royal blood, not many could handle more than one or two elements on their own.
Which made this body rather special, I guess? Well, knowing how to manage more than one elemental mana didn’t equal strength, though. The ’real’ royal might have been strong, but someone without proper guidance like me...well, it was just a matter of being a jack of all trades.
Didn’t matter though. It was enough if it could help me survive.
"So...the reason they went missing was...?" I tapped my lips while musing for the answer. From how Doun stared at the river, plus the hint, it wasn’t a hard quiz. If immersing myself in the forest made me rooted to the ground, then immersing myself in the river probably...
"They drifted in the water," Doun voiced out my guess. "The inherent characteristic of water elemental is transformation, so—"
"I could turn into water?!" I gasped. More like...I could turn into liquid?
Doun stared at my surprised yet enthusiastic face before sighing. "Most would need a lot of practice for that, but I have an inkling you’ll just suddenly do that on the first try, Young Master."
"Oh, my God!" I snapped my head back to look at the wide river. I was getting worried looking at the deep and huge place since...well, I had no idea how to swim.
But...but! If I could transform my body, making it aquatic...surely, there was no such thing as ’drowning water’, right?
*chirp?*
Sensing the spike in my energy, Jade flapped its wings enthusiastically, although I didn’t think the little bird understood much.
"I get that you’re excited, but I have to warn you that transformation is very dangerous in the first phase," Doun cleared his throat to get my focus back. "Your mind might get trapped and absorbed in the current, forgetting yourself, forgetting to turn back. That’s why those young druids went missing."
Ooh...
Well, it made sense. Just like how I forgot about the time during my first purification, staying still for hours even though it only felt like a few minutes—like the trees who saw time differently from other mortals. I guess, every ability had its own drawbacks.
That being said...
"You know a lot about this, Doun," I looked at the demon with a grin. He knew more than the book even, considering druids were rather recluse and not much known in detail about them.
At my words, the demon looked flustered for a bit, before replying with a smile. "Ah, well, I looked up my grandmother’s notes after your first time in the forest, Young Master."
Hmm? So he tried to find out more about druids?
"...huh? For...for me?"
With a slightly embarrassed chuckle, Doun shrugged. "I would like to be of help, Young Master."
Ah...looking at him, I was reminded of Natha’s vassals in the Castle. They were such kind and nice souls that kept making me feel like I finally earned a home in this foreign land.
"Ahem—I don’t think you’ll back down even after what I told you, so I’ll keep guard this time, Young Master," Doun spoke swiftly to hide his growing embarrassment, although I had no idea why he should feel embarrassed about that.
So I just laughed and thanked him, before shifting my focus back to the river.
Now, how should we do this?

chapters.title: Chapter 97: Triggering forgotten memories in another world
chapters.content:
Chapter 97: Triggering forgotten memories in another world
The river almost felt like a lake, but it was beautiful regardless. The canopy of leaves that obstructed the sky over the forest seemed to give way to the blue ribbon, letting the sunlight bounce across the body of water. It sparkled in pretty light, clear enough for fish to swim about. It was so clear that I could see the colorful stones below, giving the illusion that the river was shallow enough for a casual dip.
It wasn’t.
It was deep, at least more than two meters, definitely enough to drown me. But the current was calm, since we weren’t on a steep land. Still, I told Jade to be careful not to dive into the water. At least, not until the little bird absorbed the purified mana.
To be honest, I still had no idea how to go about this thing. So I just did what I usually do; finding a place to sit and dispersing my consciousness. Unlike with the clearing, where it had a conventional ’chair’ for me to use, there was nothing like that here. So I just plopped down on the riverside, and took off my shoes so I could dip my feet inside the water.
"Oof—" the moment my skin touched the water, a shiver ran through my spine. "I guess I should have gone here during the summer..."
Perhaps because the Lair had a temperature and weather control formation, even while the season changed, I didn’t really feel the shift. I felt the heat and the cold, the rain and wind, but it was always in moderation, like the subdued version of what was really happening outside. Even while going outside, Angwi always made sure I was dressed well, to make sure my body temperature was well maintained.
Wow...now that I think about it, they really took care of me, huh?
"Well, we’re in the mountain after all," Doun reminded me of another fact.
"Hmm..."
Putting my legs deeper into the water, I watched my reflection on the water’s surface while musing. "I thought I’m getting immune to cold because of Natha, but..."
Doun crouched on the sandy beach beside me while responding. "His Lordship’s coldness probably feels comfortable for you, right, Young Master?"
I turned to look at him with curiosity, and he added with a sheepish smile. "It’s because you don’t fear him."
"Oh?"
Perhaps because he saw my intrigued eyes, Doun continued without me needing to ask. "His Lordship’s ’coldness’ isn’t a physical one. It affected one’s mind by drawing one’s fear. The more someone fears him, the more uncomfortable that ’coldness’ feels."
Ah, so that was the answer to one of my trivial thought; about why I had never been bothered by Natha’s cold skin despite still shivering at the normal decrease in temperature.
"But of course, it’s also because His Lordship treasure you so much, Young Master. There’s no way he would cast Nightmare’s inherent trait on you," Doun added with a smile and a little wink, prompting me to turn my gaze back to the water. But even the river teasingly reflected my blushing cheek with clarity. Ugh...Let’s just focus on the training.
I scooped up Jade, who was sunbathing in my lap, and stared at the little bird. I was thinking of holding Jade in my hands, just like every time I fed it mana. But knowing about the possible side effect worried me; what if I really transmorphed and dragged this little guy underwater without noticing it?
"You stay with Doun for now, okay?" I told the little bird sternly, and received a flustered chirping.
Again, my cheek was getting headbutted, and my lips had to taste the tickling wings. But I sent Jade my concerned thought telepathically, and the bird finally relented. It dejectedly flew to the demon’s head, making the brown hair a nest while letting out a quiet whimpering sound.
Acting pitiful and adorable...where did you learn such a thing from, huh?
I tore my gaze away from Jade and focused back on the river. Taking a deep breath, I withdrew the senses I spread toward my surroundings earlier, and focused them on the water. More precisely, I focused on the mana circuits of my legs, and branched them out.
Unlike the plants, water had no sentient thought. It was an archaic form of life, and I had to immerse myself deeper than usual. Felt every drop of water, every molecule, every atomic structure and everything in between.
Different from before, I wanted to focus entirely on the water elemental, which meant I had to ignore other life forces, from the underwater creatures to the wriggling bacteria. It took a whole lot more focus than before. Slithering toward the water, chasing the cold feeling that felt different from Natha.
As my consciousness was flowing down and getting sucked into the river, I started to understand why the young druids went lost and missing. Hmm...wasn’t I considered a young druid too? I was still in my early twenties after all. By druid standards, I would be considered a juvenile, actually, just like Zia.
But "I" in my previous life was definitely an adult already, and as a human in this world, Valmeier had already been considered an adult since he was fifteen years old, which was when he started going down the mountain.
That damn kingdom, sending a boy in his teens to deal with dirty work and killing demons from the shadow...even went so far as to slander his name...It kind of made me want to burn them to the ground—
Ah, I digressed. See, like that. It was hard to focus on an objective when we tried to emulate something that wasn’t sentient. Because instead of peeking into their life, we were peeking into ourselves inside.
