"We haven’t finished the training ground and the research chamber, but other than that, we’re ready, my Liege," as usual, the only one we could count on to give a serious answer was Malta. "Young Master’s dressing room should be finished tomorrow."
My what--no, wait, there was something else there. What did she say again? Training ground? Research chamber?
Looking at my confused face, Natha immediately gave me an explanation. "Didn’t you say you need somewhere to train with weapons?"
"Oh...you’ll provide me with that?" I replied with brows raised in surprise.
[!]
I looked at my left arm which suddenly vibrated slightly. It had been a while since Alveitya made a fuss, so I was slightly surprised. Jade, too, who seemed to be able to perceive the Spear now, looked up and jumped into my left hand, nudging the mark on my palm as if trying to talk with the Spear.
Naturally, the other demons stared at me in interest. "Does it get excited?" Natha asked with a smile, and I only nodded affirmatively, because the Spear wanted to get out and I didn’t think a dining room full of demons was a good place to take out a tool that was used to slaughter demons, so I had to suppress this sentient weapon.
"What is?" Arta asked curiously, even leaning to the table, looking at me with sparkling eyes.
Natha, with a mischievous smile, answered casually. "The Spear of Judgment,"
"Hiek!" Arta pulled herself away from the table--away from me. Caba widened his eyes and even though it was subtle, I could see Lesta and Malta tensed up.
But when I blinked my eyes in surprise at their reaction, Arta immediately scrambled to wave her hands and shook her head, looking panicked and apologetic. "N-no, I didn’t mean--it’s not...It’s just a name that invokes fear, Young Master--no, I mean...I’m not saying you’re scary, it’s just..."
She stuttered, much like Caba when he thought I left the Castle because of him. "It’s fine, I understand..."
I mean...I also hated the Spear at first, when I knew it was the one who caused Natha’s wound. So I understood their instinctual aversion. After all, Caba even tried to kill me the first time because of it.
Talking about the bald demon, he was lowering his gaze, although I could see his hardened eyes. Even though he no longer kept resentment toward me, it probably still hard knowing the weapon he hated was essentially in the same room.
"No, it’s not fine," Malta shook her head. "We shouldn’t be surprised about your sacred weapon. It seems that we still lack training, so forgive us, Young Master."
"...uh, okay?" I nodded, but also made another mental note to avoid taking out Alveitya in front of friendly demons.
Natha patted my arm, and nudged Jade away so he could take my hand. "It’s quite unfortunate, but that Spear does have a lethal property for those designated as ’enemy’ by the Master," he rubbed the ownership mark on my palm. "And it has such... a dark history with demons, so..."
"So it means, as long as the Master doesn’t see us as an enemy..." Lesta smiled across from me, letting his words hang in the air.
"It’s not like I’ll just swing it around willy-nilly," I pursed my lips slightly. Yeah, their reaction toward the Spear was understandable, but what made me surprised before was that it felt like they thought I’d just take Alveitya out and let it rampage in the room.
Natha chuckled and caressed the back of my hand. "I know," he smiled sweetly, "You have better control of the Spear too now, so it wouldn’t move by itself even if it has sentience--unless you’re in danger, that is."
Right--I nodded in agreement. Even the Spear’s appearance had changed, looking more like a scepter with a deadly tip. It had been very nice and quiet inside my mana core, unlike the boisterous Jade.
"Anyway, I decided that you’ll need a special place to train, so you won’t have to mind people’s stares," Natha explained to me further. "As for the research room..." he pressed his thumb on my finger pads, stroking them gently. "You’ve been busy tinkering with that weird inventions."
I gasped. "That too?" what other reaction could I give besides that?
But is it alright to provide me with that much space? I could just do that kind of thing anywhere though; in the living room, or bedroom, or my little corner in the greenhouse...
Although I guessed it would be inconvenient if I made a mess in those rooms, huh? That might be why. Even so, preparing all of those just for me...surely there were other things those rooms could be used for--something more substantial than a single man’s hobby.
"Isn’t that rather excessive?" I looked at Natha with a slight frown.
"Hmm...it seems like our Young Master still doesn’t know what kind of person His Lordship was," Lesta suddenly said, looking at me with a deep smile and curled eyes.
It wasn’t just Lesta though; Arta was grinning widely, and even Malta let out a subtle smile. Caba was the only one whose face didn’t change--but it was because the bald demon was suddenly having a staring contest with the little elemental bird, that had been feeling neglected for the last few minutes.
I tilted my head in confusion, and Natha relieved it with a soft chuckle. "I’m not using taxpayer money, don’t worry," he patted my head in reassurance.
"That’s...good?" I replied slowly, still perplexed by the situation. I mean...yeah, it was good that he didn’t use taxpayer money, but that wasn’t really my concern.
I just realized suddenly how much money he must have used just to facilitate this move, just for me to stay here. From the construction of the portal gate to all of these rooms...how much would it cost?
"Yes, don’t worry, Young Master. His Lordship built everything with his own money!"
"Mm, it’s just a chump change for His Lordship," Caba finally decided to give his voice to the discussion.
Chump change, huh--perhaps I should ask Natha how wealthy he actually was one day.
"That’s an exaggeration," Lesta shook his head and sighed. "It’s not just ’chump change’, but it’s indeed not something that will hurt His Lordship’s finance. More importantly, it’s money well spent--right, my Lord?"
"Mm,"
Natha hummed with a casual smile, looking at me with every intention of telling me that the money he spent for me was never a waste.
Gods--I wasn’t a Rapunzel anymore, but a freaking Cinderella, huh?
Here, in this Castle, I was just his bride. His...possession. It felt weird knowing that I would have my own private room; a room I could call my own, built for me. Because even when I was the only one who use the suite in the Lair, it was essentially still Natha’s space, right?
But now...how do I put this; I could have my own mancave?!
Wow...I wouldn’t lie; I was actually so happy that I would kiss Natha if there was no one else at the table.
That being said, it was kind of weird to receive something when I practically did nothing but eat, play, and sleep. It was hard to think that I deserve such treatment, even though I knew Natha did it out of affection.
"Irregardless, there’s nothing excessive about it, unless you decided not to use those rooms," Natha brought my hand up and kissed my knuckles. "Which would mean they become useless."
And then he leaned down, whispering to my ear. "Just learn to get used to receiving something for granted."
"You’ll turn me into a spoiled man..."
"Just as how I want it,"
Damn.
Uhh...well, then...I had no choice but to accept them, I guessed.

chapters.title: Chapter 114: Between cotton candy and a soft place
chapters.content:
Chapter 114: Between cotton candy and a soft place
"You said two weeks!"
This time, Zia really was angry. She was sulking so much and refused to get out of her rooms ever since she knew I was going through the portal with Jade in tow. Like now, I had been talking to her through the door.
Well, with me and Jade leaving the Lair, it would mean she lost her two friends, and the tower would go back to how it was before I arrived--which, according to her, was boring. I remembered how it was after my only friend in the past, that author girl died, so I understood her a little bit.
"But it’s not like I go far? You can just visit me through the portal?" I reasoned with her. "I will leave my communication orb here, so you can call me whenever."
"But you won’t be physically here!" she argued. "What...what if I want to talk with you in the middle of the night? What if I want to discuss something after dinner--you won’t even be here during dinner! I’m going to have to eat alone again!"
Haa...I let out a long sigh. Even Jade only chirping sadly, putting its wings on the door. I guessed these two had really bonded.
"Come on, at least let me see your face? Jade also want to see you, right?" I looked at the sad-looking bird, who was chirping loudly in response.
Zia did not make any move for a long time, and I just crouching in front of the door with Jade, waiting. When I finally hear a shuffling sound inside, I scooped the little bird into my hands and the door clicked open not long after.
"Just so you know," the purple orbs glared at both of us, but the words were directed at Jade. "You’re a traitor too."
[Ung...]
Jade lowered its head guiltily--poor bird, it probably didn’t account for separation with a friend to be included in moving out with me. Zia stomped into her room, and I took it as permission to enter.
If you should know, her room was exactly how I imagine a teenager’s room would be; cluttered with random things, colorful, with posters of her favorite musicians. The bookcase standing quietly in the corner did not prevent the pile of books to exist on the floor, and the many crumpled papers of manuscripts told me she still struggling with her new book.
"Sit."
She threw herself onto the velvet couch that bore so many pillows it looked like a cushy fortress, hugging a big slime plushie with a sulking face. Her lower lip jutted out, and her brow furrowed deep. Jade jumped from my hands and flew to one of the pillows, nudging the succubus with its wing.
I pressed my lips to swallow a sigh while looking at her. What should I do? I never had a younger sister to be reasoned with before. And technically...she was older than me, wasn’t she?
"Hey, look," I started. "It’s not like I’ll never go back you know."
"Liar!"
"Really!" I chuckled at how Jade decided to fly to Zia’s hair and pecked on it. "This place is still the best for me to train my druid skill. Don’t you know that’s why Natha build the portal in the first place? It’s so I can go back and forth with ease."
I could see the jutted lip retracted for a bit, but she still looked madly sulked. "But still..."
"You can call me if you want to meet, and I’ll go here with Jade--right?" I asked the bird, who chirped energetically in response. "Or you can go over there. We’ll just stay in the greenhouse like the last time if you don’t want to be in the castle."
"Hnn..." she gripped her plushie and stared at me through the synthetic fur. "But...what if I want to see you and you are with Lord Cousin? You will certainly choose him over me..."
Wow...people truly assumed I only thought of Natha all day, huh? Not that they were wrong. "He’s busy working during the day, so we can always meet and talk then," I told her while taking out the communication orb that Natha gave me back then and putting it on the table. "Here, I’ll take the one in Natha’s possession, so you can call me whenever, okay? Besides...is it so wrong of me to want to spend time with someone I love? You’re a romance writer, so you should know about this."
"Ugh..."
"On that topic..." I looked over to the bookcase, where it held a number of books. I could see Zia’s pen name carved there. "I promise to read all your books, alright? So stop making a fuss."
And by ’fuss’ I meant sealing the door leading up to the portal gate.
My promise about reading her books got the succubus perked up. "Really? You promise?"
"Mm," I nodded. Romance books really weren’t my thing, but of course, I’d try reading my friend’s book. "Eruha will give me an advanced lecture on demonese, so I’ll be able to read them soon."
Now, the frown on her forehead had vanished, and Jade tapped on her hair with soft chirping. She pressed her lips for a few seconds, before grumbling quietly. "Well, I supposed you do need to be there to learn more..."
I laughed softly and leaned back on the chair. Jade flew over to me then, after making sure Zia wasn’t angry anymore. The bird perched on my shoulder, nuzzling my cheek with its round head.
"You know..." I looked outside the window, where I could still see the cotton candy cloud and the elemental bird flying about. It reminded me of my first time coming here, and it filled me with nostalgia. "This is the first place that I can call home."
And I didn’t mean just in this world. In my previous world too, there was nowhere I could call home; not the house filled with arguing sounds, or the cold and lonely hospital ward.
"So there’s no way I will completely leave this place. Not when this is Natha’s Lair, not when this is where Jade was born, and not when this is where I got my first friend," my lips stretched on their own. It kind of hit me then, that I would truly leave this place and live in the castle. "This is still where I belong, Zia, in this tower."
The succubus, without me realizing it, had stood in front of me, and reached out her hands to my face. "Okay," she spoke softly, lips trembling and eyes glazed. "Okay, don’t cry."
She wiped the tears that I didn’t even know had dropped from my eyes. Was that why Jade had been nuzzling my cheek and chirping low? It seemed like my familiar felt it before I did--the sadness that I didn’t expect before.
Perhaps because my mind was getting occupied with a lot of things--from the euphoria of having Jade evolved, to all that incident about getting sucked inside a divine abode and the moving process--I hadn’t really looked inside myself these days.
And it was such a confusing feeling. Of course, the thought of living with Natha, seeing him every morning and every night, eating and sleeping and talking and doing all mundane things with him on a daily basis...it filled me with wonderful thoughts. I felt happy, I felt excited about the new adventures in a new place, of interacting with my other new friends.
But this place...this tower, this Lair, was the place where I first felt like I was accepted. It was the first place where I felt I could move without any pain in my body, where I could run around without fainting, where I could eat whatever I want, however much I could. It was a place that never cease to be warm even when the weather started to get cold. Never cease to be beautiful.
It was the place where I finally felt like I was alive.
So even when I felt excited and happy about living with Natha, I also felt sad about leaving this place. It would be best if Natha could just live here instead of the Lord Castle, but even I couldn’t afford to be that greedy.
And I realized more and more that Natha knew about this conflict brewing inside me. Wasn’t that why he built that portal gate in the first place? Because he knew I wouldn’t be able to lose my attachment to this place.
That realization, in turn, just made me fall even more, and no matter how attached I was to this place, I still wanted to be with Natha.
But...wasn’t this wonderful?
To think I would be in this position where I felt sad about choosing between heaven and paradise. My old withering body could never.
"I’m just...going to have more adventures for a while. That’s okay, right?"
Zia didn’t answer with words. She just hugged me tight and nodded against my shoulder.
"I’ll visit often, okay?"
"Okay," she finally replied weakly.
"You can call me anytime, okay?"
"Okay,"
I could feel Jade’s confusion about my state of mind, and I laughed while patting the green head. The bird must felt both my happiness and sadness mingling inside, and wondering how could that be possible. Jade probably wondered if it should cheer me up or be excited with me, when Zia was crying silently, and tears were glazing my eyes.
It was fine. It was confusing to me too.
"Can I use your story for my book?" she asked suddenly, face still buried in my shoulder.
I couldn’t help but laugh at that, and the persisting sadness seemed to be blown away at that. "Something like interracial romance?"
"...that’s a new word. Can I use it?"
"You have to ask Natha for permission regarding the story," I patted her side and she retreated, sighing, probably knowing the difficulty in that. The mood was dipping slightly again, so I clasped my hands to gain their attention. "Hey, you know what--why don’t we have a party?"
Zia widened her eyes, and responded in a sharp whisper. "You mean like lots of snacks and drinks kind of party?"
[Candies?!]
"Yeah. You can play that band’s recording too, and we’ll play lots of games, and we won’t sleep until we’re satisfied!" somehow, my voice also turned into a whisper, as if we were talking about conspirational things.
"Just the three of us? Here?"
"Yup," I nodded firmly, before pausing in contemplation. "Unless you want to invite others, like Angwi or--"
"No!" Zia immediately shook her head, and Jade, who was now perching on the succubus’s hair, also followed suit. Both of them wore a panic expression and honestly, it was adorable. "J-just us three! Just us!"
Well, of course, I was only joking. I could already see the stony, unimpressed face of the silent maid just at the mention of the word ’party’.
"Alright," I nodded, putting my hands on Zia’s shoulder and looking at both the young succubus and the little elemental bird. "Let’s do this."

chapters.title: Chapter 115: Leaving the nest is always an emotional process
chapters.content:
Chapter 115: Leaving the nest is always an emotional process
"Sweetheart,"
Oh, how nice it was, waking up to the sweet voice of Natha. I immediately rolled to my side, chasing the source of the voice--and almost falling off the couch.
Ugh--damn, I forgot that I was sleeping in Zia’s bedroom. Ot rather...I passed out. The mischievous girl was somehow able to smuggle some wines from the cellar, and somehow, we ended up donning a few bottles on our own.
"Be careful there," thankfully, the voice wasn’t just a fragment of my imagination or drunken stupor. I felt Natha’s cold hand supporting my body, and carefully shifting me back to the couch.
Slowly, I blinked my eyes and took the chaotic condition of the bedroom; mainly from candy wrappers and snack packaging though. Oh, and empty bottles. Also, a lot of pillows and blankets from other rooms since we built a fortress last night--Angwi would be sooo pissed about this.
I looked up and blinked again to make sure it was really my Demon Lord in front of me. "Natha?"
"How are you feeling?" Natha crouched down and brushed my hair aside.
"Mm...a bit queasy..."
He chuckled in response and procured a glass of water from who knows where, which I accepted with gratitude. I looked around while drinking, spotting Zia and Jade sleeping while holding into each other on the bed. I almost laughed at that and choked in the process.
"Seems like you’re still drunk," Natha laughed softly while patting my back and taking the glass before I dropped it. "Why are you drinking so much when you can’t hold your liquor?"
I contemplate the question for a bit before answering with a grin. "Because it’s a party!"
Natha laughed again and patted my hair. "Alright," he took my hands and hauled me up. "Let’s get you better, shall we?"
My feet landed on the soft pink fur carpet wobbly, and I gripped Natha’s arms with a giggle to balance myself. "Carry me!" I raised my hands and Natha picked me up without a second thought.
"I’m going to do that already," he told me with a smile, as I circled my arms around his neck and leaned my head into his shoulder, feeling giddy and happy for no reason other than the Demon Lord’s unexpected appearance.
...huh? Right--why did Natha here? I lifted my head and stared at his handsome face as he carried me through the hall and tilted my head in confusion. "Why are you here?"
"To undo the naughty seal and help you pack,"
He answered so nonchalantly that it got me taken aback. Oh, right! I was supposed to move out tomorrow, which meant I had to finish packing my things today. Err...actually, I was supposed to do it yesterday, but Zia’s tantrum and our impromptu party occupied my mind instead.
"I’ve told Angwi to take care of your personal stuff in the suite, and you can tell me about the other."
"Other?"
"Don’t you want to bring over some books?"
"Oh, right!" I nodded enthusiastically, but got a headache right after, so I stopped and groaned into his shoulder. He chuckled and patted my waist which he held gently, for some reason chose to climb the stair rather than take the elevator or teleport as usual.
And it got me...and it got me time to ponder and feel. Those feelings that I shove away with the small silly party and everything. With every step that Natha took, my fingers clutched his clothes tighter.
"Natha..."
"Mm?"
"If you get tired of me one day, can I still live here? I don’t need to stay in the suite, but can I take one of the guest rooms?"
He paused his step for a moment, but immediately walked again like nothing happened. His hand, which was still on my side, patted me again, as if pacifying an unreasonable child.
"Don’t be silly, that kind of thing won’t happen," he said with a scoff. I was about to protest and shouted ’IF’, but he already spoke again. "But if someday, somehow, I was inflicted with a curse or an illness that makes me crazy and forget you--because that’s the only possible explanation, that I turn crazy--I already told Angwi to take you away and ensure your safety. You can ask her to stay here if you want, then."
I gripped his clothes tighter. "Promise?"
"I promise. You can ask Angwi if you want to make sure."
"Mm," I pressed my face on his neck, feeling my heart heating up, as if there was a flame burning out some unknown fears left behind there. And I felt so much lighter because of it.
I was glad...I was glad that Natha still answered my silly, stupid question. I was glad that he accepted my anxiety, even if he could not understand it. Of course, I hoped we never had to go through that dreadful future, but knowing that even when it happened I would still have a place to come back to, made me feel safer.
"I like this place," I mumbled, feeling dizzy and a bit sleepy, but also content in Natha’s embrace.
"I will be disappointed if you don’t," Natha laughed at my remark. "I built this place for you, after all."
"Huh?" I replied dazedly; hearing him but not really registering his words.
But Natha did not reply to me, just patting my side while carrying me through another set of stairs. I had no leeway to think about it further, since I drifted to sleep again, until Natha put me down in front of the washbasin and helped me sober up.
* * *
I didn’t regain my full cognition until I got my usual morning herbal drink. At that point, Natha had somehow washed my face, changed my clothes, and seated me at the dining table.
That first sip of warm herbal drink immediately cleared the haziness left in my mind, and I drank it up in one go. The hot and slightly spicy soup that the servants prepared helped me further, so by the time I finished breakfast, I got rid of my hangover.
Thankfully, I didn’t throw up again this time.
With refreshed mind, I walked around the tower with Natha to tell him what I wanted to bring to the castle; mainly just books from the library. Natha would tell me which one was already available in the castle, and which one hadn’t. It took us a lot of time to go through the whole library, and it was only after we were done that I realized Natha was here during working hours.
When I asked him, he told me that he had a leeway now, since he wouldn’t have to go back and forth so much like before, which made me feel kind of guilty. But it also convinced me even more that this decision of moving to the castle to be with him was the correct one.
Anyway, you know what was one of the best things about living in a magical world? Convenience.
Moving company? What was that when we had a perfectly spacious dimensional storage bag? For simplicity purposes, I’d call it inventory--so I could pretend I was in an RPG game or something. With just a swish of a hand, the cases and footlockers filled with books and trinkets were sucked into the void just like that.
And boy...I had no idea I owned that many clothes. Where were they even came from? I definitely never shop for those before. Except for special occasions, the golems were the ones who usually prepared my clothes, readying them in the dressing room while I took a bath. They would prepare several sets of outfits for me to choose from, but I had no idea where exactly they kept all of those.
Now that I thought about it, I always wore different outfits each day, except for my nightshirt. Seemed like it was true, that if we didn’t see it, we wouldn’t realize it. Since the entirety of my closet was obscured from me, I didn’t realize Natha had provided me with a whole clothing shop for a closet.
And he told me to just bring something casual that I liked best because there was already another dressing room full of clothes personally for me in the castle.
Yes, my Lord, I understood how wealthy you were.
Of course, I didn’t forget to pack those failed products that would become my long time project now. Natha gave me my own dimensional storage ring, by the way, yay! I could shove as much as Jade’s candies over there.
Zia also hastily put together all of her novels and tied them prettily with some ribbons before putting them into my hands. The fierce look in her eyes told me that she would give me quizzes on them to check if I really read the books.
Guessed I really needed to read them thoroughly then.
That night, we held another party; a normal dinner party this time. Angwi had seated the three of us and given us a silent lecture about how bad we were eating all of those candies and unhealthy snacks and drinking all of those wines. So we only had a big dinner, with all the demons residing in the tower eating together.
Doun, who had been the closest to me aside from Angwi, told me with a sad face that he’d wait for my next training session, and gave me all of the notes he made based on what his grandmother told him about the druids. Even the golems made the dinner filled with my favorite foods.
It was all jolly but also weird because it felt like they were sending me off to another continent while in fact, I was only going to the Capital, which could be reached in two seconds by the portal gate.
But I guessed...that was what made it feel like home.
Lastly, I took Jade first thing in the morning the next day and climbed to the rooftop, bidding goodbye to the elemental birds. Especially for Jade, who would be, essentially, leaving its nest. It became some kinda rite of passage for Jade, as the other adult birds surrounded the juvenile bird and they pressed their forehead against Jade’s. It was fascinating watching the pattern on their head glowed with each process. In the end, the elder elemental bird--the one who gave me Jade’s essence--pressed its forehead on mine, and I understood that they asked me to take care of their youngest.
And then, we walked through that gate again.

chapters.title: Chapter 116: You can expect a merchant to pull bullshit negotiation even with a child
chapters.content:
Chapter 116: You can expect a merchant to pull bullshit negotiation even with a child
Thankfully, I didn’t get sucked anywhere this time, and safely crossed the gate.
Natha had waited for me in the garden, and once I saw him...I don’t know--I just ran over and hugged him, laughing joyfully. I didn’t even know what I was laughing about; that there was no incident even though I stepped through the gate alone? That I would officially start a new adventure by living here?
Anyway, I just felt happy, and even Jade did not chirp in protest at how I jumped at Natha first thing, probably sensing the joy inside my heart.
"Welcome," Natha whispered against my lips, as if it was my first time there, with silver eyes sparkling beautifully under the sun.
Jade gave us about a minute long for intimacy, before finally chirping in protest and demanding attention. This time, Natha relented easily without even insulting the little bird, which made me rather suspicious.
And my suspicion was proved not long after.
Once we arrived at the Lord’s private quarters, Natha immediately took us somewhere I hadn’t seen before. Somewhere near the pantry where the servants prepared our meals that came from the kitchen, was a small circular staircase leading up. It led to somewhere even further up from the bedroom, as if we were going to an attic.
Wait--were we actually...?
But when we arrived at the end of the stairs, what I found was a room that felt like a fairyland--you know, like the one in D**ne* or something.
It was a room, but with a very tall ceiling that it almost felt like an open space. The window was a stone arch that allowed us to look at the scenery outside, and with another window at the top, the room was flooded with more than enough sunlight. And then there was the content of the room;
Greeneries, ivy, and climbing roses replaced the wallpaper; soft grass covered the floor like a carpet; an artificial waterfall surrounded by white stones flowed to a small pond filled with sparkling little flowers; shrubbery shaped like a bed and small, stout trees that seemed to be perfect for birds to...
No way.
I turned my head to stare at Natha, who was hiding his smile as Jade dazedly hovered into the space, as if being hypnotized. The little bird flew and perched on the stout, bonsai-like tree, and chirped at me.
[Master, sit here!]
With its little foot, Jade pointed to a cradle made of wood and roots and ivy, hanging from the ceiling. It was obvious that the swing-like cradle was made for me, but the room was for Jade. I stepped into the soft grass that suspiciously felt real, and gently took a seat on the cradle. Jade jumped off the branch and landed on my lap--we could see outside the window clearly from here, and we might be able to see the stars at night.
I could hear Natha approaching from behind, but his voice arrived first. "Since Jade is no longer a child, it should have its own room."
[What? This Jade room?] the little bird chirped in shock, the beady eyes looked even bigger as it turned around to stare dumbfoundedly at Natha. [Nightmare give Jade room?!]
How funny. The little bird was more shocked at the notion of Natha gave it something rather than the room itself.
"Here, do you see this lever?" Natha touched a handle jutted out from behind the climbing ivy, shaped like your average random branch. But there was a little bell hanging at the end of it, and when Natha pulled it down, the bell made a small sound. "If you pulled it down like this, someone will send you sli--jellies."
[Jelly?!]
Just then, we could hear the sound of footsteps from the stairs, and all of us just waited wordlessly, even Jade. And when a servant came up with a covered plate in his hand, Jade flapped its wings and hovered in the air energetically.
The servant was stunned for a second, before smiling slightly and putting the plate down on a ’table’ that was shaped like a log. Once he uncovered the plate, Jade instantly dove into the jelly, while the servant bowed once before retreating.
"You can ask for them however much you want. Just be considerate at night, because the servants need their sleep too," Natha said with a benevolent smile that not only got Jade open its beak in shock, but also me.
[Nightmare so weird!] see, even Jade became suspicious. [Why Nightmare so kind to Jade?]
"As you said, you’re not a child anymore," still with that kind and charming smile, Natha continued his bullshit. "It means you have to sleep in your own place and be able to order your own food, like a proper adult. Only children sleep with their Master and demand to be taken care of, right?"
[Ungg...really?] Jade tilted its head in confusion and dilemma.
"Like Zidoa--she sleeps alone and orders her food by herself, right?"
The beady green eyes narrowed, but Jade could also see the logic behind Natha’s explanation. [Succubus sleep alone...because succubus not a child?]
"Yes, whatever you’re thinking right now, it’s probably true," Natha nodded in agreement, which prompted Jade to roll around the plate of jelly in deep contemplation, as I looked at the Demon Lord with narrowed eyes.
You...you just want Jade to stay away from the bedroom, weren’t you?
Natha glanced at me, and returned my gaze with a wink. Haa...I couldn’t believe this Demon Lord use trickery and deceit just to secure private bedroom time.
Should I help him a little bit?
"Woow...so cool!" I clapped my hands. Jade immediately stopped rolling and jumped to its feet, staring at me, so I continued clapping while swallowing my giggles. "You have your own room! Like a proper adult! Wow!"
"Wooow..." the Demon Lord, the center of this trickery, had the audacity to clap his hands too, even looked earnest while at it.
Jade was confused, but the bird knew from me and Zia that clapping meant something good and done when we were happy, so the confusion soon turned to joy, and the little bird jumped happily with loud chirping.
[Jade no child!] this time, the sentence wasn’t uttered in annoyance, but glee. [Jade have room!]
"Mm, yes, you have your own room now," I nodded in agreement. "It means you’ll sleep here, you do understand that, right?"
[Mm...Jade want to be with Master] the little bird whined lowly for a second, head dipped in sadness. But then, the green head lifted up and Jade put on a soldier’s face. [But adult sleep alone!]
Oh, God--it was so hard to keep myself from laughing out loud, my poor innocent baby. "Yes, that’s right. Grown-ups sleep alone."
Jade nodded its head firmly. But then, after a few seconds, while I got up from the cradle, the bird threw out a difficult question.
[But why Master and Nightmare always sleep together?]
* * *
"Is there a book on parenting or something here?"
Lesta and Eruha paused to look at me, blinking at the unexpected question. We were on a break in the middle of my linguistic lesson with them, so my question probably felt like it came out of nowhere. But we were in the library, so...
"I didn’t know you already have a child with His Lordship..."
"What are you talking about?" I rolled my eyes at their display of shocked faces. "We’re physically incapable to make a child on our own."
Eruha raised his brow, somewhat dubiously, and chuckled at my response, before finally asking me in earnest. "So why are you looking for that kind of book, Young Master?"
"It’s for Jade..."
"Your familiar?" Lesta tilted his head in even more confusion. "Why would you need a parenting book for an elemental bird?"
I bit the inside of my cheek and recalled the question Jade threw out yesterday, which got me and even Natha quite flustered. In the end, Natha ran away to go back to his office, and I had to distract the bird with the jelly and a little candy bribe.
"Jade had become more talkative now that it can express its thought in words, and become...more curious," I let out a sigh. "It’s getting harder answering those questions."
The two demons looked at each other and leaned closer. Lesta, especially, narrowed his eyes and asked in a quiet voice. "What questions?"
I bit my lips in hesitation, before answering slowly. "Things like...why do I sleep with Natha in the same bed, or...why do we...kiss and...things like that..."
The room was silent after that, and when I looked at them, the two demons were pressing their lips. "Just laugh, why don’t you?" I pursed my lips, feeling the heat creeping on my cheeks.
Lesta stood up instead, and in a trembling, subdued voice, told me that he was going to try looking for the book in the library before bolting out of the private room we used as our mini-class. Since the room was sound-proofed, I couldn’t hear anything after he closed the door, but I bet he was laughing his ass out there.
Hmph--I prayed for the chief librarian to find him and box his ear for that.
Eruha was calmer about it, but I still saw the way he pressed his twitching lips together. After looking at my pouting lips, he finally let out a chuckle and diverted the topic.
"Here, Young Master, why don’t you try to read this while we wait for Eta?" he shoved a book in front of me. "This is a material they used to teach in school here. It’s written in simpler words and structure so it can be understood by the youngsters."
Oh, that should be nice. My comprehension had already gone past the children’s book, but yet at the level where I could read normal books, much less those academic theses that Eruha set as the goal. The school book should be in the middle, in terms of difficulty.
As I picked up the book, it felt lighter and I found out it wasn’t bound and covered in studded leather as the other, perhaps to lower the cost. The title printed on the hardcover was the history of the demon realm, which got me raising my brows in response.
"Perhaps you would like to read the shorter and simpler version of His Lordship’s adventure."

chapters.title: Chapter 117: The advantage of a high profile partner is you can find out about them through the media
chapters.content:
Chapter 117: The advantage of a high profile partner is you can find out about them through the media
Although I could pretty much read the book with ease, I still needed a dictionary by my side, because some words were still obscured for me. I also jotted down some notes so I wouldn’t forget about them and could revise it anytime.
For what it was worth, the book was surprisingly pretty neutral in giving out the history of the realm, unlike the content of the materials read by Valmeier in the human realm.
Although, to be fair, he was a clergy, so...I guessed fanaticism was in the package.
The school book was milder, written from an observer’s point of view with as much neutrality as one could exercise as a demon talking about other realms. Perhaps that was why the demons--at least the demons here, in the realm of greed who grow up with this book--had a more open mind than humans about other races.
It started with what I already knew from the prequel and listening to Zia; about how there used to be One Primordial God who created this world, and later on, vanished without a reason--or at least, without a reason that the mortals knew. And then the world, which was supposed to be in harmony under the rule of the three Gods, became segregated instead.
The book didn’t go into detail about what happened during those times; the struggle of wars until the three main races settled on their own territories--perhaps because it was a student book that would be read by adolescents. The book dove straight into focusing on the demon realms, explaining about the Demon King as the apostle, and the seven Demon Lords as the ruler of the seven realms under demon territory.
What I was searching for, of course, was the elaboration on the Demon Lords throughout history. Eruha told me, that writing or talking about the Demon King was not allowed, but that wasn’t the case with Demon Lords. Of course, to write and talk about all Demon Lords would be boring for adolescents’ minds, so the book only highlighted the most notable Lords in history.
It wasn’t necessarily for their accomplishments, but also for their foolishness, or even eccentricity. There was this one Demon Lord who challenged an ice dragon just because they wanted to use the ice dragon’s nest as food storage--you know, like a natural refrigerator. There was also a Demon Lord who could reign for hundreds of years just by...sleeping, somehow.
Just from the short mentioned in this book, I already wanted to read about each Demon Lord in detail. I bet there was at least one book dedicated to each Demon Lord, looking at their shenanigans. Perhaps because these Lords had full authority over their own realm, they could do whatever they pleased. Essentially, as long as they kept the realm intact, His Majesty wouldn’t bother with how they ran their place.
Every time I encountered an interesting tale, I asked Eruha to prepare the books talking about them so I could read them later on once I increased my proficiency.
And of course, what I wanted to read the most, was the section talking about Natha. For this, I made sure to check the words I didn’t know with the dictionary, instead of trying to understand it from the context alone. My notebook was on the ready, and Eruha was there to help me unravel some long sentences with difficult structures.
As the reigning Lord, Natha had an entire Chapter dedicated to him, since the book was the latest edition. It didn’t really talk about his youth days in detail, however, to my disappointment.
"It was a sensitive topic," Eruha told me. "Not for His Lordship, but for other demons."
I mulled about this for a while before asking carefully. "Because of the...massacre?"
Eruha looked stunned for a moment, probably didn’t think I would know about that. "It’s one of the reasons," he replied after pausing for a few seconds. "It’s an incident that involved one of the realms’ dark history, so it’s not really suitable for the kids. It is, however, still become one of the most debatable topics in advanced academies among scholars."
Advanced academy...must be equivalent to colleges. This was probably the academy mentioned in Natha’s journal.
Still with a careful tone, I asked again. "Is that including why they branded Natha’s father as...a traitor?"
Again, Eruha paused for a while. But this time, he was smiling in response. "I can also be called a newcomer in this realm, so I don’t think I have the capacity to talk about that, Young Master."
"Hmm..."
"You should ask His Lordship yourself about it, since it was his personal history."
"Yeah, sorry," I nodded in agreement. I shouldn’t ask about this from anyone else, since I also knew about it from reading Natha’s journal, not from the book or hearsay. "So anyway, since you mentioned it...when exactly were you coming here?"
Eruha chuckled, and, instead of answering, pointed to the book, telling me to continue reading. "I’ll tell you when you reach that point of the story."
Hmph--so mysterious. But very well, I went back to the book as the teacher told me.
While the book didn’t delve deeper into Natha’s early life, the included information basically could be summarized like this: that my Demon Lord used to be known as a genius, crazy war hero. And by genius, it was because he attended the advanced academy during his twenties.
Huh? What was so special about that, you ask? It was because demons usually attended any advanced education after their coming of age, which happened in their mid-thirties--which was why, Zia, who was twenty-nine, was still considered a teenage...I mean, juvenile demon.
But Natha not only attended the academy at such a young age, but also managed to always stay at the top of the academy leaderboard. And it wasn’t just any academy, but the one located in the realm of pride, which was considered the best and...well...full of proud students, I guessed? No wonder he garnered so much resentment. I was pretty sure now; Natha was one of the protagonists in the novel, because he almost filled the protagonist checklist; handsome, talented, tragic past, etc.
"Were you a teacher in Natha’s academy too?"
"I was," Eruha nodded with a nostalgic smile. "But I only began my vocation when His Lordship was already crowned. Technically, I was His Lordship’s academy junior."
"Huh...but aren’t you older?" I tilted my head in confusion. To my knowledge, Eruha was already two hundred years something, although he looked like a human in their mid-thirties, just like Natha.
"Vampires spend the first century of their life in the lair, to control their impulses and stabilize their mana, since we grow slower than any race," Eruha gently explained. "And after that, we have to assimilate slowly with the outside environment, so it takes even longer to put myself in society."
No wonder he still looked so young, even though his eyes felt like he was already bored with the world. I was tempted to ask about the reason he wasn’t with the Lord of Gluttony, who was a vampire too, but decided to save that for another occasion.
"I see..." I mumbled briefly before diving into the pages again. It proceeded to talk about the corrupted beast subjugation, which, according to the book, drove Natha ’crazy’.
At this point, Eruha kindly explained again. "The corrupted beast’s appearance was more or less a direct causality from the war between the human and the druid kingdom."
I couldn’t help but widen my eyes at that. My mind immediately stirred to find out the connection. "Was it because there was no one to purify the land after the druid kingdom fell?" I gasped at the realization, and Eruha nodded in satisfaction at how I could arrive at the right conclusion.
Ah, those human scums--I exhaled harshly before reading further. It stated that Natha disappeared from the public for many years after that, which the book stated as his recuperation time. "I see he had no intention to correct them," I mumbled after finding the ’recuperation’ word in the dictionary. I knew that Natha was training to control his power in his teacher’s place, as well as being called to the Sanctuary. But seeing that the officially issued book did not mention this, I concluded that Natha had no interest to let others know what he was up to during that time of absence.
Anyway, the book mentioned that Natha was only sighted about a decade after the war; not as the heir of a clan, but as a...merchant, which caused massive confusion among the public. It was more because Natha came from the [Nightwalker] Ra clan, which was one of the top five clans in the demon realm, and he was the direct descendant of the subsidiary [Nightmare] family.
Putting it in human terms, Natha was a noble. And nobles did not partake in commerce. They were the lords of their estates and lived from taxes and tributes. Not to mention, Natha was one of the King’s candidates. But then, Natha established his company in the realm of greed and the demons understood then; he wasn’t trying to contend as the Lord of Lust where the Ra clan had been reigning, but the Lord of Greed instead.
Which, in its own way, was still mind-boggling enough for those demons.
Again, the book didn’t mention in detail regarding Natha’s venture other than calling it a novelty; a weird and new way of doing business that had never been done before (Eruha said there was a book specifically talking about that from an economic point of view). Instead, it went straight to say that Natha’s way of business propel him into the demon realm’s equivalent of a Forbes list.
The book mentioned that Natha owned several companies, some of which were the investment companies he set up throughout the whole demon territory. He also invented several products, technologies, and innovations in commercial practice, including the concept of intellectual rights, even going so far as making the former Lord of Greed set up a law to guarantee them.
Yep--my Demon Lord was the father of patent in this world, y’all.
Thanks to this patent and the concept of royalties, even after he became the Lord and stopped being active in commerce, his wealth never ran dry. Not even when he stopped being the Lord, from the look of it.
I had to pause for a bit to breathe, and this was just the short version of it. Matsa Ra Natha was, in every sense of the word, a menace to the demon realm. He threw away every concept about his root as a noble, turning from a crazy war machine into a scrupulous merchant, and flipping the demon’s commercial world upside down. And now, he even took a human coined as a demon slaughtered as a bride. The one in charge of the next edition of this book would probably have a field day talking about this part.
But even after he became the Demon Lord, Natha was never lacking in adventure. One of the most notable events was the one involving the Lord of Pride. When I reached that part, Eruha smiled deeply, so I knew this was it.
The story that brought Eruha here.

chapters.title: Chapter 118: Demon Lord of Greed? More like Demon Lord of Trickery
chapters.content:
Chapter 118: Demon Lord of Greed? More like Demon Lord of Trickery
Matsa Ra Natha was many things, and among them, vengeful was one of the most notable ones.
The first thing he did after he gained enough power and money was to hunt down every single entity that marauding his house and killed his mother. He dragged those who smeared his father’s name and branded him as a traitor through the mud. And he proved to those who mocked and ostracized him how wrong they were.
One of his targets of vengeance, as it happened, was the Lord of Pride: Auddha Ya Jigisu.
It stemmed from the young Natha’s academic days. The Lord of Pride, at that time still the headmaster of the academy, was for unknown reasons, always trying to sabotage Natha’s accomplishments. He was the one who always put Natha into the hardest trials during tests, instigating a club of scholarly students to discredit the young Nightmare.
Rumor said that Natha was breaking all of the Lord’s records in the past--from becoming the youngest entree, to the leaderboard scores. Others said that it was because the Lord couldn’t take it that someone who wasn’t a resident of the Realm of Pride was beating everyone else, including the Lord’s disciples.
Of course, I heard all that from Eruha, not reading it from the book.
The book only said there was a sense of rivalry between the two Lords who were crowned around the same time. And during the septennial meeting among the seven Demon Lords where they met again for the first time after being crowned, they were engaged in verbal battles--which, as Eruha told me, was scarier than exchanging swords.
These verbal battles, eventually, led to the main events; the competition and the bet, which happened roughly fifty years ago. The competition and the bet were different things, but also started around the same time.
The bet happened before the meeting, and stated that Natha, as the king of commerce, would be able to establish the biggest trading company in the realm of pride. It was akin to declaring that he would conquer the economy of Jigisu’s realm, which of course, inflamed the Lord’s old insecurity.
The competition, on the other hand, was the result of the verbal battle, flamed by the Lord of Pride’s attempt to put Natha’s down. It was a silly competition too. They compete to build the highest structure in the demon realm.
Could you see where this was going? Yup--the Lair.
Was the Lord of Pride stupid, to compete in something that required money with Natha? Not really, because the Lord of Pride, a temperamental lich, was already in the process of building the biggest, tallest magic tower.
Natha, being the way he was, did not build the tallest building; he built a tall building in the tallest location possible. After all, it was a competition for the ’highest’ building--they measured it from how close the top was to the sky. Could always count on Natha for exploiting a loophole, I guessed.
Enraged, the prideful Lord Auddha decided that the only way for him to defeat Natha was to...build a flying castle.
"Flying..." I paused as I read the words on the page, even going for the dictionary to make sure it wasn’t a mistranslation. "Is that possible?"
"It is," Eruha nodded and explained right away. "There’s an old scroll depicting the way to build such a thing from the ancient civilization. It was said that the scroll came from a Sacred Guardian."
"Ooh..." I looked at Eruha with wide eyes, asking him to tell me more.
The book mentioned that the Lord of Pride, somehow, was able to build that flying castle and won the competition. A stupid competition where the only reward was for the opponent to admit defeat in the next septennial meeting, which was also the deadline for the building competition.
For the Lord of Pride, it was the moment of glory, when Natha bowed his head and admit that the Lord Auddha was superior (Natha did not say this, however, according to Eruha, just that he was lost). What the Lord of Pride couldn’t understand, however, was the bright smile on Natha’s face, as if it didn’t matter if he was lost.
Auddha Ya Jigisu realized what that bright smile meant not long after.
The problem with building a freaking castle-in-the-sky wasn’t the blueprint, but the capital required for it. Acquiring the blueprint from the black market’s black market already cost them so much, but the material to build it--gosh! Almost all of them were material of magic property, which meant they would be expensive. From the materials to build the base and the castle itself, to the materials needed to carve the complex formations that allowed the castle to stay in the air, to build the corresponding portal gate to transport the visitors from the ground to the sky...everything was monumentally pricey.
Building a magic tower was one thing, because they had been doing it anyway. But a freaking magic castle? Their money had been used to build the magic tower, but then the Lord suddenly asked for more money, all to fulfill his own desire. That money didn’t come from thin air, but from taxes, tributes, and donations. The Lord ended up increasing those, and even borrowed money from anywhere.
Including from one of Natha’s companies.
At first, the resident of Pride had no idea what the flying castle was for. They thought it was a defense mechanism; a flying fortress to up their firepower in case of war or invasion. But little birds told them that the building, in fact, was only for a competition with another Lord. Of course, the public was enraged. The realm of pride’s financial situation hadn’t been good for the past seven years because of their Lord’s silly competition, and because it wasn’t a venture that brought profit, the Lord didn’t even have any way to return the money he borrowed.
Within that chaotic situation, they had no leeway to realize that someone had been establishing themselves in their realm; injecting money into those who almost went bankrupt because they lent money to the Lord, lending money to their bank, and even helping the small business uniting under a trading company so they could survive.
"There was a lot of unsatisfaction, and riots happening everywhere, even in the magic tower where the Lord resided," Eruha explained further. This kind of detail was something that I couldn’t get from the book. "When the situation was over, the biggest trading company in the realm of pride was owned by His Lordship, half of their bank’s capital was coming from His Lordship, and until now, His Lordship still holds into a quarter of the Pride’s realm bonds,"
"You mean...the realm of pride had to pay Natha every year?" I gasped as Eruha answered me with a smile.
In short; Natha lost the battle, but won the war. Did he already plan that ever since he made the ’bet’?
Damn--that was so sexy of him.
But that wasn’t the extent of it. "Since His Lordship also won the bet, he had the right to ask the Lord of Pride for three tangible things."
"Ah!" suddenly, a light bulb went on in my head. "So you’re one of those things?"
"Yes," Eruha chuckled in response, and even though he didn’t say it, I had a feeling that Eruha had a part as an ’insider’ during the whole debacle. "I could not tell what the other two, however, since His Lordship never revealed them."
In other words, he told me to ask Natha directly. Fine--I scribbled the questions in my notebook.
The entry after that wasn’t as exciting as this whole bet/competition thing. I did find out that an overseer council was established in the realm of pride to watch over the Lord, and I bet my mana core that Natha had his own people among those overseers.
So, long story short, Natha was a petty demon who would drag his enemy through the mud and financial debt for revenge. Good for him. He was also a demon whose wealth would probably never end, with all the royalties and debt people owed him.
It was exciting reading and hearing about his past adventures, and I hadn’t even delved into the more detailed ones. Like I still wanted to know what he was doing in the elven kingdom when he met the three siblings, and why he was suddenly turning into a merchant.
It was also funny to think that my first home, the tower, his Lair, was a product of competition. Although, just like the Lord of Pride, he was probably already thinking about building one before.
Talking about the Lair, I also wondered how he came upon the mountain the first time, how he made the contract with the elemental birds, or even how he was battling that big tree in the clearing I used to practice in. It was quite a historical site, in its own way.
Hmm...so the Lair had been standing there for about fifty years already? But why...did I find this strange? I had no idea why, but something itched at the back of my head, as if my brain was trying to remember something Natha had said not too long ago.
Oh well, if I forgot about it, it was probably nothing important.

chapters.title: Chapter 119: Just tell me straight my Lord, you’re a protagonist, aren’t you?
chapters.content:
Chapter 119: Just tell me straight my Lord, you’re a protagonist, aren’t you?
"Looks like you’re having fun today,"
I was laying on my stomach on the bed, waiting for dinner, humming to myself while reviewing the notes I made during my ’study on Demon Lord’ session this afternoon. I didn’t even realize Natha was already back until he sat beside me and stroked my back.
"Welcome back," I giggled and lifted my notebook. "I resumed my investigation on you!"
"Oh, good job," he leaned down and kissed my crown, eyes peeking into the notebook while at it. "You got the general things, I see."
"Well, I got it from the school book, so of course it’s going to be general," I shrugged.
With his chin, Natha pointed toward the table in my little bedroom reading corner then, the one under the window. "That’s why you have a bunch of academy textbooks here?"
Lesta didn’t manage to find any parenting books in the library, although he told me he’d try to procure one. What he brought instead were books on familiar and beast taming for beginners--meaning for adolescents. Lesta added some schoolbooks that contained more general studies, from geography to the socio-economic condition of the demon realm.
"Eruha told me to look at them when I have the chance, before our next lesson,"
"Is he teaching you demonese or grooming you to be a ruler?" Natha muttered and chuckled, before looking back at my notes. "You’re getting good at the letters too."
"I practice diligently, you know!"
"I can see that,"
He proceeded to stroke my back again, and I tilted my head so I could see his face better. "Natha..."
"Hmm?"
"Can I ask you something?"
He paused for a second before resuming his stroke on my back. His lips stretched into a smile as he ask; "Is this about my father?"
I sat up immediately, blinking in surprise. "H-how do you know? Did you sense my--"
"No," he chuckled, patting my cheek gently to calm me down. "But I did read your notes."
Oh! Oh, how foolish of me. I looked down at my note; at the bold, underlined ’Natha’s Father’ and ’traitor’ with a huge question mark below the section of his adolescent era. There was even a teeny tiny note on the border: ’Should I ask?’.
I gave him a wry grin and carefully asked. "Is that alright? It’s not mentioned in the book, but I read it in your journal..."
"Sure," Natha leaned back on the bedpost and crossed his arms. "It’s not something that affects me anymore, since I’ve done my payback, but..."
"...but?"
He stared at my worried but curious face with a smile that went from soft to mischievous, while turning his face sideways. "This bard requires an advance payment, Young Master."
I blinked at his playful tone and curled eyes. It took me five seconds before realizing what he meant and leaned forward to peck his cheek as payment. "Would that be enough, Mister Bard?
"Mm, I shall take it since this is my first service, but I will expect more for my future performance," he whispered mischievously before pulling me into his lap, and I leaned back against his chest while listening to his story.
Natha was born into the Ra clan, the most influential family in the realm of lust. Apparently, this clan was a merger of three families of three races; Spectres, Nightmares, and the lust demon--Incubi and Succubi. The founders did the merging to contend for the Lord’s position against other clans--or in other words; to snatch the Key of Lust.
After they managed to do it, the Lord’s position fell to the Spectres, because they were the strongest. Nightmares were too few and rare, and their members were only about ten percent of the total force. The lust demons, although had the most number of demons, most of them were not of pure blood due to their culture of interracial mixing. As far as authority goes, the Spectres had the upper hand.
"We didn’t really mind it, though. Nightmare and lust demon wasn’t really ambitious in nature after all," Natha shrugged, while I wondered what this all had to do with the story. "So we were all living in harmony, until a problem arose."
"What problem?"
Natha looked down and with a smirk, announced in a nonchalant tone. "Me. Because I was born."
I blinked and parted my lips in surprise, brain whirring in motion. But in my position, leaning on his chest and looking up, I could see the exquisite pattern on his neck clearly, and the answer came to me immediately. So I replied while holding my breath. "Because of your alpha seed?"
"Yes,"
There were realms that employ special methods in choosing their Lords, like how the realm of greed chose the wealthiest one, the realm of wrath chose their Lord through the martial tournament, or the realm of pride which tested their Lord candidates with extensive theoretical examination. But there were also regions that had no special method in choosing their Lord; anyone who held the Key would be crowned Lord. The realm of lust was one of those.
Because of this, the Ra clan managed to hold the Lord position, with the Spectres family as the holder of the Key. Despite this, there was one thing that the clan had failed to produce; a King Candidate. There were already nine Demon Kings in history, but none of them came from the realm of lust. The Spectres had been trying various methods, including careful scrutinization to keep their bloodline pure. And yet, after more than a millennium, the awaited alpha seed showed up in another family.
Natha’s birth was causing distress among the elders of the clan, because it was a direct threat to the Spectre’s authority. And his father knew it. The joy of having a child after so many years of waiting became a dread after the elders ordered him to kill baby Natha.
"What?!" I almost jumped off his lap, but Natha held my chest back, so all I could do was look up with a deep frown and clenching fists. "Wait--did they call your father traitor because he refused to kill his own son?!"
"Haha, of course not," Natha answered with a chuckle, caressing my hair as if trying to calm me down. Why was he calming ME down? Why did he laugh?! I pursed my lips in annoyance at a bunch of old demons that I never met and were probably dead. "There’s no way that kind of reasoning would convince the other demons to call my father a traitor."
Well, that was true. If they jumped on the bandwagon of calling his father a traitor just because the man refused to kill his own son for the Spectre’s lust for power, I would have to retract my nice opinion on the demons.
"It was only much later on that I found out about it, but it seemed like the Spectres were the main culprit behind the death of many children bearing alpha seed across the centuries," Natha continued his story, still while stroking my hair in a soothing manner. "Anyway, my father refused to do it. He even made an oath to never let me become the Lord of Lust, and my family moved to a secluded estate. I also had to take my education in other regions."
Oh, gosh! I knew he had a tragic past but...
I let out a sigh and sunk myself deeper into his chest. I could feel the rumble of his soft laughter vibrating through my back, and it made my heart clench in pain. How long did it take, I wondered, for him to be able to laugh about it?
"Is that why you decided to move to the realm of greed?" I asked.
"Well, that’s only part of the reason,"
Until Natha reached adolescence, everything seemed to be fine. He lived in the academy dorm, so he wasn’t home much. But one day, he suddenly heard that his father was accused of treason by the Lord, and a letter came from home asking him to go back. When he reached the estate, his father was already in prison awaiting trial.
The accusation that he received was collaborating with the elves to take over the realm so he could plant his son as the Lord. Which was ridiculous, because the oath he took prevented him to do exactly that; if Natha was to take the Lord’s seat, his father’s soul would shatter.
And yet, the Spectre provided evidence of an attempt on erasing a soul-binding oath, so even when Natha’s father presented the oath to defend himself, it was rebuked.
"The recording evidence about my father’s talk with the elves was a fabrication," Natha explained. "My father did have several meetings with the elves, but it had nothing to do with taking over the realm or making me the Lord. The documents about erasing soul-binding oath, however..."
"It’s real?!" my eyes widened in surprise. Although, to be honest, I wouldn’t blame him at all to try. It was a cruel and absurd oath in the first place.
"It’s real, but it did not belong to my father,"
"Then?
There was a soft sound of a sigh coming out of his lips, and when Natha told me the answer, it was filled with regret and sadness. "It belonged to my mother."
Oh...
"She was a sweet mother, and she loved me so much. Too much. She felt like I wouldn’t have a future worthy of my talent unless I became the Lord," he held my hands, and I gripped them back as he continued. "Obviously, it backfired, and my father was deemed guilty. He requested an appeal and was supposed to have a re-trial in two weeks’ time while we gathered proof to defend him. But three days after the court was adjourned, he died."
At this point, I was too flabbergasted to even make a noise, just stared at him with a frown and pressed my lips.
Natha had no idea if his father was killed or died from immense stress and heartache. His death made the case end in an awkward notion; most thought he was a traitor, but some also doubt it. Those who doubted and saw it as the tyranny of the Spectres protected Natha and his mother from being prosecuted, although in the end, years later, she still ended up killed in the massacre.
Natha fled to the heavily guarded estate of his Great Aunt, and after that, it was just as I had read in his journal.
"After I came back from the Sanctuary, I left the realm of lust for good, and started a new journey," Natha told me while stroking the back of my hand, chin resting on top of my head. "I needed capital, needed resources if I wanted to have my revenge. So I gathered money, friends, and subordinates. For years and decades, I gathered proof of my father’s innocence, and asked for the lust demon’s cooperation. I told them I’d let them take the Key of Lust to honor my father’s oath, and we worked together to drive the Spectres out of power. I used my money to provide the firepower and bought the citizen’s favor through charity and investment."
I blinked as I listen to him, couldn’t say anything but wow...just wow...
This entire tale should be worthy of its own book, in my opinion.
"When what the Spectres had done to my family was revealed, I could finally free my father from being labeled as a traitor," Natha let out a long, relieved breath. "But it was also exposing the shameful history of the realm, so demons avoid talking about it."
When I clicked my tongue in response, he laughed and took my hand to his lips. "Well, how would you rate this bard’s story, Young Master?"
"Mm..." I tapped my chin in contemplation, faking a serious pondering. "The protagonist story is pretty tragic but exciting. I bet he ends up becoming a handsome, alluring, valiant Demon Lord somewhere else," I looked up with a grin as Natha laughed behind me. "Would there be a sequel to that?"
"Well...maybe, if there’s enough reward?"

chapters.title: Chapter 120: That time I got transmigrated to another world and became a trust fund sugar baby
chapters.content:
Chapter 120: That time I got transmigrated to another world and became a trust fund sugar baby
Unfortunately, the call for dinner prevented me to provide a decent reward for a sequel.
But then again, I only asked about the reason his father was called a traitor, and I already got the answer. Phew...seemed like authoritative scums were everywhere, be it in the human realm or the demon realm.
It was true then, that absolute power corrupts absolutely.
"Hmm...but Natha..." when I stared at the pink and purple jelly on Jade’s plate, something suddenly came to my mind. "Isn’t that mean...you’re essentially the one that puts the current Lord on his seat?"
"No, technically it was the previous Lord, the current Lord’s father,"
"Oh..."
Was that why Zia ran away to Natha’s place? He must have tremendous power over the realm of lust’s household. Thinking about how he screwed over the Lord of Pride and put the lich under constant supervision, and how he was the one who arranged the tournament to pick the new Lord of Wrath...
Why did I feel like he also had his hands somehow on the other realms? Hmm...as I stared at the pattern over his skin, I could feel that fate always found its bearer. All the tales were like the making of a King. I was sure that Lust, Pride, and Wrath would hand over their Lord Keys should Natha ask for them--perhaps not all willingly, but it was hard denying a request from someone who held your debt in his hands.
Hmm...yes--money maketh the world or whatever.
"Ah, right," Natha suddenly exclaimed in the middle of my scenario-making. "Malta told me your personal chambers have been completed."
Personal chambers? Oh--the research lab and training field!
"I would like to take you there myself, but I have a conference with foreign contingents tomorrow," he said with slight disappointment as he took my hand. "Forgive me, sweetheart."
"It’s fine, you don’t have to always baby me, you know..."
He chuckled and brushed my lips in response, tilting his head so he could peer at my eyes better. "You looked disappointed, though?"
"I-I’m not!"
[Don’t bully Master!] Jade jumped off its jelly and pecked the hand that Natha used to hold mine.
"We need to do something about this brat’s behavior," Natha narrowed his eyes at Jade, and they started their staring contest again, hurling insults toward each other in their mind.
I let them be this time, since it diverted the topic and attention, sparing me from further embarrassment from being found out.
Fine--so I was disappointed. Just slightly. I mean...I knew I said that I don’t want Natha to continue spoiling me. It would be unbecoming for the Lord to continuously neglected his governing duty just to indulge his lover. But still...I also wished Natha would be the one who showed me that room, since he was the one who designed and paid for it. Since it was the rooms that he prepared for me.
But, oh well. As I said, I couldn’t keep letting Natha spoil me, or I would turn into a selfish lover that held him back. Nope. Absolutely didn’t want that to happen.
So the next day, I walked out of the Lord’s private quarters with Malta, who would show me the way. I was also followed by three demons; the guards that had been assigned to me from the start, and Panne that officially been appointed as my attendant while I stayed here.
"His Lordship would like to provide you with the utmost privacy, but we also considered the safety risk, so please don’t be too disappointed with the location, Young Master," Malta told me as we walked to the southern side of the castle.
"Why would I be disappointed?" I tilted my head in confusion. I didn’t even expect to have a private room where I could conduct a more thorough experiment on the failed product, so how could I have the audacity to feel disappointed?
"For safety and containment, we have to put all rooms regarding research and development in one section of the castle," Malta replied with a tone of a company tour guide. "So that means your chamber has to be situated with all of the other research rooms."
She pointed to the entranceway leading to the southern tower of the castle, which was reserved entirely for all manners of research, from magic to alchemy. It was the closest this realm had to a magic tower, spanning thirteen floors up and possibly more down. A long bride corridor connected the research tower to the library from the third floor.
"Of course, you’ll have your own room. But it’s inevitable to come across others using the same building, so you’ll have to excuse us for that, Young Master."
That was it? She thought I would be disappointed because I didn’t have the whole building for myself? Because I had to bump into others? I couldn’t help but raise my brow.
"It’s also to make it easy for you in fetching the materials you would need or put on orders for some. Even though you use your own money, any materials for research and development purposes have to come through the same inspection and are stored in this place together..."
She was still going on about the building and the facilities, but my mind was stuck on one thing; what do you mean by ’my money’, Ma’am? I had none you know...
I wanted to ask her more about that, but at that time, we arrived at the tower’s lobby, and I couldn’t proceed with it. Because I felt so many gazes fell on me then, and became too conscious of them.
Of course, the demons we passed through as we walked also looked at me. But it was an occasional thing, and as usual, they instantly bent their waist and trained their eyes on the floor. But here...it was different.
They didn’t avert their eyes, and kept staring with palpable curiosity in their eyes. They also openly whispered to each other while looking at me, and it kind of make me feel awkward. The gazes were intense, but also bore no hostility. It was blatant curiosity that was only being averted slightly when Malta clapped her hands loudly once to disperse the attention. That being said, not everyone ceased their stare, and I had to endure it until Malta brought us inside the elevator.
"As you can see, most of them acted as they wish. The ones working here mostly only care about their project and nothing else--such as others’ opinions and convenience. But don’t worry, they won’t stare as much after a few times. Today is their first time seeing you, so pardon their...enthusiasm."
"I see..."
Malta looked at me and gave that subtle smile of hers. "If they still do and you feel uncomfortable about it, just say the word. A few threats over their research budget never fail to make them obedient."
Hey, do you want to make me into the bad guy here?
"I don’t mind some eyes, it’s just that earlier was a bit too intense," I told her with a sigh.
"Don’t worry, Young Master. Your guards are here to make sure you’re safe and comfortable. So if you feel like they stare too much, just say the word so they can give a warning," Malta said while glancing toward my two guards; Mohan and Laheer. They nodded firmly and give me a determined gaze.
As expected of Natha’s personal knight guards, they looked reliable and dependable. "Thank you," I told them with a little smile that I finally managed to make after being tensed earlier. "Oh, we’re here?"
The elevator was dinged and stopped just then, hissing open with a whirring sound of activated magic formation. The panel above the door told me that we were on the eighth floor. I expected another round of intense staring as the door slid open, but it was actually empty except for two demons with a clerk uniform, who seemed to be waiting for us in the floor’s lobby.
"Welcome, Young Master!" They greeted in unison, like highly trained receptionists.
But wait--this felt like...
"The entire eighth floor of the tower had always been dedicated to the Lord’s personal use," Malta answered my thought immediately. "Everything on this floor is for you to use, Young Master."
Oh, God, so that was true. No wonder there were lots of decorative plants in the lobby. In fact, the lobby looked as nice as a cozy lounge, something that I wouldn’t expect from a research lab.
"There’s about everything on this floor, from alchemy labs to simplified smithy. These two will help you with the floor’s maintenance, storage, and inventory," Malta pointed toward the two staff, who responded by introducing themselves; the female one was called Theemis and the male one was Zuya. Both of them were imps, of light blue skins, cute pointed ears and tails, as well as petite stature.
"If you need anything from the Lord’s storage, you can ask Zuya to procure it," Malta looked at the male imp, who energetically nodded and curtsied. "Or if you need something that’s not available in the storage, he will take care of your order."
Order...right--she said something about money earlier, which meant I would need money to be able to make an order, but...
"Ah, I almost forget," before I could voice my confusion, Malta took out something from her pocket. A...card?
It was black and rectangular, shaped just like a credit card back on Earth. Only, it was definitely made of a light, magic-conducting metal instead of plastic, and had a line of glowing letters and numbers at the top corner.
When I looked at Malta in confusion, she deftly gave an explanation. "His Lordship asked me to put all your money in a new account with our bank. This might be new, since this system wasn’t used in the human realm, but this is your account card, Young Master. You can see your account information and make payments with this."
...huh?
With a dazed mind, I took the black card Malta gave to me and stared at it blankly. She told me to send my mana into the card so I could see the account information. Once I did, the black surface of the card was filled with the card’s information, which stated the owner of the account (me) and the balance.
"..."
I...better not divulged how much was stored in this account I didn’t even know I had before.
I just knew I could make a whole castle from the most expensive candies for Jade with it.

chapters.title: Chapter 121: When you’re the actor but you don’t know the script
chapters.content:
Chapter 121: When you’re the actor but you don’t know the script
I was too flabbergasted by my new wealth that I couldn’t concentrate on Malta’s explanation on each room this floor has--I’d just ask Theemis later.
I mean...yes, I knew I was bound to a relationship with the wealthiest demon in the realm. I knew that I could just ask him for anything and Natha would buy it for me, provided it was reasonable. There were three rooms full of treasures that I could plunder to my heart’s content.
But it was different, way different with raw capital. It was different when I had the freedom to buy and procure what I wanted by myself, without having to first amass the courage to ask him for something.
So, forgive me, Malta, but right now your explanation kept bouncing off my ears.
