"Mm, my bad," Eruha acknowledged his ignorance pretty quickly, which only made Lesta even more exasperated.
But at least, it gave light to what they actually felt for each other--although they should have done it a long time ago.
That being said, this ’Eternal’ business was another matter altogether.
"Give me time to think about it," Lesta said in the end, shoulder dropped in exhaustion.
"Of course," Eruha stepped back with a satisfied smile on his lips. "Time is all I have in abundance."

chapters.title: Chapter 259: It’s mighty fun to tease other people for change
chapters.content:
Chapter 259: It’s mighty fun to tease other people for change
"So...why blood?" I asked Natha as we walked to our breakfast.
Usually, guests didn’t have to join the Lord for breakfast and could have it on their own in their room, but Sada insisted we ate with her. Natha whispered to me that she was actually lonely and wanted to eat with other people. Not many had enough wit to eat with a Vampire Lord comfortably, after all.
So now, instead of leisurely having breakfast in our room, we walked to the garden pavilion where the Vampire Lord had her breakfast.
Oh, well, at least it wasn’t the courthall.
Since we had to go to the garden anyway, we decided to have our morning stroll around the garden before heading to the place; a nice little date before Natha had his work and I had my city tour. But strolling around the garden in the winter wasn’t exactly the most exciting thing to do, since there wasn’t much to spectate.
Which was why I ended up asking him more about the vampire.
"There are four kinds of parts in our body that contain a high concentration of mana; brain matter, bone marrow, blood, and seminal fluid," he answered me in this nice, smooth voice in this educational tone that made me wish he wore his work glasses. "Taking mana from the brain and the marrow would practically kill the source, and the amount of seminal fluid one can produce at a time is not much, which leaves the blood."
Which could be extracted up to 800ml without causing death, if I recall correctly, and would replenish by itself. Pretty sustainable resource, not gonna lie.
Nata added while patting his chest lightly. "It circulates through the heart, which is located parallel to the astral body’s mana core. So it’s the most efficient resource for them."
"I see," I stroked my chin and nodded like the good student that I was. So it wasn’t just a kink--okay, okay. I looked at him and leaned closer to whisper, in case it was a sensitive topic for the vampires. "Is it drawn through biting with their fangs too? You know...like those vampires on Earth..."
"It doesn’t have to be a bite, but a puncture wound is indeed the cleanest," Natha replied with a chuckle—I guessed it wasn’t a sensitive topic since he answered me normally. "It only left two small holes that could easily be erased. The round wound acted like a straw; less messy, if compared to a slash wound."
"Ooh, that makes sense!" I hit my palm with my fist. So once again, it wasn’t a kink, folks. "Ah, I heard vampires also have some kind of poison in their fangs?"
"Ah, yeah," Natha smiled rather mysteriously, like he found our conversation to be funny. "It’s called poison, but it’s actually a relaxant and a painkiller, because who would want to consent to it if the process is painful?"
His mischievous-looking smile made me think of something else though. "...some people have that kind of kink," I muttered.
"Are you?" he looked at me with a raised brow.
"Don’t kink shame,"
"Are you?"
Averting his gaze and fiddling my fingers, I replied quietly. "I...might be curious?"
I glanced at Natha and saw the curl on the side of his mouth. "Noted," he said, totally smirking, and totally made me blush.
It was a good thing that Jade was having its morning flying exercise around the Vampire Castle so the little bird didn’t have to hear our conversation about this--because I was sure Jade would ask what kink was.
"Ah, the ’poison’ also contains an aphrodisiac property to elevate heart rate so the blood flows smoother," Natha added, the curl of his lips felt even more mischievous now.
You’re sure it’s only for that?
Welp--now it sounded even more like a kink.
Natha continued breaking down how the magic was absorbed, and the different qualities of blood from several sentient beings. There was also a matter of compatibility, which not only influenced the ’flavor’ but also the absorption rate. Apparently, drinking blood from someone with high mana purity--like me--wasn’t all that good; kind of like drinking liquor with high alcohol content, harder to digest since it was more intense.
Well, something like that. Honestly, I was so focused on Natha himself than what he said at this point, just listening to him quietly.
At the end of his explanation, he paused and looked at me, who had been staring at him all this time. "What?"
"I just...reminded of the time you were a doctor," I said, feeling somewhat like I was in a daze. Perhaps because it was also winter.
He raised his brow and smirked. "Should I make a white lab coat?"
I put my hands over my mouth and gasped. Natha in a doctor’s outfit?
"My Lord!" at his arched brow, I leaned closer and whispered. "Please do, it would be my pleasure to receive your interim examination."
"Your kink is showing, sweetheart."
"It’s my first love! Of course, I would have a fantasy about it!"
"Oh? A confession so early in the morning?" he smirked and ruffled my hair--which would anger Arta if she was here.
I giggled and wrapped my hands around his arm. "Speaking about confession..."
"Hmm? Are you thinking about Lesta and Eruha?"
"Yeah, do you know about it? The Eternal thing, I mean..."
"Hmm...Eruha told me when our working contract was up that he’d stay working with me for as long as Lesta did," he said, before shrugging slightly. "Since I already know about Eternal from Teacher, I could easily make a guess."
"Huh..."
So, while Natha knew, funnily enough, Lesta was never privy to this at all despite being the Lord’s right-hand man. I didn’t think he was the dense type, but...I don’t know, it wasn’t like I knew much about their relationship to begin with.
"You know...I thought they were lovers already, but..."
I knew being a lover and being an Eternal to a vampire was a different thing. But don’t you think you’d at least tell your partner about your intention to bind them in an eternal relationship? I mean...Natha only proposed not long ago, but he already called me his ’bride’ from the start.
"I think they already are lovers," Natha chuckled and shook his head like a man seeing his clueless friends in love. "It’s only them that don’t know about it--I mean...even you realized."
My eyes narrowed and I pinched his side. "What do you mean even me? Are you saying I’m dense or something?"
As if my pinch had no effect on him, he just turned his face to look at me and smiled charmingly. "You’re adorably dense sometimes,"
He ruffled my hair again, which I had painstakingly fixed because I didn’t have my hairstylist La Dhuarta here this time. Was I really that dense, though? The smirk and the mischievous glint in those silver eyes felt kind of annoying for some reason.
I pursed my lips and let go of his arm. "Hmph!"
"I said adorably,"
"Hmph!"
He laughed softly and wrapped his hand around my shoulder, kissing my hair and temple and cheeks until I stopped pouting and giggling as we reached the pavilion.
Which was probably why the Vampire Lord looked at us with rolled eyes. "Why are you giving me dog food so early in the morning when there are a lot of other delicious things on this table?"
She spread her arms at the round table that was filled with food already. It didn’t include all the other trolleys with even more food behind her.
Natha held my hand and led me to the pavilion while responding to Sada nonchalantly with a shrug. "Then don’t eat the dog food."
"Then don’t give me one in the first place, you brat!" the Lord snapped, but my only reaction was to giggle.
"It’s kind of weird hearing someone calling you a brat," I told Natha.
"Oh, you like that, boy?" Sada raised her brow and smirked. "You’re going to like it even more in Mother’s place then."
"Oh? Oh?!" my eyes widened in excitement, looking back and forth between Natha and the Vampire Lord.
Natha clicked his tongue in annoyance, muttering with a slight blush on the tip of his ear. "Shut up."
I couldn’t help but giggle again, since it was rare to find people who could make Natha flustered or exasperated. If my observation was correct, it was mostly those who knew him from way before he became the Lord, or when he was still a young adult.
When he was still more or less like the young doctor I fell in love with.
After satisfying myself by giggling at Natha, I took a seat beside Lesta, who was already there first with Eruha. Seeing that they were here together, it seemed that at least their talk went well? Lesta looked like he was lost in thought, however.
I leaned closer to him and asked carefully. "Lesta, are we still going to tour the city?"
He finally lifted his gaze from his empty plate, and flashed me his usual smile. "Of course."
Whew--he didn’t look like he was distressed or depressed. "Okay!"
[Candy store!] suddenly, the little bird swooped into the pavilion and landed skillfully on the table between me and Lesta, bringing an uplifting chirp into the garden.
"Jade wants to go to the candy store," I told Lesta.
"I know that, so I already put that in our itinerary," he smirked, patting the green head with his fingers.
"Yay, Jade!"
[Yaay!!]
For that, Jade even let Lesta squeeze its cheeks lightly, and the demon didn’t look like he was lost in thought again as he played with the little bird.
Hmm...well, I’m glad he looks alright.

chapters.title: Chapter 260: Look, I’m not saying I give good advice, but...
chapters.content:
Chapter 260: Look, I’m not saying I give good advice, but...
"Whoa..."
If you asked me before about what I would think about a vampire city, I would say something like an eerie castle with a gothic-esque aesthetic, elegant and sinister at the same time. Black! Red! Emo!
Or something like that? Hehe...
But while the place did have the expected aesthetic of those pointy arches and elaborate tracery, it definitely wasn’t a sinister or gloomy place, even in the middle of winter. The city itself, unlike the spacious metropolis that was L’Anaak Eed, was built atop stony hills in terraces, so the moment we got out of the castle gate, I was greeted with rows upon rows of beautiful architecture stretching down the winding terraces.
[Master! It’s like giant stairs!]
"Giant stairs indeed," I nodded in agreement. Lesta had chosen a more open carriage for us, so we could easily sightseeing even while going to our destination.
Which was supposed to be the bank--Natha’s bank--but since we had a child with us, we went straight to the candy store in the commercial district. That way, we wouldn’t have to hear Jade chirping every ten minutes asking about the candy store.
Well, that, and because I was also curious about the snacks from other regions.
Around the center of the ’giant stair’, there was a plaza with a fountain as a centerpiece. Around that plaza was the commercial district, and the canter of activity in this place. Because people came to shop? No.
They came to eat.
When I said commercial district, I did not talk about clothing stores or accessory shops. More than half the stores here had something to do with food; massive grocery stores, herb-specialty shops, rare ingredients auction houses, and of course; ready-made products and restaurants. Lots of restaurants, cafes, and food stalls.
"It’s like culinary festivals..." I could only blink in wonder as I looked around the plaza.
Immediately, all I could see were the food stalls and people walking around with food or drink in their hands. Some ate it around the fountain, and some brought it to their next destination. But while it was fascinating, it was also confusing because...uhh, would we know where we should be going?
Aside from the coachman, we didn’t bring anyone. It seemed like Natha truly trusted Lesta and his ability to protect me, since he forgo giving me guards. It was nice because it felt like we were just strolling leisurely among friends.
But then, who would guide us?
"This way," Lesta, however, pointed in a direction and confidently led us away.
"Oh, you know the way? Have you come here before?"
"Not in the Capital, it’s usually Older Sister who came," he said. "But I already memorized the layout, so you can rest easy, Young Master."
Owh--as expected of Natha’s right-hand man, to memorize the way just from the map...
We followed Lesta to a street that was filled with colorful buildings. Holding Jade in my chest, I couldn’t help but marvel at the display of sparkling, shining sweets in various shapes and sizes. Five-tired cake, chocolate fountains, and even cotton candy in various shapes. There was a stall selling my favorite caramel candy, the one shaped into various sculptures.
[Master, this place full of candy! And cake! And choco!]
We stopped at that stall for a bit to see the artisan’s performance, shaping a little bird with a round belly and pipe-shaped tail that could act as a whistle. It was so fascinating that I couldn’t help but buy it, because Jade was pecking at me excitedly. To think that this magical thing was made without magic...
Jade was fascinated by the little candy bird that was only a little bit smaller than it. But once we arrived at the store Lesta chose for us, Jade forgot about the candy bird.
Well, I couldn’t blame the little bird, though.
The place was big, almost like a small palace. And what do you know--there was a miniature Lord Castle made of chocolate in the middle of the store. I spent a few minutes just admiring the detailed works of the chocolatier with Jade, who couldn’t even let out any chirping sound for being too amazed. Besides the chocolate, they also used candy to make the glass window, from the clear ones to the colorful ones.
Before we were drooling too much, before an intrusive thought of eating it surfaced, I followed Lesta to one of the display windows, causing Jade to chirp in disappointment.
At least, until the little bird saw the rows of sparkling jewels inside the display window.
"Wow...look, Jade--it’s like a gem," I said in a whisper.
The candy truly looked like gems and precious stones. Some even looked like unprocessed minerals. But everything was so beautiful, so different than other candy we tried before. They looked exquisite and luxurious, even the box.
[Like the stones in treasure room!] The little bird hopped on top of the display window, almost pressing its head to the transparent glass.
"That’s right," I nodded in agreement. I recalled Jade’s disappointment when it knew all the sparkling jewels in the treasure room were inedible. "Now you can have the gems you can eat, Jade."
[Wooow...]
"There’s a sample here if you want to try it, Young Master," Lesta said, calling out one of the shop’s clerks who readily provided us with a long box filled with small jars; each jar contained one type of those beautiful candies.
"Oh! Which one do you want to try first, Jade?"
[Green!]
We tried the green one, which looked like our eyes, and it tasted both sweet and sour, easily right up my alley. But Jade liked something that was only sweet, so we tried another one, and then another, and another, until we ended up trying everything, together with Lesta.
And well, we ended up buying everything, because why not?
"Hmm...how many should we buy?" I tilted my head and tapped my chin in contemplation. The clerk already packing the one that Jade liked, and then the one that I liked. I wanted to buy some for Zia and Arta too, and who else? Hmm...
Oh!
"Do you think Natha’s teacher would like candy too?" I asked Lesta.
"I don’t know, but there’s no harm in trying," Lesta shrugged and I ended up purchasing the special box they had, which was filled with the best product; not only candy but also chocolate.
The clerk eagerly processed my order, which ended up being quite a lot. Turned out it was a very expensive product, since the candies were made of ingredients infused with mana, which was why they were shaped like literal jewels. Perhaps that was why the clerks became extra nice, even though they were already nice before. But hey--you know how we tend to spend a lot during vacations, right?
That being said, the fact that the final amount made no dent in my black card was scarier. Lesta said I could buy the whole shop if I wanted and the card would still have some change.
Scary-ass rich daddy. Thank Gods he’s my fiance.
"What are you going to do there, Young Master?" Lesta asked me while we were waiting for the boxes to be individually wrapped with a nice ribbon and stuff, except for a small pouch for Jade’s snack.
"Hmm...I don’t know too," I looked at the ceiling, pondering while sipping on a hot cocoa that the store made for me as a service. "I guess we’ll see if she could give us some advice on things. Oh--and I want her to teach me how to make that mark of eternal thingy!"
I was getting so excited about it that I forgot that it might be a sensitive topic for Lesta. I pressed my lips and glanced carefully at the demon, but as usual, his face was calm and unreadable. Instead, he looked kind of curious.
"May I know why?"
Why do I want the eternal mark? Hmm...
"I don’t know if I can say this in front of you, but..."
"Please be at ease and tell me," Lesta gave me an assuring smile.
Uhh...well, if he said so...
I took a deep breath and unconsciously fiddled with my sleeve. "I’m kind of...envious," I told him quietly. It was something that I had never even said to Natha. "Everyone has a long lifespan, longer than humans," I sighed, looking at all the other demons walking around with their loved ones. "While I have a longer lifespan than humans, I wouldn’t live as long as a druid, I know that much,"
It was something that had always nagged in the back of my mind. But I always countered it with the thought that it was already good that I could live this long.
That being said, I started to get greedy. And that greediness turned into anxiety.
"So...I wouldn’t be able to live as long as Natha, even though he was already much older than me," I continued, looking down at my cocoa.
In a way, I was glad that there was a large gap between the time Natha met me and the time I got transmigrated here. Because at least, I could match Natha’s lifespan a little bit, although it still wasn’t enough.
"That’s why you want to learn the mark of eternal?"
"I don’t wish for a long lifespan, but..." I shrugged and smiled wryly. "I would like it if we could be together until the end. That if one of us dies, then the other follows," instinctively, my eyes traveled to my ring finger, and I had to hold back my voice from cracking. "Because I don’t think I could ever live without Natha."
I let out a long exhale, and sipped on the hot cocoa again to warm my heart. After a minute of silence, Lesta spoke first.
"May I ask you a question, Young Master?"
"Of course,"
"How would you feel if you couldn’t have that mark in the end?" he asked, dark eyes gazing at the mark around my ring finger. "How would you feel if you...left first?"
I could see that Lesta was very careful, and very serious with his question, and it made me think that he was looking for an answer himself. I had no idea if my answer could help though, but I still wanted to give him an honest response.
"I would be sad," I looked at him with a smile, revealing what I had been worrying about. Thing I had yet found the courage to tell Natha. "Thinking about leaving Natha is sad," I continued, feeling the tremble in my heart and voice even when I said it. "Whether it ends up with Natha all alone, or Natha moving on to be with someone else..." I shook my head and let out a long sigh, "I would be sad."
"Moving on...to someone else..."
[Jade and Master is eternal!] The little bird that had been busy counting its candy inside the pouch suddenly jumped in front of me. [Jade will live as long as Master live!]
My eyes widened and I scooped the little bird, nuzzling the green head. "Oh, baby," I kissed the sweet, giggling little bird and we laughed together until the clerks came with our beautiful boxes of beautiful candies.

chapters.title: Chapter 261: For once, let me be the one who watches over other’s relationship
chapters.content:
Chapter 261: For once, let me be the one who watches over other’s relationship
After making sure Jade was satisfied with the candy, we continued with our journey to a place not far from the commercial district; the financial street.
This would be the second time I visited a bank in this world. The first time was to take all of Valmeier’s money so I could cover paid for his ’debt’ and pay the information fee on Amrita. Obviously, that bank was in the human realm, and the workers there looked at me like I was a vermin.
This second visit to a bank was vastly different. First; the bank was bigger, looking almost like a courthouse. Even then, Lesta said that the one in L’Anaak Eed was bigger, which made me decide that there was no use trying to make sense of Natha’s wealth.
Just as Natha said, the only thing I needed to do was enjoy that wealth. After all, if we could learn that mark of eternal, then we would die together. There was no need for me to receive the inheritance or anything. I looked down and patted the pendant on my chest.
I didn’t have to, but you’d probably need to learn about them, Shwa.
The second thing that was glaringly different: how the workers welcomed us. The guards and the clerks were lining up to bow and greet us with so much energy, making the clients look at us in wonder. And even though it was Lesta who was there for some business and inspection, they showed more courtesy toward me.
"Well, you’re basically the owner too, Young Master," Lesta chuckled at my surprise and confusion. "I’m just a lackey."
Lies. He definitely wasn’t just a lackey, despite always having fun by referring to himself as such. The workers, from the tellers to the Branch Head showed him high respect. If I had to compare him to the practice in my previous life, then it was probably something like an executive director.
"I don’t need to do anything, right?"
"You can wait in the VIP’s lounge, Young Master, or you can come with me to observe," he gave me the choice.
"I have this feeling that Eruha will give me a quiz once we get back so I’ll just follow you,"
He laughed at my begrudging answer, and I ended up following him into the Head’s office where he would have his meeting. They offered me the head seat around the table, but I refused because there was nothing for me to contribute to today’s agenda. Also, I preferred observing from afar, so they prepared a chair beneath the window--my favorite spot everywhere.
Do you know what they said about navigating the social life? It was to fake it. And that was what I did; acting like I understood what they were talking about by making sure I wasn’t falling asleep like Jade. I tried to maintain a calm but focused expression, as if I followed whatever they said closely.
In reality, there were too many things I didn’t understand. In the first place, I had no idea about the socio-economic scheme in the realm of gluttony, so I already lost comprehension within the first five minutes. Well, at least I knew they were talking about investment frameworks, and Lesta listened to the financial and operational report on the bank to be relayed to Natha later.
Hmm, yeah, I decided that I had no passion or talent in this side of the world. Financial was definitely not my thing. And I told Natha this once we got back to the Vampire Lord’s Castle in the evening.
"I’m envious of Jade," I told him truthfully. "I want to fall asleep too..."
Natha chuckled at my struggle to keep my mind focused on the business talk. "You don’t have to understand them. You just have to enjoy them."
I grinned and took out a box of candy from my storage ring. "That’s what I do!"
He patted my head in approval, and I gave him the most unstimulating taste among the candy inside the box. "Did you only buy candy after going around the city for the whole day?"
"Of course, not!" I said, and started to list all the shopping we did after the business with the bank was finished; souvenirs for the others.
"You buy things for others, but what about yourself?" Natha tilted his head as I spread my shopping hauls on the table.
"I bought candy and books," I shrugged.
"That’s it?"
"I don’t know what else to buy," I shook my head. It wasn’t like I really needed anything, because Natha always prepared things that I needed before I even knew I needed them.
Still, he didn’t seem to be satisfied with my answer. No--he even looked disappointed, as if he was upset I didn’t dry his coffers or something. I giggled and cupped his cheek. "Well, you’ve been taking care of me so well that I don’t feel like I need anything more."
"You should still indulge yourself," he said, before I stuffed another candy inside his mouth--a sour one this time.
"I indulged myself plenty, though?"
"Didn’t you go to the apparel store? What about the accessory shop? Did you check the auction house?"
I pressed my lips to prevent myself from laughing out loud. Why was it that he got so gunged up about me spending his money? Hmm...was he feeling guilty because he couldn’t accompany me around the city?
Interesting.
"Hmm...I guessed I wasn’t really in the mood to check on a lot of places because it wasn’t a date..." I half faked a disappointment--because the other half was true--and pouted, turning my face away from him.
"Sweetheart, I’m sorry," Natha sounded really regretful, trying hard to look at my turning face while stroking my arms apologetically. "Forgive me, yeah? I promise I’ll look for a time tomorrow; maybe we can visit some places together in the evening?"
I was only meant to tease him, but I couldn’t help getting excited by his words. "Really?" I turned my face to look at him again, but still maintaining my sulky expression. "Promise?"
"Promise," he said, before sealing it with a short, chaste kiss.
Well, I guessed there was no need for me to act sulky anymore. I giggled and threw my arms around his neck. I realized that even after doing this...selfish thing, I didn’t feel guilty or anything. I used to tell myself to never demand trivial things from him, but now I felt comfortable even when I acted greedy for his time and attention.
I wouldn’t say it was a bad feeling too. It was always nice to know that my partner cared about me this much.
"Well, alright," I nodded, squeezing his cheek to express my delight. "It’s too bad today that I can’t have a date with you, but it’s nice to walk around without guards following me for change--I mean, the visible ones," I added, because I knew there were still people guarding me from places I couldn’t see. Natha was nothing if not meticulous after all. But still, those people wouldn’t be able to do much if an accident happened next to me abruptly. "You really trust Lesta, huh?"
"Of course, there’s a reason I left a lot of my business with him," Natha replied nonchalantly, as if it was something obvious. "The La siblings are the first demons I could call my own people, so they will always have a special place in my household."
"Hmm, hmm,"
I nodded in agreement. It was clear when all three siblings held critical positions in Natha’s reign; one of them was in charge of internal matters, one of them was taking care of inter-realm relations, and another one was responsible for the whole realm’s logistics.
People would argue about Natha being biased, but I didn’t think it was weird to put someone you could totally trust in critical positions. The siblings had followed Natha even before he started his business and became the wealthiest demon in the realm. They were there when Natha took his revenge on the Spectre, and would always stand by his side no matter what. It was apparent from how they instantly welcomed me the first time without any fuss.
Moreover, they had no ties with anyone in the first place, so Natha didn’t have to worry about them bringing their own agenda to his household.
"They are also talented in their own way, so it was a bonus," Natha shrugged. "Lesta especially has the best ability in facing other people. His sisters are either too stony or too sunny."
Which was why he was in charge of foreign relations. "But he doesn’t seem like he could face Eruha well..." I muttered. It wasn’t just today--anytime Lesta lost his cool, it definitely had something to do with Eruha.
"That’s true," Natha smirked. "Fascinating, isn’t it?"
I looked at Natha and raised my brow. "You’re having fun, huh?"
"Aren’t you?"
I giggled in agreement, and then I recalled what happened in the candy store that afternoon. The conversation that we had about the ’what if’ scenario, was about what would I feel if I died before Natha because my lifespan had ended.
I didn’t think much about it before, because Jade suddenly said something so cute back then. But now, it dawned on me that I felt like Lesta was seeking some answer back then. I recalled back to my answer, and I wondered if it helped him make a decision.
I hoped so.
"What is it?" Natha asked me when he saw I was suddenly giggling to myself.
"Nothing," I shrugged. "I just hope everything’s resolved well between those two."
"That’s right," Natha nodded, although I had no idea if he wanted it to get resolved so his household’s peace wouldn’t get disrupted. "Well, let’s just observe from afar. For now, we have another feast to attend."
Ugh.

chapters.title: Chapter 262: I heard a chef is basically a scientist making edible stuff
chapters.content:
Chapter 262: I heard a chef is basically a scientist making edible stuff
Do we really have to attend all of these feasts?
Yes, yes we do. It was the custom here to hold a feast every time there was a guest, and it wasn’t just once, but on each day the guest stayed. So, yeah...I would have to power through this event every night.
But Natha told the Vampire Lord that I didn’t like taking my meal in public places--like the court hall--so the feast was now being held in the Lord’s quarters. Aside from the three vampires who attended yesterday, the other four vassals also came today. It seemed like they originally came for a meeting with Natha today, and extended their stay for the feast.
If you asked me how it felt to be surrounded by tall, pale, gorgeous people--you asked the wrong person. You had to ask their ’mother’, who for some reason stayed petite, unlike the other vampires.
For me, it was just a nice scenery, hehe. I wondered if they all looked good because they always ate high-quality food with a high content of mana. But probably because they were always on this hunt for mana, they all looked at me with interest.
No, no--they weren’t that suicidal to entertain the thought of drinking my blood with Natha by my side. But they did say they were interested in how potent my blood was.
I told you before that the high concentration of purified mana inside my system was comparable to liquor with high alcohol content. It was so thick that they would have to deconstruct the mana particle inside so they could absorb it without experiencing overdrive--which told me that if someday a vampire wanted to harm me, I could just pour my blood into their mouth and watch them seizing.
Or at least, that was the theory.
There was an excerpt from the vampire guideline book to never ask a druid for their blood even in an emergency, unless they had a way to dilute it. That was why no vampire had ever attempted to do it. But now they couldn’t help but be curious, especially because I was also half-human. They wondered if the potency was the same, and which was better between diluting it in pure water and diluting it in other drinks.
How do I say this; their curiosity was like a chef wondering the best way to process a puffer fish. Was it poisonous? Yes. Did it look tasty? Yes. Would they risk their life by pursuing it? Of course. Would they continue? Definitely.
Fascinating creatures, those chefs were.
"Are you kidding me?"
But of course, Natha wouldn’t let people have any thought about drawing my blood. I don’t think he would ever let me donate blood if there was such a thing here.
The vampires instantly made a disappointed face; Sada even pouted while eating her meal. What a curious bunch--they usually didn’t show much in their face, but if it was something they had great interest in, it was like they couldn’t let go.
"Hmm...I’m curious, though," I told them honestly, which prompted Natha to turn his head so fast toward me.
"Sweetheart--"
"See, your betrothed has more spirit to pursue knowledge!" the Vampire Lord slapped the table surface, before giving me a thumbs up.
The vampires--except for Eruha, who merely ate his meal quietly, perhaps because he didn’t want to get fired by his boss--looked at me with sparks in their red eyes. But, well...
I faced Natha and told him with what I hoped was a reassuring smile. "I want to see if I can use my blood as a weapon if a rogue vampire comes to me in the future."
"Hey!"
Natha raised his brow and nodded while tapping his chin. "Ah, that makes sense,"
"What makes sense?!"
"A valid reason," Lesta gave his approval too.
"But I still don’t like the thought of you bleeding out" Natha narrowed his eyes, looking at me sternly even though his hand caressing my hair in all gentleness.
I waved my hand nonchalantly and told him what I thought earlier. "I’m just thinking about cutting my finger a bit and dropping the blood in their mouth," with a shrug, I continued. "You know, the kind that can be healed easily with my regeneration."
The vampire parted their lips dumbfoundedly as Natha patted my head. "Only a little bit," he said, still with a stern voice but a lighter tone.
Meanwhile, the vampires looked like they didn’t know whether they should be happy or offended, chuckling among themselves. The Vampire Lord looked at me and shook her head. "There is a reason why you are Natha’s bride."
* * *
So that was how the after-dinner coffee turned into science class. Well, they were the ones who did the science, and I was the material. It was good that Jade had already fallen asleep from the day’s adventure, otherwise, the little bird would probably made a lot of fuss when Natha very carefully took out a syringe.
So much for being worried about wounds and injury--turned out they did have syringes in this world. And of course, Natha refused other people to draw my blood, even when Sada offered to call the Castle’s physicians.
"Do you even know how to do it?" she looked at Natha skeptically.
"More than you," Natha replied casually while rubbing alcohol on the inside of my elbow, looking as professional as professional could be.
It had already been almost seven decades since he became a doctor, but I guessed he still remembered everything, including how to locate the veins. To be fair, he could see my bloodstream with his eyes just like how he could see my mana veins, so it was an easy talk for him.
It wasn’t an easy task for me. If he wore a white lab coat--or even just a white coat in general--I would die. I would die and ascend.
"Calm down, sweetheart," Natha chuckled at my increasing heartbeat. Yeah, there was no need for adrenaline or aphrodisiac for me.
But how could I calm down when my fantasy almost manifested in front of me? I had to remind myself that we were in a public space and I had a needle in my hand. My face was obviously flushed, though, and I could see his smirk while he drew my blood.
And then, when it was done, he had the audacity to pat my head and said "Good boy," like I was a real patient, which made me smack his cheeks and squeeze them--because I might be tempted to make out with him then and there.
But he, the demon, leaned over and whispered to my ear. "Wait until the lab coat is finished."
Oh, for fuck’s sake.
"Hey, hey, hey--no flirting here," the Vampire Lord wiggled her finger in front of us.
But Natha did not move away from me, keeping his arm around my shoulder as we watched the vampires go on full scientist node--scientist plus chef. They had prepared vials filled with different liquids; water, wine, herbal concoctions, and something I had no idea what. They drip my blood into each vial, and what was left of it they divided among themselves.
And they proceed to taste my blood; raw and undiluted. Even the Vampire Lord.
"Ugh--" one of the vampires who seemed to be the youngest was coughing and grabbing his throat, before taking a pitch of water and pouring it in his mouth. "God--that burns!"
"Pathetic," an older vampire sneered at him, although he was also coughing once.
"This is truly potent," Atoye commented. "I feel drunk."
"But it’s nice," the Vampire Lord licked her lips, and Natha tightened his hand on my shoulder. "But I don’t think I can drink more than a spoonful."
Hmm...I wondered if that spoonful was enough to harm an ordinary vampire. Not that I wanted any vampire to come and try to harm me, though.
Done with testing the undiluted blood, they started to process the vials, and had the youngest try them because apparently, they wanted to see the effect on the weakest one. The result was as such; it was purer in water, but tasted better in wine.
"I wonder what it tasted like," I muttered as I watched the excited ’scientists’.
"Sweetheart?"
"No--I don’t mean I want to taste my own blood. I’m just curious about the sensation," I corrected myself immediately.
The Vampire Lord, hearing my words, immediately snapped her fingers and something was coming out of thin air. "If you wonder what it tasted like, you can try this."
I looked at the bottle in front of the Vampire Lord, which was obviously a liquor. Atoye proceeded to open the bottle and pour the contents into a glass before bringing it over to me.
"It is brewed with the purest mana crystal," Sada explained, and I took the glass with interest. I looked at Natha and he nodded, telling me to sip just a bit first, and so I did.
And whew--it burns my throat slightly. It was rather bitter with a slight sweetness, spreading warmth inside my body, but also felt refreshing. "Not bad...?"
"Oh-ho!" Sada suddenly slammed her palms on the table and called out to the servants to bring more wines and alcoholic drinks inside. "This means we have to party!"
What? Didn’t we just have a feast? Wasn’t that a party, already?
But I had never been truly drinking again after the kingdom’s banquet where I met Natha. Secretly, I felt excited--mainly because Natha was here and I knew I would be safe. Perhaps that was why I let loose and accepted their drinking challenge.
Different from the time in the kingdom’s banquet, this time I had already awakened my druit lineage, so I was less influenced by alcohol. It even fascinated me how much I could drink without being too intoxicated. Before I could be fully drunk, I was already feeling full from all the liquid. Not to mention all the food I ate earlier.
"Ugh...I feel so full," I patted my tummy, which felt soft and round. "It feels like when Natha is inside me..."
splurt!
I heard the Vampire Lord spraying water everywhere. Eww. And then I heard Natha’s voice. "Sweetheart?"
I looked at him, feeling dazed and a bit sleepy, but he was so handsome that I couldn’t help but keep my eyes open so I could see him. I reached out to pat his cheek, and then tugged his sleeve.
"Pee..." I pouted. "Wanna pee..."
"...okay," he laughed, looking so handsome and sounded so good. "Let’s get you out of here."
"Ngh--carry me!" I reached out my arms, and Natha lifted me into his embrace.
Wrapping my arms tightly around his neck, I giggled against his neck, and I felt my body moving away from everyone. It felt like flying, so fun! I should have asked him to carry me more often! Everyday!
"Good night," I saw Lesta give me a little wave, and I laughed, waving at him and all the vampires.
"Bye bye..."

chapters.title: Chapter 263: But sometimes, getting drunk helps us saying things we can’t usually say
chapters.content:
Chapter 263: But sometimes, getting drunk helps us saying things we can’t usually say
Dazedly, I blinked as Natha put me down on the floor and turned me around gently. It was cold and when he tugged my pants down, it got even colder.
Why did he tug my pants down?
Oh, right. Pee. I need to pee. All of those wines and meads made me want to pee. Natha even being so generous and helping me aimed, so all I needed to do was just pee.
"Okay, that’s it, let it all out..."
Mmh--his voice next to my ear was so good, I couldn’t help but shudder at it. He put his hand on my abdomen, pressing me there, reminding me of the time he sometimes pressed my slightly distended skin when he was inside me.
Why wasn’t he inside me, though?
Right, because I was peeing.
"Are you done?" he asked me kindly.
Well, I was done, but...I looked down and saw his hand on my peepee. This wasn’t right. He should stroke his hand when it was there. Why didn’t he? It’d feel good...
"Nat..." I whined and wriggled my hips, rutting on his hand.
"What a naughty boy,"
He chuckled against my earlobe and it was so, so delicious. So good. I was instantly up, and he laughed behind me. But he also started to stroke me, so it was good, mm, yeah, really good.
"Alright. Let’s get you off once and we’ll go to bed, okay?"
He kissed my temple and stroked me harder. Did he just say once? Why only once? Ahh--but I couldn’t think anymore. His touch was so good, and although I wanted him to teach me more, I was already feeling it so much just from his handjob. Throwing my head back to his shoulder, moans spilled out of my mouth, until I shuddered and released with a tight grip on his forearm.
Oh, that was good. I heard the sound of water, and then his chuckle before kissing my cheek and fixing my pants.
"Nggh?" I looked down and pursed my lips. "Why are you putting on my pants?"
"So we can go back to the bed and sleep?"
"No!" I looked up and frowned at him. "No! I want to do it!"
I could see his arching brow, and then his slightly reddened cheek. I could even feel the slight bulge behind me, against my lower back. So he was also aroused. So why did he talk about going back to bed?
"We can do it later tomorrow when you’re sober," he said with a smile, which only made me feel annoyed.
So I stomped my foot and pouted. "Do it now! I want to do it now!"
Why didn’t he want to do it now? I wanted to protest more but he had already scooped me up and carried me back inside the bedroom. "Tomorrow, okay?" he tried to coax me using a voice that had no business of sounding that good. "We can even do it immediately after you wake up if you want, so be good and have patience, mm?"
He kissed my temple again, but that just made me want him to touch me more. I bit my lips in defiance and wrapped my arms around his shoulder, leaning over and putting my mouth on his neck.
And bit him.
Whatever--this was a vampire castle anyway.
"Sweetheart," Natha sighed, but I bit him harder; not enough to draw blood, but enough to bruise him. I looked at the bite mark for a while, and, feeling dissatisfied, started to kiss it and suck on his flesh. "Sweetheart," he gave me a sigh
that almost sounded like a stern warning.
But I was annoyed so I didn’t care.
Satisfied with the reaction and the visible mark I left there, I made another one on his shoulder after yanking his shirt open. What could he do? He had to use both hands to carry me.
Unfortunately, before I could make a third mark, we reached the bed and he put me down on the mattress. He rubbed the mark that I just made, still wet from my saliva, and looked at me like I was a naughty kid. Did I care? Of course not! Right after he took off my shoes, I raised my foot and pressed it on his crotch. He grabbed my ankle to shift my leg away, but not before I felt his erection.
See, he was totally turned on!
Well, I still had another leg.
"Haa...come on, sweetheart," he grabbed the other leg too, and I raised my body so I could hit him.
"I had been missing you all day!" I yelled at him--I didn’t care if I sounded childish or selfish. "I wanted to have a date with you, but you’re always working! I wanted to have a quiet meal with you, but I can’t! Now you’re denying me too! I hate it!"
He looked surprised at my sudden outburst, enough to let go of my leg, and I used the chance to get on his lap. Grabbing his shirt, I pressed my head on his chest and felt heat stinging my eyes. "Don’t you miss me?"
"Oh, sweetheart, of course I miss you," he cupped my cheek and lifted my face. "But I don’t want to take you when you’re drunk, not because I don’t want to be with you."
"I’m not
that
drunk," I pursed my lips. Right? I mean...I could still talk..."What’s the big deal? I’m still sober enough to know it’s you!"
"Sweetheart, that’s not--"
"Aren’t you my future husband anyway?" I pouted, shaking his clothes and whining.
This time, he didn’t try to stop me, or use that coaxing ’sweetheart’ again. Instead, he looked at me unblinkingly, grasping my face a bit harder. "What did you say?"
"Huh?" there was a shift in his voice and expression, and my increasingly beating heart told me I shouldn’t let this chance go. "Aren’t you...my future husband?"
And then the world shifted, and I was on my back, staring at his sharp silver eyes. "Say that again," he commanded.
Oh? Oh! Gulping, I spoke of the word he probably wanted to hear the most. "...husband?"
My vision changed again, because I could no longer see his face. His face that was pressed onto mine, lips crashing together. His hand was on my nape, tilting my head so he could kiss me deeper, and I knew it was done. He wouldn’t reject me anymore. Not with his other hand on my waist lifting my hips so our lower bodies pressing and grinding against each other.
Wrapping my arms around his neck, I laughed between the kiss, and he pulled away just enough so he could look into my eyes with a piercing gaze. "I told you to not rile me up, Valen."
Oh, Mother, he called me by my name. It means tonight would be truly, truly fantastic.
* * *
"I’ve never seen Young Master drunk before, that was quite funny," Lesta chuckled as he walked back to his room with Eruha. "Too bad His Lordship whisked him away immediately."
"Understandable," Eruha commented briefly, and Lesta couldn’t help but glance at the vampire, who was just insinuating that he knew the feeling of wanting to keep other people’s eyes away from his lover.
Not that they were lovers.
Yet.
"Why are you walking me back?" Lesta asked as he opened his bedroom door, looking back at the vampire.
"Can’t I?" Eruha replied casually, leaning against the door frame and looking at the demon with his usual expressionless eyes.
The combination of the casual answer and the dry expression made Lesta feel lost, without any idea how to respond. He just looked at the vampire without saying anything, thinking back to his conversation with Valen earlier during the day.
Would he be able to accept if, should Eruha drink someone else’s blood after he die?
"Kiss me," he said, and this time, the flat expression shifted. Those calm eyes seemed to be shaking just a bit. "I want to know how it feels while I’m sober."
With the sound of a slamming door, Lesta staggered back as the vampire grabbed his upper arms and claimed his lips with unexpected ferocity. He was expecting something soft, something sweet, something that said ’here, have a taste’.
He did not expect for himself to get...eaten. For his lips to be sucked and bitten, for his mouth to be explored, for his tongue to be played. The grip on his arms moved to his hair, tilting him for more access, and to his back, holding him so he didn’t fall. Because he certainly would without that, from the combined weight of the tall vampire, and the way his legs lost power.
It was a kiss that made him feel like he was an object of desire. To feel like this beautiful specimen did want him. It was so much that he felt like he could get intoxicated even without the vampire’s poison.
"Are you...haa...trying to kiss me or--ngh--eat me?" Lesta pushed the vampire away to gather air back into his lungs. But it was a difficult thing to do when Eruha looked at him with a blazing gaze and a smirk.
"Well, I’m a vampire after all," Eruha said before leaning down to kiss the demon again. This time though, as if he had quenched his thirst already, the kiss was gentle and soft, just how Lesta expected it earlier. A gentle caress on the slightly swollen lips, a soft stroke on his back and waist.
Looking into the deep eyes that were filled with ardor, Lesta thought that this wouldn’t just end with mere kisses. And with that, he pulled the vampire closer and started to kiss back.

chapters.title: Chapter 264: It’s nice to have someone opening their heart to you
chapters.content:
Chapter 264: It’s nice to have someone opening their heart to you
I looked at the ceiling, blinking, before kicking my feet slightly beneath the blanket and giggling like a child.
"Sweetheart, I know you’re full of energy, but I need my rest, okay?"
A cold arm wrapped around me to prevent me from moving and shaking the bed. The soft vibration from Natha’s slurry voice tickled my nape, and I clasped my mouth to prevent myself from making another noise. Carefully, I shifted and turned so I could face him instead, looking at his sleeping face.
Okay, okay, I know I looked at him every day, but still...
I never felt bored looking at his face. Well, to be fair, I rarely do so, okay? I couldn’t just outright stare at him in front of other people, or when he was awake, because I would be too embarrassed. Before, I wouldn’t even do anything but stare when I woke up first, but these days, I got more courageous to trace my fingers on his face.
This time, he looked rather exhausted. Hmm...perhaps because I kept asking for more last night? We did it until I sobered up, and then more. And yeah, it was as fantastic as fantastic could be. He was rougher than usual, which I liked, because he had always been too gentle, despite knowing I had better stamina and self-healing ability than him.
It seemed like calling him husband pushed his button, which was...quite embarrassing, now that I was sober. Ugh, he probably would tease about it after he woke up and gained his energy back. I had a guess he would even ask me to say it again, which I wouldn’t! Unless he was asleep, or I was drunk, or...
Or I had something I wanted to request from him, hehe.
I kept stroking his cheek and enjoyed his soft breathing, until I felt someone’s presence outside the bedroom door. So I sneaked out of bed and wrapped myself in a fluffy fur coat before carefully opening the door.
The attendant who stood outside the door retreated and bowed politely. It was the one sent to serve us while we were here, the one who made our morning drink and coordinated the servants in charge of our quarter’s housekeeping.
"His Lordship is still asleep, is there anything urgent?"
By the look of it, Natha would sleep in today, so perhaps we could have a late breakfast away from the Vampire Lord? Mm, that sounded good. I had to tell this attendant while at it.
"Oh, no, Sir. Someone’s here for you," the attendant said, which had me surprised. Someone coming for me so early in the morning? Me of all people?
And then I looked toward the door and couldn’t help but smile. "Let him in. Would you be a dear and get me my usual drink?"
"Certainly, Sir."
Hmm...what a nice morning to hear some juicy story.
Making myself comfortable in front of the fireplace, I watched Lesta wobbling inside while grumbling and cursing, devoid of his calm countenance. "Rough night?"
"Help me," he said briefly, before slumping on the couch and leaning--or rather, crashing--toward me. I caught and wrapped him in a blanket, before patting his back while sending a rejuvenating spell.
Damn...what have you done, Eruha?
While I healed the demon, I noticed something--or rather, a lack of something. "You don’t have any puncture marks."
"No," Lesta mumbled into the blanket. It was quite funny hearing him let go of his usual persona. "We’re not doing that this time," and then, after a while, he added. "And that’s why I’m in this situation."
"Huh? How so?"
"We’ve never... done it without me being...hmm, poisoned?"
My brow arched, and so did the attendant who brought my herbal drink, although it was only for a second. I took my drink while stifling my laugh and asked Lesta if he wanted a drink. He asked for a wine, so I told the attendant to make a coffee. Bad Lesta!
"Wait..." While I had my drink, something suddenly occurred to me. "You mean...you hadn’t been sober all those other times?"
"Yeah," he massages his neck, and then caught the look on my face, and chuckled. "No, it is by consent."
Oh, what a relief. Wouldn’t it be weird if Natha taught me everything about consent when his subordinates did not abide by that?
"He told me about the effect of the poison beforehand, and I told him I didn’t mind with it," Lesta explained further. "It was better than agonizingly letting the poison wane by itself."
"Better because it’s good, or better because it’s him?"
Lesta paused for a bit, before answering with slightly reddened ears. "Both."
Wow. Wow. I didn’t know if I should say this, but I kind of feel excited. Not because of his problem, but because I was in a position that listened to other’s relationship matters for a change.
But let’s press on a brake here. So he told me all this time, they had been doing it while Lesta was...how should I say this, intoxicated? So he would only have a vague recollection of those events? For decades?
Geez. No wonder their relationship was vague.
"But wait--how could you tell it was good when you’re practically not sober all the time?" I tilted my head, staring at him inquisitively while sipping my drink.
"I don’t remember all of it," Lesta stretched his body once I rejuvenated him enough. "But I remember how I felt--well, my body remembers it,"
"Heh," I snickered, and he chuckled, and we ended up laughing quietly because we both knew how it felt; the feeling of leftover pleasure from a satiated body.
"Hmm..." I leaned my head onto the pile of pillows and observed the demon who finally looking alive again. "So...aside from...that, have you never talked about...well, your feelings or anything? About being his Eternal?"
"No," Lesta sneered at himself. "Because we’re stupid."
Huh.
I waited for him to elaborate, and also because the attendant came with Lesta’s coffee, which he didn’t mind taking even though it wasn’t wine. He took a sip of the steaming coffee and let it resonate with the rejuvenating spell, before finally speaking again.
"He never said anything because he was waiting for me to...I guess, to see us as something more than a vampire and a source," he said. "He told me that telling me about it before I’m ’ready’ would seem like he forced me to accept it and...well, let’s say he doesn’t want to force me, so to speak."
Oh? That made Eruha sound more gentle and considerate than I initially thought. But then again, it could also be because Lesta narrating it through his rote-tinted glasses.
"So...since he kept hiding it all this time, that means..."
"That I still think of us as a mere vampire-and-source pair?" Lesta smiled in this self-mocking way. "Well, yeah, I couldn’t help it. He never showed that he desired something more from me, so I thought that was my only value in his eyes. Well, that and a decent colleague,"
I blinked and replied carefully. "Are you...sure about that?"
"Well, I was sure," Lesta sighed. This was the first time I saw him rather distressed.
I couldn’t help but raise my brows in surprise. Was this what they meant by the eyes cannot see what the mind doesn’t know? Because I was so sure Eruha had something for Lesta, and I was sure everyone knew it too. Everyone but Lesta himself, apparently, because he thought he was nothing but a working partner.
Hmph. And Natha told me I was dense.
"Well, to be honest, it was probably just my inferiority complex," Lesta gave a sudden confession, and I stopped myself from sipping on my drink so I could hear him better. Staring at the fresh fire in front of us, Lesta sounded quite vulnerable when he spoke again. "I was just a street orphan before I met His Lordship, doing whatever to survive, even tricking adventurers and stealing petty coins. It was only after His Lordship took us that I could find education and live like a decent people."
Leaning on the couch and looking at the exquisite cross beam above us, Lesta chuckled before he continued. "Eruha, on the other hand, was noble since birth. He was born from the First Progenitor, the youngest of the Thirteen, so he is dotted upon by his siblings; which is why he is allowed to do whatever he wants. He could be the Lord of Gluttony someday, by the way, since only the Thirteen are allowed on the seat."
Oh, that was a new information. Although...well, that was to be expected. This was the land of vampires anyway, so it was only normal that only a vampire could be the Lord. And well, there was a clear hierarchy in the vampire community by whose blood they were born, so saying Eruha was considered a ’noble vampire’ wasn’t wrong.
And I guessed helping Natha would give him ample practice should he decide to take the position too.
"Umm...so did you think...you were lesser than him?" I asked carefully. "You think you don’t deserve him?"
There was only one reason why I asked this of him; because I was feeling the same in the past. I constantly thought that I was nothing, I had nothing, I could bring nothing; that I didn’t deserve to be loved by someone like Natha, even though it was all I ever wanted.
And it was probably what Lesta was thinking about. "Yeah," he said. "Yeah, I did. I think I unconsciously put myself beneath him, so I never had any courage to see past that, or tell myself to ignore it and just tell him what I feel."
Oh, Lesta...I knew that very well. And he probably had it harder, because he had to struggle with it for decades. And I could see that he had never told anyone about any of this before. He spoke quietly, sometimes with a shaking and hesitant voice, while sighing in between.
When he said ’help me’...was it not just about healing him? Was Lesta, actually, just wanted to speak to someone about this? Perhaps. Because honestly, I couldn’t see him doing that to his siblings; the stony Malta and the blabber Arta.
Oh, this made me happy, even though it could be just my delusion. But I was happy nonetheless that he was willing to speak to me about it, even though it made him look vulnerable and everything.
"So...have you made a decision?"
He lifted his head and, in a dumbfounded way, replied dazedly. "Oh, I was already in this state before even managed to tell him about it."
Pfft
--so it seemed like he already made a decision. I patted his back and sent more rejuvenating mana as a bonus, until a sleepy Natha showed up behind the couch with narrowed eyes. "What are you doing here stealing my bride away first thing in the morning?"
Whelp--I guessed that was the end of our hearty session.

chapters.title: Chapter 265: I’m collecting my fantasy must-haves one by one
chapters.content:
Chapter 265: I’m collecting my fantasy must-haves one by one
Thanks to Natha waking up like usual, we still had to eat breakfast with the Vampire Lord, who narrowed her eyes at me for some reason.
Why?
"Haa...you naughty little minx," she shook her head after giving me a bombastic review.
My eyes squinted at her as I took a seat. "Thank you?"
[Master, what a naughty little minx?]
"I don’t know, Jade, don’t remember those words," I whispered to the little bird, who obediently nodded with a serious face.
[Okay, it’s too difficult for Jade]
Good bird, good bird! I gave Jade permission to have one candy for breakfast since it was such a good bird. All of Sada’s children/Eruha’s nieces and nephews were also there before they went back to their territories. They all looked hungover, though, but still managed to stare at me like I was a fascinating creature.
"How could you look this...fresh?"
"Because I’m a druid?" I shrugged. Okay, well, perhaps I wasn’t that strong in drinking, because I still got drunk, but hey--at least I would never experience having a hungover and throwing up at Natha ever again.
"How envious," one of them, Nadira, someone who really really liked to drink, but also really really lightweight, pursed her lips and laid her throbbing head on the table.
Whelp--all I could do was grin and happily stuff my stomach with food after a nice session of a night-time body workout.
Natha patted my head because I was eating so well, and so did Sada, and then all of the vampires except Eruha gave me one too, saying it was a thank you and a goodbye, because they needed to get back to work. Uhh...it was annoying that they treated me like I was a child--although I guessed they were all several hundred older than me--but it was also nice because they were all treating me nicely.
And it was even nicer because Natha told me to wait for two hours in our room, and exactly after two hours, he came back and immediately took me on a date.
Did...did he just do everything he had to do today in those two hours so he could take me on a date? And...and he even bribed Jade so the little bird would stay with Lesta instead of tagging us?
"My Lord, my birthday is in the fifth month," I told him.
"You don’t think I know that already?" Natha laughed while lifting me into the carriage.
"But why are you doing things that felt like a birthday gift?"
"My, my, how could the Lord of Greed’s betrothed think a mere date equal to a birthday gift," he shook his head and made a disappointed look as he climbed the carriage. "’Tis nothing but a mere obligation one should carry for the beloved, more so if it were these pretty lips which invoke such an order."
...who are you?!
That was heart-throbbing, though, when he rubbed my lips as he said it. Made me gulping and all. "...uhh, did I... ask you for this? Last night?"
"No, you just whine about me working all the time and never taking you on a date," he laughed softly and kissed the back of my hand as if he were a gentleman.
"I...I did?"
Ugh--this is why I said never get drunk anymore!
He chuckled at my guilty face, and kissed my forehead gently as the carriage started to run. "It’s fine. It’s my fault for neglecting my pretty, adorable bride," he said while I buried my face in embarrassment. "And you said it so adorably too."
Aaagh! Even though I promised myself to never be the kind of lover who got jealous of his works!
Thankfully, he stopped teasing me about it, and I stopped thinking about all the embarrassment my drunken self made the moment we entered the city. I told him about all of the places I wanted to visit with him yesterday, including the nice dessert cafe in an upper district that had a beautiful view of the city landscape. I told him I wanted to see the stores selling magic tools for reference, and we ended up making a huge purchase.
But the best event should be the auction we went to after lunch, specifically only auctioning the rarest of ingredients and cooking equipment, including a one-in-a-century rainbow-colored fruit and a knife made by a renowned drow blacksmith--which Natha both purchased because I said the fruit reminded me of Jade’s tails and the knife seemed like a nice gift for Angwi. He also won some other stuff, mainly herbs, but I had no idea what their exact function was. Well, needless to say, we left the auction house with many eyes on us thanks to his nonchalant way of bidding.
What greeted us the moment we came back was Jade’s headbutt and a farewell feast, because we would visit Natha’s teacher tomorrow. By us, I mean me and Natha, because Lesta and Eruha still had their work to finish here before getting back to L’Anaak Eed.
Before we departed the next morning, I turned to look at my more-or-less teacher and told him off. "Eruha, don’t tire Lesta too much, okay? I’m not going to be here to heal him."
He looked genuinely surprised at my warning and raised his head. The vampire who rarely lied outside of his strategy movement averted his eyes and replied hesitatingly. "...I’ll try,"
"Don’t try, do it!" I puffed my cheek in annoyance, because it seemed like the extent of his willingness to try was as short as Jade’s tail in little bird form. So I looked at the vampire’s boss. "Nat!"
"If my sweetheart so wishes," Natha replied while raising his brow at Eruha, who slightly pursed his lips and put his hand above his chest.
"By Your Highness’s command."
"Hey!" I clicked my tongue at how he used the title which made me the most embarrassed. But Lesta was stifling his laugh on the side, so I guessed it was enough for now. "Well, as long as you adhere to it."
Natha patted my head softly, as one of the vampire vassals approached us to inform us that our mount beast was ready.
Yep--we weren’t going by carriage, but a mounted beast. Since we would have to traverse the jungle and mountain range before reaching the teacher’s abode, one which did not allow for movement-related magic, it was either a mount beast or our own feet.
Easy choice, if you ask me.
But I didn’t know until right when I saw it, that our mount beats would be...a wyvern.
My lips parted as I saw the large body and even larger wings filled up my vision. It was slightly bigger than a modern aircraft, looking as scary as it was majestic. The rider made the wyvern on the field in front of us, and Natha whispered to me.
"Well, we can’t do anything about the dragon, but I hope this satisfies you enough for now,"
I took a deep breath, knowing that wyvern was actually rare. They were too dangerous to be let out in the wilderness, but also too beneficial to be killed, which was why demons started to tame them. But it was also hard to breed them, so even after successfully taming them, wyverns were still few in number. Those who had them as mount beast was usually big clans or big transportation company that rented them to VIP clients, because they were that expensive. Even Natha felt having a wyvern was a pointless expense, and never thought of acquiring one--that, and he could teleport anyway.
But one look at the saddle and the identification bracelet on its leg, which bore Natha’s double-wing crest, already told me that he didn’t just rent it. He bought it.
Because...I asked him about the dragons?
"I wasn’t sure it would come right on time, but it seems like they do deliver. It’s quite hard looking for something with your color," Natha said while caressing my hair, as my eyes ran over the bark-colored dark scale, dark green skin, and leafy wing membranes.
"It’s...it’s ours?" I blinked as the big yellow eyes of the wyvern gazed in my direction.
"She’s yours," Natha said. "Go give her a name."
I pressed my lips and turned toward Natha, kissing him briefly before running toward the wyvern. The wyvern straightened its neck as I approached, and the rider as well as the vampires gave me a warning.
"Be careful, Young Master! She’s still not completely tamed!"
Really? I slowed down my steps, but as I looked at the yellow eyes with green speckles around them, I didn’t see any malice. So although I wasn’t running anymore, I didn’t hesitate to approach her. Her triangular head followed my movement, and when I stretched out my arms, the head lowered above me, looming--
"Young Master!"
--and nuzzled the side of my head. It was so big that even my arms couldn’t cradle the head, and the scales felt ticklish as they grazed me, because they were actually covered in soft, thin, almost invisible bristle.
I laughed and patted the thick flesh beneath the yellow eyes, stroking my new mount--no, companion. "Mm, mm, good girl! Aren’t you a good and nice girl?"
She made a deep sound that almost rang like a purr, and I stroked the dark forehead, from which horns with intertwining gray and green veins jutted out. The wyvern lowered her body completely now, laying--or crouching?--on the field so I didn’t have to look up anymore. Gosh, so considerate!
"Nat, she’s so pretty!" I looked back and saw my Demon Lord walking closer with a satisfied smile on his face. There was someone who wasn’t satisfied, however.
Jade hovered around me while chirping aggressively. Yeah, just chirping. The little bird didn’t even talk inside my head, just chirping, which meant it was either mumbling or cursing.
"Why, Jade? You’re pretty too, the prettiest," I laughed and patted the jealous little bird. "Come here and say hi to her, she’s going to be our friend, you know."
The beady green eyes narrowed, and Jase sulkily landed on my shoulder, watching the wyvern who only looked at Jade cooly and calmly, probably wondering why she was suddenly berated by this little bird.
I put my hand on her head, and told them; "Her name is Vrida," she blinked and purred again for a few seconds, before nuzzling my palm. "And this is Jade, my dearest familiar."
[Dearest!]
I patted the little bird, who then jumped onto Vrida’s head, just like what it did to Ignis back then. Was that Jade’s way of asserting dominance? It would be rather cute if that were the case. Just like Ignis, Vrida also didn’t mind it, probably just seeing it as a child’s antics.
"Dearest, huh? What about me?" I felt Natha’s arms around my waist and his lips on my temple.
"You?" I looked up and smiled at the pair of moonlight. "You’re the one I can’t live without."

chapters.title: Chapter 266: Of course, a Sacred Guardian’s abode should be special
chapters.content:
Chapter 266: Of course, a Sacred Guardian’s abode should be special
Of course, Natha knew how to ride a wyvern. Why wouldn’t he? He’s Natha.
But even if he couldn’t, it was alright, because we didn’t need to control Vrida. All I needed to do was ask her to take us to our destination, and voila! I might not be able to have a full conversation with her like a true druid, but there was enough bloodline inside me to make sure I could communicate with her well.
"I wouldn’t say I’m surprised, but well...you really are a druid," the Vampire Lord commented as Natha lifted me up and put me on Vrida’s back.
It was already fitted with a comfortable padded saddle lined with fur for that extra fluffiness, and I already made sure Vrida wasn’t uncomfortable with the saddle. Thankfully, it was made of high-quality materials with care and tailored to her size.
"Well, it’s also because Vrida is such a good girl," I patted the side of the wyvern’s neck, and she let out another deep purr in response. See? A very good girl!
"That’s not what I heard from her tamer, but what do I know," the Vampire Lord shrugged and suddenly threw something at me.
A small box, even smaller than a ring box. As I opened it in wonder, there was a small deep red sphere inside. Or rather...was it a pill?
"An engagement gift," she curled her lips, probably because Natha was making a surprised face, and put his hand over the box to close it as if he didn’t want the content to be spoiled. He looked at the Vampire Lord seriously, which prompted Sada to sneer. "It’s not for you, it’s for Valen, because I like him more than I like you."
"In just three days?"
"Isn’t he a charming one? You must have been so dizzy making sure he’s not getting snatched by others," she laughed merrily at the way Natha clicked his tongue.
"Excuse me--I’m still here, you know," I sighed while carefully placing the box inside my storage ring. "Thank you, Sada."
"Mm, do come here again. No need to bring Natha along," she waved her hand as if the Demon Lord of Greed was just an afterthought.
I laughed as Natha climbed behind me while grumbling, and Vrida began to straighten her legs. "What’s that pill exactly?" I asked Natha in a whisper.
"Elixir of Second Life," Natha explained. "It allows an instant healing as long as the heart still pumping blood, basically giving a second life, hence the name."
What?!
"It is made from purifying the blood of a vampire on their thousandth birthday."
Again; what?!
And why? What have I done? Now I understood why Natha was surprised. Well, I got that she liked me, but this kind of gift...was it because I willingly participated in the ’research’ yesterday night? But I also said I did it to find out the lethal dose of--wait, that’s not the time for this!
"Thank you! Sada--thank you again! I’ll make sure to visit again!" I told her loudly to make sure she heard it despite the sound of the wind that Vrida’s wings made.
She laughed and waved her hand, so I responded in kind, and we took off with the sound of laughter and loud, excited chirping, until the Vampire Castle became smaller, and smaller, and smaller.
* * *
[Wheeeeee] Jade, using wind magic to maintain balance on top of Vrida’s head, squealing excitedly.
"Is it fun?" I asked with a laugh, making sure my coat and hood stayed in place. It acted like a helmet and windshield thanks to the spell embedded in it, so I wouldn’t have to feel like riding a rollercoaster without a safety belt.
[Yeeees! It’s faster than Jade!]
It was cute that the earlier jealousy had faded just like that, now that the little bird finding Vrida fun to be around. I nodded in satisfaction and leaned against the all-time reliable safety belt--I mean, Demon Lord--behind me. Natha patted my chest to make sure my coat was securely protecting me from the wind, before wrapping his arms around my waist.
"This is nice, like riding a very fast, flying motorcycle," I giggled while holding his arms.
"Motorcycles shouldn’t be this fast and flying in the first place," Natha shook his head and chuckled. "And shouldn’t you ride on the back in that case?"
"Don’t sweat the details!" I clicked my tongue at this realistic Demon Lord, who just laughed and tightened his hold on me.
Well, anyway, although I had flown with an airship before, and had floated in the air with Natha, riding a wyvern was a completely different stuff. Of course, it wasn’t as comfortable as an airship or flying carriages, but it was definitely faster. It wasn’t just a matter of speed, though, but also the way I could see the scenery on all sides while feeling the refreshing cold wind.
And, Mother--I think I know now why there were a lot of people who dreamt of flying.
To be able to see the Vampire Castle from above, and then the whole cityscape...ah, I truly wish we managed to make a camera soon. Or better yet, a video recording. I would be able to record all of these things I saw; all the farmlands that the vampires grew, the castles they lived in, and even the ruins that explorers and adventurers raided. Riding a wyvern meant you could go low or high, and maneuver all you wanted, so we ended up looking closer at places I wanted to observe, and Natha would give explanations about them.
You know what this was called? A road trip.
It felt like something I would never be able to do if I didn’t go to this world and meet Natha. Wonderful.
From the Vampire Capital, we were heading deeper into the center of the demon realm, a mountain range that was surrounded by forest and a vast plateau. It was a place that technically fell within the region of Gluttony, but wasn’t part of anyone’s jurisdiction.
Of course, since we were in the middle of the winter, the forest and plateau were getting blanketed by snow, and didn’t look like there was anything special with the place. The snowy mountains looked more intimidating than beautiful as we were getting closer, especially because Natha suddenly told me to grab Jade. While I called the little bird to come inside my coat, Natha spread his mana around us, including Vrida, and only a few seconds after that, I felt a slight turbulence as we breached an invisible barrier.
I had to close my eyes for a bit as we passed the barrier surrounding the place, and when I opened them again...
"Oh, wow..."
It was no longer a field of snow.
As if symbolizing the eternal life and unchanging time of the vampire, the world on the other side of the barrier knew not of the changing of seasons. Or probably the changing of time. A vibrant world that was beautiful, and yet different. A lush colorful forest, a plateau dyed in yellow hue, cliffs covered in reddish algae. They circled a mountain range that was filled with white blossom trees, filling the air with a fragrant scent and a sense of serenity.
It was so beautiful, so magnificent, that it didn’t feel real. It was so much like a painting, so flawless, as if someone took a perfect photograph of the right place during the right time, and decided to live inside that photograph.
That was why I said I felt like time did not change here.
There was a weird sense of stagnancy. The scenery looked as if the place was bathed in spring festivity, yet everything felt old, ancient. Spring should be the time for a new life, for budding sprouts to peek out beneath the softening soils, for hiding animals to surface and creating more lives.
But I don’t sense those here.
I looked up and took a deep breath, spreading my consciousness to confirm my conjecture, and felt a soft force of mana enveloping the whole place. The mana strands spread out and connected to each other like a giant net encompassing the whole space, and all the flow came from a single point; the mountain.
Or rather, the building on top of the mountain.
"What is it?" Natha sensed my confusion and uneasiness, caressing my arms as Vrida glided slower toward the mountain.
"No, it’s just..." I hesitated for a bit, thinking about the way to explain it. "It’s like entering a dimensional pocket."
I looked down at my necklace, at where Shwa was, and thought about how it would feel like to be living there. This place felt like a massive version of this dimensional field, but it also did not feel artificial, just...stagnant.
"Hmm...I see," Natha nodded, seemingly understanding what I meant without any difficulty. "Is it because this place kept repeating the same day?"
...huh?

chapters.title: Chapter 267: Isn’t it nice when our imagination is finally on point?
chapters.content:
Chapter 267: Isn’t it nice when our imagination is finally on point?
"So it was true? The stagnancy I felt in this place was because it was a suspended space?" I gasped and tilted my head to look at Natha.
"Well, not truly suspended, since time still flows for her and for us," Natha explained while looking around the space he hadn’t visited in a long time. "The land just kept repeating each day."
Repeating each day but only for a select point? It would mean that anything growing during the day would revert back to the condition twenty-four hours before; the weather, the sky, the wind blow--everything would be the same. Even if I came here and purposefully spread pollen so more plants would grow, everything would return to how it was supposed to be yesterday.
Everything that was blanketed by those nets of mana.
What kind of magic did she use? It must have been so complex, to separate this space from the rest of the world, and forcefully prevented it from changing. And then putting on a barrier that made people see it as another part of nature. There were probably dozens...no, hundreds of spells woven together to keep this place like this for hundreds, maybe thousands of years.
"...why?" I asked quietly in confusion.
Why would someone want to live in a place that never changed? Of course, I loved spring too. But watching the season change, watching things grow and pass...it was the joy of the living. Perhaps it was because I had been living most of my life inside an unchanging hospital room, but...this paradise almost felt like a prison.
