"The bond of eternal means you exchange a piece of your soul with your partner," she waved her finger to separate the circle, and both turned a dull shade of their original color. "To be incomplete when you’re alone—" she moved the circles back together, and once they were connected, both circles turned a vibrant purple again, "—and whole when you’re together."
"It’s..."
"Dangerous," she said.
"I’m about to say beautiful," I scratched my neck and smiled awkwardly. I took a glance at the runs circling my ring finger.
The one I couldn’t live without
. Natha was right, wasn’t that basically what the mark of eternal was?
D’Ara smiled and stroked my chin lightly. "I guess, a lot of things in this world have both qualities existing at the same time."
Why did she say it as if it was
me
who had those qualities? Wouldn’t Natha be more fitting? He was beautiful to me, but others seemed to see him as someone dangerous—or rather, scary.
"But why it’s dangerous?"
"Placing your existence in another’s hands is always dangerous," she waved her hand and the vibrant purple circles disappeared. "It’s irreversible, so if you become enemies somehow, you can’t even hurt each other."
Hmm...I guessed that was true, in a sense that if one died, the other would too. But there was an obvious solution to this, wasn’t there?
"Then don’t become enemies," I shrugged.
Besides, why would you become enemies with your eternal? Didn’t you decide to become eternal because you wanted to live forever with each other? At least, that would be the case if they did it out of love. But I couldn’t imagine wanting to spend the rest of your life together without that kind of feeling and affection between the involved parties.
"True," D’Ara smiled deeply, but there was something in her eyes that seemed cold and bitter.
"Oh, there are people who become enemies after being an eternal?" I asked. Was she probably feeling regret and guilt for creating the eternal spell?
"You never know," again, she just smiled mysteriously while giving me a vague answer. "Eternity is such a long time to go through, and people change. People who love each other could turn against each other if they live long enough."
Change. That again. I was sure now that she had a complex about things changing. Perhaps that was one of the reasons why she disliked changes. Curiously, I looked at him and asked carefully—really carefully—and quietly.
"Is that why...you never do it?"
There was a harsh glint in her eyes that was only there for a split second, and I only managed to see it because I was looking carefully at her to gauge her reaction. I mean...I wouldn’t want to make a Vampire Progenitor mad on her turf. Not to mention the meadow we walked through seemed like a perfect place for burying someone; full of colorful flowers that Jade would love, perfect place for a homicide.
"Sorry," I apologized swiftly, fiddling with the edge of my sleeve nervously. I didn’t think he would hurt me or anything even if she was angry at my question, but I still didn’t want to make the Teacher of my future husband my enemy.
"No, that’s a normal train of thought," D’Ara, fortunately, was a generous vampire. "But to answer your question; no, that’s not why I’ve never done it—ah, we’re here."
I lifted my gaze and followed her forward. The flower field over there was thicker than the rest without any pathway, as if telling us we shouldn’t go any further unless we wanted to trample on all the flowers. And we shouldn’t do that, clearly, for the environmental reasons.
But also because there was a tomb there.
Oh, someone did get buried here.
"This is...?"
"The reason why I’ve never done it," D’Ara replied with a soft, yet forlorn smile.
My eyes widened and my lips parted without anything managed to come out. Earlier, I thought she might avoid making a mark of eternal with anyone because she saw those who did it had a falling out with each other. But this...I didn’t expect this.
"I was too late," she said, pain and regret infused in her soft voice.
The tomb looked new, as if it was only built yesterday. But I remembered that this landscape got rewinded every day, so that was probably why. I wonder if that was also why she kept this place inside this secure barrier, so that whoever was buried beneath the tomb would always be surrounded by unchanging flowers. There was no date or year on the tombstone, only a name in archaic runes that I couldn’t read. If I had to make a guess, this person probably died before D’Ara created the mark of internal. A long, long time ago, when the world was still engulfed in chaos.
Which was...really sad if you think about it.
What did she feel, I wondered, when she managed to create the spell for her child? Did she regret not thinking about it sooner?
"I’m...I’m sorry," I managed a whisper.
"Why? Did you do something wrong?" she smiled, crouching to stroke the tombstone and get rid of a few leaves on top of it.
I looked at her smile and the loving gaze she had as she looked at the initials on the tomb. Within the swirling petals and swaying stalks, she looked like a goddess who took a valiant warrior’s soul to the afterlife’s hall of valor. Beautiful, and lonely.
To love someone for eternity was a lonely affair.
"Is it not hard?" I whispered through the soft wind.
"Of course, it is," she stood up and stepped back, looking at the tomb once more before turning around. "Immortality is like a curse when you’re alone."
I scurried to follow her, and she continued with a sigh, turning her head toward a certain direction. "But there’s someone who’s as lonely as I am, so I can’t just leave this world and leave him alone," she said, before shaking her head slightly. "No, I think he’s even lonelier. At least my children could live as long as me."
Looking in the direction of her gaze, I tilted my head as my mind tried to picture a map and figure out what place her gaze was pointing at. "Are you talking about the High Priest of Dzurrakh?"
She turned her face; for a few long seconds, her eyes seemed to observe me. "Hmm...the next time I visit Terre, I’ll ask if I can bring you along."
"R-really?!" my voice went higher before I could tell myself to hold back. When she chuckled in response, I cleared my throat and scratched my cheek in embarrassment. "Also...the High Priest’s name was Terre?"
"Ah, don’t call him that though, it’s just the nickname I use," she wiggled her finger. "His name is Alteria ."
"Noted," I nodded readily. Well, I didn’t even know if I would ever have a chance to go to the Dragon Island, but I could at least tell Shwa about it.
We continued to walk through the meadow, watching the silhouette of Vrida and Jade flying around the mountain peak until we arrived beneath a big wisteria tree. The golem servants had set up a tea table there, with teas and cakes already served for our afternoon snacks. What a fancy picnic! Jade swooped down the moment the little bird saw us eating sweets, and I wondered what Natha was doing right now, alone in the castle.
"So you want to carve the mark of eternal?" D’Ara glanced at me as we enjoyed our cakes.
I bit my fork and asked expectantly. "Is it possible?"
"Not the real version, since you’re not vampires," she shook her head, but I managed to quell my disappointment because I already expected it to be the case. She added, however. "I can make a simplified version, a customized version just for you two; but it’ll need some time."
My enthusiasm skyrocketed instantly, which I guess was apparent from how my back straightened and my upper body leaned over. I couldn’t see them, but my eyes were probably sparkling as I nodded energetically.
"It’s okay, as long as it’s done before our wedding!" I blurted out before I could stop myself.
Her brow arched at my slip of tongue. "Oh-ho?"
I laughed awkwardly in embarrassment and scooted back on my chair as I fiddled with my shirt, my face burned despite the cool breeze blowing through the meadows. I cleared my throat and changed the topic before I became even more like a carrot cake in front of me.
"So...about the story of Natha’s academy days...?"

chapters.title: Chapter 276: My Lord used to be a troublemaker, but he’s still my troublemaker
chapters.content:
Chapter 276: My Lord used to be a troublemaker, but he’s still my troublemaker
"Do you enjoy your sunbath?" I cupped Natha’s face from behind the chair he sat on on the balcony. He opened his eyes, looked at me, and smiled; the kind of smile he gave me when he just woke up from his sleep. "Oh, were you asleep?"
"I was awake when you walked in," he said, patting his thigh."You’re very cheery."
I giggled and circled the chair to climb into his lap and stroked his forehead, swatting loose hair from his face. It was rare to see Natha had an afternoon nap—no, I didn’t think I had ever seen it before. Well, he was usually either working or tending to me, so he didn’t have much time for himself to just relax and have an uninterrupted rest.
"You must have liked it here since you won’t sense anyone’s thought," I stroked his cheek next, and rubbed the soft flesh around his eyes. He looked so refreshed, so well rested.
There was no one here but D’Ara and me. He had blocked himself from reading my thoughts, and D’Ara blocked herself from any mental attack—including mind reading. So he didn’t have to concentrate so much on blocking so many thoughts like usual. Perhaps that was why he spent five years here after the war; it wasn’t just to learn how to control his trait, but also to heal his mind.
"Mm, it’s peaceful," he said. "I have an island too, and there are only the caretakers and their families living there, quite a nice place,"
Did he just casually tell me he owned an island?
"But I guessed, since the scenery is different, it feels different," he continued. "This one is...nostalgic."
"Because it’s never changing?"
"Mm," he smiled, looking into the blurry horizon that would stay the same tomorrow, and tomorrow’s tomorrow. He turned to look at me after a while, stroking my waist. "So? Why do you look so happy?"
"Am I?" I giggled again, shifting my body to a more comfortable position on his lap. "I just heard a lot of interesting things."
"Really? What about?"
I grinned and pointed at him. "You."
"Me?" Natha tilted his head, before narrowing his eyes and muttered. "I don’t have a good feeling about this."
"Don’t worry, they are all cute and fun things."
"Definitely not a good feeling," he shook his head.
"Why? I like hearing how cheeky and rebellious you were," I propped my elbow on his shoulder and poked his cheek. "Like the time you were almost expelled for not coming to the academy for a whole semester because you were involved in treasure-hunting."
"Eh," he shrugged. "The lesson was boring, and treasure-hunting seemed like a more profitable way to spend time with."
Look at this demon, ditching his classes just because he was too smart for them. "Or the time you secretly let the spiritual beasts on the loose and pinned it on the lich."
This time, he was grinning. "That was fun," he said, the youthful mischievousness flashing in the silver eyes. "That prick was the one who framed me for plagiarism first."
I see. Petty was his inherent trait. Talking about petty...
"Oh, oh—I heard you liked challenging the academy professors too!"
And by challenging, I didn’t mean in debate. Well, he liked debating them too, but I was talking about duel. Like...sword and magic duel.
Apparently, if words fail, do violence.
"A bunch of narrow-minded conservatives bunch," Natha scoffed, and I couldn’t help but laugh.
"It sounds fun, your academy days,"
"Eh, it had its ups and downs," he shrugged.
I turned around so I could lean against his chest, staring at the horizon that he watched before. Vaguely, I could see Vrida perching on one of the mountain peaks. Jade should be there too, giving the wyvern the mana stones I gave them for their afternoon snacks. It seemed that Jade liked Vrida so much because she had more similarities with the little bird than Ignis; the wings and flying part, especially. They had already become the bestest buddy after two days. "I’ve never gone to school before, so it’s fun hearing stories about them," I told him.
I was homeschooled at first, and then, I received my education in my hospital room. I knew the teacher only saw it as an amusement for someone who would never live to use the knowledge, but it was one thing that made me feel like I was still a human, a somewhat part of society. Even if it was useless.
The downside of being the only student was...no friends, I guessed.
I felt him shift behind me, propping himself higher and dragging me with him. His arms circled my waist and pulled me onto his chest. "Well, the most important about going to school is the people," he said nonchalantly. "You get friends, and you get enemies."
"Ouch," I tilted my head and pondered about what might happen if I were going to a school. "Hmm...I think I might be the type that gets enemies,"
"Because of your family?"
"Yeah," I nodded, and then clapped my hands in exclaim. "Maybe that’s why I was home-schooled, huh?"
"Perhaps,"
Mm, mm, I understand it now. Well, there was also the thing about me being sick, but I was already home-schooled before I got sick. "But I can visit Grandma often thanks to that," I tapped my chin as I tried to recall my childhood. "Before I got too sick, of course."
Natha strokes my hair then, and, after a few minutes of blissful silence, something silly came into my mind. "Will you fall in love with me if we somehow end up in the same school?" I asked him.
"I think I’ll fall in love with you in whatever scenario,"
"Pfft—how do you know?" I laughed and turned my head to look at him. "What if you can’t see my soul?"
I thought you fell for me because you could see my soul, Your Lordship. Stubbornly, he argued with a huff. "Well, I reckoned I’d still fall for your cuteness."
Laughter came out of my mouth without restraint. It was funny how he insisted he would fall in love with me no matter what, that it almost sounded defensive. Endearing, yes, but also funny.
"It’s just an imagined scenario anyway," he shrugged, and then pressed his lips on the shell of my ear. "What about you? Would you fall for me too?"
He looked expectant, the silver eyes gleaming a bit brighter. I felt like he would sulk if I said something like ’I don’t know’—not that I would say it. I touched his face, pinching his cheek lightly, and stroked his jaw. "I didn’t know that you were the same person, but I still managed to fall in love with both of you anyway," I told him. Well, to be exact, I only thought he had the same face as the doctor, not the same person.
Natha leaned back and closed his eyes as I continued to stroke his face, enjoying the handsome visage that I could confidently say to be mine now. "So you’re saying you like how I look."
"Why? Are you disappointed? Do you think I’m superficial now?" I asked teasingly, and he opened his eyes, lips curled into a smirk.
"Hmm, it means you have a good taste."
Pfft—so he didn’t mind if I only liked him because he was handsome? Well, to be fair, there was nothing wrong with falling in love with someone because of their look. It was just a problem if they stayed in love
only
for the look.
That being said...
"But I wasn’t crushing on you because you’re handsome," I said. It was true that, like any other people in the hospital, his looks made my heart skip when I saw him from time to time. But I wouldn’t say I fell in love with him because of that.
"Oh? Why then?"
"Hmm..." I looked at the sky, at the memory of cold winter days, and fiddled with his hand—the hand that was almost as cold. "Because you’re warm?"
Natha tilted his head in genuine confusion, and I smiled while continuing. "When you held me, it was warm," I said, remembering the feeling of being lifted and embraced after I fainted. "And when you keep talking to me all winter...it felt warm."
Winter had been the worse season for me, because it aggravated my condition. But meeting him, talking about silly stuff and serious matters, being treated like a real person and not just someone awaiting their death...that winter, I think, was when I felt the healthiest all my life.
And then the winter ended, and our time in that world ended. I still remember those fleeting moments as I succumbed more and more to my illness when my life force diminished. Those moments were what made dying rather bearable. Ah, I tasted what it was like to fall in love, I thought.
But my life, turned out, did not end there. I met him again, albeit not knowing it was him. During another cold night, he pulled me into another embrace.
"When you helped me, and taught me a lot of things after I came to the Lair, everything felt warm," I smiled and rubbed his palm with my thumb. "You’re very warm, even though your skin is cold," I looked up to gaze into his eyes. "It’s fascinating, isn’t it?"
He stared back at me wordlessly, until he lowered his head and pressed his forehead on my shoulder. His arms tightened around my waist, and I could hear his sigh; long, and ended in some kind of groan.
"Haa..." he moved his face; eyes staring at me, and lips mouthing against my shoulder. "I lost."
"Huh?"
He shifted his head so now his cheek was resting on my shoulder instead of his mouth. "Well, I’d never win in the first place."
"Are we competing in something?" I tilted my heart in confusion, and Natha smiled charmingly.
He straightened his back then, and leaned down to kiss my lips. A brief and sweet one, as his eyes looked straight at me. "You make me want to propose to you again."
Again? My brow arched and I turned to look at the sky. Ah, the sun was setting, and the sky was the same shade of violet and orange as yesterday. The same sky that Natha saw as he thought of proposing to me.
"Hmm...in that case, I’ll be the one to do it."
Natha raised his brows, and I jumped off his lap. When I turned around to look at him, he was already straightened his back, looking at me with a mix of intrigue and confusion.
"I used my last ticket to learn about the mark of eternal; well, the simplified version of it," I told him, and his eyes widened a little bit. I stretched out my arm toward him, and, after a few seconds of confusion, he gave me his hand.
"I...want to use it as a part of the wedding ceremony, so..."
I looked at his eyes, which grew larger, feeling my heart pounding so hard I almost couldn’t hear myself.
"Ra Natha, would you be my eternal?"

chapters.title: Chapter 277: Moments Where Time Stops (M)
chapters.content:
Chapter 277: Moments Where Time Stops (M)
"Ra Natha, would you be my eternal?"
How could a single line sound so beautiful?
There were times in his life, when Natha felt like time had stopped;
The first time he embraced Valen.
The first time he realized it was Valen.
The first time he kissed Valen.
The first time he made love to Valen.
The time he saw Valen running in the field of snow.
And the time Valen asked for his life and his time, bathed in the glow of sunset.
Time had stopped; stopped so he could see everything in clarity, sense everything in minute details. The bright, captivating green eyes that hide nothing; the lovely lips delivering beautiful words; the warm glow of the twilight, and the fragrant scent of never-ending spring.
At that time, as everything felt beautiful and perfect, Natha came to understand his teacher’s decision to preserve a part of this world.
He wanted to preserve this moment.
"Yes,"
Natha said the word dazedly, breathlessly the first time. Of course, it would always be a yes. His life, which felt like it had ended, was lit up by the fire of that beautiful soul. So it was natural that his life, his time after that belonged to that beautiful soul.
"Yes."
He stood up, repeating it firmly, taking the smaller hand and grabbing it tight. Valen smiled shyly, a radiant glow, flush blooming across his cheek. It was beautiful. Valen had always been beautiful. Natha didn’t think he could take it if Valen became even more beautiful than he already was.
As the world felt like it flew slowly around him, he grasped the fair, blushing cheek with every tenderness he had on his being. "Yes," and the last one, he said in a whisper, a soft breeze that caressed the smiling, red lips. "I will be your eternal."
The kiss was soft, sweet, slow; they savored each other like they savored the unrepeating moment, careful and thorough. But as the light of the day slowly disappeared, so was their inhibitions.
As their touching lips became sweeter, their mingling breath grew hotter. Natha grabbed the small waist that seemed so fragile, and Valen let the demon lift him without ever parting their connected lips, holding on to the wide back and shoulder as they moved inside.
The journey to the bed felt both long and short, fast and slow. They wanted every moment to be as long as possible, but they also wanted to arrive at the next moment as soon as possible. The contradiction made their head spinning, delirious. They shed each other’s clothes as if the fabric made them itch; in a frenzy, in a hurry.
"Your hands, sweetheart," Natha breathed hard, cool breeze against Valen’s lips, who whined for the disrupted kiss. Adorably, Valen let go of Natha so the demon could slip the shirt off his neck and access the expanse of bare skin beneath.
But Valen didn’t like the loss of Natha’s lips on his own, so he yanked the demon up and claimed the cold lips again, warming them up with his own heat. Natha smiled through the kiss; ah, it was always adorable, the way Valen became assertive in bed, when he had always been shy otherwise.
"Clothes...you too..." the kiss paused just long enough for Valen to demand his demon to undress, before it resumed with more vigor.
Again, Natha chuckled, shedding the remainder of his clothes and freeing Valen from his pants. But he had to disappoint his beau this time, because the kiss ended there.
Valen whined, squirming slightly when the cold lips were touching his neck instead of his lips. It was nice, it felt ticklish, and it made him shudder in a good way. But he preferred that licking tongue to be in his mouth instead, so he felt rather dissatisfied.
That was, until he felt the cold lips on his hip. Looking down, Valen felt shivers run through his spine as he looked at the demon between his legs. Slinging Valen’s legs on his shoulder, Natha planted a kiss on the fair thigh, lightly biting on it.
Velen swallowed, watching those lips travel through his thigh, getting closer and closer to his twitching genitals. Oh--did Natha want to do that? It had been a while since he was sucked, and Valen felt his heart beating fast from anticipation.
The anticipation that was never fulfilled.
The lips roamed around his pelvic bone, sucking and biting on his waist, and yet, it never grazed his erection. Valen bit his lips as the lips hovered closer, but never touched where he wanted them to be.
"Nat..." he whined, twisting his hips under the demon’s hold, but Natha simply ignored his plea. Valen threw his head back in frustration, wondering if Natha was playing tricks on hi--
"Ngh!" Valen gasped, feeling his hips lifted slightly, and, at the same time, coldness assaulted his rims. "What--"
He looked down in shock, and saw the silver eyes gazing at him. Cold hands holding his thigh, and then, a lick. Valen clasped his hand over his mouth to stifle the shriek coming out of his throat. Did...did Natha just...
Another lick, and Valen jolted; back arched and legs tensing. "Na...Nat--ngh!"
Biting his lips hard, Valen grasped the dark hair between the horns grazing his thigh. What...what?! Another loud gasp came out of his mouth when a cold tongue slipped inside his...inside his...
Valen looked at the ceiling with eyes blown wide and lips parted, letting out airy gasp as he felt the tongue move and the lips sucking the soft flesh around his rim.
What is this...
What is this?!
That--they could do that? They could feel good while doing that?!
Inside the wide green eyes were the sparkle of countless fireworks, exploding inside his mushy brain. Valen thought he had tasted everything that could be tasted from sex, but as usual, he was naive. He knew it felt good when Natha rubbed him there, he knew it was good when Natha grazed him around the entrance. But having the demon’s face on the cleft of his lower cheeks, cold lips and cold tongue all moving to pleasure him in a way he never felt before, it was...
It was a new world. He was drowned in glorious bliss.
Heaven! Mother! Why did he only know about this now? Why did Natha only do this now?!
"Nat...Nat! I’m going to--"
Valen grasped the dark lock tightly, squirming and tensing, and Natha pulled away. For a split second, Veln felt disappointed, only until the cold lips wrapped around his twitching, slightly leaking head, and suck.
"Ngh!!" back arched, Valen felt his whole body trembling, shuddering as he released inside Natha’s mouth.
"...oh, Gods..." Valen said dazedly, because only calling out for Mother didn’t seem like it was enough.
Natha swallowed the sweet fluid, and raised his upper body while licking his lips. Not just for the delicious appetizer he just had, but also for the decadent-looking main course looking at him with bated breath. The main course that suddenly grabbed him and yanked him down for a hard, passionate kiss.
"You should have...you should have done that sooner," Valen whispered breathlessly.
"So you like that," Natha chuckled as he caressed the slightly sweaty hair, that he was sure would drench soon. "Should we just skip dinner?"
The green eyes gleamed, and now, Natha felt like
he
was the main course instead.
* * *
They did skip dinner, and the fact that there was no disruption in the middle of their activity meant they were either too passionate to notice anything, or D’Ara was keeping Jade with her so the little bird wouldn’t seek its occupied master.
The master was now contentedly giggling and snacking on biscuits to fill his empty stomach, looking fresh and radiant despite the heavy exercise they had just done.
Natha was slightly exhausted, but he liked seeing his sweetheart looking satisfied. The pink glow in those cheeks looked like spring blossoms, and the never-ending smile was like an energizing spell.
Talking about energizing spells...
Valen could rejuvenate other people now, meaning the half-druid could rejuvenate him. Meaning they could go on as much as Valen wanted--and while Valen didn’t have much appetite for food, he had an abundance of it in the bed.
It was fine, because Valen would always end up hungry after, and Natha enjoyed seeing Valen eating a lot. For now, though, they snack on biscuits first while they wait for the golems to prepare their midnight dinner.
"Sweetheart,"
"Mm?"
Natha looked at a pair of green eyes who looked at him with innocent clarity, as if they weren’t gazing at him lewdly not long ago. Caressing the strewn, ebony hair, Natha asked softly.
"You talked about
wedding
earlier,"
The green eyes blinked slowly, and the flush on those cheeks deepened considerably. Natha smiled and rubbed the blush, asking more. "Have you made a decision?"
Valen averted his gaze and started fiddling with the biscuit tins, something Valen always did when he was flustered. Natha thought it was adorable, so he didn’t mind waiting patiently for an answer.
A worthy patience, because he got to have Valen shifted closer to him, and whispered shyly. "Yeah," the green eyes looked at him, with a flushed face and a bashful smile. "Let’s do it in the spring."
Spring. Spring was just a few months away.
Natha felt his heart start to beat faster as Valen continued. "I don’t know if we will have an answer for Shwa immediately, but if we do, I want to have the procedure as soon as possible. And..." Valen paused, now fiddling with the green pendant on Natha’s chest. "I want to have the wedding first before then."
Ah. Ah...was there no end to how lovely his sweetheart could be?
Natha stroked the reddened cheek and kissed his sweetheart deeply, lovingly. "Gods, sweetheart..." he gazed at his lovely lover, and kissed every surface of that lovely face, as much as he could, until Valen squirmed and laughed inside his embrace.
Smiling, smiling from the bottom of his heart, from the depths of his soul, he gave one last sweet kiss on Valen’s lips. "I love you," he whispered, and he could hear the slight tremble inside his voice.
"Yeah, I love you too," Valen stroked his cold cheek, and softly kissed his cold lips.
But it was warm. His heart, his soul, his future; everything was warm.

chapters.title: Chapter 278: There’s always a lot of things to unpack after vacation
chapters.content:
Chapter 278: There’s always a lot of things to unpack after vacation
[Hmph!]
Ah, my little bird was sulking again in the morning. I hugged Jade and rained kisses on the green head until the little bird made a sound between whining and laughing.
"You also spent the whole day with Vrida yesterday, except when there’s food," I argued, and Jade gasped. The beady eyes moved, as if shaking, and in the end, Jade buried its face on my chest in fluster.
[Jade sorry!] It was only after I caressed the colorful plume that Jade lifted its green head. [Did Master miss Jade yesterday?]
"I did," well, at least before the sunset. "But you seem like you’re having a good time with Vrida, so it’s alright."
The little bird giggled and gave me a little peck on my cheek.
"If you want to come here, you can just come by yourself," D’Ara told me as we walked to the yard toward Vrida. "Wyvern always remembers the path they had visited, so she would be able to guide you here. Come with the little one."
She patted Jade, who didn’t mind being called ’little’ this time.
I bit my lips and hesitated for a bit, before shifting closer and whispered in her ears. "Will you...will you come to our...mm, w-wedding?"
I didn’t know why I had to whisper when I was sure Natha could hear me well with his heightened senses and everything. But for some reason, I was still a bit too embarrassed to say these things out loud. Well, even if he heard me, Natha acted as if he didn’t, and just continued to approach Vrida while smiling subtly.
Uhh--he definitely heard it.
"Well, of course," she replied easily. "I have to officiate you, anyway."
"...huh?"
"Well, after I pondered about it last night, rather than making you do it and risking a mishap, it’ll be better if I do it for you instead," she explained. "The mark of eternal, I mean."
Oh?
Oh!
My eyes widened, and she pinched my chin. "How about it? Would you like that?"
"Yes!" I answered immediately. It wasn’t just a matter of mishap and whatever. I was happy because it meant she would definitely come. As Natha’s teacher and Eruha’s...well, mother, wasn’t she basically a family already?
She stroked my head for a bit as we arrived beside the wyvern, and she leaned down slightly to kiss my forehead. A strange sensation came through me, and I blinked as I asked her. "What is that?"
"A small blessing," she said. Oh, right--she was more or less a demi-God. "Help with your metabolism."
...that wasn’t what I expected. But then again, she was a vampire; the Mother of Gluttony.
"Eat more, will you?" she stroked my chin again before laughing.
Well, it wasn’t like I hated eating; I just couldn’t digest things easily. I guessed, since my stomach would work better, I should be able to eat more in one sitting. So...yay?
I waved to D’Ara with Jade, and it was rather heartbreaking seeing the slightly forlorn look on her face as Vrida took off. Ah, I was reminded of the face my grandma would have when my vacation in her house ended.
And thus, our visit to the lonely Vampire Mother ended.
* * *
"Fuck!" Izzi greeted us with a curse as she stared at Vrida.
"Language, Izzi!" I hissed, scooping Jade, and looked into the beady eyes. "Don’t remember that word."
[Okay! No fuck!]
Damnit!
"How could you just come back with a dragon mount like this?" Izzi parted his lips, the golden eyes widened and sparkling bright like a summer sun.
"She’s a wyvern," I corrected, stroking Vrida’s snout.
"Same thing."
"It’s different! It would be like people calling you a drow!"
Izzi blinked. "Ah, noted," he nodded. "So, how?"
"By having a filthy rich fiance?" I shrugged. Natha ruffled my hair for that and Izzi grumbled in response.
"Should have known..."
"Ah...so that’s why His Lordship asked me to build a wyvern nest," Arta chimed in, approaching us from the Castle. "The keeper hasn’t arrived, though."
"Lesta and Eruha is still in Gluttony?" Natha raised his brow. They should have arrived before us since they were supposed to use the portal, along with Vrida’s caretaker. But it was already nighttime, and they still hadn’t come?
"Eruha sent a message, telling us they had to stay another night since Lesta is still recuperating," Arta said, scratching her neck with complicated emotion.
I spent a few seconds blinking, before letting out a sharp gasp. "They did it?!"
"Heh," Natha smirked and patted my head. "Seems like you were right on the mark."
Oh my, oh my! Lesta did say the only reason he hadn’t given Eruha an answer was because he had no leeway to do it since they were busy with...uhh, each other. So I guessed Lesta finally managed to give his answer. Still...
"Talk about fast..."
"He waited for decades already, so..." Natha shrugged. "I know how that feels," he smiled, looking at me so warmly that I started to feel warm in the face too.
Ugh...what a way to feel embarrassed as soon as we land. I turned toward Arta to distract myself, asking about someone else I wish was here to see Vrida. "Has Zia come back to the Lair? I have a ton of souvenirs for her."
The one who answered me, however, was Natha. "She visited her home for a bit."
My eyes widened, looking at Natha in wonder and swirling question. "She went home? Would she be alright?"
"Of course, she will," Natha smiled, holding my hand as we walked inside the castle. "It’s not like she’s actually an exile. She’s just fed up with home and running away like a princess."
"Well, she is a princess," I shrugged.
"That’s true," Natha smirked. "You don’t have to worry about her. Zidoa has more royal blood than anyone in her generation, so her status is the highest after that brat."
Haha...he really called the Lord of Lust a brat. "Hmm...I wonder what’s the situation with the...punishment," I muttered. It had been a few months since then, but I doubt the incubus had learned anything about love.
"You don’t need to think about his existence," Natha said coldly.
Alright, alright, my petty demon. I squeezed his hand and laughed. Well, I hoped Zia come back quickly since there was so much I wanted to tell her, including my decision about the wedding. I wanted to gather all of my close friends and tell them all at once--since I didn’t think I could repeat such an embarrassing announcement more than once.
"I wonder what’s for dinner," I muttered as we came closer to our beloved quarters. After being fed with nonstop delicacies in the land of gluttony, my appetite had risen slightly. And with the blessing from D’Ara, it increased even more.
Natha looked delightedly surprised when I mentioned mealtime first, but he also chuckled and gave me a warning. "You have to get used to normal food again, alright?" he said. "But tell Arta what you liked to eat when you were there so she can procure the ingredients."
"Can I?"
"Why can’t you?" Natha looked slightly offended. "It wouldn’t be as good unless we hire a cook from the gluttony, but--"
"Oh, no--don’t do that. The cook here might get hurt, you know."
Natha laughed and pinched my cheek teasingly. "Fine, I’ll just send them to study in gluttony."
Hmm...that much should be okay. I nodded in agreement, because the food from Gluttony was just that delicious. Probably because my druid body craved mana as much as the vampires, so their palate matched mine well.
Just not the crazy appetite.
But a long journey did tend to make people hungry, and I was so looking forward to dinner. So imagined my disappointment when the first thing that greeted me inside the Lord’s quarters was Heraz instead of food.
Umm...no offense to you, my guy, but...could you come before bed as usual instead of during dinner?
"Apologies, my Lord. I have to go away soon, so I couldn’t pick a better time," the demon said, as if he could read my mind--which made me rather guilty.
"We can do it over dinner," Natha said, and I perked up instantly, which made him press his lips to prevent a laugh from coming out.
Ugh--whatever. I was too hungry to think about embarrassment.
We waited until all the food was laid down and the servants retreated from the room. I offered Heraz to eat together, but as usual, the shapeshifter didn’t want to do anything that seemed to be stepping on boundaries.
How curious. Opti practically barged in on my first day here for breakfast.
"Anyway, you have anything new from the Hero?" I asked.
"Yes, Young Master," he took out a scroll from his coat and delivered it to Natha. "This is the update list on the Hero’s current companion," he said, and then continued to explain as Natha unrolled the scroll--since my hands were busy with steak. "The newest addition is someone...familiar."
My fork paused before the steak entered my mouth. "Oh?"
Natha looked at the list and chuckled. "Ah, it’s that person," he said. "The one you probably want to see the most."
My eyes squinted in suspense, waiting for the revelation, and Natha told me with a deep smile. "The one who tried to make something resembling a
smartphone
."
...my steak got further and further away from my mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 279: I might not have the insight of someone living for thousands of years, but...
chapters.content:
Chapter 279: I might not have the insight of someone living for thousands of years, but...
Amidst my surprise, Natha picked up my fork and delivered the steak to my mouth. He looked at Heraz and told the shapeshifter to continue as I mulled this new information. Something was tickling my scalp, like I was so close to connecting some dot, but wasn’t quite there yet.
"This is still a conjecture, but I believe the Hero and his companions will start to move soon, Young Master."
"Oh, why do you think so?"
"The magician you told me the last time; it was quite a journey to reach the place," he said. "I believe they would try to reach the magician before winter come. If they want to receive the magician’s help by autumn, they would need to start moving now."
Ah, right. It was summer in the human realm. And while they had the sponsor of Midas, which meant the convenience of transportation, the path to that island wouldn’t be easy. It would be like going to D’Ara’s abode, albeit on a much smaller scale. Unless they had a flying mount like a wyvern or griffin, they would need to thread on foot.
Not to mention, if they would immediately go to our Lair after...
Wait.
Wait...
I put my hands over my palm as the tingling in my scalp increased. What was it...hmm...
"Sweetheart? Is there something wrong?"
"No, wait--" I raised my palm slightly, before raising my gaze to look at Natha. It was then, as I looked at him, something clicked in my mind, and the tingling stopped. "Ah!"
"I got it now! Why they would dare to go to our Lair!" I slammed the dining table, surprising both Jade and Heraz. Natha, however, smiled after blinking once. "Why are you smiling like that?"
"Because you said
our
Lair," he said. "But what did you get? Why do those humans have the audacity to infiltrate
our
Lair?"
Wow...he really emphasized that ’our’. "Well, you said you built it for me--but we digress. Anyway, I figured it out after seeing the new party member."
"The inventor?" Natha tilted his head in ponder. But as expected of our academic genius Demon Lord, he figured it out immediately. "Ah, you mean, because she has a contract with me?"
"Yeah!" I nodded enthusiastically, forgetting my poor steak.
I had always been wondering about it. The fact that they knew Natha had Amrita could be obtained from two sources; either the magician told them, or the daughter of Midas was truly the author girl I knew. But that did not explain why they would be so daring as to go to the Lair--which might be counted as aggression--instead of trying to contact him through some other channel.
"The inventor knew you--at least as an investor, and knew you are at least rational," I said. "They would be in a hurry, and contacting you through the bank would be too long."
"True," Natha nodded. "A message from other realms would only come to me after months. The only reason why your letter came to me swiftly was because it’s you."
Natha did not tell me, but I had a guess that he had always been keeping a tab on Valmeier, so any contact made by him--well, me--would be treated as utmost priority. But even that took the spy at least two weeks--crossing the border illegally tended to cause that.
"Right--so she will probably tell them to try going to the Lair," I continued. "Because it’ll be far better to face you in the Lair, which was situated on the border, than going to the Lord Castle in the heart of a demon realm."
"I see," Natha nodded with a smile, but his hand was leading mine back to the plate. "Is there anything you want Heraz to do?"
"Not really," I shook my head. As I resumed my meal, I could see Heraz was frowning slightly, although his gaze was on the floor as usual.
Ah, he must be confused, hearing us talking about an event that had yet to happen. If I was alone, he might had more courage to ask me about it, but with Natha here, he held himself back because it would seem impertinent.
Well, it was better this way.
"Then, should we end the report?" Natha asked for confirmation.
I was about to nod and just told him to watch the hero as usual, but I suddenly recalled something; the red envelope inside my storage ring.
Was it fate, that Heraz gave me an update just as we got back? Or was it just the insight of someone who had lived for thousands of years?
"Ah, there was something," I looked at Heraz, who straightened his back in attention. "Please give me a list of the stuff from the Druid Kingdom’s treasury that is still being kept in the Empire."
* * *
"What are you trying to do with that?" Natha finally asked while we were soaking in the hot tub to clean ourselves from the travel’s dust.
"Hmm? You mean, the list?"
"Yeah," he wrapped his arms around my waist and pulled me between his legs.
I leaned my back against his chest and lay my head on his shoulder. "Just...in case someday I have a way to rob them," I shrugged.
I could sense Natha raising his brow even without looking at his face. "Well, well, look at you," he tilted my head so he could see my face, sweeping my wet hair off my face. "Even thinking about doing crime, now?"
"It’s not a crime to take back your rightful inheritance," I pursed my lips indignantly.
Now that I have taken the name Sil Seahl, thinking about the fallen kingdom irritated me so much. Recalling how even the royal scepter ended up being sold to another kingdom made me...ugh! Sometimes I had this thought of toppling the Empire and taking back the land that had been occupied by them.
But then, I realized such thinking was very eighth-grader. Toppling an Empire wasn’t just about destroying the palace or killing the emperor, and it couldn’t be done without meticulous planning, enough manpower, and adequate funding.
Not that I thought Natha couldn’t do it, but...would the destruction be worth it?
"Quite right," Natha nodded in agreement, before curling his lips and pinching my cheek in the next second. "Still, I’m impressed that my cute little sweetheart could think about doing something like that."
"Well, I am the bride of the Demon Lord of Greed!" I huffed and slammed the edge of the tub with my palms.
"That’s right," Natha chuckled, kissing my temple and taking my hands--which, I had to admit, was stinging a little bit, hehe...
"Hmm...if I knew your background beforehand, I would have robbed them myself a long time ago," Natha said while rubbing my reddened palm, and I couldn’t help but laugh.
"You might spark a war with the human realm, then,"
He scoffed in return. "War? I only take back my future bride’s inheritance," he said, parroting my reasoning. "They are the ones who occupied other’s territory unprovoked, and caused environmental degradation everywhere."
True. They were the ones who started the war, and because of that, the druids retreated deep into the realm, becoming a recluse race. The number of druids who wanted to roam the world to purify the mana in nature dwindled, especially because the royal blood was annihilated.
"They could taste a punishment or two."
I turned my head to laugh against his neck. See, my Demon Lord was ready for a war, even. But let’s not dwell on that now. Him mentioning of punishment made me think about my best friend.
"Nat...Zia wouldn’t be punished over there, right?" I asked him carefully, playing with the water to calm the slight uneasiness in my heart.
"Why do you think so?"
"I mean...since she was running away from home and such," I paused for a bit, sending the miniature water duck swimming around in front of me, before adding carefully. "Also...for not taking her brother’s side."
I felt his cold hand caressing my hair. "I told you not to worry, she is stronger than you thought," he tucked a loose strand of hair behind my ear, and then stroked my cheek with his thumb while at it.
Ugh...I know. I know, but...I don’t think strength mattered much in front of family, though. Be it strength or money, unless we’re planning to cut ties completely with our family, those things wouldn’t be an advantage. Perhaps...they might even become a shackle.
"But if you’re that worried, why don’t you just call her tomorrow? Didn’t you give your communication orb to her?"
"Oh! That’s right!" I gasped and my back straightened with reflex, only for Natha to pull me back to lay on him again. "How could I forget about that? Right, I’ll call her tomorrow."
I would have liked to call her immediately after the bath, but I didn’t think it was polite to disturb someone at night for trivial things. There was also a possibility that Zia had already fallen asleep. Ah...if only we could text each other...
Right. After the hero party came to me, I could just recruit the inventor to my research floor. At the very least, I’d arrange for that person to meet with Izzi, and something might come out of it. It’d be best if we could get the one staying in the realm of sloth too, but Natha said that place was too cold during the winter, so...
We soaked in the tub for a bit more, until Natha fished me out because I was getting drowsy. The long-distance travel, the satisfactory meal, and the nice bath worked like a sleeping spell. Natha even had to help me dry myself and put on the nightshirt. When he was rubbing my wet hair, however, I caught the inquisitive gaze of the silver eyes.
"Ng?"
Natha chuckled and tilted my head up. "Can you tell me now?" he asked. "What are you going to do with the hero party?"
Huh? He had been wondering about that?
"Hmm...nothing, really?" I shrugged languidly. "I mean--I just don’t want any infighting in our Lair
So I was planning to just talk to them first, and see from there."
Natha stopped his drying motion and raised his brow. "Was?"

chapters.title: Chapter 280: Coaxing your lover is different from coaxing your familiar
chapters.content:
Chapter 280: Coaxing your lover is different from coaxing your familiar
"Was?" Natha expressed his surprise and looked at me intriguingly.
"I used to," I said, shrugging my shoulder a little. "But after reading this, I started to...hmm...getting greedy?"
I recalled the red letter from my storage ring, giving it to Natha. He hadn’t read the content yet, because our Demon Lord surprisingly respected a certain level of privacy.
"Oh?" Natha took the red envelope and read the letter inside. I watched his eyes move and his brow arch while sipping on a glass of warm milk the servant put on the bedside table.
I waited until he finished reading it, and once he gave the letter back, I stood up to hold his arms. "Nat, can I ask something? No--two things!"
"Let’s hear them," he replied easily, pulling me along to sit on the bed.
I looked at him hesitatingly, and only managed to speak after fiddling with my shirt for half a minute. "Umm...I want to ask for the Amrita--"
"It’s yours."
"...thank you," I replied awkwardly at his swift answer that was bare of any hesitation, as opposed to the way I made the request. Well, he did say he acquired the Amrita solely for me, so I could see why he easily granted it to me.
But my second request might be trickier, since it had nothing to do with a physical item. And...it might be a sensitive topic for Natha.
I fiddled with his green pendant and looked at him carefully, feeling my voice waver even more than before. "And...is it okay if I use my ability again? The purification, I mean..."
Just as I thought, his smiling face immediately hardened. The silver eyes darkened, and I witnessed a cold expression I hadn’t seen in a long time. I was getting reminded of the face he made after I purified the forest village the last time.
"I promise I won’t get overboard! Promise!" I added immediately, urgently, cupping his face and stroking his cheek in the hope that it would melt his cold gaze. "I won’t do it all at once in one day, and...and...you know I already completely healed, right? And I will get a lesson from the druids in the spring, so..."
I knew it sounded like I was throwing him a bunch of words that sounded like excuses, but none of them were false. But I also knew it would be hard to convince him because I did betray his trust in this matter the last time.
And Natha...Natha wasn’t someone who forgot this kind of matter easily.
"I’m not doing it because of a sense of duty or anything, just...business, you know?" I spoke further, sliding into his lap for leverage. "You can send someone to chaperone me if you want."
With a lowered head, I peeked at him through my lashes, sliding my hand down to his shoulder, waiting for his judgment. It took a few minutes of silence before he finally replied with a sigh.
"Well, you are your own person, so I don’t have any right to ban you from doing what you want to do," he said, with a tone that sounded rather dry.
Ah...he must have felt conflicted about it. He didn’t want to chain me, but he also couldn’t help but be worried. I grasped his face and kissed his cheek. "But it’ll feel so much better with your blessing."
The silver eyes flicked to stare at me sharply; not in an angry way. From the way his hand tensed around my waist, he was just finding it difficult to hold back from pushing me to the bed. It took him a few seconds to battle his carnal desire and let out another sigh; fingers loosening around my waist.
"That’s one thing, but..." he stroked my thigh and looked into my eyes. "You want to go to the human realm?"
Oh? Was that what he worried about? It wasn’t just about me ’using my ability for strangers’, as he called it?
"Can’t I?" I put my arms around his neck, tilting my head. "I don’t think anyone will recognize me, anyway."
And truthfully, thinking about going to the realm of nature soon made me curious about the human realm too--you know, other places that weren’t searching for my dead body.
"Please?" I whispered, kissing his jaw in an attempt to appease him--just like how I usually try to appease Jade.
"Haa..." Natha, unlike Jade, did not nuzzle me in response. He leaned back until his upper body lay on the mattress, and I ended up straddling on top of him. He closed his eyes and let out a long sigh, before clicking his tongue in irritation. "I can just rob the palace for you."
"Hey, don’t make war so easily!" I slapped his chest, scowling as he opened his eyes in surprise. "What about our wedding? What about our child?"
His brow arched while my lips pursed in annoyance, and, after a few seconds, he let out a chuckle. "Fine."
I perked up, but before I could totally revel in my success, he already spoke again; grabbing my hip to get my attention. "One condition," he said, and I tilted my head inquisitively. His lips curled, rather mischievously. "Call me
that
again."
I blinked, shuddering as I took in his smile. Slowly, realization filled my mind and I instinctively shifted away as my face started to burn--only for Natha to raise his upper body and snatch my waist.
"Come on, sweetheart; you have to try to coax me somewhat, don’t you think?" Natha tilted his head, lightly pressing his lips on my shoulder.
Stop looking at me with your bedroom eyes! I bit my lips and turned my head away. No way--there was no way I could say that while completely sober. It was too embarrassing! Too embarrassing I tell you!
But this Demon Lord had to go and whispered in his sultry voice. "Sweetheart..."
Hngg!
"Valen,"
Agh!
"Uhh...umm..." I glanced at him; his dreamy silver eyes gleaming softly like a pair of moonlight, and the beautiful face that only I could see clearly.
Mother
...I’m not your strongest child
.
I bit my lips and lowered my face--my totally flushed, totally red face. "Will you...grant my request...h-husband?"
He grasped my jaw to tilt me up and kissed me. "Again," he whispered against my lips.
"Uh, why? What if it lost the effect once we got married?"
Natha laughed and rubbed my waist as he persisted with his request. "It won’t, so say it again,"
"Ngh--" I bit my lips so bad that Natha had to rub my lips to stop me.
But that didn’t mean he stopped pestering me about it. The silver eyes gazed at me, patiently waiting with a glint of expectation. Slowly, in a trembling voice that made me even more embarrassed, I said it. "Hus...Husband?"
In the next second, I got attacked by a shower of kisses.
* * *
[Master, Salamander not here yet?]
Jade greeted me with a question instead of a good morning; the disappointment was palpable from the less energetic chirp.
"Oh, that’s right!" I looked up from my plate. "I wonder if Ignis stays in the Lair or follows Zia to Lust..."
Closing my eyes a little bit, I tried to feel where my contractual beast was. Vaguely, I felt Ignis somewhere far, definitely further away than the Lair. "I think Ignis is with Zia, Jade. Let’s call her later and talk to Ignis too."
[Okay...] The little bird still looked disappointed; the colorful wings slumped down despite the jellies and candies surrounding it. [Jade want Salamander to meet Wyvern...]
I gently stroked the green head. "Vrida won’t go anywhere, so you can introduce her to Ignis anytime."
[Mm...]
Aww...looked at my little bird wanting to introduce its two friends as soon as possible!
But Jade continued to be sad, so I brought the little bird over to Vrida’s nest; somewhere not far from the platform where the airship was. Surprisingly, the keeper was already here, feeding the wyvern huge pieces of meat.
Apparently, Natha called the vampire castle yesterday, and told Eruha to send the keeper first, since no one could take care of Vrida here. The Castle’s beast keeper, while adequate to guide Vrida to her nest--she was a smart girl, anyway--wasn’t equipped with the knowledge of wyvern grooming.
"Good morning, Young Master," the keeper bowed politely; someone called Gaela. She said she had been with Vrida for three years, and seemed to be very passionate about wyvern-keeping--which was good.
"Hmm...I think I’ll have to take Vrida to fly to the Lair, sometimes...maybe after Zia comes back," I pondered aloud while watching Jade fly around the wyvern. The little bird finally perked up after seeing one of its friends. "Do you think she will feel better to live near the forest?"
"Well, it’s always preferable to have a large playing ground, Young Master." Gaela nodded. "Tamed wyvern is already used to buildings and cities, but they will amass less stress if they live closer to nature."
"Mm, I agree,"
That being said, moving Vrida to the Lair would sadden my little bird, and I also had to ask for Natha’s permission first. Not for Vrida, but for her keeper. After all, only Natha’s trusted subordinates could go to the Lair.
And...she would probably have to pass Angwi’s test first.
"Oh, right--do you know where the other two will come?" I asked her.
"Ah, Sir Eruha said they might be back this morning--hmm?" Gaela paused and narrowed her eyes, staring down the hill toward the Castle. "Oh! I think that’s their carriage, Young Master!"
I turned my head and circulated mana to my eyes so I could look afar. And what do you know--there they are, riding the carriage from the magic tower’s direction.
Wow...she could see that far? Was it because she was a wyvern keeper?
Anyway, what a nice timing. I bid farewell to Vrida and her keeper, and told Jade to come to the research room when I called Zia later, before immediately climbing down the hill to greet those two vassals. Or rather, I want to see Lesta.
And ask him about the mark of eternal.

chapters.title: Chapter 281: The most reliable source is the one who experienced it
chapters.content:
Chapter 281: The most reliable source is the one who experienced it
"Lesta!"
I ran through the yard to catch them before they entered the Castle, and almost crashed into Lesta--who fortunately still able to catch me. Although, even if he couldn’t, there were Panne and the guards behind me, and Eruha behind Lesta.
Huff...that happened because I hadn’t exercised my body lately--except in bed.
"Please be more careful, Young Master," Eruha chided me, a bit sterner than usual. His gaze wasn’t trained at me, though, but at Lesta, as if worried that the demon would get injured.
Oh-ho?
"Why do you look so happy to see me, Young Master?" Lesta, as usual, just calmly inquired, patting my clothes after regaining our balance again.
"Why? Can’t I be happy seeing you?" I puffed my cheek.
"Hmm..."
"Don’t be such a cautious person," I grinned at his narrowed eyes, and nudged him while Eruha talked to the Castle’s staff. "But I do have something I want to ask you," I whispered.
For some reason, Lesta looked better instead, as if he felt assurance in the fact that there was a concrete reason for my emotions. "I see," he nodded, glancing at the vampire for a second. "Well, I asked for another day off today, so let’s go somewhere I could rest in."
"Let’s go to the research tower."
"Excellent choice, Young Master," he said, and I chuckled while looping my arms on his elbow.
But someone else grabbed Lesta’s other arm. "Where are you going?" the voice that came out of Eruha was quite different from usual; rather abrupt, a bit higher, like he was doing it in reflex.
Wow...look at this vampire; even his eyes looked more expressive now.
But Eruha didn’t seem to be surprised, only staring at the hand holding him briefly, before responding in a nonchalant tone. "Rest," he said. Hmm...I gathered it wasn’t the first time Eruha made a sudden turn like this.
"Not in your room?" the vampire frowned slightly.
"Young Master’s research floor is calmer," Lesta shrugged.
"Hmm..."
"And warmer,"
"..."
The deep red eyes looked doubtful, although all Lesta said was true. Thanks to my one and only employee’s vulnerability to cold, the heating system on the eighth floor always cranked to the highest. We also had a soundproofing formation along the wall, and Eruha should know this.
He should know this better than anyone, and he still threw this skeptical gaze?
Interesting. Fascinating. I like this so much.
"And Young Master can rejuvenate me,"
"Uh-huh!" this time, I also gave a supportive nod. How dare you doubt the magnificence of my hideout, teacher!
But like the stubborn vampire that he was, Eruha continued to stare at Lesta until the demon rolled his eyes and sighed. "Stop staring and go report to His Lordship."
Only then that Eruha finally move along, going inside the Castle after casting one last glance at us.
"...wow," I couldn’t help but exclaim quietly while watching the back of my teacher getting further away.
"What?"
"Is it just me, or...my teacher become more expressive?" I blinked and looked at Lesta. "Do you tame him or something?"
"Hmm...is that how you see it?" Lesta scoffed and turned around so we could walk to the research tower. His lips curled into a slight smirk. "Well, I wouldn’t mind if that’s true."
I scooted closer and whispered so Panne and the guards couldn’t hear us. "Is it because you become his eternal?"
"You want to ask me about that, don’t you?"
"Can I?" I grinned sheepishly. "I asked D’Ara about it, and she promised to make a simplified version of it for us. But...I want to know what the real one feels like--if you don’t mind, of course."
Lesta titled his head. "Is that the Progenitor?"
"Yeah,"
"Well, I don’t mind talking about it," he shrugged, before turning his head to look at me with a raised brow and a smirk. "But I’ll need a bribe."
Everyone needed a bribe, these days.
"Candies? I still have the gem ones," I laughed and took out one of the nicest boxes that the store sold for a limited quantity only.
Lesta chuckled and we snacked on the candies on the way to the eighth floor, where Izzi only peeked out from the alchemy room to acknowledge my existence before locking himself inside the room again. Cold.
But it gave me a chance to be alone with Lesta and conduct this casual interview in the lounge, where no one but us was allowed to enter.
"So...I heard you had to recuperate?" I waved my hand so the fire inside the hearth burned hotter. After observing him more, Lesta did look a bit ashen and lethargic. Perhaps that was why Eruha suddenly acted so protective.
"Ah, well...I was delirious and eventually caught a fever until last night," he told me casually, leaning back on the comfortable sofa I personally chose for this lounge and hugging the plush pillow as if he was about to fall asleep anytime."Still feeling lethargic even now. I think my body still trying to get used to the change."
He said it with a nonchalant tone, but the way Eruha reacted earlier made me think that it must have been pretty bad. If it was just a normal fever, there was no need to stay there for another night since they used the portal to come back. It would be better to receive treatment here, from the Castle’s physician who actually had his medical record.
Unless, he was so weak he couldn’t even get out of bed. "Is it bad?" I asked carefully.
"Not as bad as the actual marking," Lesta looked down and touched his chest, somewhere above his heart. "But getting stabbed in the heart is more painful than I thought."
My mind stopped whirring for a moment, and I looked at him blankly with parted lips for a good ten seconds.
"...getting what?!"
"Oh, the Progenitor did not tell you?" Lesta raised his brow, and proceeded to tell me all about the procession of mark engraving on his heart.
By God...I knew D’Ara told me they were supposed to exchange pieces of their souls, but...this wasn’t just an exchange, Ma’am! This is using someone’s heart as a parchment and someone’s soul as an ink!
I thought it was supposed to be cute and romantic?! No wonder she told me it was dangerous.
"Wha...he did that? How could..." I couldn’t even finish my thought, couldn’t even imagine if I did that with Natha. Rather, I don’t think Natha would be able to do that ever. He couldn’t even see me getting a scratch!
Lesta chuckled and sheepishly scratched his neck. "Well...to be honest, it’s all my fault."
"Huh?"
He leaned back and slouched until he was half lying on the couch, holding the pillow tighter. "He wanted to use the poison, but I was being stubborn and said I wanted to experience everything with sobriety."
To experience everything while being sober...
"No anesthesia?!" I almost yelled--I would have, if I didn’t immediately clasp my mouth after in shock. As someone who already experienced lying on the operating table several times, it was such a horrifying picture.
Lesta turned his head and blinked in surprise. "A what?"
"Never mind," I waved my hand and scooted closer to him. I think, rather than physical pain, the trauma of such agony would be more persistent. No wonder he said he was delirious and feverish after that. "You’re awake the whole time? Why? Didn’t he tell you about the procedure?"
If Eruha didn’t tell him about it, I would tell D’Ara about it, and make sure he received heavy scolding!
Fortunately, though, it seemed like Eruha did tell Lesta about what he would do, or at least about the stabby-stabby part. I couldn’t help but grimace as I listened to him, feeling my chest itch a little bit as my mind recalled my past life experience.
"Hmm...how should I say this..." Lesta looked at the ceiling, patting his pillow slightly as he mulled the experience. "During all these years, I have always been under the influence of his poison. Until a few nights ago, I had no idea how he was, how I was, during our intimate moment," he said, letting out a sigh.
Right; I did hear about this in the morning after I got drunk, which was very unfortunate, but also stupid. And it seemed like Lesta knew how stupid it was now, which led to this decision.
"I don’t want that anymore. I want to be sober while we’re...getting to know more about each other," he shrugged.
"You kind of doing it backward, huh?"
Lesta raised his brow. "And you’re one to talk?"
"Well, technically--" I raised my finger to argue, but paused.
Yes, I and Natha went through the ’know each other’ phase first back when we were still on Earth, but no one knew that. I didn’t know that, and made a contract to be his bride before I even knew who he was aside from the fact that he was the Demon Lord of Greed. When I found out about everything, I was already deeply in love with him, even while thinking he was in love with someone else.
So who am I to talk?
"You know what, you’re right."
Lesta laughed and took the tea on the table which already turned lukewarm. I reached out to touch the cup and warmed it up while asking further. "Do you feel any different afterward? I mean, aside from the obvious change in your body."
I was also curious about it; how much one’s physical condition needed to be altered to be able to match the vampire’s lifespan. But I didn’t think it was something that could be explained unless we did a thorough lab check--which was obviously not available here.
"Hmm...I’m not sure," Lesta tilted his head while tapping the side of the cup in contemplation. "I think I can feel him more, physically and mentally. I know I can understand his emotions even if he says nothing, or even if I can’t see him. Also..." he turned his head toward the window, from which we could see the main castle. "I didn’t realize it before, but now that there’s a distance between us, I can instinctually sense where he is."
"Ooh..." it seemed to be a more potent effect of my engagement oath. "You become his radar..."
"Rad--what’s that?"
"Nothing," I shook my head and quickly changed the topic. "Umm...during the process, do you feel something?"
"Something?" Lesta sipped on his newly warmed tea in contemplation but shook his head in the end. "I was so much in pain I couldn’t think of anything."
Ugh--it made me shudder from the flood of uncomfortable experiences during my previous life.
"Ah...but," Lesta looked up and blinked slowly with a soft smile on his lips, like someone who was reminiscing a fond memory. "Before I passed out, I think I got to visit my memory--the time I met him for the first time, and everything leading to...this."
"Wow..." I looked at him curiously. I didn’t think I had seen Lesta make that kind of expression before; so soft and contended. "That’s...I’d like to experience that," I muttered.
"Getting stabbed in the heart?"
"No! The memory thing!"
Lesta chuckled while putting the teacup back on the table. "I’m just kidding, Young Master."
Ugh--I knew he was, but I couldn’t help but shudder thinking about getting my heart carved with no anesthetic. But I also couldn’t help but become curious; my eyes reflexively landed on his chest, and I asked carefully. "Does it leave a trace?"
Rather than giving me a simple answer, Lesta looked down and offered nonchalantly. "Do you want to see it?"
My eyes widened. "Can I?"

chapters.title: Chapter 282: How should you explain the concept of marriage to your kid?
chapters.content:
Chapter 282: How should you explain the concept of marriage to your kid?
Lesta unbuttoned his shirt without much care, and I hugged the pillow in his place because I got too excited. You know, the kind of excitement when we encounter something interesting?
He unbuttoned his shirt just enough for it to show his chest. There, above where his heart should be, was a mark, roughly as big as the brand of contract Natha put on the back of my hand the first time.
"Whoa..."
I stared at the mark in fascination. I thought it would be like a tattoo at first, but it was closer to the mark I had on my palm; the mark of Alveitya. It looked like blood veins, those blue and purple lines we could see in our wrists. But the color was deeper, darker, the lines spreading like blooming flowers.
Upon closer inspection, the mark was actually an archaic rune formation. Different from the magic circles and arrays used nowadays, the archaic rune formation was formed by combining all the runes used in the spell into a singular form. To put it simply, it was like how Chinese characters--
Hanzi
--formed back on Earth.
Looking at it like this, rather than a tattoo, it looked more like the mark had been a part of his body from the start; like a very elaborate birthmark.
It was beautiful.
"Would you like to touch it?"
"Yeah," I admitted easily. "I want to try channeling the rejuvenation mana through this point."
Lesta nodded. "Go on," he said, and my hand had already moved before he even finished the ’on’. He chuckled at my eagerness, and let me rub the mark slightly.
I did it carefully, afraid that it would still hurt. But he said it was alright, and I realized curiously that there was no scar on his skin, considering he was supposed to get ’stabbed’. Pressing my middle finger slightly on the center of his mark, I channeled the rejuvenating mana to his system.
"Oh?" Lesta raised his brow.
"Does it feel different?"
"I think it works better than usual, Young Master. Perhaps because it flows directly through my core," he moved his shoulder slightly and arched his back, probably checking how much it lifted his lethargy.
Alright, so my experiment went well. Curiously, the mark also pulsed slightly as it absorbed the mana I sent and delivered it throughout his system, truly like blood veins.
"Does Eruha have one too?"
"Yeah, but his looks even clearer, since he has lighter skin--"
Lesta stopped talking because the door to the room suddenly creaked open, and as we turned to see who was it that went past Panne and the guard to disturb our private time, we saw Arta and Opti standing at the door, looking at us with parted lips.
"Oh, my Lord! What are you doing?!" Arta clasped her cheeks in shock, while Opti arched his brow and smirked.
Ah...now that I think about it, our position--Lesta half-laying down with an unbuttoned shirt and my hand on his chest--was rather...compromising. Thankfully, Lesta was as calm as always.
"Medical check-up," he shrugged, and I nodded vigorously, still delivering rejuvenating mana inside him.
"Oh..."
"You’re lucky it’s not His Lordship that sees you like that," Opti said after satisfying himself with laughing all the way until he reached the couch.
I grinned and scratched my neck awkwardly while Lesta buttoned his shirt again. Not that I felt guilty or anything, but it was indeed something that could raise suspicion.
"Don’t worry; His Lordship would understand this time," Lesta said nonchalantly.
Well, I also thought that Natha wouldn’t be so unreasonable considering this was purely...research and medical examination. Yes! That was it. He should also know that Lesta was already Eruha’s Eternal, so...what’s there to get mad about?
But then Lesta added; "Well, probably," with a shrug and I had to smack him for giving me sudden anxiety.
"But why do you call us here, Young Master?" Arta asked while crouching beside the table in front of us. "Oh--is this from Gluttony? Can I eat this?"
Oh, right
. I took out the snacks I got from Gluttony as souvenirs and poured them on the table. I gave Arta my communication orb and told her to contact the other orb, which was in Zia’s possession right now. While she did so, I went out of the lounge to call for Izzi and asked the imps to provide my guest with more refreshments.
[Master! Is Succubus here? Is Salamander here??]
Of course, I didn’t forget to call my little bird too, who came swooping down through the window the moment I opened it. "Not yet, but we can speak to them, at least."
[Hngg...] Jade was still a bit disappointed, but playing with Vrida and the notion of hearing their voice perked the little bird a bit. [Alright. Jade will ask when they will go home!]
"Sure, you should ask them," I laughed at the way Jade called this place home when Zia’s real home was where she was now. But it also sounded nice.
By the time I came back to the lounge, Izzi was already there, huddled near the fireplace. The communication orb was on the center of the table, glowing red, and I could hear Zia’s voice as she talked with Arta.
"...yeah, so--Oh! Young Master is here!" Arta exclaimed when I came inside, and Jade jumped to the table and chirped loudly so Zia could hear.
[Is that Jade? Is Val there too?]
"Hey, are you having a nice time, there?" I asked, crouching in front of the table beside Arta. At this point, except for Lesta--who was lounging languidly on the couch--we were all huddled around the table, snacking naughtily before lunchtime.
[Not as nice as wherever you are right now, but I can make my own fun] Zia replied casually; I could almost sense her shrug all the way here. [I’ll be back in a few days, but...what’s up? I heard you gathered everyone]
"Hmm...well, I kind of miss everyone," I grinned, which wasn’t a lie. It was rare for me to completely be away from everyone. I understood why Jade missed Ignis--which the little bird expressed immediately.
[What about Salamander?] Jade chirped loudly.
"Is Ignis there?" I patted the little bird. [Jade miss you, Ignis]
[Should I project myself there?] we heard the Salamander’s voice, and in the next second, the air beside my head trembled a little bit, and a gecko-shaped flame manifested on my shoulder.
Jade chirped in surprise and delight, jumping to my shoulder to nudge the flame with its wing.
"I can only do it here, while connected to your body," the fire-gecko told us.
"Oh, interesting..." I poked the fire, and my fingers went through the body, like a hologram. Fascinating. I wondered if I could learn to do that too...
"That’s fascinating," Opti, the master spy shapeshifter, shoved his face close to my shoulder, observing the fire projection. "But anyway--you’re not gathering us just because you miss us, are you, Young Master?"
I smiled sheepishly and scratched my cheek. I knew I was the one who gathered them, and I knew I had resolved myself, but...now that I faced their curious eyes, I felt embarrassment creeping up my face. Even Jade tilted its head and stared at me inquisitively.
"Uhh...so..." I fiddled with the nearest snack packaging on the table, looking at that rather than their eyes. "So I decided to...to hold the wedding in spring..."
My voice dwindled at the end, because the room became so quiet, and I felt like my voice became unnecessarily loud because of that. My heart pounded nervously for reasons I didn’t understand, and I fidgeted in place before peeking at them.
"Well, more works for me," Lesta commented with a shrug, but he also smirked. "Congratulations, though."
"Gratz; hmm...all I need to do is attend, right?" Izzi muttered.
And it opened a floodgate.
"Aaaah!! Aaack!!" Arta tackled me to the ground--just fifteen minutes after she acted scandalized by me and Lesta. "Yes! Yes! I’m going to make the best outfit ever!"
Staring blankly at the ceiling, sometimes I wondered if Arta wanted to become a designer rather than take care of governmental affairs.
Zia, however, screamed and slammed her hand against whatever surface near her. [Noo!! You should have waited for me to be physically there first!]
"Uhh...sorry; I just want to get it out as soon as possible," I laughed awkwardly as Zia threw a little tantrum and called her cousin, Aleena.
"No--you do the right thing, Young Master!" Arta defended me as she pulled away and helped me up again. "Spring is only a little more than two months away. There’s a lot to be prepared!"
"Have you decided on a date?" Opti asked from the side, looking uncharacteristically serious.
"No," I shook my head. "It doesn’t matter to me, so Natha should be the one to decide that, since he’s the busy one."
Opti nodded, stroking his chin for a while before moving away to talk to Lesta. Looking at them made me think that this wedding wouldn’t be as simple as tying knots or exchanging vows. It smelt like a lot of complicated political and security affairs.
...oh, well--that was for Natha to take care of. He told me yesterday that all I needed to do was tell Arta what I wanted for the ceremony.
[Master] as the chaos erupted inside the lounge from Arta and Zia excitedly yelling back and forth, Jade jumped on the table, the green head tilted as the innocent, beady eyes stared at me. [What’s a wedding?]
Ah...
...help?

chapters.title: Chapter 283: The best kind of drama is the one you’re not a part of
chapters.content:
Chapter 283: The best kind of drama is the one you’re not a part of
"Hmm...it means, I will become a family with Natha," I told the little bird after mulling about it for a while.
[Family? Like with Jade?]
"Uhh...it’s kind of different," I scratched my cheek in confusion. "Let’s just say we will make a promise to live together forever."
[Jade and Master will live together forever!]
Crap. Jade was right; as my familiar, the little bird would live as long as I live, and immediately cease to exist once I died. So how could I tell Jade that what was between me and Natha was something different?
I groaned and rolled to my side on the rug, while Jade jumped down to nuzzle me in confusion. [Master?]
"I don’t know..." I muttered helplessly to the rug. "What is a wedding? What is a marriage?"
"It’s being together and making babies," I heard Izzi’s voice from beside the fireplace, and I kicked his legs lightly.
"I told you to watch your mouth!" I hissed.
[Babies...]
See?!
And then Ignis--or its manifestation--crawled to my cheek and spoke to Jade. "It means the Nightmare will be Valen’s mate."
Ignis!
[Mate?] the little bird tilted its head, the beady eyes looked here and there like someone looking for an answer during a test. Curiously, Jade perked up not long after. [Ooh!]
Ooh? What oh? What did you know about ’mate’, Jade? You’re supposed to be a child!
I groaned even more and Arta patted my head while laughing. "It’s okay, Young Master. Even Sir Jade has to know it sooner or later," she said.
I looked at her with my lower lip jutted out. I know that, but I still didn’t want Jade to grow up so fast. My little bird hadn’t even lived for a year!
"Well, how else would you explain your honeymoon, then?" Lesta shrugged. "You’ll have to leave the bird behind, won’t you?"
I blinked and sat up slowly, staring at him blankly as heat crept up my cheek. "Honeymoon..." I muttered unconsciously while rubbing the rune circling the base of my ring finger.
Arta slung her arm across my shoulder and whispered dramatically. "Honeymoon~"
[Honeymoon~] Zia cooed from across the realm, and it gate Jade chirping.
[Honeymoon?]
