I laughed. I couldn’t help it. Despite her harsh words, her expression kept softening with my explanation. As someone who had experienced the same fear, I knew how much relief it brought our souls, to know that there was someone who was willing to accept who we were. Even if it was just one person, it gave us hope and affirmation that we were indeed, a part of this world.
As evidence, I could see her cheeks and ears were slightly reddened. Probably due to embarrassment at her reflexive outburst, she shifted the topic at hand.
"But...how long have you been here exactly? You even have a child..."
"Ch--what?!"

chapters.title: Chapter 359: Reasoning with children is an art; and not everyone mastered it
chapters.content:
Chapter 359: Reasoning with children is an art; and not everyone mastered it
"Wha-child?!" I clasped the black pendant on my chest tightly in reflex.
"Huh?" Neel tilted her head in confusion. "Isn’t the little one your child? The one with the Lord of Greed."
Oh...that. I was worried for a second that someone managed to find out about Shwa. I forgot that people easily thought Jade was my child since it only happened the first time.
"Hmm...but looking at your reaction, it seems I was mistaken, but then..." Neel moved her head left and right, holding her chin and frowning as if she were in deep contemplation.
"Ah, no. Jade is my--"
"Clone?" she suddenly gasped, lifting her head to look at me with widened eyes. "Is that little one your clone?" she stood up; her demeanor was similar to when she found out about the golems. "Do you find a way to create a--"
"Stop!" I raised my palm to shut her up. Beside me, Zia was trying so hard to not laugh until her shoulder was shaking.
I let out a long exhausted sigh. "Jade is not my child--not in that sense anyway," I told the curious half-naga. "Jade is my familiar."
"...you used human as familiar?" Neel widened her eyes and scooted back.
At this point, Zia could no longer hold back and just laughed heartily while smacking the couch. Again, a sigh escaped my lips. "Jade is an elemental bird."
Neel blinked and looked even more confused than before. "The one...flying up there?"
"Yeah--well, not yet. Jade is still a ba--no, a juvenile elemental bird," I corrected myself in case the little bird could hear it.
"But how..."
"Jade is special," I smiled to close the topic. Let’s just leave it at that, because talking about it would be too long. "Anyway, are you satisfied with the room? Do you have any requests? Is there anything lacking?"
Neel cleared her throat, probably realizing that she had been overly excited about the thought that I might be able to make a clone. "I don’t need much, just tell the golem to not light the fire in my room. I like it cold."
Ah...so it was deliberate that she didn’t ask for fire. It did not matter to me because of Ignis, but Zia was kind of shivering, so I asked her if she wanted to stay here and rest or go back to the drawing room and wait for Izzi.
"Oh, I need to ask the Lord for a few things regarding the contract," she took the papers on the table and followed us out. When she was closing the door behind her, however, I could see she was thinking hard about something. "Hey, umm..." she looked at me with narrowed eyes. "If that girl knows...is that mean the Lord of Greed..."
"Of course, he does," I nodded. "He probably knew about you from the start."
Once again, she paused in front of the door, looking like her paradigm had been flipped upside down.
"Why do you think he would be interested in a ’failed’ product? Just because he’s curious? He’s still a merchant you know."
"Uhh..."
And this was just my conjecture, but...Natha probably came to them with the hope that one of them would be me. He was looking for someone who came from another world, so things like this would be quicker. Of course, he would know at once that they didn’t have my soul, but he still invested in them to build connections.
Because who knew? Perhaps one day they would come across another transmigrator, and that would be me. After all, it was easier for a transmigrator to find another transmigrator, by realizing the other had the same ’common sense’ with them.
Just like how Natha found them.
"But wait--" she closed her eyes and raised her hand like a student, brows knitted hard as she kept getting more confused. "How...how did he? Were you..."
"No, I came here fairly recently," I said. "It’s not even a year yet."
"What?! Then--" she clasped her mouth and continued in a whisper. "Was he actually..."
I smiled and told her to continue walking so we could stop talking while standing in the corridor as if we were conspiring for something. Although, to be honest, what I was going to tell her would probably shake the whole demon realm if it ever came out.
"If you think he’s like us, then that’s not it," I shook my head. "He’s a native, both soul and body, just like Zia."
"Then?"
"But he...hmm, how should I say this? An excursion? Yes, his soul visited Earth for...two months, I guess, like an excursion."
I almost said it was like an exchange study, but then Nathanael’s soul wasn’t inhabiting Natha’s body during that. Natha’s physical body was kept in the King’s Sanctuary, and while it was two months on Earth, it wasn’t that long in the sanctuary.
"Excursion...two months..." Neel mumbled in a daze behind me. "So...that’s how he knew about another world?"
"That’s when he met Valen!" Zia added to the story, giggling while clutching my arm. "It still sounds so romantic every time I hear it."
"Ngh...it’s embarrassing if you said it like that."
"But you like it, don’t you~" Zia poked my cheek with a mischievous grin across his face.
Our poor half-naga, meanwhile, kept mumbling incoherently behind me, perhaps trying to re-align her brain with all of this new information. Based on her personality, I didn’t think she would ever mention this to anyone else, but I should probably tell Natha later to include a clause of confidentiality on the otherworld matters.
Thankfully, by the time we got back to the drawing room, Neel already returned to her composed self. Jade was in the middle of a heated debate with Natha--something about the benefit and the loss of being an adult--but immediately jumped off the Nightmare’s lap and ran to me.
"Master!"
I lifted the little boy in my arms, who immediately pouted. "Nightmare is so annoying!" he immediately reported, while the Demon Lord sipped on his tea with a smirk on his face. "Nightmare say Master will leave with him for a week and Jade can’t come!"
...uh-oh. "Umm...that’s--"
"That’s true, Jade. Val will have to go somewhere with Lord Uncle after the wedding."
The green eyes widened, and Jade looked at me for confirmation. "Yeah, it’s true."
Jade gasped; his face crumbled, and his lips quivered. "Baby, it won’t be long," I stroked the green hair gently, rubbing the trembling cheek with my thumb. "Just a week...or so?"
But Jade only buried his face on my neck while holding me tightly, as if I was about to go right away. The boy even started sobbing. I held him tighter and patted his back, sighing inwardly. Yeah...I knew this conversation had to be made one day. I just didn’t think it would be today.
"Wait..." Neel paused and widened her eyes. "You’re getting married?"
"Did you not read the newspaper?" Zia was the one who replied.
"I don’t have newspapers."
"Oh..."
Immediately, Neel came back to the contract in her hand and flipped some pages to read the content quickly. "Wait...this stipulated time..." she muttered. "Do you want to make the video cam so you can use it for your wedding?"
The answer this time came not just from me, but also from Natha and Zia. "Of course."
"Damn..." she shook her head and took a seat while perusing the contract further. Well...at least she didn’t seem to have any problem with the motivation behind this whole thing.
After that, I walked toward Natha and kicked his shin, glaring at the cheeky smile he gave me. "What? He needs to know sooner or later."
Well...that’s true, but I wanted to convey it as gently as I could!
"He’s a big boy," Natha said. "I told him only children follow their parents everywhere. Kids don’t even wanna be near their parents once they get into school, you know. Thinking it’s lame and such."
"...is it?" I tilted my head while still patting the trembling head on my shoulder. I wouldn’t know, since my parents were already not around me when I was big enough to think.
Natha paused for a bit before shrugging. "I don’t know myself."
Hey!
"It’s just something I pick from observation."
Well...Natha’s circumstances were indeed...different. He already had a different childhood than the other kids, so we looked at Zia for confirmation.
"It’s true," the succubus replied easily. "Once we get to school and have more friends, we just want to spend time with our friends. It’s annoying when parents are around telling us not to do this and that. Besides," she hopped closer to me and poked Jade’s cheek. "You need to be independent if you want to be an adult. And independent people are okay being away from their loved ones for a week."
Slowly, Jade lifted his head and looked at Zia. "What about Master? Master not okay being away from Nightmare for a few days."
I coughed and Zia laughed, while Natha pressed his lips to prevent himself from laughing out loud.
What the hell? You were the one who said you can’t get away from me for too long, my Lord!

chapters.title: Chapter 360: All depressing talks should end in note of hope
chapters.content:
Chapter 360: All depressing talks should end in note of hope
"What is this?" was what Izzi said the moment he entered the drawing room, looking bewildered.
Well, it was understandable; Jade was crying on my shoulder, and I was in the middle of pinching Natha’s cheek. Zia was laughing her ass off on the couch, and Neel was in her maniac mode around a maid golem.
"Oh, you’re finally here," I let go of Natha, observing the elf that looked neater than usual. This man even took a shower, huh? Look at that luscious bright hair.
"Why is the bird crying?" he asked in confusion while naturally taking a seat on the couch in front of me.
"As usual," I glanced at Natha while patting the distressed little boy, but the Demon Lord just gave me a sweet, innocent smile as if he had nothing to do with the weeping mess on my shoulder. "Duesi, please get me a sweet cocoa with milk."
"Oh, me too! Me too!" Zia raised her hand, and Izzi silently raised his.
The maid golem, who had been standing still while Neel hovered around her, blinked and moved. "Yes, Young Master."
Neel pursed her lips as the maid left the room to make the cocoa for Jade and the other two. She went back to her chair and picked up the contract again to peruse the last two pages--the most important one, Natha said, because it contained penalties for contract termination and such.
Naturally, the elf’s golden gaze fell on her, and for quite a while, he kept staring in interest, while Zia stared at him with narrowed eyes. Cute. Izzi then shifted his gaze to me with a silent question, which I only replied with a quick nod.
Jade finally stopped sobbing when the maid golem came back with a sweet scent of cocoa and milk wafting all over the room. Neel turned her head to stare--not at the golem this time, but at the cocoa. Thankfully, Duesi brought a big jug of the warm drink, as well as many cups, so there was enough for everyone.
"Chocolate?" Jade shifted his head, peeking at the cup that Duesi gave me.
"Yep, a sweet one," I patted the green hair and Jade squirmed to turn on my lap so he could hold the cup. His eyes were swollen and his nose was red. I wished there was a picture of my child self crying so I could compare it. It was weird to say it to my face, but Jade looked really adorable right now.
I still shot Natha a glare though. See if you make him cry again!
As if escaping my gaze, Natha turned to look at Neel instead. "How about it? Are you going to sign the contract?"
"Ugh..." Neel bit the end of her pencil. She had been looking for a point to complain about, but so far, she found none--and she looked rather disappointed because of it, probably because she couldn’t grumble about how exploitative the rich were. "Fine."
In the end, she pricked her thumb and gave her blood seal on the bottom of the contract. The papers flew to Natha after that, and he skimmed over it quickly. With a spell, he made two duplicates of the contract, and gave the original back to Neel. One of them he gave to me.
"Alright, it’s time for me to go back," he placed the contract inside my storage ring and kissed my lips quickly before Jade shoved him on the jaw.
"Right away?" I looked at the silver eyes, couldn’t even hide the disappointment in my voice.
Natha chuckled and ruffled the glaring little boy’s hair. "Your kid looks like he wants to fight me," he said, although I guessed, he just didn’t want to hinder the mood.
Right. The Big Boss should never attend employee gatherings.
Still carrying Jade--who didn’t want to get away from me after Natha’s provocation--I walked Natha to the portal so I got another kiss. This time, Jade really shoved the Demon Lord’s face away from me--although it was also because Natha was covering his face with his cold hand.
"Go!" Jade stuck his tongue out while clutching his cocoa mug. "Nightmare go!"
Haa...and I thought they’d be in a good relationship now after seeing them reading the picture books together. Natha left while laughing out loud, but when I returned to the drawing room, the atmosphere was rather...awkward.
Those three sat wordlessly, looking at anything but each other. Not even Zia tried to make any small talk. She perked up when I came back, relief shown all over her face. "Val!"
The moment she called me, the other two turned toward me again, and I pressed my lips on Jade’s hair so I wouldn’t let out a laugh. Damn...not even me was this socially awkward.
But then again, all of them were people who spent their working hours being confined in their rooms creating things. I took a seat on the couch again while introducing the two inventors to each other. "Well, as I have told you in the letter, this is Izzi--and Izzi, this is Neel," I looked at them both, before training my gaze at the half-naga. "Ah, can we call you Neel?"
"Sure," she shrugged.
"Since you’ve already signed the contract, it means you’re a part of the team now," I nodded, taking Jade’s empty glass and putting it on the table. "So we need to figure out the working arrangement."
"Wait, before that..." Izzi raised his hand and glanced at Neel. "Is she...like us?"
Again, I nodded. The elf hummed and turned his head to look at Neel better. "Were you transferring mid-way like our boss here, or...?"
Neel considered the question for a while before answering. "I’m not sure," she said. "I recalled my previous life when I was seven, but I also remember all the memories of this body, and feel like I’m the one who went through all of that," she shrugged.
"Hmm...in that case, you were probably reincarnated in that body, and only regaining the memory of your past life when you’re seven," Izzi stroked his chin, suddenly looking all serious.
"I...think so too," Neel nodded slowly. There was a hesitation on her face that I presumed was born from her feeling weird about having someone to talk about this reincarnated in another world feeling. "Did you..."
"Oh, I gained my memory as soon as my brain gained cognitive function."
"I see..."
Izzi pressed his lips and asked carefully, almost in a whisper. "So, umm...were you...died, or...?"
Neel flinched for a little bit, before nodding and replying quietly. "Overwork, I guessed..."
Ah...so that was why she was so sensitive about being exploited and had no trust in corporations. But then again, she was right--no one should be exploited and a lot of corporations were indeed untrustworthy. Natha told me himself.
"Ah, I was hit by a car...or a truck? I didn’t remember."
"Ouch?"
"Oh, but it seemed like all of us were dead before coming here," Izzi turned his gaze in my direction.
Ah...true. "Perhaps...it’s a prerequisite for a soul transfer? Maybe that’s why Natha could only stay for two months there while the hero was summoned with his whole body--existence--whatever."
"That’s plausible..."
"That’s depressing," Zia, who had been left out of the conversation about being dead and moving to another world, pursed her lips.
I laughed and reached out the hand I didn’t use to caress Jade, patting the succubus’s head that was scooting closer to my side. "But we all get a second chance in life, so isn’t that nice?" I glanced at the other two. "Not everyone is lucky enough to have that."
Neel bit the end of her pencil again. "Well...if you put it like that..." the black eyes stared at me for a few seconds before she asked me carefully. "What about you?"
"Me?" I felt Zia gripped my sleeve tightly. "I just died...naturally, I guess?"
"Naturally..." Zia grumbled.
I laughed again. And the fact that I could laugh it off was a good thing for me. I didn’t feel bitter about my first life. The unluckiness of having a druid body in a place with mana scarcity like Earth; I had thought of it as fate. I truly meant it when I said all the misery I experienced was the thorny path I had to go through before meeting Natha.
I mean, death was death. Be it from illness, from getting hit by a vehicle, or from overworking, we died in the end and got to relive our lives.
Wasn’t that the important part?
"Well, now that we got our second chance, we could try to make it better than the previous one," I shrugged, carefully cradling Jade who finally fell asleep after all the exhaustion from transforming, crying, and arguing with Natha.
I looked at my worker--I mean, my partners in front of me. "First, by making that recording device and getting a lot of money."
Finally, I saw Neel grin.

chapters.title: Chapter 361: It’s nice being the one observing other’s story sometimes
chapters.content:
Chapter 361: It’s nice being the one observing other’s story sometimes
After I said it, the two inventors immediately shifted the conversation to our project.
"Oh, right. Won’t we need a room for us to talk about this project?" Izzi looked at me and Neel. "I gathered we won’t do it in the research tower."
"I won’t go to the Castle," Neel declared.
Right. That was the whole point of her coming here. At that time, Zia offered a place timidly. "Can’t you do it in the library? It has stationary and everything."
The two inventors, however, didn’t seem keen on that idea.
"Library is rather..."
"The vibe is strict, and..."
"If there’s mishaps..."
"Hmm..."
Heh--it seemed like they had bad experiences with libraries. Of course, I expect nothing less from someone who blew up a university, but I didn’t expect Neel to have it too. I had thought she would avoid any public places, but I guessed she had to go to one before she built her bunker.
"Can’t we just use one of the bedrooms?" Neel looked at me. "There are a lot of them and no one uses them."
"Oh, that’s right," Izzi nodded. "We can move some equipment here and--"
"The ante-library!" Zia interjected, startling us with a slightly higher tone. She cleared her throat and repeated with a quieter voice, half-hiding behind me. "Umm...you can use the ante-library. No one uses it, and it’s more like a place for discussion, so..."
My brow raised as I looked at her; the corner of my lips twitched as I held back from grinning. "Well, there’s a lot of table and stationary there, so it’s rather ideal, I think," I decided to...help her a little bit. "And it’s not a public library, so what are you talking about being stiff and all? The only people who use the place are me and Zia."
Izzi glanced at Nell, and the half-naga, as the newcomer, just shrugged. "Sure, if you don’t mind," he said. "I mean, you’re the owner after all, just--" he chewed the inside of his cheek before adding cautiously. "Don’t sue me if there’s...umm...accident or anything."
I scoffed and said proudly. "Do you think the library of Matsa Ra Natha doesn’t have protective magic?"
"Tsk--rich people!" Neel muttered under her breath.
I wanted to laugh, but I was afraid I would wake Jade up, so I just pressed my lips and turned toward Izzi. "Hey, why don’t you just stay here for a while?" I suggested, feeling Zia’s finger twitch on my elbow. "Wouldn’t it be complicated if you went back and forth every time? It’s not like you were banned from leaving the tower--I mean, not anymore."
Izzi bit his lips and scrunched his nose in contemplation. "Nngh--can’t," he shook his head after a minute of making a distressed face. "The furnace is there, and I can’t complete the other project from here."
"What? The amusement park one?" I tilted my head. "I thought you only need...I don’t know--papers?"
"I have to make a working miniature--a prototype, you know--to see it works on a small scale," Izzi shrugged. "That Lesta told me to; we’re collaborating on the formations needed there."
Damn--he must be eager to pay his debt now, aside from gaining more patents to his name. Made it hard for me to tell him to focus on this video recording device.
Neel narrowed her eyes and leaned forward then, the interest palpable in her face. "What amusement park?" she asked. "Are you talking about that amusement park? Rides and carnivals and all?"
"Rides, mainly," replied the elf. "A novelty of this world, no? Lots of money; very marketable," he winked, and the black eyes flashed.
"Can I...can I join?"
"Ask the boss," he shrugged. "I mean, the Big Boss," he cocked his chin toward the upper floor. "It’s his wedding gift for his bride."
"It is not," I pursed my lips.
"Yeah, whatever," Izzi scoffed. "But you know he makes it for you."
"...I know."
"Tch--rich people."
* * *
Izzi brought a chest with Neel’s prototype camcorder inside, as well as all of his research notes, putting them in the ante-library that had been morphed into their temporary research lab.
While they were talking about the completion of the video recording, I would sit in the library making more picture books for Jade--this time about the tale of a boy’s adventure on Earth’s hospital wards. We would color the pictures together and Angwi would put on a preservation spell over the papers so they wouldn’t get smudged or damaged.
Once they were done, we would read it in the garden after feeding the fish, and Jade quickly forgave me for planning to have a week-long honeymoon.
While I was busy drawing with Jade, Zia would sit on the couch facing the ante-library with a notebook or a novel in her hands--whether or not she used them was another story. I enjoyed checking on her and exchanging glances with Angwi, giggling silently behind my teacup while Jade observed us in confusion.
Anyway, it was quite fun.
And then, it was the day of Amarein’s visit. The moment I saw her coming in her bird form, I contacted Arta through the communication orb.
"Aunty!" I greeted her with a hug as usual. "Arta said she will come again this afternoon, are you okay with that?"
"Another fitting?" she raised her brow.
"Mm; she wants me to try the druid-styled outfit, and wants to know your opinion about it."
"Oh-ho," Amarein perked up slightly. "In that case, I shall not refuse the invitation."
And so, we shooed Izzi away and Neel was observing the fitting with a bewildered expression. She watched the seamstresses coming in with dumbfounded expression, but still followed us to the suite to see what the furor was about.
"Wow, you really are getting married," she said, sounding absolutely amused now that her initial surprise had passed.
I just shrugged, only for the seamstress behind me to clasp my shoulder tightly, wordlessly telling me to stay still.
"Good job, Young Master. You managed to keep your weight," Arta praised me by...squeezing my cheeks.
"It hasn’t been that long," I pursed my lips. "But I really lessened my snack and sugar intake."
"I can vouch for that," my loyal bridesmaid nodded.
[Poor Master! No longer eat candy with Jade...]
Thanks for the sympathy, I guessed? I glanced at the full-body mirror they put on the side, observing the half-ready clothes made of druid’s fabric. It was flowy, very light even though it consisted of several layers. I couldn’t move much while they stuck the fabric on me, but while they were handling it, the fabric kept on changing colors. Like how the druid wore it, the clothes had a high collar and would be fastened by tight, embroidered sash adorned with jewels, directly mined by the drows.
"What do you think, my Lady?" Arta asked with palpable anticipation.
And Amarein took upon it seriously. "Hmm..." she was no longer looking from the chair, but standing closely to observe the outfit well. "It’s quite alright. It’ll be nicer to stiffen up the upper part more, and add another layer below to deepen the color gradation. Have you thought about the embroidery on the sleeve and the sash?"
"Ah, that’s what I wanted to talk to you today, my Lady! I’m not so sure about the pattern to be used here."
"Why don’t you let the druids work on the embroidery, then? We have our own technique after all."
Arta gasped. "You mean the living embroidery?! Oh God--would you do that?"
And then the two started to get all serious about the design and the embroidery and whatnot. I had no idea what they were talking about, and as usual, just enjoyed myself becoming a diligent mannequin. Let them have fun--my duty is to wear them and look good while doing so.
"It’s pretty, but don’t you have a red one?" a voice greeted us from the window.
[Ignis!]
"Ignis!" I watched as Jade immediately flew to the fireplace, waiting for Ignis to crawl there. "It’s been a while since you graced us with your presence."
"I’m busy," the Salamander said haughtily. The tone told me he had just accomplished something great. How cute. "But the cave is done now."
See?
"Oh!" I glanced at Amarein then. "Is it possible to use it as a training ground?"
The druid lifted her head from Arta’s journal. "Not yet. It’s better to focus on mastering one element first."
"I see..."
"But there’s no reason why you can’t play in there," Ignis muttered rather sharply, prompting Amarein to raise her brow and add with a smile.
"Of course, it’s okay to play," she chuckled. "But there’s no need to purify the place, isn’t it?"
I tried not to laugh so the seamstresses did not scold me again, but it was so funny how this Salamander that had been absent suddenly acted as if I was being banned from visiting its abode. "Let’s play in the cave after we’re done training on the cliff."
The little gecko’s tail smacked the fireplace three times, before its head rested on the frame.
"There’s all kinds of creatures here..." Neel muttered quietly in the corner.
"Oh, have you met the wyvern?" Zia glanced at the half-naga.
"...the what?!"
"It’s nice, isn’t it?" I grinned at her. "I met a lot of friends after coming here."
And perhaps she could start to have some too.
I didn’t know if Neel caught on the meaning behind my smile, but I could hear her quiet mumble. "Well...I guess it’s not bad."
Hehe...
And then, the Salamander asked again. "So, will you wear a red one?"

chapters.title: Chapter 362: The prerequisite of becoming a cupid is having a pair of wings
chapters.content:
Chapter 362: The prerequisite of becoming a cupid is having a pair of wings
People said visualization was good for learning, so that was what I did.
I tried to visualize mana in the way people visualized atomic particles. All this while, I had been looking at it too abstractly, looking at the environment like I was looking at a painting. Perhaps because at the start, I saw this world as a novel. And when we looked at things too broadly, it was hard to focus.
But now, rather than looking at the whole picture, I tried to look at the centerpiece. Rather than feeling the whole mana, I tried to focus on the tip that led the whole flow, imagining them as those atomic particles and trying to lead them inside my body by moving those particles. A concentrated effort rather than relying on my druid genetic instinct.
By following the movement of a certain part keenly, I kept my mind busy enough from wandering around, even as the characteristic of mana was knocking on my mind palace persistently.
But for that, I needed to make sure I was in a deep concentration state first--which was why I started the whole lesson by practicing the new breathing exercise as a warm-up.
Once my mind entered a focus state that I built up as a habit for the past ten days, I immediately moved toward the next step; absorbing the mana.
The thing about the air was the difficulty; the way the mana was scattered everywhere. Catching millions and trillions of particles scattering in the sky was like trying to catch confetti with a bare hand; not impossible, just hard and tiring.
Thanks to Amarein’s last lesson, I managed to narrow my spreading consciousness--the room where the confetti was sprayed--to a single lane in front of me. I guided the visualized particles into my body, and made the other particles follow the one I guided inside.
In other words, rather than catching those particles by hand, I sucked them with a vacuum cleaner.
It was easier now because I only had to guide and absorb the mana contained in a designated area. And I worked, worked hard to keep my focus on those particles of mana. And just like the breathing exercise, I did not let my body process the mana automatically. I guided and followed them throughout my mana circuits and mana core.
It was exhausting.
Keeping my focus at all times was draining me more than battle training with the Castle’s soldiers--which I felt like I should start doing again--focus, Val!
Ugh--yeah, the point was that I couldn’t keep it long. I had no idea how long I was maintaining it, but I knew it was shorter--way shorter--than usual. And when I opened my eyes, I was drenched in sweat as if I was just visiting Ignis’s cave, almost breathless.
[Master alright?] Jade patted my cheek lightly, moving its wings as if wiping the dripping sweat.
"It would be easier if you expelled the purified mana directly to the environment," Amarein brushed off the stray hair sticking to the side of my face.
"Yeah, but..." I looked at my palm, where a marble-sized energy was condensed. "I won’t be able to measure the progress, then."
Amarein smiled and nodded with a proud smile. "That’s true, and congratulations," she whispered, stroking my chin. "You succeded."
My mouth stretched into a grin automatically. Yes, the output was small, or rather, I ran out of steam before I could procure much.
But hey--I’m not floating!
"I think we could try doing it while riding the wyvern tomorrow," Amarein said, helping me to my feet again.
"Oh! Vrida will be elated!"
Jade was also chirping cheerfully, and after I caught my breath, Amarein made a staircase on the side of the cliff leading to Ignis’s cave, who had been waiting for us in the Salamander form.
Like the time in the volcano, Ignis was swimming around the pool of magma. It moved to the edge of the pool to greet us, raising its flaming head on the scorched ground. The flame was hot, but not unbearable, and it didn’t affect me nor Jade. I stroked the salamander’s head and Jade jumped onto Ignis’s back.
"What a place!" Amarein exclaimed in awe. "You don’t need to purify the mana, but you can hone your control over fire, Valen."
"Come swim with me," Ignis told me with a rare eagerness.
"Not that much," Amarein shook her head, to the salamander’s disappointment. "Only after you were sure you could transmorph well."
Patting the disappointed Ignis, I looked at Amarein with raised brows. "You permit me to transmorph?"
"Fire is fine; it’s a limited and controlled environment," Amarein nodded while patting my head. "And you’re contracted to the owner of this domain, so--Ignis, isn’t it?--could become your anchor."
"Oh!" I looked at Ignis and Jade with a grin. "Let’s do it someday, when I’m proficient enough," I paused then, and added sheepishly. "Although...I...don’t know how to swim..."
"Flame doesn’t need to know how to swim in liquid fire," Ignis told me dryly. "But I’ll wait," it said, before adding after a few seconds. "You have to come here often to train."
Ah, I wanted to pinch the scaly cheek. "Of course! I’ll visit a lot with Jade."
At least, when Izzi wasn’t visiting for the project. I couldn’t leave Zia alone to watch the two inventors working. I needed to distract her from time to time--and observe them while at it.
But anyway, my problem was no longer the anchor, but focus endurance. So I had no problem with doing the purification again on top of Vrida. Just like the day before, the output was still small, but succeding twice meant it was legit!
I let myself eat a piece of my favorite honeycomb candy as a celebration afterward.
"We will try the water next time," Amarein said before going back. "It should be easier to manage than the air, but keep practicing the breathing exercise so you may retain your concentration longer."
"Yes, Mam!" I gave her a salute with a hand over my left chest.
"Good luck, my dear," she stroked my cheek once before turning into a bird again, leaving with one of my wedding outfits to be embroidered by the druids.
* * *
The next time Natha came back, he came together with Izzi, who didn’t seem to really want to be there. But paying debt came before comfort!
He spent a while checking on the progress of the project with the other two in the ante-library, making me feel rather useless. I mean, I was the client and the overseer, supposedly. But then again, Natha was the one who paid their salary, so...
Not to mention, my knowledge about this stuff was very surface-level. I could read the formations, but understanding the depth of the application and the flaw in it needed years of academic class--which I did not attend, of course. Eruha was more inclined to teach me about the social-economy-political condition of the Demon Realm.
But since we were all gathering in the library anyway, Angwi made an exception and served the afternoon tea there. Otherwise, those two inventors would just holed up in their new research headquarters until dinner time.
I shall not be charged with neglecting my employees’ welfare, thank you very much.
Once again, Jade turned into the human form; but not so he could argue with Natha. Quite the contrary, Jade wanted to show that he would talk with everyone but Natha--even the silent Angwi and the newcomer Neel. It only made the Demon Lord smile in amusement, however, thinking that the little brat was acting cute.
That being said, Izzi and Neel were still busy huddling together with a chart and a blueprint in hand, even while their other hand shoved cakes into their mouth. I scooted closer to Natha, who looked at me with a raised brow. But I just gave him a silent stare before glancing toward Zia, who was looking at the inventor duo silently.
Natha looked at his distant niece and the corner of his lips twitched. "Interesting," he muttered quietly behind his cup.
"Right?"
"Zia? Zia?" Jade tugged on the succubus and whispered. "Zia? Why Zia ignore Jade?"
The little boy, who didn’t want to talk to Natha, wanted to play with the others. Unfortunately, the others were quite busy in their own world, so Jade was rather annoyed.
"Huh? What?" Zia flinched and looked at Jade, who pouted and instantly sulked.
"See? Succubus ignored Jade!" the little boy grumbled and stomped away to the other side of the table to...smack the elf.
"What?" Izzi widened his eyes in confusion, turning away from the blueprint in his hand. "Why are you hitting me?"
"It’s Elf’s fault!"
"What is?"
I unconsciously grabbed a savory popcorn that Angwi so kindly made for me this afternoon, scooting closer to Natha while seeing this unfold.
"It’s because Elf never play with us anymore! Always look at paper and paper!"
"Huh?!"
I didn’t think that was it, Jade, but continue.
"Now Zia don’t want to play with Jade too!"
"Jade, that’s not--"
"Succubus, quiet!" Jade pointed a small chubby finger at Zia. "Succubus ignore Jade! Only look at Elf! We always play together in the past! Jade don’t like this!"
A pair of small palms slammed the table, and I almost choked on my popcorn. Both Zia and Izzi blinked in confusion at the sudden outburst that seemed to be coming out of nowhere.
"Wait..."
"...uhh?"
And then, Zia stood up; the pink face went deeper in red. "I...I’m not looking at him! I’m looking at them!"
Doesn’t that mean you admit you were looking, Sis?
Izzi, looking flabbergasted, raised his head and met Zia’s glare. "Umm..."
Abruptly, Zia turned around and ran out of the library. Izzi blinked in a daze of confusion and fluster, while Neel tilted her head--having no idea about what was just happening. Jade widened his eyes and ran to me.
"Master? Why Zia go? Zia is angry at Jade?" the little boy asked with a voice full of concern.
I pressed my lips to hold back my laughter and pulled the little boy to my lap. "I’m not sure, Jade. Let’s leave Zia alone for a bit, and then we’ll go look for her, okay?"
"...okay," Jade nodded before hugging me and sighed. "Jade will give Zia candy."
"Alright, alright..."
Beside me, the old man Natha just sipped on his tea while murmuring. "Youth."

chapters.title: Chapter 363: I believe that practice makes perfect
chapters.content:
Chapter 363: I believe that practice makes perfect
I waited until the tea became cold, before taking Jade to look for Zia. It wasn’t hard, really. There were only two places where she would be when she sulked; the library and her room.
So, there we were, knocking on her room. Zia wasn’t answering, of course, so I employed the best weapon. "Zia? Zia~ Jade want to see Zia..."
We waited for a few seconds before a quiet voice told us that the door wasn’t locked. When we entered the room, Zia was crouching on the armchair near her lit fireplace, hiding her face behind her knees.
Jade ran to the succubus and held Zia’s legs. "Zia, Zia, Jade sorry!" the little boy said. "Jade don’t know why, but Jade sorry that Zia upset..."
Oho--to think my little familiar would be willing to apologize without having to be explained that what he did might be upsetting to others...
You’ve grown, Jade.
"Jade just...Jade just upset because Zia don’t play with Jade anymore these days, don’t draw picture book with Jade anymore..." he fiddled with Zia’s sleeve, looking up with a pair of round green eyes. "Zia just looking at Elf, so Jade thought Zia want to play with Elf more than Jade."
Oh my, look at this very reasonable explanation.
"But Elf only play with Naga, and Jade upset because it make Zia not play with Jade..." the little boy pursed his lips, before taking out a few pieces of candy and putting them on Zia’s palm. "Jade sorry...will Zia forgive Jade?"
Oh, I should totally gave a piece of Gluttony’s candy to Jade later.
Zia lifted her reddened face slightly--of course, she wouldn’t be able to get mad at our cute little Jade. She sighed and let Jade grab her hand. "I’m not upset," she said quietly while I took a seat at another chair. "I’m just..."
She didn’t continue with words, only her face got a bit redder. So I took it upon myself to finish it for her. "Embarrassed?"
"Ugh--" she bit her lips, before finally taking a deep breath and nodded. "Yeah..."
Of course, Jade didn’t understand why. "Embarrassed? Why Zia embarrassed?"
"That’s..." Zia pursed her lips and averted the bright, inquisitive green eyes. "Jade needs to grow up a bit more to understand."
Indeed--and I had no intention of letting my little bird-boy grow up too fast.
Wait...would Jade morph into my adult self after he grew up?
Oh--I digress.
Anyway, Jade didn’t seem to like it that his lack of experience in life hindered him from understanding something. But he got over it quickly after seeing how uncomfortable Zia looked. "Hmm...okay, Jade won’t ask" he shook his head lightly. "But Zia not angry with Jade, right?"
"No," Zia shook her head too.
Jade grinned and stretched his arms up. "Hug?"
Finally, the succubus’s lips cracked a smile. She lifted Jade to the chair and they hugged each other tightly. What a cute sight. Good, I would be able to leave Jade here tonight, fufu...
And then, we heard a knocking sound on the door again. I could guess who it was, so I just stayed in my chair, looking at the dancing flame on the fireplace, pretending to not care. With a quiet sigh, Zia stood up and put Jade on her chair, before walking to the door and opening it after a few seconds of hesitation.
"Oh, umm...hey..." Izzi’s voice could be heard from the door, sounding rather timid and awkward.
I told Jade to keep quiet by placing my finger over my lips--and the good boy clasped his mouth with a pair of small hands--before we carefully peeked at the slightly cracked door.
"What do you want?" Zia asked curtly.
"Ah, no--just...are you alright?"
"Why wouldn’t I be?"
An awkward silence ensued, and Izzi’s shadow seemed to move in confusion; hand scratching his neck. "I see...that’s good," he said. "I’m going back for today."
"...okay."
Another silence, which almost made me suffocate. How could Natha be so patient with me when I fumbled with my words and thoughts?
"Tomorrow, there’s..." Izzi started to speak again, but immediately stopped and, after a while, corrected himself. "I can come tomorrow, right?"
"I’m not the owner of this place."
Damn, Sis--couldn’t you be more affectionate? I would have told her to be more honest, but...it would sound too hypocritical, wouldn’t it?
"Well, I’ll come here in the morning," he said, finally sounding firm. "See you tomorrow."
"...see you," Zia replied in a voice that almost sounded like a whisper, before closing the door.
As the succubus stood in front of the door silently, as if pondering about the way she responded earlier, I couldn’t help being a bit mischievous. "Zia..."
"W-what?"
"The male protagonist in the draft you’re writing now," I tapped on the corner of my twitching lips, "is an elf, isn’t it?"
What I received in return was a glare. "S-shut up!"
Ah...how fun!
* * *
After ditching--I mean, persuading--Jade by saying that he needed to cheer Zia up, I made a journey to return to the library, and met Neel on the stairs.
"Oh, Neel," I observed the half-naga for a bit, but she didn’t seem to get affected by what happened earlier. As an outsider, she probably felt more confused than anything. "Is Natha still in the library?"
"No, he said he’s going to check on the cliff or something," she shrugged.
"Oh, Ignis’s cave?"
She stopped walking and tilted her head. "Your talking gecko has a cave?"
"Oh, I didn’t tell you? Ignis is a Salamander."
"...well, fuck. You really have everything here."
I couldn’t but laugh, and like a summoning spell was activated, Natha’s figure came behind me in a flurry of black feathers. "You smell like fire," I said as he wordlessly picked me up like he would pick Jade.
"Like warmth?"
I patted his cheek and kissed his forehead lightly. "I like you cold better," I whispered, before turning my head to Neel and waving her goodbye.
While carrying me in his arms, Natha turned around and climbed the stairs to our suite. "So, I can have you for myself, now?"
"Yep," I tilted my head and whispered in his ear. "I left Jade with Zia."
"Good," he let out a harsh exhale. It seemed like he was feeling sulky because I was more interested in watching the drama and left him to look for Zia--this jealous demon.
To appease him, I held on tight and lowered my head to kiss him all the way to the suite. By the time our lips parted, the coldness had been washed away from his eyes. "How’s the cave?" I asked with a giggle.
"Pretty nice for a trap door," he shrugged.
"Right?" I laughed and gazed out of the window, to where my wyvern was. "And we had Vrida watching the river, so we’ll be informed immediately if anyone comes."
"Hmm..."
As expected, he still sounded displeased with the whole idea of letting them into the tower instead of intercepting them before they crossed the border. "I want to talk to them," I said softly, giving him my sweetest smile. "If we confront them outside, they might just run. But inside...they’ll be trapped," I tilted my head to look into his eyes. "Don’t you think it’s better that way?"
Natha did not give a reply, but the gleam in his eyes told me he was rather enjoying the concept of trapping the Hero and his companion in a place that Natha could control. "Promise me--"
"I won’t be reckless," I smiled and brushed his neat hair. "And I’ll call you immediately after they appear."
"You better," he looked at me with a pair of stern gaze.
"I promise," I told him, and then sealed it with a kiss that did not end until my back touched the mattress. "Oh, I forgot to tell you!"
Natha pulled away and hovered above me. His eyes were on my face, but his fingers were on the cords tying my tunic. "What?" he asked.
"I succeeded in absorbing the air elemental mana the other day!" I grinned and let him silently undress me: "I’m not floating one bit! She didn’t need to pull me back once on the second day!"
Natha made a pondering face--although his fingers didn’t stop, and the outer layer of my clothes had become undone. "I can’t decide whether I’m feeling happy because my bride is so talented, or feeling sad because it means he wasn’t thinking of me anymore."
"Pfft--that wasn’t what I meant," I flicked his nose lightly and pulled him a bit closer by his lapel.
"Enlighten me, then."
I grasped his cheeks and looked into his eyes. "It means I have gotten better at controlling the mana coming inside the body," I said, and watched his brow arched slightly. "So, I was thinking that I might be able to control another kind of substance too."
His brow arched higher and I ran my hands along his shoulder, down to his arms that were perching on my waist. Leading one of his hands over to my abdomen, I whispered. "What do you think about...a practice session?"
The only answer I got was his hungry touch and thirsty kiss.

chapters.title: Chapter 364: Drama is fun if you’re a part of the audience
chapters.content:
Chapter 364: Drama is fun if you’re a part of the audience
"What’s the commotion?" I stirred at the vague sounds of chirping and conversation, slipping deeper into the blanket and Natha’s embrace.
"The Elf is here," Natha murmured against my hair, pulling me closer to him by my waist.
I blinked drowsily for a minute, trying to digest the information. My blurry eyes glanced at the window, where the sunlight had just trickled into the room. My head was raised in surprise when my brain registered this. "This early?"
"He came from a bakery or something," Natha pushed me back to the bed, so I laid on top of his bare chest.
"You mean...the bakery that Zia liked?"
"Maybe?"
I whistled and looked toward the door. So that was what he meant by coming here in the morning. Honestly, that bakery was truly good. They were so good that the bread and pastries were usually sold off in an hour or two after the place was open.
"What? Do you want to come down for some bread too?" Natha tilted his head; the silver eyes finally opened.
I grinned and lowered my head to bite on his pecs. "I have my own bread here."
His sleepy eyes became focused then, and I was flipped to my back in an instant. "What is this? My dear bride had become so good at seducing me," he whispered sharply before returning the bite all over my shoulder, pulling out laughter from my lungs.
"Well, if I had to be honest, I just don’t want to disturb them," I shrugged and circled my arms around his neck.
"Hmm..."
"So we have a lot of time alone this morning," sneaking my hands into his hair, I pulled him down and bit his ears. "Since we have more babysitters down there."
"That, I approve," he kissed me once, and suddenly, I was in the air, being carried to the bath chamber. Needless to say, we spend waaay longer time there than usual, playing with...water and such.
Ah, I was reluctant to admit it, but...there was a part of me that thought this situation--where we had to live separately--had a nice aspect to it; like how Natha was getting more honest with his thoughts, or how he got more clingy, or...like this, where his carnal appetite was increasing.
I didn’t even have to beg or give him any rejuvenation spell. Ah..what a dilemma...
Oh, Mother--looked how pervert your son had become!
I wouldn’t tell him that, though--didn’t want to make my Demon Lord sulky again. It was good that he banned himself from reading my thoughts, or he might have misunderstood it again and thought that I was fine with us living separately.
Because the answer was no! Sure, it brought something amazing into our sexual life, but I would still rather wake up looking at his face, feeling safe with his cold arms around me.
Anyway, it was almost midday when we were finally presentable to come out of the suite. They were in the drawing room this time, and Zia was writing another fairy tale for Jade. Izzi, meanwhile, was crouching on the floor binding all of the picture books we had made for Jade, turning them into a real book, not just a pile of sketch papers being tied by strings.
Such a productive ’date’, if it could even be called one.
Knowing their personality, though, I didn’t think they would have made considerable progress. I was sure they already caught on to the fact that both of them might feel something toward each other, but we have someone whose experience in love came from fantasy, and someone who probably never courted another person before, so...
Still, I don’t think they would take five decades like the ones in the Castle. In this case, we could send our gratitude to Jade the wing...bird?
"Master!" Jade ran from Zia’s side to jump into my arms the moment I stepped foot inside the drawing room. "Why Master take so long?"
"Ahem--I...overslept?"
I heard Izzi snorted from the floor, even though his hands were still moving to bind the papers together. I saw that he even made a nice leather cover for the books, so I would have praised him if it wasn’t for the sound he made earlier.
"How early did you wake up today, Izzi?" I tilted my head, asking dryly as I glanced at the basket which was already half-empty now.
Izzi coughed and grumbled, before getting back to his book-binding. To get the best products that Zia liked, he would have to go to the plaza at the crack of dawn, so he would be ahead in the queue. For someone who preferred to sleep at dawn, it would mean that he was forgoing sleeping altogether.
Pretty sweet of him, honestly, and I could see that it was effective, seeing Zia’s reddened ears.
That being said...
"I just...couldn’t fall asleep and decided to go around the city," he mumbled quietly. "It’s not like I go out of my way to buy it..."
See? He would never admit it, this stupid guy.
"Oh? What a disappointment," I scoffed while taking a seat around a tea table so I could get my very late brunch. "And here I thought you were trying to do something nice for Zia."
Izzi flinched and the tools in his hands clattered to the ground. "Th-that’s...I mean...well, uhh..." he looked at Zia and me back and forth as if his brain was being fried while deciding between avoiding any accusation of him having a crush and not making Zia displeased at his intention.
In the end, it was Zia who scolded me with a flustered face. "Val!"
I just stuck out my tongue and pretended to ignore them. Hmm...now I know why others liked to tease me so much; it was indeed fun teasing other people about this kind of thing. I hid my giggle behind Jade’s confused head, and Natha ruffled my hair slightly before picking Jade off of my lap.
"You have quite a mischievous side, huh?" he said quietly while putting the annoyed Jade on another chair. "Don’t disturb your Master when he’s eating."
At Natha’s words, Jade pressed his lips and nodded, sitting calmly on his slightly elevated chair while watching Angwi put down our brunch spread on the table.
"Well, I learned from the others," I shrugged and grinned sheepishly. "But Jade, did you morph again today, or you haven’t changed back since yesterday?"
"Jade not change back!" the little boy threw his arms in the air cheerfully. "Master gave Jade lots of yummy balls when Aunty here, so Jade have lots of power!"
"Oh! Good boy!" I ruffled the green head and pulled his chair closer so Jade wouldn’t be so far away. The little boy giggled proudly, which he totally deserved!
The first time Jade changed into human form, he could only maintain it for a few hours, before falling into a deep sleep for the rest of the day. I did observe that the time Jade needed to maintain that form was getting longer and longer, but this would be the time he managed to last through the night. What an excellent child!
"Right--I shouldn’t lose to Jade, right?" I clenched my fists to energize myself. "I need to work harder so I can keep the focused state longer!"
Last night, I was practicing the way to control--ahem--substances inside my body by trying to fuse my essence with Natha’s after he released his seed inside me. And I realized a fatal flaw in this whole plan;
I had to do it with a dazzled mind that was battling the highest level of pleasure.
At the peak of the high, my nerves were tingling all over, and I could hardly think of anything but Natha’s name. How on earth could I concentrate enough to fuse our essence?
Ah...the road wasn’t covered in thorns, but it was sure slippery as hell.
Perhaps sensing my disappointment, Jade curled his fingers to follow my move and pumped his little fist in the air. "Master, go go!"
I couldn’t help but laugh at the adorable display, and once again pumped my spirit. "Mm!"
"Easy there," Natha chuckled and tapped the center of the table, where our food had been left untouched. "Fill yourself with energy first before attempting anything, yeah?"
I grinned and swiftly dug into the food. Since I skipped breakfast, it should be alright to stuff myself now, right? After all, I was also spending the whole night...umm, exercising, in some way. And I had to feed my greedy unborn child before coming down earlier, so I was famished!
"You know..." I pondered while munching on my brunch. "People say sparring could enhance one’s concentration," I looked at Natha and spoke carefully. "Should I...go back to train with the Castle’s soldier?"
I felt Alveitya buzzed inside my left arm, but I told the spear to not get excited. Natha sometimes tended to get extra protective of me, to the point that he couldn’t even pierce my ears with his own hand. There was always a possibility that he no longer wanted me to fight.
But then, he nodded without hesitation. "Sure."
"Oh?"
That was unexpected. He didn’t even pretend to mull it over? Was his protective era over now?
"You’ll come to the Castle more often that way," he said with a shrug. Pfft--this demon. And then, he added with a smile. "Besides, I know our soldiers are not good enough to hurt you."
Hey, even if it’s true, you shouldn’t diss your own people, my Lord!

chapters.title: Chapter 365: There’s a reason why game systems use numbers as parameters
chapters.content:
Chapter 365: There’s a reason why game systems use numbers as parameters
Hmm...Natha was right; these soldiers couldn’t hurt me.
Despite getting a bit rusty from skipping cold weapon training these days, I didn’t feel threatened during the mock battle. At first, I tried hard to trace back Valmeier’s muscle memory, for the first time ever since our soul merging, I pulled him out to invade our cells. But the guard regiment that sparred with me ended up sprawling on the floor one after another before I could even feel any sweat rolling down my back.
I didn’t even release Alveitya’s power, just using it as a simple spear.
[Boring...]
Even my cheerleader stopped cheering after seeing that I didn’t need one. Jade simply perched on one of the Colosseum’s pillars to wait for the training to be over.
"Haikal..."
"Yes, Young Master?" the guard commander replied while staring at the soldiers who were still helping each other to get off the ground with cold eyes.
"Umm...were you being careful not to hurt me?"
I mean...it was possible, right? Perhaps they were worried that Natha would punish them if they put even a scratch on me, so they deliberately used weak attacks. Or perhaps they wanted to coddle me, so they didn’t want to give me a hard time.
I wouldn’t blame them if they did, but I needed to have a hard time right now!
Haikal, however, just looked at me while blinking slowly, and the soldiers were making pitiful faces. "Young Master..."
"Yes?"
"I feel this sometimes, but you seem to forget quite often that you were once the spearhead of the human kingdom," Haikal told me. "You seem to think that we just give everyone the moniker of slaughterer."
...oh. Oh. Right. I had considered the demon realm to be my home and country when I was actually a war veteran who had never been absent from the battlefield since I was sixteen. Honestly, Valmeier had never bothered to compare himself with other people, because what was important for him was fulfilling his duty, which was to fight in the war until the King told him to stop. Since I was inheriting his memory, I also had no concept of power scaling.
Well, it wasn’t like I ever needed to fight after I met Natha.
I used to spar with the soldiers before, but...since I was only doing it as a light exercise, I didn’t take it too seriously.
"And I think you don’t understand that you’ve gotten even stronger than before," Haikal added.
"I do?"
"Stupid Valen," Ignis chimed in from the pillar where Jade was perching. "You’ve completely healed now, and you’ve made a contract with me. You’ve also started to take a proper lesson with that druid, so of course you’re stronger now."
Ah...
Behind me, the hovering Alveitya also buzzed in agreement. Hmm...now that I think about it, at the time I was diligently sparring with the soldiers, I was still trying to accustom myself to handling the spear, recalling Valmeier’s muscle memory. But now, our soul was already fused, so it was no longer a mere ’memory’.
"I see..."
"Yes," Haikal nodded.
"Oh, but what to do..." I clasped my cheek in confusion. "I wanted to spar to train my focus in a high-stakes situation."
This was my current challenge. I could train my focus in a meditative state with the breathing exercises I did every day, and by following Eruha’s lecture--which I did not dare to be tardy about or he would give me a deadly headmaster stare. But I still couldn’t do much in a situation where my brain had to experience all kinds of things at once.
"Hmm...would you like to take a walk with me, Young Master?" Haikal unexpectedly responded to my lament.
"Oh? Sure..." I let Alveitya hover around and play with Jade and Ignis while I followed him.
He led me down the arena and out of the Colosseum after telling his lieutenants to increase the training portion of the soldiers--oops. It seemed like he wanted to tell me something that might be too sensitive for ordinary soldiers’ ears. He started to speak when we walked through the park separating the barracks and the research tower area.
"It’s hard for me to say this, but the Realm of Greed had been known to not possess a great military power," Haikal said with a tone that I could only infer as a lament. "At least, if we’re talking about general demon resources."
Ah, he meant the soldiers’ levels were low. I did recall hearing Natha talk about it.
"To compensate for it, His Lordship provided us with great armaments," he continued. "Although thankfully, we hadn’t seen the need to use it so far."
Understandable. The way for the wealthy was to be overgeared after all. Just looking at the formation barrier carved all over the Castle and its wall, the place was basically a fortress. And such formation barriers that needed the employment of dozens--or even hundreds--of formation masters could only be achieved by a realm that was rolling in dough from taxes gained by the commercial activity alone.
But...what did Haikal tell me all of this? It had nothing to do with my current problem.
"That being said, Young Master, it’s not like we don’t have an elite few whose abilities are on par with the warriors from Wrath," he said.
"Oh, you mean...like special forces?" I suddenly get excited.
Right--Natha used to have a group of dedicated guards hiding in the shadows to protect me before. And there was also the company of shapeshifters that acted as his spies--although...they were probably more of his people than the realm’s assets.
"Yes; someone as meticulous as Natha would always prepare some hidden cards," I nodded in agreement, and Haikal put on a prideful expression as if I was praising him instead of Natha. This loyalist.
And then, something suddenly clicked, and I stopped walking, looking at the guard commander with widened eyes.
"Wait, you mean..." I parted my lips, and Haikal’s stiff lips stretched into a subtle smile as if he knew what I wanted to say. I lowered my voice and ended up asking in a whisper. "You mean...I could try to fight them?"
"Yes," he confirmed it with a nod.
Oh! That’s right! If fighting with mere foot soldiers was not enough, I could just fight with the ones above them!
Wait!
"What about you? Or Caba?" I unconsciously stepped closer to him, and Haikal stepped back in reflex, even lowering his head. Oops. I stopped and took a deep breath to control my excitement, but I still couldn’t help but wait for his response while staring keenly.
"That’s..." his reply was delayed for a few seconds. "I don’t exactly mind, Young Master. But.."
"But?"
"Whether it’s with me or the others, you would need His Lordship’s permission first."
Oh...
And just like that, my excitement deflated like a popped balloon.
* * *
Natha said before that he knew the soldiers wouldn’t be able to hurt me. Perhaps that was why he easily gave me permission to train.
But what about fighting his vassals? Would he still be so generous?
I used to just waltz into his office when I visited the Castle before, but this time, I sneaked into the Lord’s quarters to take a shower, even though I wasn’t sweaty. I changed my dusty outfit, and asked Panne to fix my hair so I looked presentable enough. As a bonus, I even begged Izzi to birdsit Jade while I visited Natha’s office.
This time, I fully intended to seduce the Demon Lord.
Only after I was sure I looked good did I walk to Natha’s office. It was close to luncheon, so the timing was rather perfect. Before I reached his office, however, I saw him walking through the corridor--probably to visit me in the training area.
"Nat!"
I ran to him without hesitation and gave him a tight hug, long enough for him to question it. "Hmm...seems like my bride wants something?"
I looked up and pretended to be offended while his aides walked away to leave us alone. "Why do you say that?"
"Because you’re being clingy in a place where people can see," he smirked and lifted me in his arms. "Not that I mind. In fact, you should do it more often."
Ugh--no way. I was already embarrassed enough as it was.
"So? What is it?" he asked while resuming his walk with me in his arms--this time heading to the garden. He stroked my cheek and brushed away a stray hair that stuck to my face when I was running earlier. "You even make sure you look prettier than usual."
Hehe...so he noticed. Didn’t matter--what important was the effort. Holding onto his shoulder, I bit my lips and asked carefully. "Nat, I have a request..."
"Yes, what is it?" he smiled brightly, as if he was gaining pleasure from fulfilling my desire.
I wasn’t sure he would still smiling after he heard what I wanted.
"Umm...so..." nervously, my hand ended up fiddling with the line of his lapel. "You know how I want to train my focus by fighting the soldiers?"
"Isn’t that what you’re doing today?"
I nodded and, as my heart started to beat loudly, I lowered my face. "But, you know...they are kind of...weak? So I didn’t even need to concentrate," I bit my lips unconsciously. "So...I wonder if it’s alright for me to fight someone more powerful--you know, like your elite troop or your vassals..."
I finished my request without looking up, and for a while, I didn’t hear his response. I was too scared to look at his face, so I just kept my gaze down and held him tightly while he continued to walk toward the garden.
When I felt like my heart would burst from worry, he finally spoke. "Is there no other way?"
"Well...I don’t know any," I replied quietly.
"Hmm..."
Carefully, I looked up to see his face. Contrary to my expectations, he didn’t seem to be that angry. The silver eyes didn’t look cold or hard, just full of thought.
"Nat?"
He continued to walk toward the lake and stopped at the edge, looking at the cold water in silent contemplation. I didn’t even have enough courage to ask him to put me down.
And then, I heard him mumble. "I guess...it’s better to do it in a controlled environment rather than on the battlefield."
Huh? Huh?!
"Is it alright?" I swiftly asked. "I can do it?"
He finally looked at me; His gaze was solemn and there was a wry smile on his lips. "As long as there’s a healer present."
"Yes!" I grasped his face and kissed his cheek hard, before pulling away and tilting my head. "But, Nat...I am a healer..."
"Ah," he blinked. "I forget."

chapters.title: Chapter 366: There’s a lot of paths leading to Rome...I hope
chapters.content:
Chapter 366: There’s a lot of paths leading to Rome...I hope
"Most of them are working, so you’ll have to wait while I call someone," Natha told me as he walked me back to the portal after lunch, following a hovering spear and two little companions perching on its staff.
I just nodded obediently, since it was already good enough that he let me train to fight. "What about doing it with Caba or Haikal?" I asked. "Or...you?"
He did not answer, but his hold on my waist tightened. When we reached the labyrinth garden, he finally spoke again. "Do you remember the time you were panicking when you found out about my wound?"
"Oh..."
Instantly, I knew what he meant. Just like how I was scared and disgusted at the thought of wounding him, he was afraid of the thought of wounding me. Even if it was accidental, or was done in a good sport.
"Okay, I got it," I nodded. "But what about the others?"
He chuckled and pinched my cheek--perhaps a response to my persistence. But at least he didn’t seem to mind it. "Haikal might do it, being a challenge-lover that he is, but Caba..." his lips curled. "I don’t think he would have a heart to do it."
"Why?"
"Because his power lies on him going berserk," Natha explained. "Do you think that puppy will have the heart to let himself lose his mind while fighting you?"
I couldn’t help but giggle when Natha called the bald vassal a ’puppy’, although it fit the demon tremendously. "Well, Haikal said he doesn’t mind as long as you give permission, so I’ll tell him the next time I come here."
"Tell me too," he leaned down and gave me a peck on my cheek. "I’ll watch."
"Okay!"
I kissed his lips briefly before crossing the portal with my three companions. Now that I had Natha’s permission, I could do the training without any burden. Hmm...yes, it was indeed better if we had our partner’s support.
With this, my days were filled with tampering with my body and mind. As soon as I woke up, I did my breathing exercise before ingesting any substance--including the usual herbal drink. I would have liked to do it as long as I could, but Amarein told me to set a fixed time every day, so that was what I did.
Something about how it was a marathon and not a sprint.
She said I shouldn’t exhaust my mind on a single day, just to become too tired to do it the next day. I wasn’t sure if it would increase my endurance, but..well, she was the teacher, wasn’t she?
After having breakfast and talking to Shwa with my other companions, I would train with Alveitya to move my body around as per Arta’s instruction. I got hungry easily that way, but I also burn that many calories to balance it out.
When Haikal finally had free time, we sparred inside the Colosseum. At least, we were at first.
As expected of the Commander, he was on another level compared to the other soldiers. We agreed to not use any magic, just poor cold weapon; me with Alveitya, and him with his sword.
And oh, it was thrilling.
I could feel that he still held back at the start, probably an unconscious reaction because he was facing his Lord’s betrothed while the Lord was watching. For that, I responded with brutality, attacking him without any inhibitions. Since Natha had insisted on bringing a healer, I chased for blood, and soon, Haikal could no longer afford to be careful.
He shed his armor, along with his hesitation, and we duke it out, filling the arena with the sound of clanking metals until sparks were flying around. And Gods...was it exhilarating! His movement turned faster, and the swing of his sword became heavier, even without infusing any mana. I’d say he was as good as one of Wrath Generals in Valmeier’s memory.
I had no time to think of other thoughts but the battle, keeping my eyes on Haikal’s movement and gaze as we engaged in a deadly dance around the arena. The interesting thing was that...none of our attacks landed on the others. We attacked and parried ferociously that the one who got wrecked was the arena instead.
In the end, though, the quality of the weapon spoke for itself, and I managed to deflect Haikal’s sword from his hands, ending the battle with the tip of Alveitya a shy away from his neck.
Both of us were panting heavily, staring at each other. There was a small commotion when the audience was clapping and hooting from the side. I could hear a loud chirping too instead of a disappointed ’boring...’ like last time. Despite all of that, however, I gasped.
"No!" I let go of Alveitya--which instantly hovered around me in concern--and held my head, crouching down in devastation.
"Sweetheart?" a worried voice called out, and I felt a cold hand on my back. "Sweetheart, is something wrong?"
"It is!" I gripped Natha’s hand tightly as I looked at him. The corner of my lips lowered by themselves as I felt so, so stupid. "I’m supposed to try controlling my mana while fighting, but I forgot!"
The whole reason I did this training was so I could train myself in multi-tasking--controlling the mana inside my body while my brain was focusing on something else. But I was so engrossed in the fight that I forgot about it.
Natha blinked slowly, before bowing his head and stifling a laugh. "Don’t laugh! This defeats the whole purpose of training!"
I smacked his arms, but Natha continued to laugh while pulling me into his embrace. Behind me, I could hear Haikal mutter while letting out a relieved sigh. "Whew--thought my head would fly for a second."
I pushed Natha away from me and looked at the guard commander. "Hey, hey, let’s do it again! Perhaps if we also use magic--"
"Sweetheart..."
"Uhh, perhaps not now, Young Master," Haikal scratched his neck, glancing at his sword that ended up slightly chipped. "If I pushed mana into my sword before fixing it, it won’t be able to hold through the fight."
"Oh..." I pursed my lips in disappointment.
Natha patted my head and made me look at the gentle silver eyes. "Remember that it’s not a sprint, sweetheart."
Phew...I took a deep breath and nodded. "Yeah, okay...sorry," I muttered as I tried to suppress my impatience. "And thank you, Haikal."
"It is my pleasure, Young Master."
Natha pulled me up again, still with leftover laughter in his brightened face. Well, at least, he looked even more beautiful like this. "Don’t get too disappointed," he whispered while we were walking down the arena. "You can still train on the real-life simulation, can’t you?"
I tilted my head in confusion at first, but the glint in his darkened eyes gave me the answer already. Again, I smacked his arm and hissed. "Pervert!"
But well...I wouldn’t refuse the offer.
* * *
"Eruha..."
"Yes?"
"When you drink Lesta’s blood, does your body automatically process it, or do you need to manually absorb the mana?"
It was a purely educational question, but Lesta was spraying water from his mouth on the side. Whatever. After failing again last night during the...simulation time, I suddenly thought that I probably should ask someone who needed to absorb foreign substances on a regular basis.
Who else but my dear teacher I could turn to?
Not to mention, I knew that sometimes...they did while having sex, so...
Kind of a similar situation with me, no?
"Depends," Eruha answered my question seriously--because, again, this is an educational discussion. "Normally, I just let my body process it--there are other things I need to put my mind to, after all."
Lesta threw him a cushion, which he easily caught in the air with a small, playful smirk on his lips. Geez--I thought this was an educational discussion!
"So, what’s the other condition?"
"If I have to use the mana immediately, I need to manually separate the mana from the substance, and instead of letting it be absorbed in the vessel, I push the mana directly to the mana circuit."
"Oh-ho!" I straightened my back. "And how do you separate them?"
"Why? Are you trying to drink blood too, Young Master?"
"Of course, not!" I pursed my lips. "There’s other kind of...substance, that I wanted to...well, rather than separate, I guess I’m trying to fuse them? But I also need to catch the essence of those substances before fusing them, so..."
I realized then that I was kind of blabbering, and when I lifted my face, I was greeted by Eruha’s pondering face and Lesta’s cheeky smile.
"What?" I glared at Lesta, who only curled his lips before responding with a shrug.
Eruha, however, mulled over my words seriously. "Does this perhaps have something to do with your dryad heritage?"
Lesta’s lips curled even higher, and this time, I was the one who threw a cushion to his face. "...yeah," I decided to just focus on Eruha. As expected, he was very perceptive.
"Hmm...this is something I never thought I would impart on other people," Eruha stroked his chin. "I shall think it over and come up with a plausible lesson."
Ugh...I was just asking for some advice, but...he was trying to turn it into a whole lesson? Not that I had any objection.
As long as it would help me with my end goal.
I stroked the black pendant over my chest with a smile.
"Oh, right," I looked at Lesta then, because Eruha was busy thinking about the vampire method of absorption. "Are you going to live together in the end?"
The cheeky smile on Lesta’s lips vanished then. Or rather...it was replaced by a bashful expression. Hehe...I got a taste of teasing people now and I would not stop!
"I heard from Arta that you were all sitting down to talk about it over dinner."
Although, from the way Arta told me, it sounded more like Lesta and Eruha arguing while Malta became a referee. Arta? She just watching while eating some popcorn.
And I mean that literally.
I glanced at Eruha then, and by the small smile on his lips, I knew he had won.
"We...are planning to move after your wedding," Lesta said with a tinge of red on his ears, and this time, I was the one who gave him a wide, cheeky smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 367: When you reach that phase of no longer looking at the price tag
chapters.content:
Chapter 367: When you reach that phase of no longer looking at the price tag
"This is possible?"
We--me, Zia, and Arta--were huddling around a fabric that was my druid-style wedding outfit. Amarein had visited again, bringing the outfit that had been specially embroidered by the druid.
And Mother...Mother! The embroidery wasn’t just beautiful--it was alive! And by alive, I meant they seemed to flow and move like those optical illusions. The leaves and the flowers along the hem looked like they were rustling in the wind, and I couldn’t help but stroke the Great Tree embroidery on the sash.
"It’s so pretty..." I sighed in awe, feeling like hugging the fabric, but was too afraid to damage it. I didn’t even let Jade touch it. "Am I really going to wear something this pretty?"
"Of course!" Arta nodded while huffing with pride. "We’ve poured everything--blood, sweat, tears, and tons of money--into this so you will be the most dazzling flower in the entire world."
B-blood too? What have you been doing, Arta?!
"Anyway, I think it’ll be nice if you wear this at the first banquet," Arta stroked her chin. "I thought it’d be best if you come out with a couple outfit with His Lordship, but...now I think it’ll be better to show each of your heritage during the first banquet."
"Is that the one where the important people are invited?" I asked while very carefully letting go of the fabric.
"Yep!"
Arta led the seamstresses to put the outfit inside a chest with preservation magic on it, before securing it like a banker would secure their bonds. I had this feeling that perhaps, for her, items belonging to my wedding were more important than the whole Castle’s logistics.
"My deepest gratitude to you, Lady Amarein," Arta bowed gracefully at the druid.
"It’s for my beloved nephew, so of course we’ll do it happily," she patted my head, and as I looked at the chest containing the outfit, I could feel the love that my distant relatives had for me.
I grinned sheepishly and leaned into her for a hug. Truly, I was so loved in this world, huh? Perhaps the reason for the lack of affection on Earth was so I could be more appreciative of what the people in this world did to me.
"But, my Lady..." Arta scooted closer and clasped her hands together. "If it’s not so impertinent of me, may I know what kind of method you used for the embroidery? Of course, you don’t have to answer if it’s a tribe’s secret or something..."
Amarein chuckled at how Arta frantically shook her hands, with a face that was a mix of caution and expectation. "Sure, I can tell you. Knowing it doesn’t necessarily mean you can replicate it, after all."
We moved to sit on the couch then, while the maid golems served our tea. "We don’t use plant-based threads," Amarein said, to our surprise.
"Huh? Then what..."
"We made threads from elemental stone."
It wasn’t just me that got surprised, but also Arta and the seamstresses. Even Neel, who wasn’t really interested in dresses and outfits, lifted her head from the corner. We were all looking at Amarein, surrounding the couch like a bunch of students.
"What do you mean, Aunty?" I asked curiously. "How can you turn elemental stone into thread?"
"You can do that too, my dear, once you master your control," she stroked my nose. "It’s just a matter of giving shape to the elemental mana byproducts. The drows could also turn elemental stone into liquid."
"Like metals?" my eyes widened.
From my meager knowledge, the demons and humans only utilized the stones by absorbing the mana inside to themselves or a device. It was rare, but there were also those who crushed the stone into powder. Threads and liquids, though...
"Is that why they are so good at making accessories and weapons?"
"That’s right," Amarein nodded. "Turning elemental stones into threads needs refined control over mana, so not all druids could do it too," she smiled, looking at the interested demons in front of her. "So you can’t replicate it even if you want."
That didn’t make them disappointed, though. Their eyes were still bright from the new knowledge. "How many stones does it need for the work you did on Young Master’s outfit, my Lady?" Arta asked with palpable eagerness.
Amarein, however, just glanced at me before responding with a smile. "I shall not divulge that."
Arta and the seamstresses whined, but Amarein merely sipped on her tea without giving anything more. I had a feeling that...it would cost a lot. But you know what? I have stopped worrying about cost and whatnot now because...does it matter?
