"I don’t, but..." she smiled wryly. "That’s not exactly why."
"Oh?"
"I...don’t think I have the right."
I retracted the hand I was about to use to lift the teacup. "...why?"
She lifted her face, and I could see the same forlorn gaze I caught in Natha’s face earlier. "Because I have been hurting him."

chapters.title: Chapter 461: A lot of things in this world could be solve with a simple communication
chapters.content:
Chapter 461: A lot of things in this world could be solve with a simple communication
What?
I was surprised for a second, but quickly managed to control my expression--easy; just took the teacup and hid behind it as I mulled over this information.
Hurt. What did she mean about hurting? I was surprised, but also...it kind of gave me more understanding of why Natha seemed rather dismissive about informing Nezja about the wedding, like he didn’t care whether she knew it or not, or whether she would come or not.
I had thought it was only him being considerate of her circumstances, or perhaps it was just how people his age looked at such things. But it seemed like there was something more there.
It was weird though...
From what I read in Natha’s journal, his great-aunt was the one who took him in after the massacre that killed his mother. It was also his great-aunt who brought him to the King’s Sanctuary. In the journal that I read, I didn’t sense any hatred toward her, and...well, logically, she played a good part in his early life, wasn’t she?
But then again, I only read about his early days and not after, so...
"What...do you mean?" I asked carefully after sipping on the tea. After making sure I had put on a proper poker face through the reflection on the tea, I put the cup down and looked at her.
She looked at her tea; eyes glazing in reminiscence. "When he told me he was going to be a Lord, I opposed him. So much so...that we ended up fighting and I kicked him out of my place."
Oh...
"I told him that I won’t consider him family again," her lips stretched slightly into a bitter smile.
Uh-oh.
"It was a long time ago, and through our mutual acquaintances, we do manage to be speaking again, but...as you can see," she lifted her face and returned to that stern expression again. "We are almost like a stranger to each other."
Ah...so that was why they spoke stiffly, as if they were in a formal setting. I thought that it might be because this great-aunt preferred that kind of style, but again...there was a whole different reason behind it.
I couldn’t help but frown slightly, lifting my teacup again as I mulled about this. Honestly...yes, it must have been hurt to be kicked out of his only family’s house. Not that Natha couldn’t survive, since he still had his family’s money--or what was left of it--but...
Natha didn’t have a lot of safe places for him in this world at that time. Aside from D’Ara’s abode, the only place he could consider as ’home’ was probably his great-aunt’s place. And even though he could come to D’Ara all the time, she wasn’t family in the end.
So I got it that Natha felt hurt. My question was...why did she oppose Natha becoming the Lord so much?
Rubbing the cup slowly, I tried to recall what I knew about Natha’s family. "Was it...because of his father?"
I tried to put myself in her position. Ever since Natha was born, their family had been hounded by threats from the then-ruling faction of the Spectre race. Natha’s father had tried his best to convince the Lord that Natha would never attempt to become one in the future, but he still got executed in the end. I had no idea what really happened, but I had a conjecture that the massacre and all the stuff Natha had to face in the academy had something to do with it.
Perhaps...
Perhaps she thought that Natha was betraying what his father had sacrificed himself for. It was the one thing that ended their family and killed so many people, and in her eyes, it might seem disrespectful.
"You are...a perceptive kid," Nezja smiled, before correcting herself. "Ah, I guess I shouldn’t call the Lord Consort a kid."
"Oh, don’t worry about it. D’Ara treats me like I’m a baby sometimes," I waved my hand dismissively. I mean...even Natha had lived for almost a century, so...how long had she lived? Two hundred years? More? A twenty-something like me must all look like kids in her eyes.
Surprisingly, she was chuckling for a second. A soft one, but it was still there. Unfortunately, it was soon getting shadowed by her sad gaze and bitter smile. "You’re right," he let out a quiet sigh. "I loved that child tremendously--Natha’s father, I mean. He was so alike my brother, who was practically raising me. It hurt me when he got executed, and it opened all the pain when Natha said he wanted to be the Lord."
"At that time, the Spectres were still ruling, and we still lived in partial seclusion. No matter how good her performance was in the war, people still saw him as the son of a traitor," she continued with a heavy voice. "I thought...how much more would he want to drag my nephew’s name through the mud? He was already branded a traitor, and if Natha became a Lord, the stigma would become even thicker. The accusation would become true."
Oh...I bit my lips and gripped the cup on my lap tighter as I felt my fingers tremble a little bit. Knowing that Natha only wanted to become a Lord because of me made me feel guilty.
"I’m...I’m sorry..."
She raised her brows slightly in surprise. "What for?"
Uhh...would it make sense if I said he did it because of me? Technically, this body lived in this world less than thirty years ago, so how could I say Natha planned to become a Lord for me...seventy years ago?
As I refrained from answering, she let out a small chuckle. "Well...of course, I found out later that he actually made a whole plan to get rid of the Spectres, but..." she gazed at the garden beyond the glass window. "It was too late. By the time I could accept his decision, the distance between us had become so wide that making a bridge seemed impossible. When he spoke to me again for the first time using a formal speech and gesture, I knew that we became nothing more than a pair of strangers."
Hmm...this sounded complicated, but...not really?
I put the teacup on the table and looked at her eyes. "Aunty...I don’t think Natha hates you at all."
She smiled wryly. "He’s good at hiding things."
"Not from me."
Well, I hope so anyway.
"...you’re right," she said with a smile. "Pardon me for making assumptions."
Phew--I didn’t want to show off or anything, but listening to her, I knew that both she and Natha had the same problem; too many years had passed without any reconciliation attempt. Sure, they were ’talking’ to each other, but it was on a greeting level and nothing more.
I wouldn’t have thought of doing anything before, but since Natha had become my husband, I should have the right to meddle for a bit, right?
"I..." I took a deep breath and braved myself to speak. "I didn’t have a very functioning family."
I could see her surprised arched brow and the question in her eyes, but I continued. "The only ones I could call family were Grandma and Grandpa, but...I couldn’t spend much time with them and when I finally could...they weren’t here anymore," I gripped my hands tightly as my heart clenched at the thought of them. "I always regret that, wishing that we have more time."
"But your grandparents did not hurt you, did they?"
"No," I shook my head. "But...if my parents came to me to apologize sincerely, I would forgive them. I would talk to them, we would talk to each other, and I would try to figure things out."
I knew she must have understood what I was trying to say since she was Natha’s grand-aunt. There was a possibility that she thought my words were just something that came from a kid who didn’t understand anything. I might overstep my boundaries just because I became Natha’s husband, but...
But I still wanted to say what I could.
"Of course, I couldn’t say it would be the same for him, but..." I looked at her and shrugged. "You don’t know, do you? You’ve never talked about it."
She didn’t respond, but I could see her eyes shook a little bit.
"This is only my thought, but..." I recalled back to the forlorn look I saw in Natha’s face earlier. "I think both of you think you were hurting each other."
She did not bother to mask her surprise this time. Her eyes widened; doubt and hope were interchanging in her shifting expression.
"Natha had his own reason as to why he wanted to become a Lord, which he probably couldn’t say to you," I continued. "But you know, don’t you? Natha had always been clever, so there was no way he didn’t know how you might feel about it. The fact that he told you about it first meant he didn’t want to lie or hide it from you because he knew how much this matter meant to you."
She blinked repeatedly, eyes glazing in a daze.
"He knew you were in pain for his decision, but because he was also stubborn about it, he agreed to just leave your place," I exhaled heavily. "And just like you said...the gap between you kept increasing, and when you met again, he had no idea how to face you properly, and it just...snowballing from there, I think?"
I leaned back, even though it would make me seem slouching, but...honestly, I was kind of tired.
"You know...Natha is cheeky, and he could be so, so petty about things," I smiled as I recalled his youthful shenanigans he told me sometimes before bed. "He wouldn’t care even if his opponent was an elder. For someone like him...do you think he would treat you politely if he really hates you?"
I looked at her, and the glazed eyes were now filled with realization. "No," she said quietly. "No, he would spit on me--or something equal to that."
"Right?" I laughed, letting the heavy breath leave my body slowly. "For me, it just looks like you need to talk and clear the misunderstanding."
"Misunderstanding..."
"Uh-huh," I nodded. "So, it’ll be better if you talk it out, right? Like, right now?"
"Oh, that--"
I stood up and yelled like Jade usually did. "Naaaat!"
I counted, but he teleported in just one second. "What? What’s wrong?"
He grasped my cheeks and looked at me up and down, checking for any...injury? What did he think might happen between me and his grand-aunt that would cause a druid injury? Geez...
Wordlessly, I took his hand and pushed him into my seat. I pressed his shoulder and looked at Nezja. "There! You can talk now!"
"Sweetheart?"
I cupped his face and gave him a hearty kiss before retreating with a grin. "It’s my turn to enjoy the garden now."

chapters.title: Chapter 462: what’s the use of friends if not for promoting wild ideas?
chapters.content:
Chapter 462: what’s the use of friends if not for promoting wild ideas?
What happened after I sat Natha down with his great-aunt was rather blurry.
I remember sitting on a swing in the backyard where they could see me from the sunroom. The night breeze, the soft swaying of the swing, and the exhaustion from today’s event all contributed to a drowsiness that sent me to sleep right then and there. When I opened my eyes again, it was already morning in the huge bed of Lord’s quarters.
My eyes were only half-open when Natha already gave me a kiss on my forehead, my eyelids, cheeks, nose, my chin--anywhere but my lips. I laughed and grasped his face to direct his lips to mine, which he gave while embracing me tightly.
"My precious treasure," he whispered against my lips. "My most precious treasure."
Umm...it was nice to hear such things in the morning, but why did you have to make me fluster right after I opened my eyes?
I knew it was not an attempt at seduction, however. The softness in his eyes told me he was genuine. My fingers raised to stroke his cheek before I could realize it, perhaps because he looked so vulnerable suddenly.
"Did you have a good talk with your great-aunt?"
Rather than answering, he turned his face slightly to press his lips on my palm. It kind of looked like he was nuzzling my hand the way Jade or Vrida did, which was adorable. I could feel the line of his lips stretched as he closed his eyes, and it was enough to tell me that last night’s endeavor brought a good result.
"Do we have another banquet tonight?"
"No," he kissed my palm and got up. "Just a little soiree in the afternoon."
"Oh, is it like...afternoon tea, or something?" I rolled to my stomach and lay down for a bit more while Natha was fetching my morning herbal drink.
"You can see it like that," he replied. "It’ll be a more casual setting where we could converse more with the guests--not just a greeting."
"I see..."
Uhh...so I had to interact with more people? Well, at least it shouldn’t be too much since it was a soiree. I rolled to my back again and got up to receive the warm drink Natha brought me. "Who are the guests?"
"People with decision-making power in Realm of Greed," Natha said with a deep smile, before adding in a whisper. "It’s essentially a business meeting, so don’t think too much about it."
What are you talking about?! Shouldn’t a business meeting require more thinking than a regular soiree? This demon...just because business was second nature to you...
Phew--I puffed my cheek and blew on my drink to calm down. "Where are we going to have it?"
Natha tilted his head and smiled mysteriously; eyes curling and gleaming in mischievous light. "You’ll see."
* * *
[Papa! So many fishes! Fish house all over the wall!]
I’d see...
Oh, I saw it alright. The sparkling blue-tinted room. Rays of sunlight streamed from above, casting a dreamy reflection on the floor and table.
When I heard he was building an aquarium, I was thinking of a single massive fish tank. I had no idea it would be as close to the aquarium on Earth as this. All hail magic, I guess, because I didn’t think it would be possible to install something like this on a Castle’s reception lounge without it.
It was even more magical because there was no visible filtering system and cables, thanks to the magic formation that Lesta probably worked hard to complete. The floor-to-ceiling tanks along the wall were joined in seamlessly so that if I ignored the huge double doors on either side of the room, I would think we were transported into an underwater observation deck.
I had to admit that I couldn’t breathe for a few seconds when I entered the room.
That wasn’t the case for Jade though, who immediately flew toward the ’wall of fish’s house’ in front of us. The little bird was immediately face-to-face with a fish that was bigger than its wingspan, which made Jade startle for a second before shrieking in delight when more fish came near. There were way more variants here than in our pond back in the Lair--including those that weren’t fish--so Jade was beyond thrilled. For the little bird, it would feel as if it was plunged into the vast blue sea.
Oh, wait...
"Jade, do you want to enter the tanks?" I broke out of my trance and Jade was in front of my face in record time.
[Jade can? Can Jade?!]
"Is it okay?" I asked Natha, who had been watching us silently from behind.
"Sure; we still didn’t have a swimming bird variant," Natha shrugged.
Jade twirled in the air while chirping excitedly. [Hurry, Papa! Hurry!]
It had been a while since I made an air bubble for Jade, and it was kind of hard making it while laughing. Not that Jade needed air for breathing, but my little bird couldn’t swim, and I didn’t want those pretty feathers to get all wet in the middle of the soiree.
The moment I finished the air bubble, Jade immediately rushed inside and rolled around happily, before pointing toward the tank with its wing. Natha flicked his wrist and Jade was thrown inside the tank with a shriek. The moment it fell into the water, however, the shriek was quickly replaced with a joyous chirp as the fish came and surrounded the bubble, nudging it forward and around.
As I laughed at the scene, I felt a pair of cold hands around my waist. "Do you like it?"
"Do you really need to ask that question?" I held the arms hugging me and leaned back against his chest.
"I’m glad," he kisses my temple gently. "It’s your first wedding present."
"Huh?"
Wedding present? From him? But...I thought we got married, so...why would the groom give a present?
And what...first?! Were you going to give me more than one?
Before I could voice my surprise, however, one of the staff told Natha that the guests had arrived. I kept my surprise inside then, and immediately forgot about it once the event started.
Just like last night, I tried my best to remember their name, what their position was, and what was their role in the society. Observing the way they talked to Natha was interesting, and I wanted to send my gratitude to Eruha for all of his lessons because otherwise...I would barely understand what they were talking about.
The conversations were rather boring in my opinion, but the food was great as usual, and because this was my second last outfit, Arta had lifted my snacking ban. I could eat whatever I wanted now--all those delicious cakes in front of me! Between the cakes and pastries, and watching Jade rolling around between the fish and making friends with the jellyfish who thought the air bubble was one of them, it was pretty easy to survive the soiree.
At least until one of them talked about the aquarium and how Natha was building it solely for me and I ended up blushing like crazy. It didn’t help that Natha replied to it with a smug and proud smile, saying things like it was a given that I should receive this kind of stuff and whatnot.
Ngh--it felt like I was entering the aquarium to get cooked, because at the end of it, I left the lounge with a face as red as a boiled crab.
[Papa is so red! Papa should enter the tank like Jade!] my little bird said innocently, making me even more embarrassed. Perhaps I should really dunk myself inside the tank.
But was that the end of my fluster? Oh, of course, not!
"Did you pack what I gave you?" Zarfa whispered after Arta finished clothing me in my going-away outfit--a nice leather coat that was almost identical to Natha’s.
The one who answered her, however, was the one who packed my suitcase. "Don’t worry, Miss--I already did," Arta raised her thumb. "As well as the gift from the courtesans."
"Why would you do that? And why did you give me such things?!" I hissed at them, and Zarfa wiggled her fingers at me.
"Sometimes, it’s more alluring to have a few strands of clothes than being completely bare."
What do you know? You were a virgin!
"Don’t worry; leave everything to Lord Uncle. He will know what to do with them," Zia, yet another virgin even though she was a succubus, patted my shoulder.
"Wouldn’t that be more embarrassing?"
"Wouldn’t that be the point?" they winked at me and ugh--whatever.
I left the giggling girls who kept advising me wild things and went to Angwi. She shook her head and patted my hair in a consoling manner--as I thought, you were the best, Angwi. But that wasn’t why I came to her. I took the black pendant that usually circled my neck, and placed it in Angwi’s palm.
This time, I would spend time only, and only with Natha, so I had to leave Shwa behind. My heart felt heavy, and my neck felt too light, but still...
"Please take care of Shwa and Jade," I held her hand tightly. "And Ignis and Vrida...and Zia too."
She gave me a little smile and patted my head again. Just then, the door was opened and I heard the sound of serious chirping and Natha’s whisper--I guessed they were on negotiating terms again. The moment Jade saw me, however, the bird ran and hugged my cheek, nuzzling my neck in a show of sorrow I didn’t catch when Natha was bribing her earlier.
"Be good, okay? I’ll be back in a week."
[...’kay]
I hugged the little bird one last time and sent him to Ignis, who immediately wrapped its flaming tail around Jade. At last, Natha took my hand and led me to the balcony. I thought we would go immediately, but I saw a surprise there.
"Great-aunt!" I approached her, whose smile had become less stiff. There was a new spark in her eyes as I got closer, and she stroked my cheek gently once I stood in front of her.
"My little darling," she said, and then softly embraced me. "Thank you. Thank you so much."
I blinked in surprise for a few seconds before holding her back with a smile laugh.
"I’m glad," she whispered more, holding me a bit tighter. "I’m glad it’s you. I’m glad that you’re the one who stays by his side."
"And I’ll do so until the end of our time, Great-Aunt, so you don’t need to worry," I patted her back, and she pulled away with a brighter smile than before. I could see the tears pooling in her eyes, which were adeptly blinked away.
"Yes," she cupped my cheeks and gave me a soft kiss on the forehead. "Yes, I believe so."
Ahem--we heard Natha clear his throat and the great-aunt chuckled in response. "Right, I won’t hold you much longer," she looked at Natha and suddenly had the stern gaze back. "Be good and don’t tire him too much."
This time, I could hear several coughs and people clearing their throats in the back as Natha looked at his great-aunt dumbfoundedly.
"Me? Tire him out?" he scoffed while pulling me by my waist. "It will be a miracle if he manages to stop before I beg for it."
Nezja’s flabbergasted face was the last thing I saw before Natha enveloped us in his wings.

chapters.title: Chapter 463: consummating your marriage is not merely physical
chapters.content:
Chapter 463: consummating your marriage is not merely physical
This teleportation took more time than usual. It was at least five seconds, I think? Meaning the distance was really, really far. I didn’t think it took this long when he brought me from Lenaar to the Lair.
But I understood why; he did say we would go to an island. An island where there would be only the two of us there. I heard that during my seclusion period, he distracted himself from the stress of not seeing me by going to the island and preparing the place we would stay in during our...ahem--honeymoon. I wonder what kind of place it--
"Oh..."
My eyes fluttered the moment his wings retreated. In front of me was a cabin--a log cabin. It wasn’t big or fancy; in fact, it looked so ordinary that I would have a hard time believing Natha would stay in this kind of place any other time. It was small enough, and probably only consisted of a bedroom with a bath chamber, living room, and a kitchen.
Without looking closer, it would look like a random cabin in the middle of the woods that an explorer might use to rest in the middle of their adventure. But once I focused more, there were a lot of formation runes carved all over the cabin; preservation, protection, detection, warning system, temperature and humidity control, even mundane--but most important--things like bug repellant array.
And yes, as you might guess, it was in the middle of the woods. There was a canopy of tree foliage above the roof and wildflowers surrounded the cabin. The front porch of the cabin was well maintained, with a swing hanging from the ceiling. The front yard was decorated with a white gravel path as well as various shrubs of berries.
Oh, it was wonderful! But what made me inhale sharply was the patio attached to the side, which connected to the living room. I wasn’t sure if I should call it a patio or a pier, because I could jump right into a river from there.
Uh-huh; the cabin was also a riverside one. I couldn’t see it from here, but I could hear the sound of a waterfall from somewhere, deeper in the woods.
"Oh, Mother..."
I grasped my chest and exclaimed in awe. Oh, it was exactly like my dream. A simple place enough for two people to have fun and know each other more, surrounded by nothing but nature.
"Nat...it looks wonderful!" I turned to look at Natha. Even without looking in the mirror, I knew my eyes were sparkling at that moment.
"I’m glad," Natha took my hand and kissed our mark. "Would you like to have a tour?"
"Of course!"
He took my hand and started to lead me somewhere--but not toward the cabin. I tilted my head in confusion, but he took me toward the river instead. A bit further away from the cabin, at an angle that I couldn’t see because it was covered by a fence of trees, I saw a small...boat? Canoe?
"Are we going to...?"
With a smile on his face, Natha led me into the small boat that was only fit for two people. "You don’t think I only own the cabin, don’t you?" he smirked as he loosened up the rope tying the boat and weightlessly stepped into the boat.
"Are you flexing, right now?"
"What are you talking about? I’m just giving information," Natha chuckled while he tapped on the boat and it started to move. Whoaa...magic sure was convenient. "When I say something is mine, it means yours too."
"Oh, so we’re talking about asses sharing, now?" I arched my brow and he laughed.
"Sure, let’s say it like that. Now, you should focus on assessing your new asset, Young Master."
Pfft
--well, it sounded like a jest, but he was right. Who said honeymoon was about sex, huh? It could be about wealth distribution, healthy discussion about marriage responsibilities, distribution of household roles, or like in my case; about visiting yet another one of my husband’s collections.
People did not collect islands, you say? That means you did not know enough plutocrats.
But anyway, the place--ahem, my island--was different from the one in the middle of the lake. The mana was still rich here, so it almost felt like I was in the realm of nature. The river was flanked by trees that weren’t as sentient and scary as the ones in the Lair, so it felt more peaceful than eerie. The tree branches hung above the river and created a long tunnel of green and blue leaves, with sunlight streaming through the gap between the foliage.
"How peaceful..." I leaned back on the comfortable seat so I could look up and enjoy the intertwined branches.
It might be weird coming from someone who lived in probably the most peaceful corner of the world, but to be honest, I rarely had time to myself. With Jade and the others always made sure I never felt lonely, my surroundings were actually quite boisterous.
I didn’t hate it, of course. But sometimes, it was nice to have a quiet moment to myself. I got it during bathtime, usually, when Jade rarely joined me unless the little bird wanted to play with water. But here...it was quiet everywhere, with the voices of nature playing absentmindedly in the background.
Now I know why people called some trips a ’healing’.
Of course, it was more wonderful because I wasn’t actually alone.
Stretching my legs, I entangled them with Natha’s. He had been observing me quietly with a smile on his face, and a soft gaze in his eyes.
"Is this another wedding present?" I tilted my head.
"Hmm...part of it," he said, lifting my leg and draping it across his lap.
"’Part’? What’s the full version, then?"
"Wait for a bit," he said mysteriously, and the boat kept on going slowly through the river.
Oh, well--what’s the hurry, anyway? I decided to just enjoy the leisurely automatic boat ride. Natha even took out a bottle of fruit juice as a refreshment. He told me about the foreign plants and wildflowers we saw from the river, and explained what stuff we could do on this island--including playing in the waterfall and some spelunking that would make Ignis jealous. I couldn’t wait to do some foraging too since we came in the middle of spring, and--
"Close your eyes, sweetheart."
Suddenly, Natha put his hand on my eyes, shielding me from view. What? What is this? He leaned down to whisper in my ear. "I’ll give you another present."
Immediately, I quieted down and crouched obediently in my seat, waiting for time to pass. The sounds of chirping from the birds flying back to their nest got less and less, and in its place, I could hear something different; a splash? A swash?
"...are we...near the sea?"
I started to sniff around, inhaling the slightly unique smell of the salty wind. Instead of answering, Natha finally moved his hand away, and directed my gaze to the front.
Oh, it was the sea. It was the sea, alright. But that wasn’t the only thing.
It was a sunset. A sunset against the sea, spread in front of me as if it came out of a painting as our boat stopped in the middle of the estuary. It was different than the rewinding, unchanging sunset I saw in D’Ara’s abode. The swaying water made the enormous ball of orange look ever-changing and alive. Thinking that I wouldn’t be able to see the same sunset tomorrow made me reluctant to even blink, keeping the scene in my memory as much as I could.
"Oh...we should have brought the recording bird!" I sighed in regret.
"But then, it wouldn’t feel as special, would it?" Natha rubbed the back of my hand. "It’s precious because there’s a possibility of losing it."
Well...he was right about that. Besides, we would be too busy looking at the captured scene in the receiving crystal instead of watching the actual sunset.
But...

"I love you," I held him tight and kissed him with all my heart. "I love you so much."
I whispered the devotion that I only wanted him to hear, just like the promise he made that he only wanted me to hear. In this place, where there were only the two of us.

chapters.title: Chapter 464: playing house is not as easy as I thought
chapters.content:
Chapter 464: playing house is not as easy as I thought
"Ah, I should have lit up the lantern first before we went," Natha slapped his forehead when we returned to a dark cabin. Dark everywhere, honestly, since we were in the middle of the woods.
Thankfully, there were fireflies and some glowing moss around the cabin and the river, so it was actually pretty nice--not a horror vibe, I mean.
"I’m sorry sweetheart--I want to make it perfect, but..."
I couldn’t help but laugh at his worried face. It was kind of cute that he always wanted to look cool and everything, but I loved his occasional slip-up as much as his cool countenance.
"I don’t want it to be perfect, though..." I grinned and kissed him before climbing up to the dark porch. "You’re not in front of your subordinates anymore, so stop acting cool in front of your husband."
"Say that again," he pulled my waist and pinned me against the porch railing. "And stop acting shy in front of your husband."
Ouch? But I laughed and put my arms around his neck. Well...we were in the middle of nowhere after all. "Fine, you petty husband."
The soft vibration of his laughter came before his kiss, which continued until we entered the cabin. We had to fumble in the dark, however, and I couldn’t help but break the kiss to laugh as we stumbled around the furniture. Natha chuckled and finally lit up the mana lantern around the cabin.
Oh, it was as lovely as I imagined! We had a fireplace, which Natha immediately lit. There was a snug-looking couch and a fluffy rug in front of it, as well as some blankets and pillows. That was it. Nice and simple. There was a kitchen on the other side of the room, and across from the sliding window that was attached to the patio, there was a door that should lead to the bedroom.
I skipped toward the door and opened it--of course, it was still dark. Natha came and activated the mana lantern too, and I immediately found out that the bedroom was basically a copy of the Lair’s bedroom. I laughed at how the bedroom was basically bigger than the living room, but I was happy that we still had a big bed even here.
"I’m going to make us dinner, so you can rest for a bit," Natha said after chuckling at how I jumped into the big, plush bed.
I gasped and hurriedly got up. "No!" I recalled what we talked about before. "I’m going to unpack our luggage. Hurry take them out!"
He raised his brow for two seconds before bursting out laughing. "I guess you are serious about that," he said while taking out our suitcases from his storage ring.
What? Did you think it was a mere glib?!
I puffed my cheeks and he laughed some more while walking out of the bedroom. Huffing, I turned to face the suitcase and...uhh...perhaps it was a glib.
Why did I pack so much stuff? Natha only had a single suitcase, but why did I have three? I didn’t remember...ah, of course I didn’t. It was Arta and my mischievous friends who packed my stuff for me while I was busy attending the soiree.
Uhh...what should I do with these suspicious boxes that those girls put between my clothes? I mean...I knew it wouldn’t be weird to have them on a honeymoon, but...should I put them in the closet? Should I put them beneath the bed? Should I put them in the open...
Err...maybe not.
Should I show these to Natha and let him decide what to do with them? Uhh...oh, whatever--let’s just put everything in the closet for now. I had to unpack quickly so I could watch Natha cook!
Or so I planned, but honestly...I hardly ever unpack shit before. I didn’t even unpack when I was in the Human Realm, just took the clothes I wanted to wear and threw the dirty ones inside the laundry bag Arta gave me--which went to the storage ring instead of the suitcase. I did the same thing in the druid settlement too, whereas Natha always took care of it when we traveled together.
Damn. I wasn’t cut to this simple and humble life, it seemed. Who knew taking out clothes and hanging them tidily in the closet wasn’t that simple? Should I put the outerwear in a different cabinet? What about the nightwear? Should I hang them or just let them fold? I should put the toiletries in the bathroom, right? Oh, where should I put the shoes...
Aaagh! It was so weird without someone consulting me or simply chirping in the background as moral support!
...oh, gosh! I had become spoiled!
"What are you doing, sweetheart?" Natha patted my head as I lay face down on the bed. For some reason, I felt exhausted from this simple task.
"I’m disappointed at how spoiled I have been," I mumbled against the sheet. How dare I say things like ’I’ll take care of the house’ when I got confused with a simple activity like unpacking luggage.
I heard Natha’s suppressed laugh, but before I could glare at him, he was already hoisting me up and carrying me outside. "You did good," he said--which helped nothing because I knew he would praise me for anything. Still, I liked it. "Now let’s get some dinner, mm?"
"Aaah! I wanted to see you cook, though..." I pursed my lips in disappointment.
"We’ll be here for a week. You’re not thinking that I’ll only cook for one time, are you?"
"But I want to see it every time!"
"Should I throw everything and cook again, then?"
"Don’t waste food!"
He bit my shoulder in response and we laughed as he put me down on the couch. Ooh! We didn’t even have to eat properly at a dining table? Sweet!
"We can eat outside tomorrow," he said. "Have breakfast on the patio or a picnic on the beach."
"Oh! Oh! Let’s do that!" I nodded enthusiastically while receiving a plate from him.
"Hmm...I should have brought a set of picnic tables to be put outside..." Natha narrowed his eyes as he made another assessment of the cabin. "Maybe a parasol..."
"You can do it next time," I shrugged as I took a bite of the sliced meat. "We’ll definitely visit this place again, ri--oh! This is so good!"
"Is it really?" he stroked my bulging cheek and wiped a sauce on the corner of my lips.
I nodded enthusiastically. "Mm! I like that it’s smoky and well done."
"Pfft--" he pressed his head on my shoulder as his own shook a bit. I tilted my head in confusion and he looked at me with a wry smile. "That’s a new way of saying charred and overcooked."
"It’s not intentional?"
Again, he laughed silently at my shoulder, with just a shaking back as an indication. When he pulled back and leaned against the couch, he even had tears in his eyes.
"Oh, I did want to put a perfect meal for you, but...I guess I was too nervous and ended up messing up a lot."
Oh...so it didn’t seem like I was the only one struggling with the role today. "But it’s really good, you know!" I argued honestly. "The flavor is still there! It’s different from the one made by the cooks and Angwi, but it feels...hmm, how should I say this? Rustic? It’s like a barbeque, makes me feel like I’m in one of your adventures! Oh...now I want to be in one of your adventures..."
I looked at the crackling fire dazedly while continuing to put the food in my mouth. Mm, it really was good. Above anything else, it was made by someone whom I loved and who loved me with all his heart. There was no way it wouldn’t taste good.
"I’ll be sure to do it better next time," he said while placing a salad on my plate. "Eat this. I’m sure I didn’t mess this one up."
"Well, this is already good for me," I shrugged. "But sure, I’ll look forward to it."
When I put the last meat in my mouth, Natha suddenly grabbed my chin and kissed me. Soft, just a mere touch, but long, and making me forget about the dinner for a few seconds until he pulled away and leaned his head against my shoulder.
"God, I love you so much,"
"Me too," I laughed and shoved a meat into his mouth. Why was the one who cooked only watched instead of eating?
But then he asked me to continue to feed him, which of course I did happily. I used to be the one getting fed and spoiled so it was fun. It was fun to stay in a warm room with a fire crackling softly in front of us. It was nice to bare our hearts and souls, naked in mind with the one I loved. It was fun to just jest around and away from pretense.
It was fun to be in love.

my duty," I gripped him even tighter--almost squeezing his cheeks, really. "You had an affliction, you were in pain. Isn’t it normal for your husband to take care of you while you’re experiencing it? Wouldn’t you do the same? And you forget the most important thing..."
I paused then, waiting for him to digest my words and make a reply. "...yeah?"
"I wanted this," I loosened my grip then because I might laugh at how stupid he looked at that moment. "And I will continue to do this in the future. So stop being like this, okay?!"
I smacked his cheeks and squeezed them together one last time, before giving him a heartful kiss and a little threat. "I’m going to be really angry if you stay like this."
He flinched and straightened his back, as if...kneeling in attention--if there was such a thing.
"You are so silly," I laughed and pinched his nose. "Why are you even like this when I enjoyed it so much, huh?"
He blinked and parted his lips, for a few seconds but couldn’t force any words out. "You...enjoyed it?"
"Oh, I did! I still do!" I let out a sigh as my mind recalled the fresh memory of that continuous tingling sensation. "You were so hard and wild and oh--you even got bigger!" I clasped my hands and turned toward the full-length mirror in the corner of the room, giggling as I saw the peeking bite marks and hickeys all over my skin. "Even the marks are persisting--I love it!"
Natha did not make any sounds for a few seconds more, and when he did, he almost stuttered. "I..." he paused and swallowed before continuing. "Did it...not hurt? Didn’t I hurt you?"
"No?" I ran my fingers through the marks, feeling the slightly coarse surface. "I mean...it’s almost like a play? It felt--ahem--good, for me...?"
I grinned sheepishly, suddenly feeling embarrassed at the details.
"I..." Natha parted his lips without continuing his words again. In the end, he was back to burying his face in my lap. I had thought he would cry again, but I could hear his groan. "Oh, my Lord..."
And then what happened before happened again, only that his ’I’m sorry’ became ’Oh, my lord’ for a few minutes. I didn’t know what to do since he seemed to be in the middle of trying to get his bearing again, so I just let him hug my waist while I patted his back. What finally stopped him was...my grumbling stomach.
"...oops?"
Well...what could I do? I hadn’t had anything for days.
He laughed, for the first time that day, and looked up, raising his hand to caress my cheeks. "I’ll cook something good this time, I promise."
When he stood up, I raised my arms instead. "Carry me! I wanna see you cook!"
He chuckled again and carried me to the couch in the room, positioned me so I could watch him in the kitchen while comfortably snuggly with some plush pillows and blanket on the couch. Naturally, he did not forget my morning herbal drink...although it wasn’t morning anymore.
"Anyway, do you know how long did we..."
"...three days," he said from the kitchen.
"Oh! Just like our airship adventure!" I giggled behind my mug. I might be sober, but counting the hours and days was not in my repertoire. I didn’t even know how Natha knew what day it was. "So...is this the fourth day?"
"Fifth if we count the day we arrived."
Oh, right--I recalculated again and realized that I must have slept quite a lot after all of those satisfying sex.
"Wow..." I exclaimed and giggled again. We didn’t mean to, but the honeymoon turned out to be filled with wild sex. Although, in the end, we didn’t use any of those wedding gifts.
"I’m...glad...that you seem to enjoy it," he let out a sigh as he approached me with a tray full of glistening roasted poultry with vibrant veggies and fruits and creamy-looking mashed sweet potatoes...
My stomach grumbled again and he put the tray on my lap. Oh--what a treat! There was also a fragrant soup that invited me to slurp it right away. The warmth coated my stomach further and I sighed in satisfaction. He didn’t lie--it was better than the last one already.
"When did you wake up? Seems like you’ve been preparing this for a long time."
"A few hours ago," he said while stroking my bulging cheeks filled with the roasted poultry he spoon-feed me. I wondered how many hours of that he spent in silence while cursing himself before finally tidying up the house and starting cooking in distress.
Oh, my poor husband.
I pinched his cheeks and told him to eat too. After making sure he ate some, I finally asked what I had been curious about before. "Nat, do you...remember everything?"
He paused and pressed his lips, before shaking his head. "Only what happened at the beginning..."
Ah, figures. If he remembered, he would remember me being completely ecstatic throughout everything, and even begging him to not stop. I guessed he only moved by his instinct from then on.
"Too bad..." I muttered. "It was quite nice."
"How could it..." he stopped and took a deep breath before exhaling it slowly and shook his head. I held my laugh and shoved more food into his mouth. "That’s not how I want our honeymoon to be," he said after swallowing what I gave him. "I can’t believe we lost four days just like that..."
It wasn’t a loss for me, but I guessed I shouldn’t say it. "We still have three days, no? What do you want to do anyway?"
"Cosplaying as normal newlyweds?" he said while glancing around with a wry smile. Oh, right--we did want to feel how it would be like if we lived in a house with only the two of us. "I want to take you around the Islands, to the waterfall and the cave behind it--I know you’d like that."
I perked up immediately. I did like the sound of that!
"Also...I was planning to bring you underwater and--"
"Let’s do it!" I almost slammed my palms against the tray. "We should totally do it! You promised me!"
"Sweetheart, we’re just--"
"So? I can still totally do it! I want to do it!"
This was what a honeymoon was for! Right? Right?
He looked at me wordlessly for a few seconds before laughing into his palm. "Ahh..." he sighed and rubbed my wrists to calm me down. "I know, sweetheart, but..." he suddenly looked rather embarrassed. "
I
am the one who needs a little break."
...oh. I giggled and returned to my meal.

chapters.title: Chapter 468: of course, it’s always a good moment to discuss about your future child
chapters.content:
Chapter 468: of course, it’s always a good moment to discuss about your future child
"Hehe..."
I covered my mouth without succeeding in stopping the giggle that had been coming out every time the memory of those wonderful three days was replaying randomly. Three days of Natha taking control and doing everything I wanted him to do to me before I even needed to ask...
Aaah...superb!
"I don’t know what to feel about that giggle of yours," Natha laughed as he led me by my other hand.
"Why? I feel good," I laughed and hugged his arm. "Or are you disappointed that you can’t remember it?"
"Hmm...kind of," he chuckled. "Three days went just like that, without me remembering, even though this is a precious time when we can be together without anyone around. It’s kind of unfair, don’t you think?"
I bit my lips and glanced up, whispering as if someone could hear us. "Should we...prolong it?"
Natha curled his lips and shrugged. "I don’t mind, but your child would."
Oh...right--already I could picture Jade wailing and screaming ’Papa! Papa!’ and throwing a tantrum in the Lair. Zia and Angwi would have a hard time calming the little bird if we stretched it for more than a day.
Besides, I couldn’t possibly ask for the Lord to be away for more than a week, right? Not to mention, he had also taken himself out of work since the day of the wedding, so...
Regrettably, we still had to come back the day after tomorrow.
Oh, well. Better used the time we still had, then!
Which was why we were walking through the woods in the evening. The sky had darkened after I finished a long hot bath while being pampered by an endlessly-feeling-guilty Natha. But that did not stop me from the desire to explore the island.
I mean...into the dark woods with just the two of us? Surrounded by fireflies and glowing moss flanking our path? Sticking close together with a warm glowing lantern in his hand?
What could be more romantic than that?
Okay, there are a lot more, but still...
"Is there a ghost here?" I whispered while looking around the dark forest. But honestly, even the dark forest here looked gentler than the forest around the Lair on a sunny day.
"Do you wish there will be?" Natha chuckled.
"It’ll be a nice story," I giggled. "I can try to scare Jade with it."
"What a bad papa," Natha laughed as if he wasn’t the one who teased my little bird the most.
"But Jade is so adorable while being scared," I giggled recalling the chubby cheeks trembling at the beady eyes shaking. It was particularly adorable when Jade tucked its head beneath its wings. It was also cute when Jade frowned and puffed its cheeks in anger...
I gasped and turned my head to look at Natha. "Could it be...did you like teasing Jade so much because of the cute reaction too?"
Natha curled his lips as he glanced at me. "I like your reaction too."
"Hey!"
The empty path was filled with his laughter as we continued our journey through the woods, toward the sound of water further down the road. The dense trees prohibited me from seeing a glimpse of the waterfall, but I could hear it loud and clear, getting louder the more we walked.
Finally, after walking in the dark for about fifteen minutes, we freed ourselves from it. Unfortunately, there were no ghosts, just fireflies following us to the waterfall like intrigued observers. But wow--what a waterfall!
"It’s huge! It’s bigger than the one in the druid settlement!"
And it was tall too! Too bad that the trees around our cabin were also tall, so I couldn’t see the waterfall from there. But I guessed there was beauty in having such scenery hidden, because otherwise, I wouldn’t bring my lazy ass all the way here, just enjoying the view from the patio.
"It’s a nice waterfall during the day, but it’s even better at night, in my opinion," Natha said as we approached the lake. It was so clear that I could see the bottom of the lake, where colorful stones covered the ground. Each stone was shining with different colors and made the lake look like it was made of rainbow. "The stones absorbed the sunlight by the day and reflect it by the night."
"Whoa..."
Truly, there was nothing I could say but ’whoa’. It looked like colorful lamps were lighting up beneath the water’s surface, and it was just...magical. The lake was shallow enough for me to put my arm inside and pick up a glowing stone. The stone, however, stopped glowing and became a regular red-colored stone once I took it out of the water.
"It only glows when in contact with water," Natha explained. "I’m intrigued to take it back for the pond, but I reckoned it will take away the magic of this place."
"Yeah," I nodded and carefully put the stone back where it belonged. "Let’s not disturb the place. We can just come back here in the future with Jade and the others."
"Others?" Natha raised his brow. "Should I build a resort or something here?"
"Hehe..." I grinned and fiddled with his fingers. "Maybe just a few more cabins?"
He leaned down and bit my cheek in response, making me shriek in reflex. As revenge, I had to chase him through the shallow lake to pinch his cheeks back--which took time since I had to roll my pants first. I managed to catch him halfway through the lake, and at that point, the stray splash from the waterfall had reached us.
With a laugh, Natha carried me and summoned his wings to cover us like an umbrella. He trudged through the lake and accessed a hidden passage by the side of the waterfall to slip behind the curtain of water. For a while, I could only hear the thundering sound of the waterfall as I clung to Natha and ducked behind his wings. When the wings fluttered open, I was greeted by the dark interior of a cave.
"Whoaa...it’s like my dream adventure!"
I couldn’t help but exclaim as I looked at the dark cave with an unknown end and the sparkling curtain of water at the entrance. Natha snapped his fingers to conjure a floating light so we could see the cave better.
"Do you know where it leads to?"
"The other side of the island. We can explore it tomorrow if you--"
"Why tomorrow?" I tilted my head. "It’s dark anyway, so wouldn’t it be better to explore it while it’s also dark outside? I don’t really want to spend time inside a dark cave during the day when I can enjoy the beach instead."
Natha blinked for a few seconds before laughing. He bent his waist in a polite bow and gestured toward the cave. "After you, Young Master."
* * *
"Is there something like a haunted house challenge or night courage test here?" I asked as we traveled through the narrow cave. The place was a bit humid, perhaps because it was placed near water, but pretty empty.
"I’m not sure since I never played with other kids," Natha shrugged. Well...same. "I think rather than ghosts, kids do this kind of thing for some athletic challenges--like seeing who is faster going back and forth, or who can go through a foggy forest without getting lost."
Ugh--where’s the romance in that?! The act of getting closer with your partners as you went through a scary experience and seeking courage in each other?
"I think parent’s expectations were scarier than any ghost," Natha said nonchalantly.
"Wow..."
This demon also had no romance.
"Also, there are more dangerous creatures in this world than a cursed spirit," he shrugged.
"Oh, right..." I nodded in agreement. Hell--even other demons and other races were more dangerous than a ghost...I think. Suddenly, something came to my mind and I gasped. "Is Valmeier’s grandfather considered a cursed spirit?"
"More like...cursing spirit?"
"Pfff--"
Our laugh echoed in the cave and I flinched for a bit when I heard my own voice. It made us laugh again and the sound kept echoing endlessly for quite some time. Pfft--it could be fun too, this stuff, even without ghosts and such.
The path, I realized, was going uphill gradually. Natha said that the exit was located on the other side of the island, but it didn’t seem to be anywhere near the beach. In fact, when I asked, there was no beach on the other side of the island, just cliffside and jagged rocks. Our cabin was facing the only beach, probably for security reasons.
After the uphill journey, we took while talking about our colorless childhood, I could see the shine of moonlight from the exit. The cloudless sky and the spread of millions of stars felt like a reward that welcomed us to the surface.
We climbed out of the cave’s mouth, which was nestled between rocks and ivies, and laid down on the grass in front of the cave while looking at the spread of glittering carpet above us in wonder. Were they stars millions of years ago, or were they the swimming souls waiting for reincarnation?
"Nat..."
"Hmm?"
"I want Shwa to have a different childhood than us," I gripped the hem of my tunic and started to fiddle with it.
I could feel Natha raised his upper body and looking at me. His cold hand covered my fiddling fingers and held me tight, stopping my tremble and calming my strong emotions. Only then did I realize that I was rather agitated, perhaps because I remembered the feeling of emptiness inside that darkness; the loneliness.
"I...I want Shwa to play with other children, experience the life of a loving family, and go through as many adventures as Shwa wants," I took a deep breath and looked at the pair of steady moonlight. "I don’t care who Shwa was, I don’t care what fate Shwa is going to be tied to in the future, but I want a safe and healthy childhood for my child."
Natha smiled and leaned down to kiss me. "Our child," he whispered against my lips and rubbed my hand assuringly. "And I’ll make sure we do just that."
Yes--I pulled him for another kiss, feeling the relief spreading all over my tensed body. Shwa was our child above everything else, and that was the only thing that mattered.

chapters.title: Chapter 469: There’s a plus and minus of having an older partner
chapters.content:
Chapter 469: There’s a plus and minus of having an older partner
After spending the night talking about Shwa, I got a bit homesick for missing my children back home and cried a bit before sleeping. That didn’t make me want to go back the next day, though.
Not with the blue sky and warm sunlight showering me as I lay on the patio listening to the sound of trickling water and chirping birds while my husband cooked me some breakfast. Nuh-uh. I’d stay for a bit longer in this quiet paradise.
"Isn’t it funny? We’ve been here for five days, but this is the first time we enjoy the morning scenery..." I giggled while looking at the swaying leaves above me.
"Sorry about that," Natha’s reply came with a waft of sweetness coming from the plates in his hand.
"I didn’t blame you," I raised my upper body so I could sit and receive the plate, which got me gasping. "You made a pancake!"
Might sound dramatic, but there was no pancake in Demon Realm’s breakfast--especially the one with a drizzle of syrup. Sweets for breakfast? Nuh-uh--not in Natha’s watch. The only sweets he allowed during breakfast came from the fruit. Huff--this old-fashioned Demon.
But what is this? What. Iz. Deez??
"Tried to make it with egg whites," he said, generously putting a small pot of fragrant syrup in my hand. Wow...even allowing me to put as much as I wanted? I see that he still felt guilty even now.
Well--I wouldn’t say no to this.
I drizzled the syrup on top of the thick, fluffy pancakes before he could change his mind. For the same reason, I immediately took a bite of it. My eyes widened as if I had just gulped a tankard of coffee, and I looked at Natha with sparkling eyes.
It was
sooo
good! So soft and fluffy and just the right amount of sweetness. I had no idea what kind of syrup it was, but it smelt so good--like flowers and fruits.
I couldn’t even tell him how good it was because I kept shoving the pancakes inside my mouth without any rest. That was how soft and fluffy it was--I could eat it all without needing to drink in the middle.
"I’m glad you like it," Natha chuckled while stroking my bulging cheek. "But it slower, sweetheart...I don’t want you to choke. No one is going to steal it for you."
But you might change your mind and decide it wasn’t healthy for me to eat a lot of flour in the morning.
I didn’t voice it, but perhaps he understood from my gaze, because he told me right away. "I told you that you can eat whatever you want after the wedding, didn’t I?"
"Oh," I swallowed the pancake in my mouth. "You really want to plump me up..."
He smiled sweetly while putting another pancake on my plate. My eyes narrowed and I whispered in a low voice.
"Are you going to eat me later, my Lord?"
"Oh," he raised his brow and bit my cheek lightly, before whispering to my ear. "How do you know?"
* * *
No, he did not eat me...yet.
He took me to the beach, which was as lovely as everything we had seen on this island. A soft, white sandy beach that was perfectly warm instead of scalding hot. When we arrived, the wave was just a shy rolling thing away from the beach--very tame, very much calling me to run along its side.
The last time I went to the beach was when I was a little kid, before my body couldn’t take any more mana deficiency and had to be hospitalized. It was such a faraway memory that I hardly remember it anymore. I didn’t even remember who I was going with--probably a family vacation.
I was glad that my first time visiting the beach in my adult--and second--life was with the love of my life; not just my lover, but my husband.
Athough the first thing I did was run from that husband. More precisely, I instantly ran toward the beach and the moment it was in my eyes. Leaving my footwear behind on the side of the woods, I ran with raised arms and screamed like Jade flying all over the realm of nature.
"Wheeee!" I laughed and screamed and flinched when the wave hit my ankle, wetting the pants I had yet to roll.
But you know what was the best thing about having a private island?
No one would care even if you get wet from head to toe! No one would even care if you went around naked!
I didn’t bother to roll my pants or take off my clothes. Didn’t bother to tie my hair too, just let the seawater spray all over my face. The water was warm and comfortable to touch, and I was contemplating having a dip when a pair of contrasting cold arms caught me and carried me high, right before a particularly big wave hit us.
The saltwater sprayed hard into my face and entered my mouth, and I caught between laughing and coughing in Natha’s arms. "Pfft--ahaha! Aaagh!"
Wave after wave was crashing into us strongly, and I got drenched quickly, until my hair could no longer swaying in the wind. Even while being held tightly by Natha, and in a higher position from being carried, I still got blasted from head to toe. Of course, Natha got even more drenched than me.
But damn...why did he even look sexier getting wet like this? His wet hair, water dripping through his patterns, and the sculpted body visible from the clinging wet shirt...
How unfair!
"What?" Natha looked up at my pursed lips. "Do you have enough playing with water?"
I grasped his face and kissed him hard. Gods, this beautiful specimen! I kissed and kissed him again. He was mine, uh-huh, he
is
mine.
After that thought, my kiss became more... possessive. And I guessed he knew it, because he started kissing back. The waves kept on crashing and hitting us, but they might as well have been nonexistent because I could only focus on how beautiful my husband was and how nice his kiss felt.
"Natha," I called him between the kisses, between breaths that felt heavier and hotter amidst the chilling breeze. "Natha..."
I wanted to say I loved him, and how I cherished him, and how I would never take him for granted...but all I could utter was his name. Hoping he could understand that much from my stuttering breath, I kissed him with my heart and soul.
Naturally, it did not end with just that.
Naturally, in a place where there were only the two of us, amidst the sand and the rolling waves, we shared silent words of devotion through intimate touches.
This time, he made love to me. In a gentleness that I knew him with, he took his name from my mouth. With all the sobriety and adoration in his eyes. And I loved it. I loved his gentle and soft touch as much as I loved his wild and rough side. I enjoyed the loving caress as much as I enjoyed the possessive clutch.
Because all of that came from him, from the one I loved and promised to be together with forever, until death came to us and took us to be together in another realm, for another adventure.
Of course, a sober Natha was as much fun as the dazed and muddle-head Natha. He made me flustered with all of his sweet words and alluring voice, and took me to plunge under the sea.
Obviously, you didn’t think we did it to scuba dive or something, did you?
Ahem. Anyway--he fulfilled his promise. It was...something. Rather hard doing it while fighting buoyancy, and I felt like we might traumatize a few fish there, but gosh, was it fun! Fun, indeed!
I almost wanted to do it again, but afraid a colony of crabs might get pissed and decided to snip-snip.
The thought itself stayed with me until night, however, that I still giggled after I was snuggly tucked beneath the blanket before we went to sleep. "It’s more fun than I expected," I told Natha when he asked me why I couldn’t stop giggling.
"Is that so? What did you originally expect anyway?" he asked while patting me like usual.
I blinked and, thinking back, started to get bashful. "Umm..."
"Except sex," he added with curling lips.
"Uhh...umm..." I bit my lips as I tried to recall stuff. "Err...you...cooking?"
His brow arched. "That’s it?"
"W-well...I don’t have much experience with this, okay?" I pulled the blanket up to cover my lower face. "A-and...it’s because everyone kept talking about t-that!"
Unconsciously, I glanced at the bedside table and the unused stuff inside the drawer. Natha held my cheek and turned my face back toward him. "Well, well...I know my pretty husband has a huge appetite," he strokes my lips provocatively. "But I came to understand that he also became even more of a pervert lately."
N-no need to out me like that, okay?! Besides...
"W-what’s wrong with being a pervert with my own h-husband?!"
His lips stretched wider. "Nothing, nothing at all," the silver eyes curled gleefully. He leaned down and I thought he would kiss me, but he whispered into my ear instead--which was kind of better. "We still have time to utilize everything in that drawer."
I perked up. "Really?"
"Sure."
"Now?"
He blinked and laughed against my shoulder, before sighing long. "No, sweetheart. Give mercy to my back, will you?"
...oops. Well, sorry Old Man.

chapters.title: Chapter 470: Know your enemies so you can avoid them
chapters.content:
Chapter 470: Know your enemies so you can avoid them
Like everything good in this world, this private vacation too, had to come to an end.
After spending the last day doing some adventure--and by that, I meant exploring the island too, not just...ahem, playing with stuff--we finally bid our little nice cabin goodbye. This time, I managed to do what I was meant to do before--tidying up the cabin while Natha cooked.
Another list of my ’married life’ had been crossed!
Granted, it was only two times, but...I still did it! Yay! Because, you know...there was no way I could do this in a place with dozens of servants tending to me, right? They would be horrified if I started doing something, even just preparing my own clothes, thinking that I was not satisfied with their service. I once decided to bring some books from the library by myself, and the servants were crying, asking if I was going to sack them since I didn’t call them for help...
Anyway, I did everything I wanted to do and then more. I got to spend time with Natha the whole day--the whole week! Which had never happened before. Even while living together, we had our own activities; Natha with his work, and me with...whatever I had in hand. And once we returned, we’d be back to do our own thing, so...I didn’t think we would have another time when we could be together all the time like this.
Right. That was what a honeymoon was for, right? To give time for us to be together before they started our life as a...ahem, m-married couple?
"It’s kind of sad..." I muttered as we gazed upon the cabin one last time. The lantern had been snuffed, the curtains were drawn.
It was time to say goodbye.
"We’ll come here again some weekend if you want to get away," Natha stroked my shoulder in consolation. "Now, shall we go?"
"Mm...alright," I nodded and turned to hug him. Half so I wouldn’t need to look at the house, and half because we needed to teleport.
The usual black wings enveloped us, and I closed my eyes to wait until we arrived.
And I knew we arrived because I immediately heard a loud chirping. [Papaaaaaa!]
Even before the black wings completely uncovered me, the bundle of colorful feathers already tackled my chest. [Papa! Papa! Papa!] The loud chirp filled the entire courtyard, enough to make bystander stop.
Well, they also stopped to bow and greet the Lord, so...
[Papa so looong! Jade miss Papa so much!] big drops of tears falling from the beady eyes along the chubby cheeks.
Ah...if we truly prolonged our stay for another day--or days--I could already imagine the extent of chaos that would befall the Castle. But gosh--my child was so adorable too! I hugged Jade tightly and patted the green head. "Oh, I missed you too, baby!"
[Papa...] Jade rubbed its chubby cheek against mine, but quickly turned toward Natha. [Nightmare, give Jade a yummy stone! Hurry!]
"We’re just back and you already extorting me?" Natha chuckled.
[But Nightmare promise Jade!]
I could only raise my brow as an unknown transaction happened in front of me. Natha conjured up a high-quality elemental stone out of nowhere and threw it in the air, which swiftly caught by Jade’s beak.
Well, there was only one reason why Jade would want an elemental stone right away--he wanted to transform. He could just ask me for some energy, but I guessed it would take too long, or...
Oh--was Jade thinking I might be too tired from the journey?
Aww...
I watched with glazed eyes as my little bird transformed into a little boy, who immediately jumped into my arms again. "Papa!"
"My baby!"
Ahh, this Jade is easier to hug--although so much heavier. I carried him all the way to the Lord’s quarters while he clung to me like a koala and buried his face in my neck, rubbing his face there. Oh, it seemed that I missed this child more than I thought because even after we arrived, I didn’t want to let go of Jade.
"Hmm..." Ignis muttered quietly and patted me with its tail as a greeting before crawling away inside the fireplace.
Natha ruffled mine and Jade’s hair--seemed like he was already expecting that I would immediately get snatched from him. "Let’s have afternoon tea and some sweets."
Jade gasped and lifted his face from my neck. "Candy for Jade too?"
"Sure."
Again, Jade gasped. "Why Nightmare so nice today?"
"What do you think?"
The green eyes narrowed in deep thought. "...Nightmare is happy?"
"Good boy," Natha smiled and ruffled the green head again before walking away, making Jade watch him with a blank, surprised look.
"...oh," adorably, Jade retreated to my neck, hiding his bashful face behind my hair.
Oh, how cute. It was so rare to see Jade getting flustered by Natha like this. I patted the green head while wondering how adorable it would be to see Natha and Shwa together...
* * *
Just like the process of my move to the Lair, the process of moving back to the Castle was easy; all I needed was to move my books and stationery.
Clothes? I had more clothes than before in my Castle closet...for some reason. Jade’s room had also gotten wider--even wider than the one in the Lair, because this one also had a walk-in closet full of children’s clothes and all kinds of accessories from shoes to hats and gloves.
Was this...the ’bribe’ Natha promised Jade? Aside from the elemental stones, I mean.
Phew.
Ignis, however, chose to stay in the Lair as I had thought. After all, its nest was over there. Well, unlike Jade or Vrida, Ignis was never the clingy type anyway. Our independent Salamander only came out whenever it wanted, but it also would appear whenever I summoned it. No biggie.
Vrida, naturally, moved back to the Castle. I had asked her if she would prefer to stay in the Lair, but the wyvern did not want to be too far away from me. Oh, well...as long as I took Vrida to fly a lot, she should be fine.
The most complicated thing about the move this time was...yep--the gifts.
More gifts still came after the wedding; some even came from those who had given me one before. Seemed like they felt their gifts were inadequate after attending the reception, so they sent ’additional’ gifts. Thankfully, I didn’t need to send them thank-you notes--there was no such culture here, apparently.
Not that I didn’t want to do it, but do you have any idea how many gifts came? Hundreds! Thousands!
At any rate, managing the storage for those gifts was dizzying. It occupied my first few days of getting back to the Castle. Of course, all I had to do was merely decide which stuff to put in which room or which cupboard, but still...
Sometimes...having too many things was not a good thing, folks. I shall live in moderation if I could, but alas--I was the spouse of the Lord of Greed.
Ah, aside from the gifts, there was also a stack...of chests, filled with correspondence. For some reason, people wanted to talk to me, building some connection.
Why? Did they think they could butter their way up to Natha through me?
"Of course," Arta, who had seemed to be my caretaker more than taking care of the Castle’s logistics these days, told me in her confident voice. "Everyone with functioning eyes would be able to see how much His Lordship adores you--be it at the parade, or the banquet, or the soiree."
"R-really?"
Phew--why was the room getting hot all of a sudden?
"No--at this point, everyone with functioning ears would have already heard about it too from those who saw it with their own eyes," Arta wiggled her fingers. "They knew His Lordship has a
veeeery
soft spot for you, and would probably grant everything you ask him for."
I...didn’t think that was true. I mean...I still danced around him every time I wanted to make a request.
"Anyway, with that assumption, of course, people would try to curry favor with you," Arta shrugged. "They thought if they asked for something through you, His Lordship might be generous and grant it."
"But even if they don’t ask you, just maintaining a good relationship with you will become a plus when facing His Lordship," Lesta added.
I turned toward him and tilted my head. "When did you come?"
I found out that Lesta finally moved to live together with Eruha in that mansion opposite the house where Great-Aunt stayed that one night. So now, instead of during breakfast, I saw him later in the day.
"Just now," he shrugged. "Anyway; that’s why from now on, you should learn more about politics, Young Master."
"
Eeeeh
? But..."
"No, no--not to jump into politics," Lesta shook his head and grinned. "It’s to know how to avoid it altogether."
I clapped my hands. "A-ha! So it was like studying about scams so we wouldn’t get scammed?"
"Precisely."
Thus, my life in the Castle began by studying how to avoid getting dragged into a court drama.

chapters.title: Chapter 471: It’s something you can only do when you’re ready
chapters.content:
Chapter 471: It’s something you can only do when you’re ready
Apparently, one of the promises Natha made to Jade was that the little bird--or boy--could sleep with us from time to time--which Jade used a lot at the beginning to make up for the time I was away.
Especially when Jade turned into a boy, because he wanted to sleep hugging me a lot. How could I ever turn down such an adorable request?
It was rather funny, however. Naturally, as both my child and my husband wanted to hug me, I had to sleep in the middle--embracing Jade while Natha hugged me from behind. But, more often than not, I would wake up with Jade sleeping between me and Natha instead.
I wasn’t sure how it came to be, but I could make a guess. As a habit, my body couldn’t help but instinctively look for the familiar coldness from Natha’s skin. Because of that, I would unconsciously turn around to dive into Natha’s arms. And Jade, who had lost my hug, would look for it dazedly and climb over my body to slip between me and Natha.
Et voila!
But do you know what was even cuter? The conversation they had when they woke up before me.
"Nightmare, Nightmare should teach Jade how to make Papa’s drink," I heard Jade whispering carefully, probably so that he wouldn’t wake me up.
Naturally, I pretended to be asleep still.
"Why? You can’t even reach the tabletop," Natha, of course, wouldn’t miss a chance to mess with Jade.
"Jade can! Does Nightmare not know a thing called stool?"
Wow...I left for a week and my kid getting better at countering.
"But it’s my job to prepare his drink--why should I tell you?"
"But Jade want to!" the boy started to get frustrated and raised his voice, but seemed to be immediately covering his mouth, before lowering his volume again. "Nightmare know it’s going to be soon..."
"What is?" Natha sounded amused. "Whisper it to me."
Unfortunately, since I was pretending to be asleep, I couldn’t hear what Jade was telling Natha.
"I see..." Natha sounded strangely accommodating. "Then what should I do on that day, since you will take my job?"
"Umm..." I heard some rustling sounds and Jade’s fidgeting as the boy tried to think. "Uhh...Jade don’t know!"
"That’s unfair..."
"But...but can’t Nightmare think of something? Nightmare is supposed to be smart!"
Oh, wow...did Jase just praise Natha? Probably unconsciously, and just so he could get what he wanted, but still...
"Hmm...this is hard," I could hear the cheekiness in Natha’s voice even with closed eyes. "You should do something for me first, don’t you think? Give and take."
"Give and take?" Jade repeated in confusion. "What Jade should give Nightmare?"
Oh-ho! I was also curious about this--almost made me want to open my eyes and peek at them. But I held back since it might prevent this interesting negotiation from happening.
"Isn’t it time for you to stop calling me with just ’Nightmare’?"
I could feel Jade flinch; his emotion was rushing through our bond, telling me that this child was actually flustered.
"Wh-why?"
Wow, he even stuttered.
"Why not?"
The reply seemed to catch Jade off guard because he actually got silent in stun.
"I’m not the only Nightmare out there, ain’t I? What are you going to do if my great-aunt is here? Are you going to call both of us ’Nightmare’?"
"Uhh...umm..." Jade fidgeted so much I could feel his little feet moving against my arm. "B-but..."
"But?"
Jade swayed harder and I couldn’t help but open my eyes a bit to peek at them. The little boy was shaking his head and covering his face. "N-no! Jade can’t do it!"
This child was growing so panicky that he even forgot to keep his voice low. At this point, I was sure that Natha knew I had woken up, but he acted like he didn’t, tilting his head and pulling Jade toward him instead so he could peel the tiny hands away from the flustered face.
"Why can’t you do it?" Natha asked again, persistently, although he did it in a soft and patient tone.
"Because...because..."
"Because you’re embarrassed?" Natha laughed while patting the green hair. "You look just like your Papa when you do."
Jade gasped and covered his mouth. "Really?"
"What kind of observation is that?" this time, I couldn’t pretend to sleep anymore.
"Papa!" again, Jade gasped and was about to move when Natha caught him and pulled the little boy further away in a tight hold. Naturally, Jade was rebelling. "What is Nightmare doing? Let go of Jade!"
"Nope," the demon’s lips curled into a smirk. "Not before you call me by name."
"No--Papa!"
Uhh...sorry, Jade--but this was rather fun. I did want to hear you call Natha by his name, because...it was funny. I knew very well that Jade liked Natha very much--except for the time Natha was acting annoying by calling him ’brat’--so I knew it wasn’t because Jade didn’t want to. If I had to guess, it was probably because Jade had been too used to calling Natha ’Nightmare’, and it was hard to change the habit.
Although he got used to calling me ’Papa’ so quickly.
"Uhh..." Jade’s lips started to quiver, but Natha was having none of it today.
"Don’t cry," he stroked the bowed lips once. "What is there to cry about? Only a child cries because they want to run away."
I didn’t know if that was the right thing to say in this situation, but apparently, it was effective for Jade. The little boy immediately straightened his back, pressing his lips as if he wanted to prove that he wasn’t a child. "J-Jade...is not...a child."
Natha merely smiled and waited, and so I did the same. We looked at Jade in anticipation, and the little boy fiddled with Natha’s necklace just like I usually did when I was nervous. "Uhh...Na..."
Unconsciously, I held my breath as I waited for that single word, almost as if I was waiting for my child to speak his first word.
"Na...Naih--uhh...Nnnn...Na-tha?"
Oh, gosh--why did I feel so touched? Just look at those softened silver eyes and the sweet smile across Natha’s lips. "That’s not so hard, isn’t it?"
"...’s hard," Jade pursed his lips.
"But you can do it," Natha said it as if Jade was just going through a big hurdle in life, while ruffling the green hair. "Good job."
"Yes, what a good boy," I laughed and reached out my arms to fetch Jade from Natha. "Come here."
"Papa!" Jade ran away from his nightmare and scampered toward me, holding me tight as if worried Natha would snatch him again. "Naih...Natha is a bully!"
Natha just scoffed as he got off the bed, but I could see the palpable glee from the brightness in his eyes when Jade did not revert to call him ’Nightmare’ again.
"But Jade," I caressed the sulking child. "You bullied him too when you refused to call him by his name."
Jade froze and hiccuped, eyes widened in surprise and confusion. "Jade did?"
"Didn’t Ignis tell you?" I tapped his nose. "Name is important."
"...oh!"
"Right?"
Natha chuckled and leaned down to kiss the top of my head, before grabbing the flabbergasted child from my lap. "Let’s go and make your Papa’s morning drink while you contemplate on life."
The stunned little boy got even more stunned, probably didn’t think Natha would pay his side of the bargain right away. Only after they almost reached the bedroom door did Jade stir and speak.
"Natha, Jade is sorry!"
"Mm, accepted. Sorry for calling you a brat too, yeah?"
"Okay!"
Wow...just like that? I could feel my lips stretched wide seeing my two favorite...entities getting along so well first thing in the morning. I doubt it’d stay long, but let’s enjoy things while they last.
I stretched in a good mood and rolled out of bed to get some fresh air from the balcony while they made me a drink. Taking a deep breath, I closed my eyes to savor the warm sunlight and inhaled the scent of life sprouting all over the Castle, hand traveling unconsciously toward the black pendant hanging on my neck.
But as I did, I couldn’t help but see that beautiful scene in my eyes; the curling eyes, the gentle smile, the way his face softened in a different way than the time he looked at me. It made my heart warm, and extremely greedy. And the greediness just kept growing when he came inside, leading Jade carefully as the little boy holding onto a full mug.
"Papa! Jade and Natha make Papa’s drink!"
"Thank you, baby!" I took the mug before it could spill, and gave my sweet child a forehead kiss as a thanks.
Jade giggled and climbed onto my lap after I took a seat and sipped on the nice drink that smelled slightly burnt but still delicious nonetheless. As Natha stroked my cheek absentmindedly while checking on his morning letters, I swallowed my nervousness and spilled my greed.
"Nat," I held the cold hand stroking my cheek and waited until he turned and looked into my eyes before continuing. "Let’s do it," I gripped his hand tightly. "Let’s have Shwa."

chapters.title: Chapter 472: When you want soon but you don’t know by how much
chapters.content:
