"There’s a line a husband should not cross," he said while glancing at my friends, who were tilting their heads at him. "And that includes barging in their spouse’s day out with friends. You won’t be able to gossip about me if I’m there."
Pfft--I couldn’t help but laugh and kiss him some more. "Gosh, I love you so much."
And with that, we left for the Amusement Park. It was an impromptu trip, somewhat, so there was no security protocol in place except for the Lord’s Hound and the Castle’s Chief Guards. Oh, and Arta also came because there was no way she would stay put when we were going to play--although she used ’babysitting Sir Jade’ as a justification to come.
Well, since Natha would not let me carry Jade around anyway...
That being said, the Castle staff had already come earlier to give an announcement so the citizens wouldn’t get surprised or crowded me. I doubt they would do that with Caba and Haikal flanking us, but it was nice to know we could play with ease.
"Whoaa..."
Zarfa and Aina, disguised as unknown high-class demon ladies, exclaimed at the view of the rides. Don’t be fooled, though...
"Oh! How to make this going--wait, is this how they function? But can it be done with this composition?"
"Hmm...how much money should I pour to have this at home? Ah, I should consider the patent cost too--wait, would it be better to just treat this like a franchise? Maybe I could just pay for the operating license and let Doc’s company do the rest..."
Yeah...they were more excited about the tech and the economic aspect of the place, even though they were the ones who said
play, play play
earlier. Their
ooh
and
ahh
only lasted a second before they started muttering business. I knew they were already familiar with the concept, but still...
Jade and Arta blinked in confusion, and I just sighed before clasping my hands loudly. "Hey, you told me you want to play!"
"Oops!" Zarfa giggled and hugged my arm apologetically. "Sorry, sorry--it’s a habit. It’s that...what’s that called again?"
"Occupational hazard," Aina replied, still making notes in her little book.
Zarfa snapped her fingers. "That!"
"So, are you going to do market research or play?"
"Why not both?" Zarfa laughed and after dragging Aina, we joined the queue for the rollercoaster.
The staff and other citizens told us to go ahead, but I vehemently refused and chose to get in the queue. While they were looking at us in admiration, my decision had nothing to do with being a good citizen or giving a good example. I was just...simply wanted to be in a queue.
I mean...when I came here for the first time, the place was practically open only to me. Be it the rides or the food stall, I would always be the priority. That was wonderful and all, but I also wanted the experience of a regular visitor. Queuing with friends wasn’t something I could experienced in my previous life, after all.
Zarfa hugged my arm and whispered. "Another one on your bucket list?"
"Mm," I nodded, a big smile dancing on my lips. "It’s no longer a bucket list though."
"Oh?"
"It’s just a list of something I’ll definitely do in this life."
She laughed and nodded in agreement. This life--yes, this time, we would live for a long, long time.
* * *
Going on a ride after luncheon, turned out, was a bad idea. We gave up after two rides and ended up leaning against each other on a picnic blanket in the big garden inside the amusement park, sipping on a mulled wine to chase away the nausea.
"Ugh...I kind of forget I used to avoid spinning rides..." Zarfa groaned.
"Shouldn’t...ate all those meats..."
I fared much better thanks to my natural rejuvenation--which was slower than usual, but still helped me a lot. So I could at least laugh it off. "It’s also nice just sitting like this watching people going around."
"You did enjoy people-watching," Zarfa chuckled while patting my head.
Well, it was the only thing I could do from my hospital room’s window. I used to imagine where those people came from, or what were they doing before coming to the hospital. When Ceci joined me, we would act like those detectives on television shows and make all kinds of silly deductions.
This time too, I watched the demons going around the park happily with their friends and family. Winter did not deter them from going out and playing, thanks to the temperature control magic put inside the park. Snow would fall on the city, but not around this park.
Was that why the place was even more popular in winter? Most tourist sites were closed in this session after all.
Seeing the big smiles on the visitors’ faces put a smile on mine too. There was something gratifying to know a place built for me brought happiness to a lot of people. It felt way better than having the whole place for myself as Natha initially offered.
The garden, which was provided for the visitors to rest like we did, was also filled with picnic blankets. Most of them were families; parents and their excited children. A small playground in the center became a melting pot for those children, including Jade, who had no concept of nausea like us.
"One day..." I muttered softly to no one, but Zarfa hugged me from the side and grinned.
"Well, one will be here shortly anyway," she poked my cheek. "You’ll be able to come in a few years, won’t you?"
"Yeah," I pressed my lips to avoid grinning widely like a fool.
But I couldn’t help the image that came automatically. I saw us in the park, having a family picnic. I saw us walking on the pavement, being dragged by Shwa from ride to ride. I saw Natha with a cute animal headband around his horns and two cotton candies in his hands for Shwa and Jade.
It was a blissful scene I couldn’t even dare to imagine in my past life. I didn’t even have the confidence of living past adulthood, so how could I dare to imagine having a family?
But hiding beneath the blissful feeling was an inevitable insecurity.
"Honestly, I don’t know if I can be a good parent," I said quietly. "You know my family’s circumstances."
"Hmm...because you don’t have good parents?" Zarfa leaned her head on my shoulder. I just shrugged weakly and she held my arm slightly tighter. "Personally, I don’t think you need to have good parents to be one, and some people still turn out to be bad parents even though they have good parents."
"...you think so?"
Zharfa shrugged. "I mean...my parents were good parents for me, even though my big family was crap."
Ah, she was talking about her previous life too.
"But...do you think I’ll be a good one?" I bit my lips.
"I think so," she raised her head and poked my cheek. "Because you’re a good person."
"That doesn’t mean--"
"No," Zarfa let go of my arm and shook her head, but there was still a confident smile on her face. "But a good person will at least try to be a good parent--at least, that’s what I think."
She squeezed my cheeks and chuckled when I just blinked slowly at her. "And I know very well you will try your best, seeing how you’re already worrying about it like this. Besides," she glanced at the playground, where Jade was climbing on a large swing with four other children. "You’re already rising one well."
"And you won’t do it alone, will you?" Aina chimed in from my other side. "You will have a lot of people to ask advice from, and more importantly..."
"You have that dear husband of yours~"
Suddenly, the conversation shifted and they started to tease me about Natha and whatnot, but that was fine. It was a cheap price for the confidence I gained when we returned to the Lord Castle.

chapters.title: Chapter 567: It’s easier to endure something when you know there’s a reward in the end
chapters.content:
Chapter 567: It’s easier to endure something when you know there’s a reward in the end
"You should tell me when the baby comes, okay?" Zarfa gripped my hands tightly when it was time for them to return to the Human Realm.
"Okay, okay~" I replied lightheartedly, but she tightened her grip and stared me down.
"Promise me!"
"Promise!"
I replied loudly in reflex as if a drill sergeant was talking to me. Or was it the head nurse? Ugh...
But Zarfa smiled sweetly and nodded in satisfaction as if she hadn’t just given me a mean glare a few seconds ago. "Good, good--just let me know through your husband’s staff over there, ’kay?"
I laughed and hugged her for one last time. "Alright, Aunty~"
She held me tight and whispered. "What about the templars?"
On our way back from the amusement park, the two of them told me briefly about their mission in that accursed kingdom. Jade had fallen asleep from exhausted playtime, but even then, the two didn’t seem too keen on sharing too much. Not out of secrecy, but because it was very uncomfortable.
I understood though--the biggest victims of the kingdom were, after all, girls. Those bastards were targeting virgins, so they deliberately looked for young girls because they were less likely to be ’tainted’ already. Utterly disgusting.
They did not say it outright, but I had a feeling that their ’vacation’ here was their way of forgetting the awful experience while rescuing those girls. The details were heavily omitted, but it seemed they found a mountain of bones beneath the church where they did the blasphemous act of extracting mana.
Aina and Zarfa weren’t exactly in the frontline, because they were more of a supporter rather than warriors, but even what they heard was enough to anger them. What surprised me was how they also sounded angry toward the templars.
I don’t trust them. They wait so long for the ’hero’ to come before doing anything.
Zarfa thought that it wasn’t like they became invincible with Jin’s presence; they just became slightly stronger and thanks to her, well-funded. They said they were bidding their time, but Zarfa felt like they were just cowardly sitting around until the ’goddess’s messenger’ came to the rescue.
They probably wanted someone to shoulder the blame if something went wrong with the operation.
Of course, everything was just her conjecture, but I had no reason to refute it since I wasn’t personally there. There might be a lot of bias there, but why would I defend them anyway? Zarfa just wanted to believe that a lot of girls might have been saved if the templars made a move earlier. Then, the Hero and his companions would have made a move much faster. After all, the only reason they knew about what happened there was because of Zarfa’s ’vision’ from her previous life.
Well, I could feel her sentiment, so...what should I do with those templars? They said I could only learn about Valmeier’s parents if I visited the church myself.
"I’m not sure," I told her. "Truthfully, I don’t want to have any distractions right now."
Shwa would always be my priority, especially when it was less than a month before the birth. I couldn’t say it out loud, but honestly...I had no attachment to Valmeier’s parents. They were not mine, and I didn’t even have an attachment to mine. I also knew Valmeier considered the old priest as his parent more than anyone, so I didn’t really have any motivation.
Still...
"Perhaps later," I muttered hesitatingly. "Once we don’t have anything to worry about."
At least, I should do that much for Valmeier’s sake.
"Okay, I’ll tell Jin just that," Zarfa nodded. She actually looked relieved that I didn’t show any apparent interest. Ever the protective friend, this one. "Just focus on my nephew for now."
I raised my brow. "It’s suddenly a boy, now?"
"Yep. You can have a girl for the next one."
I didn’t even know if we could have a
next one,
but I still laughed at her confidence. She giggled and took something from her pocket, placing it on my palm.
"Here, Jin told me to return this to you."
I looked at my palm and stared at the small iron plate that functioned as a map to find the church. Well, he wouldn’t need this anymore since they had already found the place.
"Thanks," I nodded and clutched the necklace. While I didn’t have any attachment to Valmeier’s parents, this was still the only link he had to them.
It was a weird concept, but well...the mother was still Grandma’s daughter.
Zarfa took a deep breath and, despite all the laughter we had earlier, looked like she wanted to cry again. Ah...this part of her still did not change even after two lives. She hugged me again, longer this time, and Natha let us have our moment.
I guessed he was over the jealousy period now.
"Be well," she whispered. "Let’s live for a long, long time, okay?"
"Okay," I nodded.
Well, that was always my intention anyway.
* * *
After my human friends left the Castle, we entered a frenzy period of increased security. More soldiers were stationed in and around the forest, and all goods coming to the Castle were under strict scrutiny. Caba even conducted the inspection himself, especially if it was the goods for my needs.
At first, the merchants were panicking, thinking that we received another hint of attack. But this time, the Castle gave a clear explanation right away; that it was just a precautionary measure because the Lord’s child would be born sometime soon.
We weren’t very sure before, since all I had was Lord An’Hyang’s words about how the name of the baby was so fitting. But after the last growth period, I became sure of it. Called it an intuition, since I had no way of explaining it. I just knew.
It would be soon. Soon.
And it was reflected in how greedy my little flower had become, to the point that I needed at least one container per day. Thankfully, my wise husband had stocked up a lot whenever he could, so even if I had to do it daily, we did not run out.
Moreover, Amarein came and added several containers worth of mana to my stock, so I could say my condition was even better than the last time, when I was hovering at the low every day. Also, she would stay in the Castle until the birth, pushing aside all of her priestly duty.
"It’s Mother’s decree," she told us.
This time, Amarein did not come alone. She brought a squadron of druid rangers to help with the security effort. It was immensely helpful since they knew more about the barrier and could communicate with the forest directly.
But that wasn’t all. A group of drow hunters also came from Ahrat, and Issa had sent elven envoys--both for the same reason;
Mother’s decree to keep me and Shwa safe.
Naturally, Natha also recalled most of his best agents back to L’Anaak Eed, while the rest was tasked to report any sign of the first bloom.
Thanks to this, the Castle was rather...packed. It slightly reminded me of our wedding, and for some reason, I felt giddy. The fact that Mother made a move meant she also foresaw that Shwa would be born shortly...right?
Even without the tight scrutiny at the Castle’s gate, people would have questioned the appearance of elves, drows, and druids around the Castle, who actively patrol the estate. Stories were spreading from merchants to merchants, from guilds to stores, and from sellers to buyers.
Soon, it was widely known that we were expecting the birth of a child shortly.
Well, that was what Arta told me. But she also told me that the citizens were excited about the news, which was weird to me.
"...why?"
I mean...I could understand if the culture was to let the child hold the Lord’s title like in a monarchy. But we weren’t like that. Shwa could inherit Natha’s money and become the wealthiest still, but...it wasn’t like he would become a crown prince or anything.
Arta chuckled when I reacted in confusion. "Young Master, it seems like you’re underestimating how much the citizens adore you."
"Huh? But...why?" it only confused me even more. "I don’t think I ever do anything for them."
"You did a lot of things just by existing, Young Master," she laughed. "Ever since you came, His Lordship had gotten even more generous than before. He distributed a lot of aid and relief to celebrate something about you."
"...he did?"
"Even the amusement park was built for you," Arta gave me a wink.
"But wasn’t that all Natha’s doing? It wasn’t like I asked him to do it..."
Arta leaned forward and looked at me keenly. "And whose child is that child?"
"Well, Shwa is our--" I paused when I realized what she wanted to say. "Oh..."
"Right," she pulled back and nodded. "They admired His Lordship and adore you. And now, you will have a child together," she smiled and looked at me with a soft gaze. "I don’t think they are excited about the future Lord or anything, Young Master. They are just happy because it’s a happy occasion for you."
Arta then turned toward a portrait hung on the living room’s wall. Of me and Natha in a matching outfit during our wedding.
"Just like how they are excited about your union, they are excited about the fruit it will bore."
I bit my lips and patted my flaming cheeks. Oh, how blissful it was, to have so many people feeling happy about my happiness. It was weird, a concept I couldn’t imagine existing in my life before.
Once again, I was grateful for enduring everything in my previous life because this reward was so very sweet.
And within these happy moments, a report about the first bloom sighting started to come.

chapters.title: Chapter 568: You should never underestimate childbirth
chapters.content:
Chapter 568: You should never underestimate childbirth
The first report came on the twenty-fourth day of the second month.
"The first bloom had been sighted in Aeraneed."
"Confirmed?" Natha put his utensils down and looked at Opti with utmost seriousness--even more so than the time the Realm of Wrath waged war.
"With the Chief Gardener’s endorsement."
It was the northernmost city of the realm. The second report came the next day, followed by the third and fourth sighting on the twenty-sixth at the same time. By the time the first bloom reached the port city, Natha had ceased all activity to stay in the Lord’s Quarter.
No matter how many times it was, every new report made me flinched in both anxiety and excitement. I didn’t even have the chance to feel guilty about pulling Natha from all his duties or making Malta, Lesta, and Eruha flooded with work.
Thankfully, nothing big was happening outside--nothing that the vassals couldn’t solve. Was it my good karma? Or perhaps Shwa was just a good child. But the situation leading to the birthing time was very smooth. Opti even brought a piece of good news on the morning of the twenty-eighth.
"The war is tipping to Wrath’s side; they managed to seize the fortress and now taking up a defensive stance."
We were all raising our brows around the breakfast table--even Amarein. "Defensive? Wrath?"
Opti grinned and gave me a wink. "They said they’ll hold the advance until the baby’s safely born."
Oh, gosh...did those battle-frenzy warriors really reign in their thirst for revenge for our sake?
"Give them my gratitude," Natha wrote something on the napkin--some numbers--and gave it to Opti. "This much should suffice."
After another wink, the teenage-looking spy dashed out again.
See what I meant by everything seemed to be going smoothly? Still, although we had no idea when the exact date would be, Natha stayed with me all the time. He even stayed with me in the bathroom, saying it might happen there.
How should I say this; he looked more anxious than I was.
Was it because of that? I actually felt rather calm. The anxiety and worry were overshadowed by the excitement and impatience of holding Shwa in my arms. I went to bed wondering if it would be tomorrow, and I spent the regular after-breakfast transfusion time talking to Jade about all kinds of things we would do with the baby.
"Your frown will become permanent at this point," I pressed a finger in the middle of Natha’s brows and giggled. It was tea time on the twenty-ninth, and he had been glancing outside as if he could spot the first bloom of the garden from there.
Well, he might be able to, but there was no guarantee that the first bloom of L’Anaak Eed would start in the Castle. Hell--there was no guarantee that it would happen when the first bloom arrived in L’Anaak Eed. What if it only happened after the whole districts had their first bloom?
After a few days of feeling jittery, I learned to just go with the flow.
Instead of loosening his furrow, he just looked at me up and down. "How are you feeling?"
"Good," I shrugged. "Good enough to not feel lethargic. You were the one who checked on my core an hour ago."
"Anything could happen in an hour," Natha grabbed my hand and checked on my pulse. Again.
Well, I just let him since he looked so endearing. It never felt annoying watching his handsome face hovering with a concerned face around me.
Hmm...pretty privilege even worked on a married couple, huh?
"What about the pendant?"
"I’m wearing it," I pulled the chain of the emergency mana Amarein gave me the last time. "You saw it when you changed my clothes this morning."
"Who knows if it’d fall somewhere in between," Natha grumbled, and I started to see the familiarity between him and Jade.
That boy might have taken after my appearance, but he was definitely taken after Natha somehow in the personality department.
"Do we need to be this concerned? We already prepared a lot of mana containers," I stroked his cheeks to try to calm him down. "It’s not like I have to push the baby out of my womb."
Not like I had one. Logically speaking, Shwa should come out of the flower--like Thumbelina or something. The only thing to be concerned about was probably the mana intake needed for the final push, but we already prepared everything we could; the mana containers, the mana pendant, and eating the mana-rich food diligently all this time. We even had Sada’s pill should something unwanted happen.
"But--"
"I agree--you should calm down, boy," D’Ara came to my support from the couch, sipping on her tea. Natha looked offended, but she added before he could say anything. "I’m not saying you should be less vigilant, but the more you’re worried about the sweetling, the more you should stay calm. What if something really happens and you can’t function because you became too agitated."
Natha’s face tensed up for a second, before he closed his eyes and took a deep breath. He looked at me and pressed his lips on my palm, sliding down to kiss my wrist before taking another deep breath.
"Okay, you’re right..." he exhaled slowly, and I used this rare chance to pat him on the head--which Jade also followed while giggling.
I leaned down and whispered in his ear, hiding my blush from everyone. "I’m happy to see how much you’re worried about me, though."
Finally, Natha let out a soft chuckle--something I realized I hadn’t seen for these past few days. So I added, smiling widely to reflect my blissful state. "But I’m happier seeing your handsome smile--"
I paused. Everything felt frozen around me. The time felt frozen. Or was it me? Was it my heart that stopped working?
My eyes flickered as a cold sensation shot through my spine, and a flame raged in my core. Instinct kicked in and I tried to take a deep breath, but all I heard was a sound of wheezing. Everything felt sluggish, and I gasped in a desperate attempt to suck on air.
"Sweetheart?"
"P-Papa?"
I heard voices; Natha and Jade, D’Ara and Amarein, the servants and the vassals--but everything felt distant, and the once bright afternoon shifted into a dim twilight as if the sun was swallowed by the cloud.
And I fell. My legs trembled so much that I couldn’t stay up, and they kept trembling even when Natha caught me and carried me to the bedroom. I could feel the agitation in his tight hold and the cold seeping out.
"He’s losing mana," someone said--was it Amarein? I could hear them fine, but everything sounded so vague. "The pendant kept him safe for now."
"For now?!"
"The mana flow is very unstable. Let’s proceed with the transfusion as planned."
What happened? Through flickering eyes, I saw Natha pinned my arm down and push a needle into my wrist. Arta and Panne were carrying the preservation chest where the mana containers were. Somewhere outside, Jade’s fearful wail and Lesta’s shooting voice intertwined.
And I was still trembling; seizing.
"Sweetheart...sweetheart, I’m sorry--" Natha’s trembling voice clashed with the sound of my clacking teeth.
Ah, fuck--why couldn’t I stop shaking?
D’Ara pulled my eyelids to keep my eyes open and stared into my soul; my core.
"The baby is coming," she said. "The soul is separating itself from Valen."
Shwa!
Shwa is coming!
Suddenly, nothing registered in my head anymore but Shwa. The cocoon inside my soul was trying to break free. The flower in our garden was trying to bloom for the last time.
All alone.
"Nat!" with an energy I didn’t know I had before, I grabbed Natha’s hand tightly, staring into his silver eyes. "Nat!"
"No."
I looked at his shaking eyes incredulously, continuing what I wanted to say anyway. "Go--go to Shwa. Please!"
"No!" he stood up indignantly, as stubborn as a petulant child. But his fear was seeping out and filled the room with chilling cold. "I am not leaving your side at a time like this!"
"Ra Natha!"
The room went silent at my angry shout. I swallowed the bitter, hot saliva pooling in my mouth and pressed down on the pain spreading through my body. I glared at him and put every bit of strength left in me into my voice.
"Go...to your child! Our child!" my breath was rough at the end of that short demand, so all I could manage afterward was a soft plea. "Please, Nat...please..."
"Natha, you should go," D’Ara held me and placed her hand over my solar plexus, soothing the chaotic flow of mana in my core. "Stabilize the flow of mana from your child’s side."
Natha looked at me with a crestfallen face, but I no longer had any leeway to think about anything but keeping myself conscious. He staggered back and turned around to walk outside, but he returned to the bed right after, almost stumbling into the mattress.
"I’m sorry," he cupped my face with a pair of trembling hands. "I’m sorry..."
I received his kiss and despite urging him to go earlier, held him for a few seconds more.
"I love you," he whispered, with all his love and fear in his eyes.
I swallowed hard and whispered as loud as I could. "I love you too, Nat."
At that moment, I knew that both of us did not want to let each other go. But I pushed him weakly, and he let me go obediently. Natha stood up and shoved a box in D’Ara’s hands, before disappearing quickly before his resolve waned again.
The moment his presence vanished from the room, gone from the Lord’s Quarter, my strength left me. The tenacity I clung to while holding all the pain crumbled, and pain...pain unlike any other blasted through my body as my soul was ripped open.
And I screamed. I screamed and screamed as the sheet was ripped by my clawing hands. I screamed as they tried to pin my struggling limbs down. I screamed like I never screamed before in my life.
Until my airway shut and my breath stopped.

chapters.title: Chapter 569: And thus the Flower blooms
chapters.content:
Chapter 569: And thus the Flower blooms
When the agonizing scream stopped and was replaced by a choking sound, they instantly knew something had gone terribly, terribly wrong.
"Young Master!"
"Valen?" Amarein reached out her trembling hands, but stopped in dread as Valen’s back arched and his body seized. His head stretched back, neck tensed and swollen, as if something was shoved inside his throat. "La-Lady D’Ara!"
"He can’t breathe," the vampire frowned as she held Valen carefully. "Sweetling..."
"My Lady, I don’t think the transfusion can keep up!"
D’Ara clenched her jaw--she knew; she had seen the rapid decrease of Valen’s mana. The flow was so chaotic that it blocked the gates, even hindering the airways. She had to do something, or the sweetling might lose his life. Something that could stabilize the flow of mana and fill the core all at once.
Her gaze fell to the box on the bedside table that her disciple gave her earlier. She put Valen down and took the box. "Sweetling, I’m going to use this."
Opening the box, D’Ara took out a blood-red pill and put it inside Valen’s gasping mouth. She moved her fingers, glowing in soft mana, along Valen’s chin and swollen neck. Following the fingers’ movement, the pill rolled inside Valen’s mouth and down, struggling and pushing through the blockade in his throat. With the help of the vampire’s mana, the pill managed to slip through and enter the lump of energy in Valen’s solar plexus.
There, it dissolved and took over.
"Ugh!!" Valen gasped as his airway was forcibly opened with a blast of energy.
On the other hand, the massive energy accumulated from decades of fermentation spread all over his body, filling the barren circuits with raw unprocessed mana. The core that had to accept the foreign energy jolted, and Valen seized again. Screaming again.
"Nggh!"
"Hang in there, sweetling," D’Ara pressed her palm against Valen’s stomach, guiding the rampaging mana inside, that was fighting between channeling some volume outside and keeping Valen’s alive. "You can do it."
Amid Valen’s painful scream, an anguished wail could be heard from below. A little boy shrieked with so much sorrow that the person holding him could do nothing but hold him tight so he wouldn’t fall down or run upstairs.
Jade, who could clearly sense the dire condition of his father screamed in fear, in despair, clinging to the poor demon patting him patiently. But no amount of soothing whisper could calm the boy who could feel his father’s writhing and ripping soul. All he could do was wail and scream in misery of the pain he could not feel.
Natha would have screamed too had he the chance. The bond was telling him that his beloved was dying, and there was nothing he wanted more in this world than to hold his sweetheart at that moment. But he stumbled inside the shed with tears dripping from his shaken eyes, staggering toward the tensing flower.
Betraying his stature, Natha fell on the wildly swaying grass. As he tried to get up, his eyes fell to the pulsing mark on his finger; the bond between him and his sweetheart. And suddenly, something occurred to him;
If Valen died, he died. So what was there to be afraid of? It would be a pitiful situation for their child, but thinking that he would jump into nothingness together with his beloved calmed him down.
"Haa...Haa..." he regulated his breath as he crawled toward the shuddering flower, wiping the tears wetting his cheeks. "Baby..."
The garden was a chaotic mess of swirling mana storm centered at the lone flower screaming silently. Natha held the flower, embracing it, flowing his own mana to help the little, confused one.
"Baby, your Papa is having a hard time," he whispered softly, sorrowfully. Even if he thought it would be alright to die, he wanted his sweetheart, who hadn’t even enjoyed two years of healthy life, to continue living for a long, long time. "Please, please..."
He held the trembling bud and poured his mana into the tangled mess of mana, forcefully trying to smoothen the flow.
"Let’s not make it hard for your Papa, yeah?"
He pressed his head on the petals, who seemed to be hugging him back anxiously. Ah...this was why Valen told him to be here.
"Is it hard for you, baby? I’m here, I’m here," Natha stroked the flower, enveloping it in his mana. "I’ll help you, alright? I’ll help you, so let’s do this gently."
Gradually, the tangled mess of mana unraveled as he infused more and more mana. The mana the flower absorbed also flew more steadily, and Natha could feel his mark throbbed less intensely than before. The flower, gathering all the mana inside it, tensed up.
"You can do it, baby," Natha whispered soothingly, trying to keep his child as calm as possible. "Our smart baby..."
With both mana and praise pouring into the flower, the petal swayed and bent upward toward the center, as if shielding the bud. The flow of mana suddenly stopped and Natha pulled his hand away, holding his breath as the flower shuddered and tensed.
It stopped moving for a few seconds that felt like hours for Natha, before a burst of energy exploded. The petals trembled for a second more, before falling to the side one by one.
And there, in the middle of it all, wriggling defenselessly, was a vulnerable figure of a baby.
"Uu..."
"...ah..." slowly, fearfully, Natha reached out for the vulnerable curling figure in the middle of the petals.
More beautiful than any flower.
"Uu...uu...waaaaah!"
A heartful cry pierced the garden, and every blossom in the realm bloomed, welcoming the little flower to the world.
* * *
It was dark.
A familiar darkness, and I was running along an invisible path. I ran and ran and ran, excitedly looking for the cocoon that was always there. But no matter how long I ran and how frantic I was searching for it, I couldn’t find the cocoon.
My
cocoon.
As dread and despair started to overcome me, I opened my eyes with a sharp gasp.
"Shwa!"
As if I had been deprived of air my whole life, my body suck on it eagerly. Staring wide-eyed at the ceiling, I gradually registered the presence of other people around me.
"Valen!"
"Young Master!"
Did I lose consciousness? How long had it been?
"Are you okay, sweetling?"
I turned toward the soft voice of D’Ara, who looked at me with unusually soft gaze. "I’m...yes..."
"I used Sada’s pill," she said with a calm tone. Why was she so calm? "I’ll give you one of mine late--"
"Shwa!" my brain finally caught up with what happened and grabbed her arm. "What about Shwa?!"
At my impolite and impatient gesture, D’Ara smiled and held my chin, gently turning my face toward the window, and there I saw--blossoms. Blossoming flowers swaying in the wind. From the bush flanking the path to the orchards on the back. The road was decorated with blooming flowers, and the air was sparkling with fluttering petals, bathed in the golden light of dusk.
The world, which looked dim before, suddenly brightened as if they were cheering up. As if the most wonderful thing had emerged. As if the world was alive once more.
Oh...
Like the petals outside, my heart was fluttering. When I let my senses kick in, I could feel it, clearly, the approaching presence. Two of them.
As if answering the summon of my crying heart, black feathers swirled inside the room before parting slowly like a glistening curtain. Before the wings disappeared fully, I could see it already;
A little bundle lying protected in Natha’s arms.
"Shwa--"
I scrambled forward before Natha even made a step, but D’Ara held me back and whispered soothingly. "Shush, sweetling; they’ll come to you."
As Natha stepped closer to the bed, to me, his footsteps sounded so loud in my ears. I didn’t think I even breathed or blinked, just staring at the small thing bundled in a blanket and Natha’s coat. When Natha arrived in front of the bed, my arms reached out before my brain could give any command, and my breath stuttered the moment the little bundle arrived in my arms.
"Oh..."
The bundle wriggled, and the blanket shifted. Fair and frail, a baby curled while breathing calmly. Dark hair crowned his little head, and faint blue markings decorated his skin. Ah...it’s a baby boy.
"Oh..." I opened my mouth, but nothing could come out but an exclaim. All I could think about was how beautiful he looked. My baby.
Our
baby.
I raised my head to look at Natha, and it was only then did I realized how red his eyes were. So he had been crying, just like me. But underneath those red and swollen eyes was the brightest smile I had ever seen from him.
With arms wrapped around us, his lips whispered against my temple. "Thank you," he closed his eyes and kissed me tenderly. His voice, trembling like our heart, contained an unspeakable love that transcended everything. "Thank you."

chapters.title: Chapter 570: Isn’t it normal for parents to wish their child stay as their child?
chapters.content:
Chapter 570: Isn’t it normal for parents to wish their child stay as their child?
"P-p-papa..."
While we had done crying in the bedroom, Jade was still sobbing when Lesta brought him up. His chest heaved up and down pitifully, but he paused and hiccuped when he saw me--as well as the bundle in my arms.
"Come, baby," I waved my hand as Lesta put him down. "See your little brother."
The green eyes widened as Jade wobbled to the bed. Gripping the sheet with his small hands, the little boy climbed up with Natha’s head, carefully peeking at the small bundle. With a small voice, he called out.
"Shwa?"
As if listening, the baby wriggled slightly inside the blanket, moving his cute little head. Arta and Mara had cleaned him up--even though he wasn’t covered in anything but a bit of pollen--and wrapped him in a soft baby blanket instead of the one Natha used, which was taken from the bed inside the garden.
Perhaps because of that, the baby looked more comfortable and yawned adorably. Natha said Shwa had cried when he ’bloomed’, and some with sharp ears in the Castle had heard it; but the baby was calm and did not even whine ever since. Such a good kid.
Jade gasped at every movement and looked at me with sparkling eyes. "Can Jade touch?"
"Be careful," Natha said while taking Jade’s hand, leading it gently to the pink cheek. "Softly, like you’re holding a crystal glass."
Jade, who had once dropped a crystal glass and received scolding from us, pressed his lips and nodded seriously. His small fingers gently poked the baby’s chubby cheek and held an even smaller fist with another hand in fascination.
"Wow..."
Wow
, indeed. All of the jumbled feelings in my heart could be summed into that one simple word. Just wow. The things I never thought would come true; the miracle that felt like a dream. Everything was safely stored inside the blanket in my arms. I kept staring at his face and refused to let him go except for the time Arta and Mara cleaned him.
Rather than possessiveness, however, it was like...I wanted to make sure it was real, that Shwa was really in my arms, that our baby really had come out into this world. I wanted to make sure it wasn’t a dream or hallucination, and what better way to make sure of it than feeling the warmth and weight in my arms and listening to the little heart beating all the time?
"But..." Jade tilted his head, suddenly jutted out his lower lip in disappointment.
"What’s wrong?"
As we all looked at Jade in confusion, the little boy pursed his lips. "Baby don’t look like Jade or Papa."
I pressed my lips and held my laughter because I didn’t want to shake the baby, but...looking down, I stroked the pink cheeks that shuddered adorably at my touch. Except for the faint blue markings that were definitely Natha’s, the baby had my skin and hair. Also...
The baby’s long eyelashes fluttered, perhaps because of the sound of giggling, and the green eyes blinking in a daze. "Look, he has green eyes like us," I said, which made Jade brighten up.
"But Jade is right," D’Ara chuckled. "Your baby looked like baby Natha."
I perked up and blinked my widened eyes. "Really?"
Not to disappoint Jade, but I really wanted our child to look more like Natha. Not that I was disappointed about him not having blue skin, but...I guessed I just wanted him to have both of our features.
"I’m sure," she tapped her chin in contemplation. "You should ask Nezja about it; she probably still keeps some portraits."
"Oh!"
"Huh...I don’t even have my own child portraits," Natha chuckled and joined me in stroking our baby’s cheeks.
Excitedly, I turned to the side. "Arta!"
"I’ll inform the Lord of Lust of this good news," she smiled widely and skipped out of the room with Lesta.
Right--we also needed to inform Zia about this, and Zarfa too! Amarein appeared in the corner of my vision and--oh, wouldn’t I need to inform the druid too?
I turned to look at Natha, but he stroked the back of my head gently. "Patience," he said. "I’ll arrange to inform who needs to know, but there’s no need to crowd the baby with a lot of people at once."
Oh, that was true. I nodded bashfully, embarrassed for my own hastiness. There were still a lot of things we needed to do regarding Shwa, including setting up security measures and bringing in the nannies. It would be better to only let other people meet Shwa once everything was settled a bit more.
"Papa, this look like Natha too," Jade ran his finger through the baby’s arm; at the blue markings that looked just like the patterns on Natha’s skin.
"Ah, right!" I looked at Natha in confusion. The euphoria made me look away from the problem, but since Jade brought it up, might as well ask about it. "I wanted to ask about this; this couldn’t be alpha seed, right? I mean...Shwa is not a pure-blood."
Surprisingly, D’Ara replied with a nonchalant tone. "Why not?"
"Huh?"
She tilted her head and smirked. "In the first place, this ’seed’ comes from An’Hyang, and where did his power come from?"
"The...Primordial God?"
She snapped her fingers and winked. Sitting on the bed beside Jade, she stroked the baby’s hair. "Rather than as a qualification, however, this is just a seal of his power."
"Oh?" I looked at Natha and we both raised our brows.
"The reason why no mortal can contain the soul and vessel inside their body is because of the enormous power it carries," the vampire explained. "To bring that enormous power into a mortal vessel, it had to be in a sealed state."
The power...of Primordial God? I frowned unconsciously. I was under the impression that my child would be born as a regular child. As a mortal. As
our
child that carried our genes. A child that would play around and learn about this world normally. A child that would study and work hard to get his power in the future.
D’Ara chuckled at my expression and patted my head instead. "Well, it’s not something that could be helped. Compared to the Primordial One’s original power, it wouldn’t even feel like anything," she said. "That being said, whether or not that power will awaken or kept being sealed for eternity will be up to this child."
"Umm...what about...memories?"
"Most of it is gone, but what remains is also sealed somewhere."
My frown went deeper. Not that I wouldn’t stop treating him as my child if he got his original memory, but...what was the point of regressing into a mortal vessel if the memory stayed? Wasn’t it ’memories’ that were burdening the Primordial One in the first place?
D’Ara smiled and gently laid her hand over the baby’s midriff. "The seal is in his soul, and it will be even harder to unlock than the power," she explained more. "I don’t think it will get unlocked unless something shocking happens and it is needed."
"I see..."
"Well, let’s not think about that now," Natha rubbed my shoulder and kissed my temple softly. "Not today--today should be the day of nothing but happiness."
Ah...I looked up and smiled against his jaw. "You’re right."
"Oh!"
I flinched and looked down as Jade, who was still stroking the baby in fascination all this time, suddenly exclaimed. "What’s wrong, Jade?"
Jade rubbed the baby’s head and blinked with wide eyes. "Papa, there’s something here!"
"Huh?"
The little boy moved his hand all over the baby’s head and stopped on the other side. "Oh, here too!"
Curiously, I rubbed the place that Jade touched, a little bit above the baby’s temples and hidden near the hairline. There, easily missed, were two little pointy ’bumps’. I blinked and turned to look at Natha, before coming back to the baby’s ’bumps’.
"This is...horns?"
My baby had horns? Like Natha?
"Oh, my..."
I giggled and held the baby a little bit tighter. Oh, I can’t wait to see what he would look like once he grew up!
* * *
There was only one phrase that could be used to describe the atmosphere around the Castle after all the flowers in the whole realm suddenly bloomed.
Happiness.
The tension that had enveloped them since the last week of the second month had completely shifted, as if spring had come early. But indeed; looking at all those flowers in the garden made them feel like basking in the spring breeze--even if the breeze was colder than usual.
But who cared about the cold breeze when everyone was showered with happiness? The Lord was definitely happy when he gave away bonuses to all of the Castle staff, distributed gifts to the citizens, and donated a lot of funds to the orphanages and shelters.
So, was there any reason for the Castle and the citizens not to feel happy?
There was no official announcement yet from the Lord’s Castle, but rumors had already spread about the anticipated new addition to the Lord’s family. The bards connected the rumors with the sudden mass bloom all over the realm, and made legends out of it. Poems and songs about the early spring filled the taverns and plazas, as the housewives spun romance stories worthy of plays.
Amidst all kinds of happy and fun speculations, several guests arrived at the Castle, both through the front gates and the back gates.

chapters.title: Chapter 571: Only leave your baby with someone you can trust with your life
chapters.content:
Chapter 571: Only leave your baby with someone you can trust with your life
The first ’guest’, if you could call her that, was neither Zia nor Zarfa;
It was Angwi.
It had been weeks since I saw her, and Natha only told me that Angwi was fine; that she ate and drank properly, and that someone always checked in. I was curious, but I refrained from asking what Angwi had been doing to the Spectre, because it felt like peeking into her wound. I had delivered my punishment in that forest, so the rest was for her to own.
This would be the first time we saw each other again after that fateful night in the dungeon.
She came on the second day of the third month, just two days after Shwa’s birth. While the nursery was ready, I still couldn’t let him away from my sight, so we put Shwa in the Master bedroom. One of Zarfa’s gifts was this cute baby carrier that we placed in our bedroom, and it was nice to be used before we moved to the bassinet.
Thanks to my natural rejuvenation and Natha’s constitution, we had no qualms about waking up every few hours to feed the baby with the sap of the Great Tree. While it was called ’sap’ because it came from the tree, it looked just like milk, and was traditionally given to baby druids to enhance nutrition intake. Amarein had generously provided us with several bottles--enough to sustain the baby until we had a wet nurse.
It couldn’t be helped since this conceiving effort did not equip me with breastmilk.
It was during one of these feeding times, sometimes after lunch, that Angwi arrived. She didn’t look any different; still in her maid outfit that was different from the Castle’s staff. Still with a stoic face that softened a little bit as I welcomed her.
"Angwi! Come, come!"
Jade jumped off the couch and grabbed the hesitant demon closer, pulling on one of her six arms. I waved at them and pulled the baby bottle away. Just like when he was still inside the flower and absorbing my mana, he was still a greedy little one when it came to food. Feeding time was always done in a flash, and even after we finished, his little mouth would still pout and make a sucking motion for a while.
It was always fascinating to watch it, and never ceased to make Jade giggle. "Look, look--isn’t baby cute?"
Arta nodded silently, staring at the baby without blinking for a minute, before shifting her gaze to me.
"Me? I’m completely fine now," I told him with a smug grin. "How couldn’t I when my baby’s here now? But...thank you for worrying."
I had no idea if she heard anything about that day, but everyone had been worrying and treated me like I went through a real childbirth. But I felt completely fine--if anything, I was back to my peak now that our little flower had drank milk instead of mana.
Angwi stared into my eyes for a while, probably looking for a sign of weakening or something. But she must have seen that I was healthy, since she nodded in satisfaction and patted my head as if praising me.
While I was giggling bashfully, Jade tugged on the demon’s hand. "Angwi, baby is closing his eyes now, but baby have Jade’s eyes!" the little boy bragged. Probably because it was the only feature that Shwa shared with him. This morning, I heard Jade asking D’Ara if his hair could change color. Cute.
I laughed and nodded enthusiastically. "That’s right! He also has these very cute horns--do you want to touch them?"
Angwi blinked and her fingers twitched. Her hand moved for a few centimeters before two others grabbed it.
My eyes widened in surprise at her hesitation. "What’s wrong?"
What I got, however, was a wordless frown. It was clear that she felt conflicted about something, but I could not yet see what it was about. I wanted to ask, but she didn’t seem ready to share it with me.
In that case, I’d just tell her what I wanted to tell her.
"Angwi," I fixed the baby’s blanket and held Shwa closer to my chest. "Can you be Shwa’s principal nanny?"
After I finished my request, Angwi stood frozen for two seconds before stepping back in shock. I had never seen her eyes widen that much before. It wasn’t just a surprise though; I could also sense dread. Fear. I had felt it so much from Natha yesterday that it became the easiest emotion I could detect.
"Umm...I understand if you don’t want to meet anyone. We’ll also prepare a room just for you, and you can go back to the Lair anytime you want," I added swiftly, waving my hand frantically in the air before fiddling with Shwa’s blanket. "I just...I don’t really trust anyone but you to take care of him."
I wanted to ask her about it once she finished her revenge, but since she was here already, I decided to just ask. Seeing her reaction, however, it seemed like I was being too hasty.
"Uhh...but if you don’t want to--"
Angwi swiftly crouched and grabbed my hand, shaking her head strongly. Rather than surprise and dread, she looked rather...sad. She bit her lips and kept shaking her head, as if disheartened.
"What do you mean you’re unqualified?" I frowned deeply. "You took care of me, you took care of Zia, you took care of Jade. Who else would I trust to take care of my child but you?"
She paused and, after a few seconds, slowly raised her head to look at my eyes. Her eyes were filled with self-doubt, and it broke my heart to see her, who was usually full of assurance and certainty, look like this.
That damn Spectre!
"Of course, I’m sure!" I replied to her wordless concern firmly. She wavered for a bit, but there was still a lot of doubt in her eyes. So I turned toward my trusted ally. "What do you say, Jade?"
"Angwi is the best!"
As expected of my first child. I returned to Angwi and scoffed. "See?"
It might seem like I was forcing her into agreeing, but honestly, if it was because she felt it would be too much of a burden or if she wasn’t comfortable around children, I would have relented. But Angwi was feeling inadequate and doubting herself instead, which I knew surfaced from facing all of her past scars.
In that case, I did not want to give up.
"So, will you do it?"
I looked at her without averting my gaze at all. I wanted her to see how much I trusted her. We had arranged for two nannies and two battle maids to stay by Shwa’s side always, but...truthfully, even if they were chosen from the most trustful source, I was still traumatized by Uncle Sol’s discipline. I wanted someone who I completely trusted, my own people, to be there too.
Perhaps, this fiery spirit and desperation reached out to her since she took a deep breath and finally nodded.
I gasped and looked at Jade with a wide grin, who immediately jumped around us while cheering. "Yasay!"
"Yaay!"
We laughed and hugged Angwi together as I pretended I didn’t see her glistening eyes. I let her go after feeling she took another deep breath, and swayed Shwa gently in my arms. The baby had wriggled and was woken up by the noise. I giggled and tilted my head. "Would you like to hold him?"
Angwi was hesitant at first, but finally nodded and took Shwa, cradling him gently in her arms. She was more proficient than I initially thought, which made me think she had done this before; taking care of babies, I mean.
Well, didn’t matter. I giggled quietly with Jade as we saw the small smile appeared on her lips.
"Oh-ho! So this is where the baby at?"
As we watched Shwa sway back to sleep in Angwi’s arms, the door opened and someone I hadn’t seen in a long time appeared with Natha in tow.
"Ah!"
Ears and tails swaying as she sauntered inside, Rubha gave me a little curtsy. "Good day, Young Master," her eyes and lips curled prettyly. "Ah, Madam Angwi."
Angwi looked at me inquisitively. "Oh, Rubha is--"
"I’m going to be the little prince’s wet nurse," the fox said in a singsong voice.
"Don’t use that term!" I hissed.
She tilted her head. "Wet nurse?"
"No, ’little prince’!" I pursed my lips and crossed my arms. "The druids still use that to call me, so it sounds weird."
She laughed loudly, filling the room with a bell-like sound. "What shall I call the little lord, then?" she walked closer and stopped in front of Angwi. "Little Master?"
Rubha reached out to stroke the baby, but Angwi shifted slightly that her hand missed. I raised my brows in surprise at this sudden display of protectiveness, but Rubha simply retracted her hand with a giggle.
"My, my," she covered her lips and turned around, waving her hand as she went out to go to her own room. "Just give him to me when he’s hungry."
I looked at Natha, who was as surprised as me. But we ended up giggling silently to not disturb Angwi’s effort to put Shwa to sleep again.
That night, with Angwi there, we finally had enough confidence to let Shwa out of our sight. The baby slept in the nursery instead of the Master bedroom, with the troops of nannies waiting upon him at all times.
But I had yet to get used to not having Shwa near me, so I couldn’t help but wake up in the middle of the night when I heard his little cry. Together with Natha, we crept toward the nursery, only to pause in front of the door as the most beautiful voice grazed our ears.
And from the little crack of the door, against the soft light of the mana sconce, I saw my baby swayed gently in the cradle of red arms. The most beautiful lullaby, like a heavenly choir, flew softly from someone who had vowed to never sing again.

chapters.title: Chapter 572: Once you have a child, your friends’ priority is shifted
chapters.content:
Chapter 572: Once you have a child, your friends’ priority is shifted
On the fifth of the third month, a human storm blasted into the nursery.
"My nephew!"
Zarfa, bringing even more gifts than before, burst into the nursery like Jade, even though she was twenty years older than my two-year-old bird. Son. She didn’t care, throwing her arms in the air, running in with sparkling eyes and cheeks flushed from both cold and excitement.
Haa...how could I scold her if she looked that happy about my child?
Thankfully, Shwa was a calm and gentle boy; he didn’t cry from loud noises, although he would throw a tantrum if we didn’t feed him on time. This greedy little boy.
Or perhaps he realized that his blanket, the neatly arranged toys, the clothes he wore, and the storybooks lining up on the shelf were from this one sugar aunty.
"I was right! It’s a boy!" Zarfa slid onto the floor, clasping her cheeks as she stared at the baby in my arms.
She came right when I was visiting Shwa for my daily dose of personal bonding. While we had a whole troop of nannies and guards tending to his needs, I didn’t want him to get attached to them instead of me Natha, so I always made sure to hold him several times throughout the day; letting him hear my heartbeat and feel my temperature.
Natha usually came in the morning before he went to his office, and the evening before dinner. It was cute seeing the tall, imposing demon holding a baby that was shorter than his forearm, and I made sure to snap a few pictures for my...ahem, collections.
The nannies said I didn’t need to worry about not connecting though; they said Shwa always responded the moment I entered the room. He would stir even when he was asleep, and he would shift his head in my direction.
It was probably their attempt to console me, but it was okay--I was happy to hear it even if it was a lie.
Zarfa was fortunate to visit while Shwa was awake. The druid rangers who came, as well as the other vassals, always caught a bad timing when Shwa was asleep. And when my baby was asleep, he rarely woke up even when we poked his cheeks. He’d definitely wake up when he was hungry or peed though, along with a piercing cry.
Waking up when he was full and clean like this was rare. The rich aunty must be a lucky one.
"Aww, look at you cutie wittle pootatotie~" she squeezed the baby’s curled fists and made a weird cooing sound.
"You realize you sounded weird, right?"
"Who cares what people think about me? I’m rich!" Zarfa scoffed. "Who cares about others? Aunty only cares about her mega adorable nephew~"
I rolled my eyes and turned my head toward Jade, shaking my head and squinting my eyes to warn him about following this weird aunty’s antics. No, Jade. You shouldn’t copy her.
"Aww! You use the blanket Auntie gave you? Such a handsome little boy!" she said unreasonably--since there was no way Shwa could choose which blanket to use himself.
"You said he’s cute," I reminded her.
"Two can be right at the same time!"
Zarfa clicked her tongue and we suddenly heard a soft giggling sound. We all collectively froze, even Angwi, and stared at the wrapped baby in my arms. Shwa, my beautiful little flower, parted his little lips and made a squeaky sound. The green eyes curled and the chubby cheeks reddened.
Needless to say that we all gasped.
"Baby laughing!" Jade jumped and clapped his hands excitedly.
Gods...I didn’t want to sound like the kind of parents who thought their child could do no wrong, but at that moment, I felt like I could forgive this baby for anything he might commit in the future. He was just so, so, beautiful. I swear I would reign myself better as to not spoil Shwa too much, but at that moment...just at that moment, nothing in this world was more precious than that little giggle--not even Natha’s handsome face. Nothing in this world was more melodious than that squeaky little sound--not even Angwi’s secret lullaby.
"
Kyaaa
! Look at this cutie!" Zarfa clasped her cheeks and shook her head wildly like a fan girl in their idol’s concert. "Who’s a cutie, huh? Who’s a cutie?"
I narrowed my eyes after coming back from the daze prompted by that adorable giggle. "I thought you don’t like children?"
"Wrong!" she snorted. "I don’t want to have children on my own--doesn’t mean I dislike them."
"I see..." I stroked Shwa’s pink cheek and glanced at Zarfa. "Do you want to hold him?"
Zarfa flinched and pulled back slightly. "...n-no."
Huh? I didn’t expect this reaction. She shifted away nervously, even though she didn’t have any qualms about carrying Jade before.
"Why? You said you don’t dislike him," I tilted my head curiously.
"I love him to death, and that’s why I don’t want to accidentally hurt him," she pursed her lips. "He’s too small...what if I hold him too tightly? What if he wriggles around and I drop him?!"
"Oh, make sense..."
Pfft--I didn’t think she would have all of those colorful thoughts just from one prompt of holding a baby. Hmm...now that I thought about it, I never had that kind of thought before. Did it come naturally if it was your own child? Natha also looked very natural--although, to be fair, Shwa was just a tiny bundle he could hold with one arm.
...
"Valen!"
Once again, the nursery door burst open; this time bearing a newly adult succubus and her elf boyfriend. Why did they keep coming roughly, though? Shouldn’t they know there was a baby inside?!
Phew...but I’d forgive them since they came with genuine affection. And because I missed them.
"Zia!" Jade got up and ran to hug the succubus, who wore more mature clothing now. Too bad--I like those cute frilly gothic stuff.
Zarfa also got up and cheekily made a curtsy. "Oh, if it isn’t Lady Matriarch Ra Zidoa."
"Zarfa!" Zia was bashful at first, but immediately came forward and hugged her, laughing at the jest. Perhaps she preffered it more than a serious formal reaction. "How come you’re here before me?"
Zarfa smirked and wiggled her brow. "By the virtue of inter-realm portal."
"Tsk--we should install one too!" Zia clicked her tongue before suddenly gasping and, just like Zarfa earlier, kneeling on the ground and holding the baby’s fists. "Dearest young cousin! Oh, he’s wriggling--Izzi, look! Look!"
"I’m looking," the elf muttered quietly, careening his head to take a peek at the baby who was surrounded by his aunt and cousin.
I had a feeling he was looking more at Zia though, smiling in relief. She probably had been having a hard time as the new matriarch, and this courtesy call could be treated as a little vacation. Well, she did seem like she was having fun playing with Shwa, if her sparkling eyes and rosy cheeks were any indication.
And different from Zarfa, she was eager to hold Shwa. It seemed like she was used to handling babies back home--you know, since she had a lot of siblings, both legitimate and not. Shwa was making a fuss at first, but gradually calmed down after Zia swayed him gently.
I nudged the elf who was watching the view in a daze and whispered. "Makes you want to have one, huh?"
"Don’t tempt me," Izzi hissed, prompting my brow to arch in surprise.
Not tease but
tempt
? Oh, this elf!
I wanted to tease him more, but I didn’t think it was an appropriate topic to be had in a nursery, so I saved it for a later time. Instead, we moved to the lounge across the hall to not crowd the nursery, while also having a peaceful tea time. Angwi had taken Shwa again so we could enjoy our tea, and I could finally talk to Zia.
"Hey," I chuckled as he fidgeted awkwardly.
"Hey," she bit her lips and shifted closer, looking at me worriedly. "Are you okay? I heard--"
I swiftly placed my fingers on her lips. "I’m fine. Don’t I look fine?"
"Well, yes..."
"Then let’s not think too much about something that’s already passed."
Zarfa didn’t know about it, and Jade did not know the details. I didn’t want to taint the beautiful memory of Shwa’s birth with what happened back then. The fact remained that I was alive, so there was no need to make a fuss about it.
Well, to be fair, I also didn’t remember much after I lost my ability to breathe,
Zia bit her lips and pulled me into a tight embrace. "I’m so glad," she whispered in a strained voice. "I’d hate myself if something happened to you again while I wasn’t here."
I patted her head, feeling a bit melancholic. Ah...I did miss her. "What about you?" I stroked her cheeks, which seemed to have lost some fat. "How do you fare?"
"I...I managed," she fiddled with her skirt. "Great Aunt and Sister taught me a lot. I have a lot to study for now, but once I get used to it, I won’t have to stay in the realm all the time."
"Oh, isn’t that good?"
"Yeah," she suddenly looked bashful, which made my brows arched by themselves. Glancing subtly at Izzi--who was having a staring contest with Jade--she added in a whisper that was so quiet only I could hear it. "I...I’m thinking about visiting the elvendom."
My brows wriggled in response. "It’s getting serious, huh?"
She bit her lips again and smacked me with her face flaming in flusters. I couldn’t help but giggle gleefully since it had been a while since I could tease anyone. "I’m happy," I whispered back as I held her hands. "You’re both my precious friends after all."
"Oh, Val..."
"And...ahem--" I leaned closer and whispered in her ears. "I’m not trying to burden you or anything, but it would be great if Shwa could have a playmate--"
"Val!"
Zia smacked me in fluster again, and I laughed as Zarfa shoved her head between us and wiggled her brows mischievously. "Oh, juicy~"

chapters.title: Chapter 573: Baby is the center of the universe
chapters.content:
Chapter 573: Baby is the center of the universe
"Oh, you people are here."
Natha came at the end of our tea time, glancing at the guest briefly, kissed me briefly, and made an immediate beeline to our baby. He took Shwa from Angwi’s arms and walked around the room with a baby in his arms, stroking the dark hair and talking in a whisper with him.
"As if we are invisible," Zia scoffed. "Doesn’t even care that his cute, hardworking niece is here after two months."
I shook my head exasperatedly. "He used to check up on me every few hours before--now he barely gives me a glance if Shwa is in the same room."
And to think he refused to stay with Shwa during his birth...see how he immediately shifted now? Well, not that I have any complaints about him putting so much attention to his mini version--and it was super adorable anyway--but it was fun talking smack about your husband with your friends.
Of course, the one who always had a beef with Natha chimed in eagerly. "Natha don’t play with Jade again," the little boy climbed to my lap. "Don’t read picture books for Jade again."
I thought you didn’t like to spend time with him? I squeezed his cheeks while stifling my laugh. Hmm...if it came to it, Jade did not act as jealous as I thought he would be. Even though our focus all shifted to Shwa, he did not throw a tantrum and said things like I didn’t love him anymore.
But then again, Jade spent all his time in the nursery--playing with Shwa when the baby was awake and reading the picture books that Zarfa gifted them when the baby was asleep.
It was good that we had a lot of nannies because turned out, they had to babysit my eldest child too.
"Your husband’s priority had shifted, huh?" Zarfa laughed.
"Just like yours," I shrugged, and she laughed even louder.
"Well," unbeknownst to us, Natha had walked to the couch and leaned against the backrest right behind me. "What can I do when my husband only talks about Shwa and always in the nursery when I check on him?"
"Oh, so your priority shifted too," Zia nudged me in return, and what could I do but laugh awkwardly?
Well, let’s just all agree that our attention shifted to our baby, who was more beautiful than the blooming flower outside.
"But it’s like arriving in another world here," Izzi muttered as he looked outside the window occupying our view in front of our couch. "Are all these flowers blooming for your baby?"
"Of course! Because Shwa is flower!" Jade spread his arms and stood up on my lap so he could see the baby in Natha’s arms. "All flower go boom and puff when Shwa is born!"
"Wow~" both Zia and Zarfa clapped their hands enthusiastically, while Izzi looked at me with narrowed eyes.
I shrugged. What could I say; I wasn’t conscious to witness it. Oh, how sad. Actually, Jade also did not see it because he was busy screaming and crying in Lesta’s arms at that time. But he heard the servants all talked about it and had been telling anyone new about it too.
"For me, it’s always a different kind of world," Zarfa laughed. "It’s the end of summer in the Human Realm."
"Oh, right!"
"Talking about the Human Realm," Natha got off the backrest and returned Shwa--who had fallen asleep--to Angwi. "I thought you’d come with that girl."
"Oh, Aina?" Zarfa put her teacup down. "She was in her lab when the news came, being all serious, so I didn’t want to disturb her. I think she became extremely motivated after seeing that transfusion thing--of right!"
Zarfa snapped her fingers and pointed at Izzi, who cluelessly blinked while eating his cookie.
"I think she’ll come if she knows Izzi is here!"
Zia stiffened and shifted closer to Izzi, as if to cage him from going anywhere. "W-why?"
"Nothing like whatever you think!" Izzi spoke swiftly, shaking his head and glaring at the giggling Zarfa.
"Because she wants to talk about the transfusion, of course," Zarfa shrugged and covered her smirking mouth. "Oh, my...what did you think would happen, Matriarch?"
The pink skin of our young clan head became even redder. "N-n-nothing?!"
"Wow~you’re jealous because of that?" I chuckled, recalling the outburst incident that revealed Zia’s feelings. She was jealous of Neel then, and she was suspicious of Aina now.
But I forgot that this girl stored all of my secrets too. "I don’t want to hear that from someone who cried a lot because he thought his lover loved someone else for half a year!"
"Huh?"
"W-why are you spilling that now?!"
"Shut up! You of all people shouldn’t tease me!"
"Hey, hey..."
While Izzi was trying to calm his girlfriend, Zarfa was clapping her hands while laughing as if it wasn’t her who teased Zia the most. I smacked her in reprimand, but it just made her laugh even louder.
"Alright, alright--that’s enough," Natha chuckled and patted my shoulder. "It’s my fault that Valen misunderstood anyway."
Phew--we took a deep breath and calmed down. Fortunately, Shwa and Jade were already in the nursery with their nannies. I glanced at Zia, and after staring at each other wordlessly for three seconds, we burst out laughing.
Izzi rolled his eyes and sighed exasperatedly. "You’re always chaotic when you’re together."
"That’s called having friends, Izzi," Zarfa waved her hand, and Izzi glared at her again since she was the one who actively provoked them all the time. No, Izzi--she would get more excited if you show that kind of reaction. Look at her smirk! Zarfa tilted her head and resumed the interfered topic. "Anyway, how about it? Should we call Aina over?"
Izzi turned toward Zia, as if asking for permission. Oh, you weren’t bad, huh? She flinched slightly and blushed, before clutching his sleeve and nodding adorably.
Ah...a girl experiencing her first love was indeed the cutest.
Not as cute as Shwa and Jade though.
"Well, I don’t know when else I’ll be here, so might as well," Izzi said after they finished whispering to each other. "But it’s not my own creation, so you should ask the other too."
"D’Ara wouldn’t mind. Oh--we should call Neel too, then!" I clasped my hand. "I haven’t seen her since that first transfusion!"
Izzi scoffed. "That’s because she had used all of her outdoor energy for that few days of visit to the Castle."
I blinked and tilted my head. "But...she was indoors?"
The only ’outdoors’ she had to experience was the journey from the portal to the Lord’s Quarter, and she spent all of her time inside this room to make the transfusion device. The other time was when she controlled the recording devices at that party, but she was also tightly inside a carriage and a closed-off box.
"Anywhere outside her room or bunker is ’outdoors’ for her," Izzi shrugged.
"I...I see..."
"But she likes talking about this kind of thing, so just call her. Tell her about the baby too--I don’t think she’ll know unless you say it to her face," Izzi added.
"Huh..." I blinked. "Oh, right!"
Zarfa laughed again. "What--you haven’t told her?"
"I mean...Doun and the twins knew and came, so I thought..." I mumbled in defense, but Izzi immediately snorted.
"How would she know if she never saw them?" the elf smirked. "Her meals were probably made and delivered by the golems, right?"
Ugh...that was true. I should have known since she did not show herself even when Doun and the twins came to congratulate me and saw the baby. I was so busy feeling so elated about Shwa’s arrival that I hardly cared about who came. To be honest...I also did not consider her existence before the invention topic came, hehe...
Zarfa tilted her head and arched his brow. "You knew her so much, Izzi~"
"Ceci..." I glanced at Zia, who was once again stiffened and gave Izzi a side-eye.
Izzi frowned and quickly came to her defense. "What’s wrong with that? She’s my part--colleague..."
"You almost said partner, huh?"
"Business partner!" Izzi slammed the armrest and stroked Zia’s shoulder in reassurance. "Business partner!"
"Ceci..." I let out a sigh and smacked the giggling girl again. However, talking about Neel who hated the crowd reminded me of someone. "Ah, what about Aunt Nezja? Where is she?"
I thought she would come with Zia and Izzi since they were in the same place, but there was no sign of her.
"Oh, about that..."
Zia suddenly blushed, which made us look at her curiously. It was Izzi who finally answered. "She said she didn’t want to come with us, so she came a bit later," he said while scratching his neck awkwardly. "I think she’ll arrive tonight or tomorrow morning..."
Huh? What with those faces? Zia was even half-hiding behind Izzi’s shoulder with a reddened face.
"She didn’t want to spend the journey third-wheeling between a couple in their sweet phase," Natha translated the reason further before sipping his tea.
"Uncle!"
Zia was literally flaming now, looking more like Angwi with that deep red skin. We couldn’t help but giggle at her reaction, which made her get even redder. If we teased her even more, I felt like steam would start to come out of her ears.
Well...where else would we see a succubus getting flustered this much from a talk about her love life?
Ah...I couldn’t wait until everyone was here.

chapters.title: Chapter 574: Is it really a reunion without a bit of chaos?
chapters.content:
Chapter 574: Is it really a reunion without a bit of chaos?
"Baby..."
Neel stared at Shwa, who was blinking slowly at her from my arms cradle. As far as I know, babies couldn’t see clearly at first, but they could still differentiate shapes and colors. In Shwa’s case though, he could also differentiate mana--that was how he knew if Natha and I came closer. After all, we had been feeding him with our mana since he was still inside the seed.
He seemed to recognize Jade somewhat since the little boy had a trace of my mana. For others, however, Shwa would just stare blankly, perhaps trying to register them. He managed to recognize his principal nanny who sang him a lullaby every night, but that was it.
Still...wasn’t that pretty good for a week-old baby?
Neel stood still, almost as if frozen. At first, I thought she was angry that we forgot to tell her directly, but then I saw the sparkle in her eyes and the slight tremble on the tips of her outstretched fingers.
"This...won’t break if I touch it, right?" she whispered hesitatingly.
Ah...it was kind of fascinating how everyone had a slightly different but also kind of the same reaction. I laughed and shrugged. "Depends on how hard you do it."
She gulped and moved her hand to poke the baby’s arm lightly; so lightly that it was barely a touch. Only after I told her she could touch a bit ’harder’ did she hold the curled fist and sway it slowly, as if making Shwa wave his hand. She slipped her thumb between the curling fingers and kneaded the baby’s palms, making Shwa wiggle from the ticklish sensation. He let out a small giggle, and Neel froze.
"Wow..." she exclaimed softly.
I never thought of Neel as one to get touched by a baby, but there she was, staring blankly at the wiggling and giggling baby. The amazement was clearly reflected in her eyes, which, in itself, amazed me.
"Babies are...amazing, aren’t they?" she said in a daze.
Oh, she even spelled it out loud.
"They are made by mortals, and receive a soul capable of growth..."
Huh?
She continued with a serious tone. "It’s like...an inventor’s greatest wish."
Ah...I just remembered how fascinated she was about the golems. It was a bit unsettling though, if she treated babies like golems. Did all inventors have this kind of thought? I looked at Izzi in concern, but he just shrugged nonchalantly.
"I’m not that deep of a person," the elf said nonchalantly. "I just want to make a gun."
My brow arched. "Because it looks cool?"
"You know it," Izzi smirked. But he still patted his ’business partner’ in a warning. "Well, that’s a profound look at things, but don’t ever cross the line, okay?"
The half-naga snapped at him with a hiss. "What do you see me as?"
"I don’t know, dude..." Izzi smiled wryly. "You act like a mad scientist sometimes."
"I don’t want to hear anything from someone who neglects the pact of invention to frolic with his girl," Neel sneered and looked at Izzi with a gaze of betrayal.
Obviously, Izzi gasped in shock. "Wh-what’s wrong with pursuing love?"
"T-that’s right! It might work as inspiration, you know!"
And naturally, his girlfriend--the pursuer of one true love--supported him wholeheartedly. Although while hiding behind him with reddened cheeks.
Izzi nodded and snapped his fingers. "Y-yes! T-that!"
"Hmph--doubt it," Neel clicked her tongue and turned back toward Shwa, who despite being surprised by the sudden increase in volume, did not cry--like the good boy that he was. Neel let out a rare smile and lightly tickled the side of Shwa’s tummy. "Well, at least, this one is worth going out for~"
Wow, even using a cheery tone. Babies sure are miracle makers. I used Shwa’s fist to pat her hand and laughed. "Well, we’re glad if it’s worth it."
"Aina’s here!"
Again, the nursery door opened with a slam as Zarfa rushed inside like a storm. Really--couldn’t these girls open the door like sane people?
"So unfair!" Aina stomped her way inside. "You should have told me right away!"
"Hehe, I said I’m sorry already," Zarfa stuck out her tongue and winked. Yeah, she wasn’t sorry at all. "I mean, can you blame me? You didn’t even budge when I called you before..."
"You should have just smacked me!"
"What if something breaks because of that?!"
"Eh--it’s fine~" the petite girl waved her hand dismissively. "It’s the baby’s father’s money after all."
"Oh!" Zarfa gasped and covered her lips with her fingers, letting out an evil witch snicker. "Huehehehe~"
Natha, who personally came to fetch Aina for time efficiency, shook his head in exasperation. "I’m going to let it slide this time."
"Hehe..."
Aina grinned and made a high-five with Jade before tip-toeing to us. She covered her mouth as she came close, but I could see the fireworks in her eyes. "Aaack! He’s so cuuutee! Even though he looks like the Big Boss, he’s so cutee!"
"What do you mean ’even though he looks like’ me?" Natha narrowed his eyes, but Aina kept muttering as if she didn’t hear anything.
"Mm, mm--but since he has Valen’s gene too, I’m sure he will still grow up cutely. Yes, yes--not scary at all," Aina nodded fearlessly, grabbing the baby’s feet in greetings. "Don’t worry, baby--you won’t grow scary like your father. Please stay cute like Valen and Jade."
"Don’t worry, Aye! Baby is flower, and flower is cute!"
"Right~? I know Jade will agree!"
What even was that conversation? The fearless inventor and the fearless little boy kept talking about how cute Shwa was and how scary Natha was. But why did they talk this way when they knew Natha was scary? Perhaps because they were a pair of brave souls. Or perhaps because they knew Natha was too tired to argue with two kids.
I giggled and placed the baby in Natha’s arms to heal his exasperated mind, and ushered the rest of the girls to the room across the hall while asking Izzi to babysit Jade for a bit.
"It’s been a while since we were all gathering like this, right?"
"You’re right," Aina nodded, grinning toward the succubus. "When we came here the last time, Zia and Izzi already eloped--"
"W-what are you talking about?!" Zia coughed on her tea.
"Eeh~but it’s romantic, isn’t it? Eloping?"
"Well, it is..." the romance author mumbled, before snapping back to reality and shaking her hands strongly. "B-b-but we did not elope!"
Zarfa sunk herself into the chaize lounge while clicking her tongue. "Tsk--I had wished for some juicy tea."
"T-tea?"
"Isn’t an inter-race couple already juicy enough?" Neel tilted her head.
"It’s not that uncommon among lust demons," Zia fiddled with the handle of her cup.
The one that wasn’t her anyway.
"Hmm? But I heard you don’t usually do it with elves though?" I tapped my chin, recalling our conversation with Aleena back then.
"O-ho?"
My eyes squinted as I tried to recall the content. "Something about elves not liking the promiscuous nature of lust demon?"
Zia groaned and Aina clapped her hands. "Ah, like those strongly religious people?"
